Uniform Title: Devīrahasya Main Title: Devīrahasya with Pariśiṣṭas Editor: Ramachandra Kak

Editor: Haribhaṭṭa Śāstrī. Description: The *Devīrahasya* and *Uddhārakośa* are published together in a single volume. Edited by Rāmacandra Kāka and Haribhaṭṭa Śāstrī, it was originally published in Kashmir in 1941. The *Devīrahasya* is considered to be a part [of this collection].
of the *Rudrayāmala*. It appears to have been composed in Kashmiri, as it repeatedly refers to the goddesses Jvālāmukhī, Śārikā, Mahārājñī,
Śāradā, Bhidā, and Bālā, who possess shrines in the Kathmandu Valley.
They were very popular. The presence of the Arabic terms *phirangahā* and *safak* on pages 307 and 317 indicates that it was composed at a time when Muslims were already established in the valley.
The *Devīrahasya* is divided into three parts as follows:
A) The *Pūrvārdha* (First Half). This consists of twenty-five chapters (*paṭala*) dealing with: (1) initiation; (2) mantras of form; and so forth.
(3) The mantras of Śiva; (4) the mantras of Viṣṇu;
(5) the unlocking (*utkelana*) of mantras; (6) the vitalization (*jīvana*) of mantras;
(7) the methods for removing curses attached to mantras; (8) the mental recitation (*mānasa-japa*).

(9) The method for employing specific seed-syllables (*bīja*) uttered before and after particular mantras (*pārāyaṇa*). (10) The preliminary practice (*puraścaraṇa*) of mantras. (11) The sacrificial rite (*homa*) performed for [the mantras].
(12) The preliminary practice of mantras. (13) The diagrams (*yantra*) used for worship. (14) The method of wearing amulets containing those diagrams.
(15, 16) The *ṛṣi*, meter, and other attributes of mantras; worship in...
(17, 18) Cremation grounds; (19) purification of the implements used for worship; (20) the origin of wine; (21) the ritual consumption of wine;
(22) prayers and hymns dedicated to the *śākta* practitioners (*vīras*).
(22) Purification of wine. (23) Purification of the consort.
(24) Various types of rosaries and their purification. (25) Purification and other rites for the maṇḍalas.
B) The *Uttarārdha* (Second Half), also known as the *Rahasyavijaya*,
comprises thirty-five chapters containing the *pañcāṅga*— consisting of the *paṭala*, *kavaca*, *paddhati*, *sahasranāma*, and *stotra*— of Gaṇeśa and Sūrya.
Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa, Śiva, and Durgā.
The appendix (Pariśiṣṭha) provides the *pañcāṅgas* for Jvālāmukhī,
Śārikā, Mahārājñī, and Bālā— the family deities of the Kashmiri paṇḍits.

B) The *Uddhārakośa* (Treasure of Mantras), located in the appendix. Composed in the form of a dialogue between Dakṣiṇāmūrti and his disciple Akṣobhya, it is a collection of citations from no fewer than forty-seven [sources].
Tantric Works. This consists of seven sections: 1) The mantras of the goddesses Tripurā, Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, Tārā, Bhuvaneśvarī, Mātaṅgī, Śārikā, Rāñjī, Bhīdā, and Jvālāmukhī, together with certain...
1) The seed-syllable mantras and their names. 2) The mantras of Bhadrakālī, Turī, Chinnamastā, Dakṣiṇākālikā, Śyāmā, and Kālarātrī.
3) The mantras of Vajrayoginī, Vārāhī, Śāradā, and Kāmeśvarī.

Gaurī, Annapūrṇā, and Kulavāgīśvarī, together with those of Gaṇeśa, Vāṭuka, Kumāra, Mṛtyuñjaya, Kārtavīryārjuna, Sugrīva, and Hanumān; 4) the mantras of the nine planets; 5) the names of the letters of the alphabet.
The Sanskrit alphabet. 6) The mantras of Bhavānī, Bagalāmukhī, Indrākṣī, and Khecarī. 7) Descriptions of the goddesses, deities, and planets mentioned in the preceding sections.

p. 1) Now begins the Śrīdevīrahasya.
Oṃ, salutations to the illustrious Gaṇeśa. Salutations to Tripurasundarī.
The Illustrious Bhairava said:
Now, O Goddess, I shall declare a most wonderful secret.
That which has not been spoken in all the tantras, such as the Yāmala and others; || 1 ||
O Pārvatī, this Tantra known as the *Parādevīrahasya*, which embodies the elevation of mantras, is the essential reality of the venerable sixteen-syllabled mantra; it is my very soul.
It is not to be disclosed and must not be given away; it bestows the highest fruit, grants both worldly enjoyment and liberation in this world, and brings happiness to practitioners.
The Śrī Devī said:
O Blessed One, Knower of all Tantras, Śaṅkara, Lord of the Kaulas!
By your grace, I have come to know the reality of the Goddess, which is so very difficult to attain.
The secret Tantra, consisting of mantra, has been indicated by you yourself;
now, preceded by initiation, speak to me that which is known as the secret of the Supreme Goddess.
Śrī Bhairava said:
O Īśānī, listen with devotion to the Devīrahasya,
by the mere hearing of which one obtains the fruit of ten million pūjās.
Now I shall declare the supreme decision regarding the teacher and the disciple;
having investigated [the matter] according to rule, the wise one should perform the rite of initiation. (7)
From Brahmā down to a mere insect, the entire world— both mobile and immobile—
is deluded by its state as a bound soul (paśu) under the supreme Goddess, devoid of true desire.
Nevertheless, through his grace and by service to his lotus feet,
the Kaulika, liberated from the state of a bound soul (paśu), shall thereafter attain knowledge.

Having received initiation into that [mantra] from Śiva by worshipping the feet of the Guru, the practitioner becomes initiated and wise; one devoid of initiation remains a bound soul (paśu). || 10 ||
O Goddess, for one who has no initiation in Śiva, life is fruitless;
such a person shall never cross over the ocean of hell at any time.
O Goddess of the gods, for the beast (paśu) who is devoid of initiation and of despicable birth, a flood of sins approaches while merit flees far away. (12)
Therefore, O Goddess of the Gods, this supreme initiation should be received with effort by the wise,
whether in childhood, youth, or even old age.
Otherwise, the sinful one would go to hell and lead his own ancestors to hell; therefore, O Śivā, a man who acts like a beast shall enter the womb of a beast.
O Goddess, having obtained the latent impression (vāsanā) acquired in a previous birth which bestows the supreme goal, one should seek out a Guru who is initiated into the Kaulika conduct. 15.

A guru who is of noble lineage, knowledgeable in the tantras, pleasing in all his limbs, free from disease, devoid of greed, and one who has reached the further shore of the entirety of the Agamas. || 16 ||

Having first obtained [the initiation] through devotion and having bowed down, he especially gratified the Goddess according to the prescribed rule for the initiation determined by the Siddhas, Sādhyas, and Aris.

The practitioner should accept [the disciple] with supreme devotion, by which the teacher and the disciple—possessing beautiful limbs, of noble birth, and initiated from the womb—are brought together. (18)
A child or a youth devoted to the guru, endowed with wisdom;
a devotee devoted to the Goddess, fearing sin and self-controlled. (19)
Having seen [this], one should bestow the supreme initiation; thereby, one becomes a partaker of the ritual portion.
The Śrī Devī said:
"O Blessed One, ocean of compassion, I have this great doubt."
In whose mind there is supreme devotion, for such a person there is no other guru. || 20 ||
O Lord, what will he not accomplish—one who is of noble birth, knowledgeable in all tantras, capable of accomplishing mantras, and endowed with supreme devotion? (21)
Śrī Bhairava said: O Goddess of the gods, one who is uninitiated and devoid of a preceptor, yet possesses devotion to Śakti, should treat a book as his guru in the absence of a guru.
O Goddess, if there should be someone who is a guru, expert in the tantras, initiated with the mantra of Śiva, a Vaiṣṇava, and endowed with auspicious characteristics; || 23 ||
O Goddess, he who abandons that [Guru] and, though devoted to another,
regards a book as his Guru, shall become a slayer of Śiva.

One should worship a Guru who is of noble birth and knowledgeable in the Tantras for the sake of attaining success in mantra; O Goddess, one should abandon a Guru who is foolish, greedy, or even of noble birth [if he lacks these qualities]. 25.
One should not undergo initiation for one's father, nor for one's maternal grandfather, nor for a younger uterine brother, and especially not for a maternal uncle. (26)
One should not practice deceit or greed out of a desire for wealth, even in one's mind;
rather, one should act out of a desire for the next world or out of fear of the next world.
The Śrī Devī said:
O Blessed One, O Supreme Lord, out of a desire for the welfare of practitioners, tell me: at what time should the supreme initiation be received by practitioners? (28)
The venerable Bhairava said: On an auspicious day, under a favorable lunar mansion, at a solar transit, or during either of the two solstices—
On the day of Navarātra, during the Śrāddha for one's parents, or on the anniversary of one's own birth; || 29 ||
O Goddess, on the ninth day of the lunar fortnight, during an eclipse of the moon or sun,
under the asterism Tiṣya, or under one's own birth-asterism, the wise teacher should bestow initiation.
There, first, having bathed under an auspicious constellation and having worshipped Bhairava,
he went to a divine riverbank, beautiful with creepers and flowers.
Or, having reached a most meritorious island, difficult even for the gods to attain,
or likewise a temple of the deities, one should then quickly bow down.
Having performed his daily rites, O Goddess, the Guru, having smeared [or drawn] according to the rule, should construct a beautiful four-cornered altar in the northeast direction. (33)
There, O Goddess, one should visualize the Śrīcakra of the Supreme Goddess (Parādevī) upon the yantra with vermilion while reciting the root mantra, O Śivā.
A triangle joined with a bindu, a hexagon, a circular mandala,
an eight-petaled lotus marked by three circles, and adorned with an enclosure of earth.
O Goddess, one should worship this initiation diagram at the time of initiation;
O Śivā, [the deities] Gaṇeśa, Dharma, Varuṇa, and Kubera should be worshipped together.
In the intermediate directions, the lords of the intermediate quarters are to be worshipped in due order with the seed-syllables Tāra, Māyā, and Ramā, using incense, lamps, and flowers.
O Goddess of the gods, one should worship Māyā, Mohinī, Menā, Maṅgalā, Sarvamaṅgalā, and Mahāvidyā within the six corners.
O Goddess, with the seed-syllables *tāra*, *māyā*, and *ramā*, and with perfumes, unbroken rice, and flowers,
one should worship Gaṅgā, Yamunā, and Sarasvatī in front of that [liṅga].
The wise one should worship in the triangle, beginning from the northeast (Īśāna), the southeast (Āgneya), and the east;
in the Bindu, he should worship the Supreme Goddess with the venerable Mūlamantra.
[One should worship] Sadāśiva, Mahāraudra, Kāmeśa, and Kāmaneśvara with perfumes, unbroken grains, flowers, and the like, as well as with incense, lamps, and other offerings. || 41 ||
O Goddess of gods, the eight Mothers are to be worshipped on the eight petals with offerings of food, water for sipping, and well-scented betel leaves.
O Goddess, preceded by the eight Bhairavas, [the goddesses] beginning with Brāhmī are [invoked] with the mantra:
Brāhmī, Nārāyaṇī, Kaumārī, and Aparājitā. (43)
Māheśvarī, Cāmuṇḍā, Vārāhī, and Nārasiṃhikā should especially be worshipped in this manner, following the counter-clockwise sequence.
O Mistress of Bhairava, one should worship the eight Bhairavas right there:
Mahākāla, Kālāgni, Karāla, and Vikarālaka; || 45 ||
O Īśānī, having duly worshipped Saṃhāra, Ruru, Supta, and Unmattabhairava there with perfumes, unbroken grains of rice, and flowers according to the prescribed rite, [one should proceed].
O Goddess of the Gods, having worshipped the yantra, one should then fully honor the Guru;
thereafter, one should dig a triangular pit in the east in the form of a yoni.
There, having first worshipped the fire-drill (araṇi), one should invoke the Fire in Śivā;
one should utter the Praṇava (tāra), the three fires, and the word "Agni Vaiśvānara."
One should kindle the pair [of sticks] and say, "Come here," and address them:
"Establish your presence here; grant me my boon"—thus the pair. (49)
Then, having uttered "phaṭ" followed by the wife of fire (svāhā), one should worship with fragrance;
O Śivā, one should offer clarified butter as an oblation with the mantra of Parādevī.
In the fire of Śiva, one should offer a hundred supreme oblations with the root mantra,
using ghee, sugar-candy, grapes, dates, lotuses, and milk-rice (pāyasa).
There, having invoked the Goddess and meditated especially upon the Supreme One,
the Guru, seated facing east, [should look at] the disciple facing north.
O Goddess, having established [the deity] according to the rules and performed the purification of the seat (*viṣṭaraśodhana*),
one should perform the rite of offering the vital breaths (*prāṇārpaṇavidhi*) accompanied by the sequence of the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*).
Having performed three breath-controls (prāṇāyāmas) and having completed three sips of water (ācamanas),
O Goddess of the Gods, one should bind the directions there with the root mantra and meditate upon Parā.
O Maheśvarī, for the sake of the disciple who is peaceful and for the supreme delight [of the Guru], the teacher bestows the initiation,
which is most difficult to attain, in the presence of the fire before the Yantra.
With his heart absorbed in bliss, the lord of practitioners should slowly offer the Great Vidyā, the Śrīvidyā, three times each at the root of the ear.
First, O Maheśvarī, one should offer the mantra of Gaṇeśa along with its ancillaries; then the Gāyatrī of the Goddess, and then the root-mantra.
Having thus offered [the oblation], O Goddess of Gods, and having performed the fire-sacrifice according to the rule,
the disciple, having received initiation, should worship the Guru according to his capacity.
Having gratified them with prostrations, sacrificial fees, and auspicious garments,
and having quickly received their permission, O Supreme Goddess, he set out for the recitation of mantras.
O Īśvarī, O Śivā, a disciple should never, under any circumstances, show the yantra, the mantra, the rosary, or even a single part of the tantra to his guru.
Then, having completed the fire oblation (homa) and having gratified Vaṭuka, the host of Yoginīs, and the spirits with the bali offering, one should dismiss the Goddess and the God.
The Śrī Devī said:
O Blessed One, Lord of the Gods, bestower of grace upon devotees,
one should mutter the supreme root-vidyā of Gaṇeśa and Gāyatrī.
Whether reciting a Śaiva mantra or a Vaiṣṇava mantra, what kind of knowledge (vidyā) would that lord of practitioners obtain? Cut through this doubt of mine.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
O Goddess of gods, on the first day, the practitioner [should act] with devotion to the Guru.
O Goddess, one should mutter the supreme root-vidyā of Gaṇeśa and Gāyatrī.
Then, O Goddess, during an auspicious moment, one should recite the Śaiva mantra, having obtained it within a few days through the grace of the Guru’s feet. (65)
Then, having always satisfied the Guru with devotion toward Śivā through salutations, worship,
and prayers, one should thereafter pray to Śrīvidyā.
O Goddess, without the Śrīvidyā, a practitioner is considered uninitiated;
one who is uninitiated is called a *paśu* (bound soul), and due to being a *paśu*, he shall go to hell. (67)
Therefore, at one's own auspicious birth, having worshipped the Guru with devotion and first requested Śrīvidyā, one should receive it for the sake of attaining all perfections. 68.
O Girijā, having obtained the Śrīvidyā of Mahātripurasundarī— which is difficult to attain— along with Śiva, its limbs, and its ancillaries, one should then pray for the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
O Supreme Goddess, even for me there can be no success without Śyāmā;
therefore, the best of practitioners should recite the twenty-two-syllable Vidyā. (70)
Through the recitation of the Śyāmā-vidyā, the Śrīvidyā will quickly attain perfection.
Kālikā is said to be tāmasī, while the sixteen-syllabled mantra is rājasī.
The supreme goddess is of the nature of sattva, the Great Śrī consisting of sixteen syllables;
kingdom may be given, one's head may be given, and even one's progeny may be given to a seeker.
A house filled with wealth may be given away, but the sixteen-syllable mantra must not be given;
rather, one should obtain the knowledge of Tripurasundarī through the grace of the Guru. (73)
"One who is a worshipper of Śrīvidyā should not say even in his mind, 'I am [a follower of another path]';
rather, he should worship the Dark Goddess (Śyāmā), the Supreme Knowledge (Parāvidyā), who exists as a manifestation of the divisions of Śrīvidyā. (74)
By that means, success—which is difficult even for the gods to attain—will be swiftly achieved.
Whatever the Guru does not explicitly state even by way of a glance, one should not perform that.
The Guru alone is the supreme Goddess; the Guru alone is the supreme goal.
He who performs any action while transgressing the Guru shall go to hell. (76)
Thus, O Goddess, one who is devoted to the Supreme, initiated, and a worshiper of the Guru, should perform recitation (japa) and worship day and night according to the Guru's instruction. || 77 ||
Having received initiation from a guru himself, he becomes an initiate and a vessel for merit;
O Goddess, having worshipped and entreated his guru for the sake of the Śakti-initiation, [he proceeds].
For one who, having been initiated, possesses no power, that initiation is indeed fruitless;
even if his mantra has been recited for ten million lifetimes, his knowledge does not reach fulfillment.
Then, having worshipped the disciple in Śiva, the Guru, who knows the supreme truth, should cause the disciple to contemplate his wife as the supreme form, the very form of the Goddess. (80)
Having worshipped the Supreme Śakti with prostrations and hymns from the highest limit, and having honored her as a mother or a daughter, O Goddess, one should then initiate [the disciple]. 81.
Having first worshipped Parāvat, O Śivā, the Guru should then bestow the initiation; having sat there facing westward.
Having made her face the east for the sake of initiation, one should worship her as one would the King of Yantras;
then, O Goddess of Gods, having worshipped [her] before the Yantra in the temple of the deity.
Having become Śiva, one should impart the supreme knowledge (parāvidyā) into the root of the ear;
having received that knowledge which is identical with Śiva, one should worship the guru like a father.
Having accepted his command upon one's head with perfumes, unbroken grains, flowers, and the like, preceded by sacrificial fees and garments, one should always perform the recitation (japa). 85.
And having become initiated by Śakti, even one who is himself initiated in Śiva—even a mortal being—shall attain immortality in Śiva. (86)
O Goddess, if Śrīvidyā is obtained through the grace of the Guru’s feet, she is Śyāmā and she is Śivā; for him, the three worlds are brought under control. 87.
This supreme secret has been declared by me to you out of devotion;
O Great Goddess, this [secret] of the procedure for initiation must be guarded with great effort. (88)
Thus ends the first chapter, the exposition of the procedure for initiation, in the *Śrīrudrayāmala Tantra*, within the *Śrīdevīrahasya*.
Now begins the second chapter;
the illustrious Bhairava said:
Now, O Maheśvarī, I shall declare the mantras along with their ancillaries;
O Pārvatī, listen to those of the Goddesses, the Vaiṣṇavas, the Śāktas, and the Śaivas. 1.
Tripurā, Bālā with three syllables, as well as Tripurabhairavī, Kālikā, Bhadrakālī, Mātaṅgī, and Bhuvaneśvarī; || 2 ||
Ugratārā, Chinnaśīrṣā, Sumukhī, and Sarasvatī;
Annapūrṇā, Mahālakṣmī, Śārikā, and then Śāradā. (3)
Indrākṣī, Bagalā, Turyā, Rājñī, Jvālāmukhī, as well as Bhīḍā, Kālarātri, Bhavānī, and Vajrayoginī. (4)
Vārāhī, Siddhalakṣmī, and then Kulavāgīśvarī;
(Padmāvatī, Kubjikā, Gaurī, and then Śrīkhecarī);
O Goddess, Nīlasarasvatī is remembered as the supreme power (Parāśakti) thereafter.
O Goddess, I shall now declare the mantras of these Śaktis together with their ancillaries.
Thereafter, O Pārvatī, I shall declare the Śaiva mantras; listen duly.
They are Mṛtyuñjaya, Amṛteśāna, Vaṭuka, and Maheśvara. (7)
Śiva, Sadāśiva, Rudra, Mahādeva, Karālaka, Vikarāla, Nīlakaṇṭha, Śarva, Paśupati, and Mṛḍa. (8)
Pinākin, Giriśa, Bhīma, Gaṇeśa, Pramathādhipa, Kumāra, Krodhana, Īśa, Kapālī, and Krūrabhairava. || 9 ||
Saṃhāra is Īśvara, Bharga is Ruru, the imperishable Kālāgni, Aghora, Mahākāla, and he is remembered as Kāmeśvara. || 10 ||
O Goddess of gods, hear the Vaiṣṇava mantras hidden within the tantras, by the mere hearing of which a practitioner of mantra shall go to the abode of Viṣṇu. (11)
Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, Viṣṇu, Nṛsiṃha, Varāha, Paraśurāma, Sītārāma, and Janārdana. || 12 ||
Viśvaksena and Vāsudeva— these ten Vaiṣṇava mantras, O Goddess, are most excellent and should be recited by the best of practitioners.
O Maheśvarī, I shall speak the extractions of the mantras of these Śākta, Śaiva, and Vaiṣṇava [traditions]; having heard them, conceal them with great effort.
One should place the Vāgbhava, the Kāmarāja, and Śakti, with the name in the middle;
ending with "namas," O Goddess, this is the eight-syllabled mantra of Bālā. (15)

[The mantra] "aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ bālāyai namaḥ" is Bālā. [The mantra of] Vedhas consists of the seed-syllable below, the syllable above that, Jiṣṇu, Tamas, Parā, Chavi, Śakti, the Head, Kānti, Tamas, Māyā, and the Head of Śarad. (16)
On the fringe of the Goddess’s illusory darkness is the fifteen-syllable mantra:
*ka e ī la hrīṃ*, *ha sa ka ha la hrīṃ*, *sa ka la hrīṃ*.
This is clearly the Vidyā known as Lakṣmī, Parā, joined with Madana, Vāgbhava, and Śakti, and also described as the *Tāra* (Oṃ) and the *Bhūtikamalā*.
The procedure for the venerable sixteen-syllable mantra, however, has been declared in reverse order starting from Śakti; may it be auspicious and complete. || 17 ||
Clearly: Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Aiṃ Sauḥ Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kaeīlahrīṃ Hasakahalahrīṃ Sakalahrīṃ Sauḥ Aiṃ Klīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ.
O Goddess, I shall declare the secret of Tripurā, her profound mystery: the powers of the Eternal One (Nityā), namely Vāgbhavī and Kāmaśakti, are to be worshipped. (18)
With the seed-syllables *tāra*, *māyā*, and *ramā*, the name is placed in the middle, and *aśmarī* at the end;
this mantra is considered common to all Śaktis. (19)
O Goddess, in the worship of Tripurā, when there is a separate recitation of the mantra,
one should utter the triad of Kālīs, the pair of Kūrca mantras, and the pair of Lajjā mantras.
To the south, "Kālike," and again the seed-syllables as before;
there should be two *ṭha*s at the end of the mantra—this is the mantra of Bhuvaneśvara. || 21 ||
The twenty-two-syllable Vidyā is proclaimed as the Queen of Vidyās (Vidyārājñī).
Clearly: *krīṃ krīṃ krīṃ hūṃ hūṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ dakṣiṇe kālike krīṃ krīṃ krīṃ hūṃ hūṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ svāhā*—this is Kālī.
The Śaktis beginning with Kālī are to be worshipped using the seed-syllable of Kālī alone;
otherwise, there would be a loss of accomplishment in the supreme worship of Kālikā. (22)
One should utter the three *kālīs*, the pair of *kūrca*s, the pair of *lajjā*s, and the word *bhadrikā*; then one should recite the seed-syllables (*bīja*) in reverse order. (23)
The great mantra of Bhadrakālī is joined with two *ṭha*s:
*prakāśam*—*krīṃ krīṃ krīṃ hūṃ hūṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ bhaiṃ bhadrakāli bhaiṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hūṃ krīṃ krīṃ krīṃ svāhā*. This is the Bhadrakālī [mantra].
O Great Goddess, in the worship of Bhadrakālī, the attendant and other Śaktis are to be worshipped with the seed-syllables of Kālī, Kūrca, and Parā. (24)
Having extracted the Tāra and the Parā, and [the mantra] "Rājamātaṅginī," one should extract the pair: "dehi mama sarvārthasiddhim. (25)
This mantra, ending with two *ṭha*s and a horse (*turaga*), is dear to kings.
Explicitly stated: *oṃ hrīṃ rājamātaṅgini mama sarvārthasiddhiṃ dehi 2 phaṭ svāhā*—this is Mātaṅgī.

O Goddess of the gods, the powers belonging to the retinue are to be worshipped with the syllable *Tāra*. One should utter the seed-syllable of *Māyā* in the middle, followed by the name, and say "namas" at the end of the mantra.
This single-syllable [mantra], known as Bhuvaneśvarī, is recognized throughout every world.
[In] the manifest [form]: "Hrīṃ, obeisance to Bhuvaneśvarī"—thus [one worships] Bhuvaneśvarī.

At this time of worship, the Śaktis are to be worshipped with the Māyā-bīja (Hrīṃ). [The mantra is: Tāra (Oṃ), Parā (Hrīṃ), Vadhū (Śrīṃ), Kūrca (Hūṃ), Turaga (Phreṃ), and Sakala (Klīṃ) at the end. (28)
Tārā, who carries one across the ocean of existence, consists of five and a half syllables:
*oṃ hrīṃ śtrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ*; this is Ugratārā.
The Śaktis situated in the center of the wheel are to be worshipped with the [syllables] ending in *tāraka* (the *t* sound) and *anta* (the nasal *ṃ*). 29.
Lakṣmī, Lajjā, Māyā, and the twelfth Mātrā;
then the two Vajravairocanīs, joined with Māye phaṭ svāhā.
Clearly: *śrīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ vajravairocanīye hrīṃ hrīṃ phaṭ svāhā*—this is Chinnamastā.
The Śaktis belonging to the retinue are to be worshipped with a pair of Māyās (the syllable *hrīṃ*).
One should utter Vāgbhava, Kāmarāja, and likewise the word Ucchiṣṭa. || 31 ||
Having uttered "Caṇḍālinī," one should extract "Sumukhī Devī";
then "Mahāpiśācini" and the syllable of Māyā, which is the triad of lotuses (paṅkaja).
O Maheśvarī, this mantra, ending with the wife of Vahni (the *svāhā* suffix), is to be kept secret:
*aiṃ klīṃ ucchiṣṭacaṇḍālini sumukhīdevi mahāpiśācini hrīṃ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ svāhā*. This is the mantra of Sumukhī.
The other Śaktis are to be worshipped mutually with the seed-syllables of speech and desire.
The Tāra (Om), Māyā (Hrīṃ), and the Seed-syllable of Speech (Aiṃ); O Maheśvarī, the Tāra again—this well-known mantra of Sarasvatī consists of the syllables of Śiva. || 34 ||
To be explicit—as follows: *Oṃ hrīṃ aiṃ hrīṃ oṃ sarasvatyai namaḥ* for Sarasvatī.

The goddesses who attend upon the Goddess should be worshipped with the syllables of the Tāra (oṃ), Māyā (hrīṃ), and [the seed-syllable]. One should then utter the Tāra, Parā, Kamalā, Kāma, and Viśva. (35)
The two *ṭha*s [are placed] after Bhagavatī, Māheśvarī, and Annapūrṇā.
(p. 13) It is explicit: *oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ namo bhagavati māheśvari annapūrṇe svāhā*.
Aṇṇapūrṇā;
the goddesses situated near the [central] goddess are to be worshipped by means of the two initial seed-syllables alone. (36)
*Tāra*, *parā*, *ramā*, *kāma*, *vāgbhava*, and the seed-syllable of *śakti*;
then "O Mahālakṣmī, be gracious," followed by the pair [of syllables], and the three lotuses. (37)
This great mantra, ending with *svāhā*, bestows the state of Mahālakṣmī. It is revealed as follows:
*oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ aiṃ sauḥ mahālakṣmi prasīda 2 śrīṃ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ svāhā*. This is Mahālakṣmī.
The supreme powers are to be worshipped by means of the three primordial seed-syllables alone. || 38 ||
*Tāraṃ*, *māyāṃ*, *śriyaṃ*, *kūrcaṃ*, *sindhuraṃ*, *śarma*, *pro*, *retaḥ*, followed by the name, *aśmarīṃ*, and at the end of the mind (*manas*); this mantra is difficult to obtain on earth. (39)
Clearly: "Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hūṃ phrāṃ āṃ śāṃ, obeisance to Śārikā"—with this mantra, O Śiva, one should worship the goddess Śārikā through Māyā, as well as the goddesses who constitute her retinue.
One should utter the name preceded by Tāra (oṃ), Māyā (hrīṃ), Smara (klīṃ), and Śakti (aiṃ). || 40 ||
At the end of the mantra for the Blessed Lady Śāradā, "parā vanam" is clearly [appended]:
*oṃ hrīṃ klīṃ saḥ namo bhagavatyai śāradāyai hrīṃ svāhā*— this is the mantra of Śāradā.
O Śivā, these powers (śaktis), which bestow the supreme goal, are to be worshipped by those seeking liberation. || 41 ||
The Praṇava, Kamalā, Māyā, Vāgbhava, Śakti, and Manmatha; then Indrākṣī, Vajrahaste, Hara at the end, and Agnivallabhā. (42)
The root mantra: Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ sauḥ klīṃ indrākṣi vajrahaste phaṭ svāhā; thus [is] Indrākṣī. These deities of the Śrīcakra are to be worshipped with the three initial seed-syllables.
O Goddess of gods, [the mantra] "tāraṃ mṛtsnāṃ ca" and "bagalāmukhi sarva" (or "sarvadā") [should be recited].
The mantra consists of: "duṣṭānām vācam," followed by the pair "mukhakam padam stambhaya," then the pair "jihvām kīlaya," and finally "mṛttāram" with two "ṭha"s (ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ). 44.
p.
14) Aloud: Oṃ hlīṃ, O Bagalāmukhī, paralyze the speech, mouth, and feet of all the wicked; nail down their tongues! Hlīṃ oṃ svāhā. Thus [ends the mantra of] Bagalāmukhī.
The other deities belonging to the retinue are to be worshipped with two seed-syllables;
one should place the Praṇava, the Tāraka, Jyotis, and Tārā in the center, along with the name.
O Great Goddess, this mantra is the destroyer of enemies, known as Aśmarī.
[The mantra is]: *oṃ truṃ trauṃ troṃ mahāturyai namaḥ*—thus is Mahātūrī.
O Goddess, one should worship the attendants with the *praṇava* (oṃ) in due order. (46)
*Tāra*, *parā*, *ramā*, *vahni*, *kāma*, and *śakti* constitute the six-syllable mantra; then *bhagavatyai*, *rājñyai*, *māyā*, and the two *ṭha*s at the end. (47)
Aloud: *oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ rāṃ klīṃ sauḥ bhagavatyai rājñyai hrīṃ svāhā*—thus [is the mantra of] Mahārājñī.
One should worship the retinue of the Goddess, O Śivā, with the two syllables *tāra* (oṃ) and *agni* (raṃ).
Tāram, Lajjām, Śrīyam, and likewise Jvālāmukhi mama. || 48 ||
"Devour all enemies; at the end of the double [mantra], the *kūrca* (the syllable *hrīṃ*) and the *haraṃ* (the syllable *haṃ*) are followed by *payaḥ* (the syllable *saḥ*).
The revealed [mantra] is: *oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ jvālāmukhi mama sarvaśatrūn bhakṣaya bhakṣaya hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. This is Jvālāmukhī."
O Goddess, one should worship the supreme deities belonging to the retinue with the syllable *Tāreṇa*.
*Tāra*, *parā*, *ramā*, *vedī*, *candra*, *manmatha*, *śakti*, *bhīḍā*, *bhagavatī*—thus [is the mantra], ending with *haṃsarūpiṇi* and the two *ṭha*s. (50)
As is clear: *oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsraiṃ aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ bhīḍābhagavati haṃsarūpiṇi svāhā*—this is Bhīḍā.
O Goddess of the gods, one should worship the attendants with the letters beginning with *parā*.
The Praṇava, Vāsanā, Māyā, Manmatha, and then Kamalā. || 51 ||
In the middle, within the border of the name, one should state "make everything submissive" twice; then say "give virility," followed by the name. This is known as Gaṇeśvarī-aśmarī.
Aloud: *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ kālarātri sarvaṃ vaśyaṃ kuru 2 vīryaṃ dehi 2 gaṇeśvaryai namaḥ*. Thus [ends] Kālarātrī. (p. 15)
Having worshipped Tāracandra, one should then worship his retinue:
Tāra, Ramā, Ramā, Tāra, Tāra, Māyā, Ramā, Ramā. (53)
The mantra ending in *hūṃ phaṭ* is declared to be the accomplisher of all aims. [The mantra] is:
*oṃ śrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ śrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ*—this is Bhavānī. O Goddess, one should worship the supreme attendants with the seed-syllables of *mā*. (54)
The syllable *parārṇa* (pha), followed by *vajrayoginyai*, and ending with two *ṭha*s preceded by the *praṇava* (*oṃ*);
this mantra is the lord of all accomplishments and bestows victory upon practitioners. (55)
The root mantra is: *Oṃ hrīṃ vajrayoginyai svāhā*; thus is Vajrayoginī.
O Goddess of Gods, one should worship the retinue with the seed-syllable of Māyā (*hrīṃ*).
One should place the central name in the middle, consisting of the syllables of Candra, Vāhlīka, Moha, and Candra. (56)
The Moon, the Monastery, the Pair of Lotuses, Hara, and the Water-mantra;
one should worship the members of the retinue with the seed-syllable of the delusion of latent impressions (vāsanā).

The root mantra: Aiṃ Glauṃ Laṃ Aiṃ, obeisance to the Blessed One Vārtālī, O Goddess Vārāhī, O boar-faced one! Aiṃ Glauṃ Ṭhaḥ Ṭhaḥ Phaṭ Svāhā—this is Dhūmravārāhī. [The mantra for Śyāmā is: Tāra (Oṃ), the pair Ramā (Śrīṃ Śrīṃ), Māyā (Hrīṃ), the green [syllable] (Aiṃ), the Moon (Aṃ), and Manmatha (Klīṃ).
The mantra named Śakti, for the removal of urinary calculi, has been proclaimed by Siddhalakṣmī. || 58 ||
[Aloud: Oṃ śrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ hsauḥ aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ, obeisance to Siddhalakṣmī—thus is Siddhalakṣmī.
O Śivā, one should worship the other attendants with the syllable *ramā*.
Then follows Tāra, Kāma, Ḍimbala-lakṣmī, and the beard [mantra] named Kāṅkṣā. || 59 ||
The moon, the lotus, longing, the lotus, the courtesan, the lotus, the forest, and Manu.
The mantra for illumination is: Oṃ klīṃ hrāṃ śrīṃ hūṃ jhaṃ jhaṣahaste kulavāgīśvari aiṃ.
"Ṭhaḥ jhaṃ ṭhaḥ strīṃ ṭhaḥ svāhā"—with this, O Goddess, one should worship Kulavāgīśvarī and her retinue with desire, in due order. (60)
*Tāra*, *parā*, *ramā*, *kāmā*, *vīcī*, and *padmāvatī*—
the mantra "grant me a boon" (*dehi me varam*) joined with the pair [of seed-syllables] and ending with *haraṃ nīramayaṃ* is the mantra. (61)
One should worship the supreme goddesses who constitute the retinue with the highest [mantra].
Explicitly: *oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ blūṃ padmāvati mama varaṃ dehi 2 phaṭ svāhā*—thus for Padmāvatī.
Then Tāra, Ramā, Vāgurārṇa, and the name [of the deity] in the middle, followed by Parā. (62)
The lotus-mantra consisting of the forest bestows the fruit of all accomplishments;
O Goddess of the Gods, one should worship the members of the retinue with the net-mantra. 63.
The manifestation [is as follows]: Oṃ śrīṃ prīṃ kubjike devi hrīṃ ṭhaḥ svāhā; this is the Kubjikā mantra. Then:
the Praṇava, Kamalā, Māyā, Vālhīka, and Śiva; followed by Gauri, Śarva, and Vana, O Goddess—this is the mantra that bestows the accomplishment of all aims. (64)
Clearly: "Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ glauṃ gaṃ gauri gīṃ svāhā"—thus is Gaurī.
The excellent practitioner should worship her along with her retinue by means of *ramā*.
Then [he worships] Bhekī, Tamaḥparāśakti, Khecaryai, and Aśmarī. (65)
This mantra, named Khecarī, bestows the state of moving through the sky (khecaratva).
O Dear One, one should worship the goddesses belonging to the retinue with the supreme [mantra].

This is clear: *malahrīṃ sauḥ khecaryai namaḥ*—this is the Khecarī mantra. *Tāraṃ*, *vyoṣaṃ*, *vāgbhavaṃ*, *kūrcaṃ*, *nīlasarasvati*, *haraṃ*, *nīraṃ*, at the end of the *manu*: this mantra bestows eloquence. (67)
O Goddess, one should worship the retinue with *vyoṣa* according to the prescribed rite. [The mantra] for Nīlasarasvatī is: *oṃ hrāṃ aiṃ hūṃ nīlasarasvati phaṭ svāhā*. [The general formula is:
*Tāraṃ* (oṃ), *Ramā* (hrīṃ), *Parā* (hrūṃ), *Kāmaḥ* (klīṃ), *Śaktiḥ* (sauḥ), then *Vastraṃ* (the seed-syllable of the garment), and finally the name. (68)
O Goddess, this king of mantras is proclaimed as the Vāgbhava with two *ṭha*s.
[The mantra is: *oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ sauḥ hsauḥ parāśaktyai aiṃ svāhā*. Thus is Parāśakti.
One should worship the other goddesses belonging to her retinue with the root mantra.
Thus concludes this chapter, rich with Śākta mantras, which is difficult even for the gods to obtain.
Now, O Pārvatī, listen as I shall declare to you the Śaiva mantras. (70)
This supreme secret has been revealed to you because of your devotion; it is more hidden than the most hidden, and must be guarded like one's own womb. (71)
Thus ends the second chapter, titled "The Description of the Extraction of Śākta Mantras," in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*, within the *Śrī Devī Rahasya*.
Now begins the third chapter;
the venerable Bhairava said:
O Goddess of the gods, that God of gods who is known as Mahāmṛtyuñjaya—
O Pārvatī, listen as I proclaim the extraction of his mantra.
The three-eyed one (tryakṣa), born from the heart (hṛjja), is also adorned with power (śakti); therefore, protect me from that doubt twice in the same way.
From that, power (śakti), space (kha), autumn (śarad), and the star-born from the heart (hṛjjatāra).
O Goddess, this is the extraction of the mantra of Mṛtyuñjaya. || 2 ||
O Maheśvarī, I shall declare the extraction of the mantra of Amṛteśa,
by the mere knowledge of which one obtains the fruit of initiation.

The syllable *tāram* (om) at the heart, the name [of the deity] with the arrow (*śara*) in the middle, and likewise *viśvam* (hūṃ) at the end—this mantra is the lord of all accomplishments, dear to Sumukhī and Śiva. (4)
One should extract the *praṇava* (oṃ) and the seed-syllable of prosperity (*bhūtibīja*) for Vaṭuka;
then one should utter "for the rescue from calamity" (*āpaduddhāraṇāya*) followed by two *kuru*s. (5)
To Vaṭuka is the supreme seed-syllable; this mantra is difficult even for the gods to obtain. O Great Goddess, [it begins with] Tāra (Om), the three pungents (Vyosha), and then "to Maheśvara. (6)
At the end of "Viśva," one should offer to Manu; this mantra bestows all accomplishments.
With "Tāra" (Om), "Viśva," and "Śivāya," this mantra grants both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
The syllable *tāra* (om), followed by *vyoṣa* (huṃ phaṭ), and ending with *namo śivāya*—this is another mantra.
These are the mantras of Śiva.
One should extract the syllables *tāra* (om), *vāṇī* (aiṃ), *śarat* (hrīṃ), and *kāma* (klīṃ), followed by "to Sadāśiva."
At the end of the universe, this mantra is remembered as the supreme jewel upon the crest of all mantras.
Thus [ends the mantra] of Sadāśiva.
One should utter the Tāra (Om), the three pungents (vyoṣa), "Śivo Rudra," and the pair [of words] "prasīda" (be gracious);
at the end, O Īśānī, are two Ṭha-sounds. This mantra is difficult even for the gods to obtain.
Thus for Rudra:
*Tāra*, *Parā*, *Śiva*, *Devī*, *Mahādevāya*, and two *Ṭha*s.
This mantra, O Goddess, bestows Śiva and grants the supreme goal to the devotees of Śiva. || 10 ||
*Tāra*, *Kālī*, *Śiva*—these names constitute the form of the Fourth (*turīyarūpa*) [meaning ending in the dative case], along with two *Ṭha*s.
This mantra, renowned as Bhairava, bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation in the Kali age. (11)
Thus [is the mantra] of Karāla. One should assign the Tāra (Om), Vāgbhava (Aiṃ), and Māyā (Hrīṃ) to Vikarāla; having uttered "Ṭha" twice at the end, this is declared to be the King of Mantras. (12)
Thus [ends the section] of Vikarāla.
The syllable Om is green, and the seed-syllable (ḍimba) for Nīlakaṇṭha is Aśmarī.
This ten-syllable mantra is the extraction of the mantra of Durgā’s Lord, Nīlakaṇṭha. 13.
One should utter the Tāra (Om), the Parā (Hrīm), and the seed-syllable of Ramā (Śrīm), followed by the word "Śarvāya";
at the end, O Goddess, one should say "Aśmaryai. This mantra is known as the bestower of enjoyment. || 14 ||
The Praṇava, Vāgbhava, Māra, Śakti, and the forest of Paśupati—
this mantra is beloved by the God of gods and is the means to liberation. (15)
The mantra is recorded as "Tāraṃ ramā mṛḍāya" (Oṃ Śrīṃ Mṛḍāya), with "Viśva" at the end.
One should utter "Tāraṃ hṛjjam parā lakṣmīḥ" (Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ) in the middle for Pinākin.
O Goddess, this mantra for the destruction of urinary stones (aśmarī) begins with "Ame" and "Mano"; it is the slayer of enemies.
O Goddess, the mantra for Giriśa's stone-disease consists of Tāra, Śiva, Maṭhaṃ, and Giriśāya. (17)
One should extract Tāra, Parā, Bhadrikā, and Bhīmā at the end; then Aśmarī, Manu, Māyā, the syllable Śiva, Māyā, and Mahāgaṇapa. (18)
At the end of this mantra for the removal of urinary calculi, this mantra which removes obstacles [should be recited]:
one should extract the Tāra (Oṃ), the Parā (Hrīṃ), Vāhlīka (Śrīṃ), and the Lord of the Pramathas (Hūṃ). (19)
"Be gracious"—this mantra, ending with "dvayam āpaḥ," is difficult even for the gods to obtain.
"Complexion for Kumāra"—the mantra ends with "manuḥ," followed by the supreme "viśvam. (20)
It is remembered as the bestower of the status of all the lords of gods, the giver of fortune, and the giver of liberation;
O Goddess, it consists of *tāram*, *kālī*, *śivaḥ*, *krodhaneśāya*, and *aśmarī*. (21)
This mantra is the lord of all accomplishments and the destroyer of the host of enemies; with *tāra*, *parā*, *ramā*, *lakṣmī*, and *īśāya* as the seed-syllables (*vana*), it is the mantra. (22)
Tāra (Om), Śiva (Hrīm), and Kāmarāja (Klīm) should be addressed to Kapālīśa;
having extracted two Ṭha-s at the end, this mantra shall consist of ten syllables.
One should extract the syllables *tāra* (oṃ), *kālīyuga* (hrīṃ hrīṃ), *māyā* (hrīṃ), and the fierce *bhairava* (huṃ);
at the end, one should utter *prasīda* twice followed by *āpaḥ*. This mantra bestows all accomplishments.
*Tāram*, *vāṇī*, *śarat*, *kāmaḥ*, *saṃhārāya*, and *aṅcale vanam*—this ten-syllable mantra of the God of gods has been described to you. (25)

The syllable *tāram*, *mā*, *bhūtiḥ*, *mā*, *lakṣmīḥ*, *īśvarāya*, and *aśmarī* constitute the mantra; then *tāram*, *bhāsvatī*, *māyā*, *bhargāya*, and at the end *aśmarī* constitute the mantra. || 26 ||
*Tāra*, the ocean (*abdhi*), *parā* as the seed-syllable (*bīja*), and *rurave*; then *aśmarī* is the mantra (*manu*).
Following that, the *praṇava*, *kamalā*, *māyā*, and the word *kālāgnaye*. (27)
O Goddess, at the end of the *viśva* [syllable], this king of mantras belonging to Manu has been declared:
*tāram*, *vyoṣam*, *śivaḥ*, O Goddess, and *sadyojātāya* along with *aśmarī*. (28)
This is remembered as the mantra of the imperishable Śiva Ugratārā:
Mātrādi, the six Abhijñas, Vahni, Kuliśa; then Bila, Mārajit, Vahni; Vajraka, Gautama, Agni-yugala; and Rātri-Agni marked with Vajra.
Śaṅkhu, Ru, and Tamī, auspicious; Baka-yuta, Śakti, Vavajrāśmaka; Rātri, Abdhi, Induja, Sindu, Matsya, and Kuliśa—this is the Āghorika mantra. || 29 ||
The mantra of the Lord of the Kings of Kings consists of two *kūrca*s, the two words "Mahākāla" and "prasīda," two *māyā*s, and the wife of Fire (svāhā). (30)

The Vāgbhava, Madana, Śakti, and Tārakā Mā, adorned with the entire Vidyā; this sixteen-syllable procedure, consisting of the seed-syllables joined with Tāra and in reverse order, is remembered as Śiva. || 31 ||
Thus, this entire essence of mantras, the supreme and most secret mystery, has been declared by me out of devotion to you; it must not be told to one who is evil-minded.
Thus ends the third chapter, titled "The Description of the Extraction of the Śiva-mantra," in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*, within the *Śrī Devīrahasya*.
p. 21) Now begins the fourth chapter.
Śrī Bhairava said:
Now I shall truly declare the mantras of the Vaiṣṇavas,
by the mere remembrance of which one who has been initiated becomes truly initiated.
I shall now proclaim to you the extraction of the mantra of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa,
which bestows the eight supernatural powers immediately upon practitioners and is very difficult to obtain.
The Tāra (Om), followed by Parā (Hrim), then the green syllable (Śrīm), then the name, then "Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇāya," and finally "Viśvam"—this is remembered as the mantra. || 3 ||
One should utter the words *tāram*, *ramā*, *vāgbhava*, *kāma*, *śakti*, *māyā*, *agni*, and *rādhe*;
then *kṛṣṇāya*, *kūrca*, and twice *haraṭha*. This is the mantra of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the crest-jewel of all kings of mantras. (4)
*Tāraṃ parāyugaṃ tāraṃ viṣṇave viśvamañcale*—this mantra of Viṣṇu, the God of gods, has been proclaimed to you. (5)

*Tāra*, *Ramā*, *Bhū*, *Vijavāk*, *Smara*, and *Śakti*; then the seed-syllable of Man (*nṛbīja*), the deity Narasiṃha marked by the fourth [vowel], *Vāk*, *Taṭa*, *Phaṭ*, and *Vana*—this indeed is declared to be the Lakṣmī-Narasiṃha mantra. (6)
One should utter the syllable *tāram* (Om), the letter *ram*, the goddess *sakalā*, and *smara*; then one should say the words "to Lakṣmī-Varāha.
At the end, add "aśmarī," which bestows the abode of Viṣṇu; this is remembered as the mantra of Lakṣmī-Varāha. || 7 ||
*Tāram*, *parā*, *bhūti*, *ramā*, the letter *ku*, [the name] *śrījāmadagnyāya*, and a pair of lotuses (*sarojayugmam*);
likewise, *āpaḥ* at the end—this is declared to be the mantra of the noble descendant of Bhṛgu, the bestower of all desires. (8)
One should utter "Tāra," "Parā," "Ramā," "Lakṣmī," "Sītā," and "Rāma," followed by "prasīda" twice and ending with "āpaḥ"; this mantra is the cause of liberation.
O Goddess, one should utter "Tāram," "Mā bhūtimā," "mākhyām," and "Janārdanāya," followed by "viśvam" at the end; this mantra of Manu, O Goddess, is the destroyer of enemies.
One should utter the Tāra, the pair of Parās, and Lakṣmī, followed by "to Viśvaksena";
then the Kūrca and the three lotuses with water—this is very difficult for Vaiṣṇavas to obtain.
One should utter Tāra (Om), Parā (Hrīṃ), Ramā (Śrīṃ), Vaṇī (Aiṃ), Kāma (Klīṃ), and the word Lakṣmī;
then "Vāsudevāya" and "Viśvam. This mantra bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation. || 12 ||
This is the most essential truth, a secret, a mystery, and supremely wonderful;
it is the very essence of all Vaiṣṇavas and must be guarded like one's own womb. (13)
Thus ends the fourth chapter, titled "The Exposition on the Extraction of Vaiṣṇava Mantras," in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*, within the *Śrī Devī Rahasya*.
(p. 23) Now begins the fifth chapter.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Now I shall declare the Great Principle (mahattattva), which bestows the supreme goal of mantras;
by the mere knowledge of which, one’s vidyā is swiftly accomplished.
I shall now declare the Utkīlana-vidhi, the secret of all mantras;
it must not be given to those who are not devotees, nor should it be told to just anyone.
O Goddess, I shall now describe the supreme method for unblocking (utkīlana) the mantras of the Śāktas, especially those of the Śaivas, and the mantras of the Vaiṣṇavas.
First, O Goddess Pārvatī, hear concerning the three-syllabled Bālā;
by uttering the word *vāṇī* at the end three times, there shall be the "unbolting" (*utkīlana*) of the mantra.
O Goddess, for the sake of accomplishing the recitation, one should utter the final *kūṭa* at the beginning twice; this is the supreme method for unbolting the mantra of Tripurabhairavī. (5)
One should extract the first syllable of each of the three peaks;
by reciting the sixteen-syllable Śrī-mantra, there shall be the unbolting (utkīlana) of the mantra.
Now, O Maheśvarī, I shall declare to you the secret of Kālikā;
this supreme vidyā of twenty-two syllables shall be unbarred.
One should first utter *bhadrikā* and at the end recite [or mutter] the three *kālis*;
O Goddess, in this manner, the "unbolting" (*utkīlana*) of the *bhadrakālī-mantra* is accomplished.
At the end of the two *ṭha* syllables, the best of practitioners should place the *parā* mantra and recite it;
O Goddess, this constitutes the "unbolting" (*utkīlana*) of the mantras of Rājamātaṅginī.
At the end of the entire [mantra], O Pārvatī, the reciter should offer everything and perform the recitation;
this shall be the supreme *utkīlana* of the mantra of the illustrious Bhuvaneśvarī. (10)
O Pārvatī, having recited "Vadbūm" and so forth at the beginning, and having muttered the *tāra* (the syllable Om) at the end—this is declared to be the *utkīlana* mantra of Tārā. (11)
O Pārvatī, one should first recite twelve measures (mātrās) of the mantra; this is the supreme method for unlocking the Chinnamastā-mantra. 12.
The practitioner should recite the *vāgbhava* mantra at the beginning and at the end of the forest;
likewise, this shall be the "unbolting" (*utkīlana*) of the King of Mantras, Sumukhī.
O Goddess, one should first utter the Vāgbhava [syllable] and recite the Praṇava at the end of Viśva;
this is the mantra of the Sarasvatī-mantra known as Utkīlana.
O Goddess, one should first recite "viśva" and then recite "madana" at the end of the forest [of the mantra]; this is the mantra for unlocking the heart of the Annapūrṇā-mantra. (15)
O Goddess, one should first offer three lotuses with the mantra of Ramā, and then three at the edge [of the cloth] with the mantra of Mahālakṣmī; this is the mantra known as "unbolting" (utkīlana).
O Maheśvarī, one should first recite *sindhuraṃ* and at the end [recite] *māyā*; this is the mantra for the "unbolting" (*utkīlana*) of the King of Mantras, Śārikā. 17.
O Śivā, having first placed the syllable *vana* at the beginning and the *tāra* (oṃ) at the end, one should recite this mantra of the King of Mantras of Śāradā, which is known as *utkīlana*. || 18 ||
One should recite the seed-syllable of Śakti at the beginning and the Manmatha syllable at the end of the two Ṭha letters;
this is the mantra for the "unbolting" (utkīlana) of the King of Mantras, Indrākṣī. (19)
One should mutter the *praṇava* at the beginning and end of the mantra "mṛdbījam" (OM).
This mantra of Bagalāmukhī bestows the perfection of unsealing (*utkīlana*) other mantras. || 20 ||
At the edge of a urinary stone, the best of practitioners should recite the Praṇava three times;
this mantra of the Turyamantra bestows the fruit of unlocking.
O Maheśvarī, having likewise placed the *tāra* (OM) at the beginning and at the end,
one should recite the mantra for the sake of achieving the *utkīlana* of the Mahārājñī-manu. (22)
O Goddess, one should first recite the syllable *ramā* and then recite the entire mantra at the end;
this is the mantra for the Jvālāmukhī-mantra that is capable of unlocking it. (23)
One should first recite the seed-syllable of the altar (vedībīja) and then mutter the Praṇava at the end of the name;
this mantra of the Bhīḍā-mantra bestows the fruit of "unbolting" (utkīlana). || 24 ||
O Dear One, one should place the Vāgbhava at the end of the Viśva-mantra and recite Kāma at the beginning;
O Goddess, this is the mantra for the "unbolting" (utkīlana) of the Kālarātri-mantra.
One should recite the three *tāra*s at the end and first recite the three *mā*s;
this mantra of the King of Mantras of Bhavānī removes the defect of being "locked. (26)
O Goddess, one should recite the mantra of Vajrayogeśvarī at the end;
this mantra, known as Utkīlana, bestows the fruit of mantra-siddhi. (27)
O Goddess, one should first recite *maṭha*, and likewise *hara* at the end of the two *ṭha*s;
this is the mantra known as *utkīlana* for the king of mantras, Vārāhī. (28)
O Goddess, one should first recite the *harita* mantra and at the end of the universe recite the *vāgbhava*.
O Goddess, this is the mantra of the *siddhalakṣmī* heart-mantra, known by the name *utkīlana*.
O Śivā, one should first recite the *ḍimbabīja* at the edge of the forest;
this is the mantra called *utkīlana* for the *Kulavāgīśvarī-mantra*. (30)
O Goddess, one should first recite the seed-syllable *vīci* and the *tāraka* at the end of the two *ṭha*s;
this is the mantra of the Padmāvatī-hṛdaya known as *utkīlana*.
One should first recite the snare mantra; one should recite the entire [mantra] at the edge of the forest.
This is the king of mantras of Kubjikā, which removes the defect of being pinned down.
O Goddess, at the beginning of the *maṭha*, one should place the *praṇava* of Manu, and at the end of the two *ṭha*s;
one should mutter this mantra, which is the "nail" (*kīla*) of the Gaurī-mantra. (33)
O Supreme Goddess, one should first recite the mantra *viśvam* at the end of the *śakti*;
this is the mantra for the "unbolting" (*utkīlana*) of the King of Mantras, Khecarī. (34)
O Śivā, having first placed the *kūrca* and at the end of the mantra the three pungents (*vyoṣa*), one should recite;
this is the mantra for the "unbolting" (*utkīlana*) of the Nīlasarasvatī mantra. (35)

O Goddess, one should first recite the mantra of Śakti at the beginning and the mantra of Vāsanā at the end; O Goddess, the mantra of Parāśakti is the mantra that removes the defect of the seal (kīla).
The illustrious Bhairava said:
"Now, O Goddess, some of the most excellent mantras of Śiva have been declared by me as 'unlocked' (niṣkīlita), while others, O Pārvatī, are 'locked' (kīlita)."
Maheśvara, Śiva, Rudra, Mahādeva, Karālaka, Vikarāla, Śiva, Śarva, Mṛḍa, and likewise Paśupati. || 38 ||
Pinākin, Giriśa, Bhīma, Kumāra, Lord of the Pramathas, Krodheśa, Īśa, Īśānī, Kapālī, and Krūrabhairava. || 39 ||
Saṃhāra, Īśvara, Bharga, Ruru, and Kālāgnibhairava—
these mantras, O Great Goddess, are free from the defect of being bound.
Merely by means of the preliminary rite (puraścaraṇa), they will swiftly grant the fruit;
or else, O Goddess of the lords of gods, I shall declare the reality that is higher than the highest. 41.
Having heard these Śaiva mantras, keep them most secret.
O Goddess of gods, the wise one should mutter the seed-syllable of each mantra at the beginning of every mantra.
By performing this three times, the practitioner effects the "unbolting" (utkīlana) of the mantra;
[the deities are] Mṛtyuñjaya, Amṛteśāna, Vaṭuka, and Nīlakaṇṭha. (43)
Sadyojāta, Gaṇeśa, Deveśa, Aghorabhairava, Mahākāla, Mahādevī, and Kāmeśvara, O beloved. (44)
O Goddess, these mantras have been pinned down by me for the sake of attaining mantra-siddhi;
O Mistress of the Gods, hear now the supreme method for unpinning these mantras. (45)
O Dear One, by the mere utterance of which the perfection of mantra (*mantrasiddhi*) arises—
one should first recite the heart-seed syllable (*hṛdbīja*) and at the end recite the power-syllable (*śakti*). (46)
O Pārvatī, there is a mantra for the Śrī Mṛtyuñjaya mantra called "unbolting" (utkīlana); one should first recite the Tāra at the beginning and the Śakti at the end of the mantra.
This [mantra] of Amṛteśvara shall remove the defect of "locking" (kīladoṣa). The best of practitioners should recite the Praṇava at the beginning of Parā and at the end. (48)
This mantra of Vaṭuka shall be the destroyer of obstructions;
having first uttered "Hari," one should recite "Śiva" at the end of the mantra. (49)
O Pārvatī, this mantra of Nīlakaṇṭha Durgāśiva is for the purpose of piercing;
the practitioner should recite "Śiva" at the beginning and "Tāra" at the end. (50)
This mantra of Ugratārā is the "nail" (kīla) of the mantra;
O Goddess, the practitioner should recite *māyā* at the end and *śiva* at the beginning. (51)
The mantra of Mahāgaṇapati is named "the Uprooting of the Mind" (manorutkīlanā).
O Goddess, one should first recite the mantra of Viśva, and then the beginning of the mind (mātrādi) for the sake of the fickle one.
This mantra is the "uprooting" (utkīlana) mantra for the Aghorabhairava mantra;
it is traditionally taught that Mahākāla is likewise "unbolted" (niṣkīlita) by these as well.
O Śivā, by the grace of this mantra, all [obstacles] are rendered unbarred;
one should recite the first three syllables from the three peaks of Kāmeśa. (54)
The mantra for the unlocking (utkīlana) of the Śrīvidyā-Śiva-mantra is as follows.
Now, O Pārvatī, I shall indeed declare to you the mantras of the Vaiṣṇavas. 55.
O Īśvarī, for those [mantras] whose pinning (utkīlana) has been performed, one attains Śiva merely by reciting them;
first, one should offer the green [syllable], and at the end, the Praṇava.
This is the mantra for the "unbolting" (utkīlana) of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa;
the practitioner should recite the Vāgbhava syllable at the beginning of the mantra or at its end. (57)
This mantra of the Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa mantra removes the defect of being "locked.
One should recite the pair of *parā* mantras at the end and the *viśva* mantra at the beginning of the primary mantra. (58)
This mantra of Viṣṇu is known as the "unbolting" (utkīlana) mantra;
the best of practitioners should recite the seed-syllable of Smara at the beginning and the seed-syllable of Nṛ at the end.
This mantra of the Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha mantra removes the defect of being "locked. The best of practitioners should recite *tāra* (om) at the end and *ramā* (śrīṃ) at the beginning. (60)

The supreme unbolting (utkīlana) of the Lakṣmī-Varāha mantra occurs when one first recites the "breast-seed" (kucabīja) at the beginning and the pair of lotuses (padmayugma) at the end of the mantra. (61)
O Śivā, for the sake of unblocking the supreme Manu of Bhṛgu, one should recite "Parā" at the end and "Ramā" at the beginning, O Pārvatī, for the sake of accomplishment. (62)
O Pārvatī, the practitioner possesses the mantra of Śrī Sītārāmabhadra, which is a pillar-stealer; he should first recite "Mām" at the end and "Mām" at the beginning.
The mantra of Janārdana, known as *utkīlana*, should be recited by the wise man once; he should utter "Lakṣmī" at the beginning and "Parā" at the end.
O Goddess, the mantra for the uprooting [of obstacles] is the Viśvaksena-mantra; O Goddess, the wise one should recite "Kāma" at the beginning and the "Tāra" (Om) at the end of the mantra. (65)
The mental mantra of Vāsudeva is known as "Utkīlana" (the unbolting).
Thus, O Great Goddess, this is the reality of mantras that bestows the supreme goal;
it has been told out of affection for you, and it must not be disclosed by those who discourse on Brahman.
Thus ends the fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the Method for Unveiling Mantras," in the *Śrīrudrayāmala Tantra*, within the *Śrīdevīrahasya*.
p. 29) Now begins the sixth chapter.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Now, O beloved, I shall describe to you the mantras for reviving [the dead];
by the mere utterance of these, the mantra becomes a bestower of supernatural powers (siddhi).
The wise practitioner should first recite the power (śakti) of the three-syllabled goddess Bālā;
this mantra, known as Sañjīvana, is divine for the accomplishment of the mantra. || 2 ||
First, one should recite the three *parās* of the *jīvana-bhairavī-mantra*;
O Goddess of the Gods, the wise man should then recite the three *kūṭas* of *trikūṭā*. (3)
O Goddess, the second triad of syllables is the life-restorer of the mantra;
it is the perfected lore of Mahāśyāmā, free from all defects. || 4 ||

O Goddess Śivā, this auspicious pair of verses should always be recited by virtuous seekers of liberation who know Brahman for the sake of accomplishing their chanting; O Auspicious One, one should utter them at the end of the mantra.
O Sovereign of practitioners, this Sañjīvana mantra belongs to the heart-mantra of Bhadrakālī;
one should recite the Tāra (Om) and Parā at the end of the recitation and at its commencement.
The revival of the mantra of the goddess Rājamātaṅginī occurs when one first recites the supreme [seed-syllable] of the root-mantra three times.
O Maheśvarī, the supreme revivification of this mantra of Bhuvaneśvarī occurs;
one should recite Kālī and Tāra at the end of this mantra. (8)
O Maheśvarī, this Sañjīvana mantra belongs to the heart of Ugratārā; at the end [of the recitation], one should mutter the root mantra of the vāsanā. (p. 30) 9.
O Goddess, this mantra is the reviver for the heart of Chinnamastā;
one should recite "Parā" at the beginning and likewise "Kāma" at the end.
O beloved Mistress of Mantras, the reciter of the mantra should recite the two *tāra*s at the end of the king of mantras of Sumukhī; this brings about restoration to life. (11)
This *sañjīvana* mantra of Sarasvatī should be used;
one should first recite the *viśva* [syllable] at the end, followed by two *ṭha*s, O Kālikeśvarī. (12)

The practitioner should first recite the Kāmarāja mantra and then the Vāṇī mantra at the end [of the sequence], by which the supreme restoration of life for the two mantras of Annapūrṇā may occur. (13)
O Goddess, for the Mahālakṣmī-mantra, there shall be supreme restoration to life;
the best of practitioners should recite the *kūrca* at the beginning and the *parā* at the end. (14)
O Dear One, the root mantra of Śārikā becomes life-restoring;
one should first recite the Kāmarāja mantra and likewise the Māyā-bīja at the end.
The life-restoring mantra (sañjīvana-manu) of the King of Mantras, Śāradā, is thus remembered;
the practitioner should first recite the seed-syllable of Manmatha and the seed-syllable of Śakti. || 16 ||
O Goddess, the supreme Sañjīvana mantra for the root-mantra of Indrākṣī consists of the seed-syllable *mṛtsnā* and the Praṇava; one should recite this at the edge of the forest.
O Dear One, the supreme reviving power belongs to the Bagalā-mantra-king; one should recite it three times at the end of the root mantra and perform japa. 18.
The supreme Sañjīvana mantra has been determined as part of the Turyā-mantra;
O Maheśvarī, one should recite the seed-syllable of Fire at the end and Śakti at the beginning. 19.
O Maheśvarī, this mantra of the Queen is remembered as one that brings back to life; one should recite the *kūrca* at the beginning and the *turaga* at the end.
This is the mantra named Sañjīvana for the heart of Jvālāmukhī;
one should recite the Vāgbhava syllable at the beginning of the Praṇava and the Supreme Goddess (Parā) at the end of the two Ṭha syllables.
This is the *sañjīvana* mantra of the *Bhīḍābhagavatī* mantra; the best of practitioners should recite *tāra* at the end and *ramā* at the beginning. (p. 31) [Kh: after that] || 22 ||

The *sañjīvana* mantra of Gaṇeśvarī Kālarātri is as follows: the best of practitioners should first utter the *kūrca* (hūṃ) and at the end of "Hara" (ha), he should recite "mām" (me). O Pārvatī, thus should the practitioner recite it.
For the root mantra of Bhavānī, there shall be the supreme *sañjīvana* (revitalization):
having uttered *māyā*, O Goddess of gods, three times at the beginning and likewise three times at the end.
O Goddess, the *sañjīvana* mantra is the *manu* of Vajrayoginī;
O Pārvatī, the Kaulika should recite *maṭha* at the end and *maṭha* at the beginning. (25)
This mantra of Dhūmravārāhī is named Sañjīvana;
one should recite the Manmatha [seed-syllable] at the beginning and at the end of the root-mantra, which is green in color. (26)
This *sañjīvana* mantra belongs to the *siddhalakṣmī* mantra;
the best of practitioners should recite it with *kāṅkṣā* at the beginning and *ramā* at the end. (27)
O Goddess, there would be the restoration of life through the mantra of Kulavāgīśvarī;
O Mahādevī, O Śivā, one should recite *Kāma* at the beginning and *Ramā* at the end.
This mind-animating [mantra] is remembered as being within the heart of Padmāvatī;
one should recite the supreme [syllable] preceded by the Praṇava at the end of the lotus and at the beginning of the snare. || 29 ||
This mantra is called the "Life" (jīvana) of the root-mantra of Kubjikā;
one should recite Vāhlīka preceded by the Praṇava at the beginning, and Śiva at the end of the root-mantra.
This mantra of Gaurī is known as Sañjīvanaka;
O Pārvatī, the practitioner should recite the Viśva-mantra at the beginning and the Kūṭa-mantra at the end.
O Śivā, for the Khecarī-mantrarāja there is the Sañjīvana [vidyā];
the best of mantra-practitioners should recite Vāṇī at the beginning and Parā at the end.
O Goddess, there may be restoration to life through the mantra of Nīlāsarasvatī; O Śivā, one should recite the Vāgbhava syllable at the beginning of the Praṇava and the Kāma syllable at the end.
This is remembered as the *sañjīvana* (reviving) mantra of the *parāśakti-mantra*.
Now, O Maheśvarī, [I shall describe] the *niṣkīla* (unimpeded) mantras of Śiva. (34) p. 32)
I shall declare to you the supreme secret reality that brings about revival;
the practitioner of mantra should recite the Tāra-mantra separately at the end of each root mantra. (35)
O Dear One, this shall be the reviving mantra for all Śaiva mantras;
nevertheless, I shall now declare the reviving mantras for those that have been pinned down (kīlita).
By the mere performance of these means, the root-vidyā is quickly accomplished;
the practitioner should first recite the pair of syllables that constitute the name of the Sun. (37)
This mantra, known as Sañjīvana, belongs to the Mṛtyuñjaya-mantra;
the leader of mantra-practitioners should recite "Viśva" at the beginning and "Viśva" at the end. (38)
The mantra of Amṛteśvara shall be the supreme means of restoration to life;
O Pārvatī, the practitioner should recite "Vaṭukāya" at the beginning of the invocation. (39)
This rare mantra of Sañjīvana for Vaṭuka has been proclaimed; O one honored by practitioners, one should recite "Śivam" preceded by the Praṇava at the beginning.
The mantra known as Sañjīvana belongs to the Śrī Nīlakaṇṭha mantra; having uttered it three times at the beginning of Parā, the wise practitioner should recite it at the commencement of his japa.
This *sañjīvana* mantra is known as the *sadyojāta-manu*;
O Goddess, having uttered "Śiva" twice at the end, one should recite it from the beginning of the recitation.
O Pārvatī, the practitioner should first recite the seed-syllables of the vajra at the beginning of the mantra of Mahāgaṇapati, which is known as the Sañjīvana-mantra.
O Pārvatī, this mantra of Mahākāla, which belongs to Aghoradeva, is known as Sañjīvana; it is the king of mantras, free from all defects. (44)
Merely by its utterance, mantras are always accomplished.
O Goddess of the Gods, one should utter the second syllable from among the three peaks (kūṭas). 45.
O Śivā, by reciting the mantra of Kāmeśa, one attains restoration to life;
now, indeed, I shall declare the restoration of life for the mantras of the Vaiṣṇavas.
O Goddess, by reciting this, the practitioner becomes like Bhairava himself.
O Pārvatī, the practitioner should recite the green [syllable] at the end of the root mantra. (47)
The *sañjīvana* [mantra] for the *lakṣmīnārāyaṇa-manu* is supreme;
the practitioner should recite the *vāgbhava* [syllable] either at the end of the mantra or at its beginning. (48)
O Goddess, the Sañjīvana mantra is known as the mantra of Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa;
the best of practitioners should recite the Praṇava at the end of the universe (the mantra). 49.
O Goddess, this mantra of Viṣṇu is known as Sañjīvana; O restless one, one should first recite the seed-syllable of man (nṛ-bīja) and then the Praṇava.
The mantra of Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha known as Sañjīvana should be recited while filled with bliss, having uttered the word "Ramā" three times at the end.
The Sañjīvana mantra is remembered as belonging to the Lakṣmī-Varāha mantra;
O Pārvatī, one should first recite the supreme pair (the two syllables) of this king of mantras.
The mantra of the most excellent Bhārgava Manu is known as Sañjīvana.
O Goddess, one should recite the Praṇava at the end of the mantra and the entire [mantra] beginning with Tārā.
O Pārvatī, the Sañjīvana mantra of the sage Manu is for the Śrī Sītārāma mantra;
the practitioner of mantras should recite "Viśva" at the beginning and "Parā" at the end.
This mantra of Janārdana is remembered as a life-restorer; the practitioner should recite it with "Parā" at the beginning and "Parā" at the end, together with the Tārā. || 55 ||
This is the Sañjīvana mantra for the Viśvaksena-mantra;
the wise one should recite "Ramā" at the beginning and "Ramā" at the end during the initial recitation. (56)
This Manu is the life-restorer for the mind of Śrī Lakṣmī-Vāsudeva;
thus, this entire essence of mantra, a wonderful secret and quintessence,
has been declared by me out of devotion to you, yet it must be guarded like one's own private birth.
Thus ends the sixth chapter, titled "The Description of the Method for Reviving Mantras," in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*, within the *Śrī Devī Rahasya*.
p. 34) Now begins the seventh chapter.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
O Śivā, I shall now describe the lore that removes curses;
listen to it, for in the Kali age all mantras have become devoid of luster. 1.
She who is Bhairavī is indeed Tripurasundarī;
she who is Tripurā is Kālī, and she who is Śyāmā is remembered as Parā. (2)
O young girl, release Tāra, Parā, and Ramā from Śiva’s curse;
release Hara from the water, for you are remembered as the remover of the curse of the young girls.
O Speech, O Autumn, O Smara, release, release [me] from Rudra’s curse!
O Goddess, the two *ṭha*s in the word *turaga* effect liberation from Bhairavī’s curse. (4)
One should extract the first peak-syllable consisting of the three seed-syllables of Bālā, the Tāra, Parā,
and Ramā, followed by "liberate from the curse of Sadāśiva"— thus one should utter the pair.
One should recite the "Śaratkūṭa" at the end; this is the knowledge that removes curses.
This supreme Śyāmā-vidyā consists of twenty-two syllables and is the highest.
Although the Mahāśrīṣoḍaśī-vidyā is free from all defects,
nevertheless I shall proclaim this difficult-to-attain lore which removes curses.
Just as the mantra of the twenty-two-syllable goddess is indeed accomplished:
Kālī, the Kūrca (hum), the supreme name, and likewise Dakṣiṇe Kālike. (8)
O Goddess, having uttered the curse of Vasiṣṭha, release the two;
Kālī, Kūrca, and Parā—this [mantra] consisting of these three syllables shall be the remover of the curse. || 9 ||
O Kālī, O Bhīmā, O Bhadrakālī on the shore of Śiva’s [abode], O Bhīmā—release the curse! This is the *yugmāpa* vidyā that removes curses. (10)
"O Mātaṅgī, release the curse of Kāla upon Tārā and Parā;
this mantra is a remover of curses for the horse at the edge of the water. (11)
Liberate both Māyā and the curse of Bhairava from the hem of the garment;
this Vidyā, belonging to Bhuvaneśvarī, is the remover of curses. (12)
"Oṃ, Kāminī, Māyā! Release [her] from the curse of Brahmā!
Release her from the waters of Tārā! This is the lore that removes curses. (13)

Release me from latent impressions, from the lotus, from illusion, and from the curse of Rudra; release me, O Waters, from what has been described by me as the liberation from the mark of Chinnamastā. 14.
The Vāgbhava, the Kāmarāja, and the Śiva-śāpa—liberate [her]. This supreme Nīrami-vidyā is the foremost remover of curses. || 15 ||

One should utter the Praṇava, the Vāsanā, and the Tāra, followed by "Sarasvati," then "quickly release me from the curse of Durvāsas," and finally the two syllables "Ṭhaḥ Ṭhaḥ" for the release from the curse. 16.
Tāram, Parām, Annapūrṇe, Vimocaya Śivaśāpam;
Kūrcam, Hara, Vanam—O Goddess, this is the Vidyā that removes curses. (17)
Tāraṃ Ramā Mahālakṣmi, release [him] from Viṣṇu’s curse; O Īśānī, [release] the horse from the water. This is the vidyā that removes curses. 18.
O Goddess, release Tāra, Sindhura, Śārikā, and Brahmalāñchana; this knowledge, which removes the curse, consists of the two syllables "moca" and "ya. (19)
Tāra, Māyā, and Śāradā—liberate [me] from the curse of Viṣṇu.
O Great Goddess, this Vidyā, consisting of Śakti and Water, is the remover of curses. (20)
*Tā-raṃ*, *vāṇī*, *śarad-kāmaṃ*, *indrākṣi*, *brahma-lāñchanam*—release these two, and *āpaḥ*; this is the knowledge that removes the curse. (21)
O Bagalā, [the mantra] beginning with *tāram*, *mṛtsnām*, and "release from the curse of Rudra"—this knowledge, O Goddess, consisting of *tāram*, *mṛdam*, and *vanam*, removes curses. (22)
*Tāraṃ* and *tārām*, and on the fourth [syllable], *śivaśāpaṃ vimocaya*; *tārakam* and two *ṭha*s, O Goddess—this is the Vidyā that removes the curse. (23)

*Tāraṃ vahniṃ śaradrājñi brahmaśāpaṃ vimocaya | vimocaya vanaṃ devi vidyeyaṃ śāpahāriṇī || 24 ||* O Queen of Autumn, [beginning with] *Tāra*, *Vahni*, and *Śaradrājñi*, release [us] from the curse of Brahmā! O Goddess, release the forest; this is the lore that removes curses.
Tāra, Ramā, Parā, Jvālāmukhī, Bhairavalāñchana, Kūrca, and Nīra—O Great Goddess, this is the Vidyā that removes curses. (25)
Tāraṃ parāṃ ramāṃ bhīḍe, release me from the curse of Dhruva;
O Great Goddess, release me from the waters—this is the vidyā that removes curses.
*Tāram*, *vāṇīm*, *ḍimbam*, *kālarātrim*, and *śivasya*;
*śāpam*, *mocaya*, and *nīram*—this is the lore (*vidyā*) that removes curses. (27)
Tāraṃ Ramāṃ Ramāṃ Tāraṃ; O Goddess, release [me] from the curse of Rudra! Kūrcaṃ Haraṃ Vanaṃ—this is the lore that removes curses. || 28 ||
One should extract the mantra: Tāraṃ parāṃ parāṃ tāraṃ Vajrayogini.
This vidyā, which releases one from the curse of Śiva, is the remover of curses. (29)
O Vārāhī, release Tāra, Ramā, and Nāradāṅka;
O Great Goddess, this is the lore that removes the curse, along with Maṭha and Nīra.
Tāra, Ramā, Siddhalakṣmī—liberate [me] from the curse of the Siddhas!
Vāṇī, Śarad, Smara, Nīra—this is the knowledge that removes curses. (31)
Tāraṃ, Vyoṣaṃ, Ramā, Kāṅkṣā, Kulavāgīśvarī, Sphuṭa, Śivaśāpaṃ, Muñca, and Āpaḥ—this is the vidyā that removes curses. || 32 ||
*Tāram*, *māyā*, *padmam*, *padmāvati*, likewise *hareḥ*, the pair *śāpam muñca*, and *nīram*—this is the vidyā that removes curses. (33)
Tāraṃ, Māyā, and Kubjikā—O Great Goddess, at the end of the water [mantra], this vidyā releases one from the curse of Jahnu; it is the remover of curses. (34)
*Tāraṃ śivaṃ gauri bhṛgoḥ śāpaṃ mocaya mocaya* (O Gaurī, [you who are] the *tāra* and Śiva, release me from the curse of Bhṛgu, release me!).
O Goddess, this mantra, ending with *nīram*, is the knowledge that removes curses. (35)

this is the lore that removes the curse. *Tāraṃ* is the syllable *oṃ*, *vāṇī* is speech, and *nīla* refers to the color blue—this is Sarasvatī, whose form is like that of Hari. *Parā* is the Supreme Goddess, O Great Queen; Release the waters at the end of Manu's age; this knowledge is the remover of the curse.
O Tārā, O Śakti, O Supreme Power, release [me] from the curse of Śiva;
release me, like the water of autumn! This is the Vidyā that removes the curse.
Now, O Maheśvarī, I shall declare for you the all-encompassing vidyā that removes the curse of Śaiva mantras that have been rendered ineffective (kīlita). || 39 ||
Listen to the vidyā that removes curses from mantras that have become blocked;
by the mere utterance of which, even a wicked mantra becomes effective. (40)
Tāra, Parā, Ramā, Vāṇī, Kāma, Śakti, and Sadāśiva—O Śiva, release [her] from the curse; this is the knowledge that removes the curse. || 41 ||
*Tāram*, *hṛjjam*, *śarad-rudra-śāpam*, *mocaya mocaya*;
*śara-dhṛj-jam* and *tāram*—this is the vidyā that removes the curse. (42)
Then [say] "Tāram," and then "O Amṛteśāna, release me from the curse of Śiva";
with "Tāram" at the end, this mantra is the remover of curses. (43)
Tāra, Parā, and Vaṭuka—release [him] from the curse of Brahmā. This mantra, consisting of the two [syllables] and the Devīpraṇava, is the destroyer of curses. 44.
"O Tārā and Nīlakaṇṭhā, release the mark of Durvāsas!
O Mahādevī, release the waters! This is the vidyā that removes curses. (45)
The syllable *tāram*, the supreme luster, the syllable *tāram*, the sound of the newborn, and the two *ṭha*s—O Goddess, release [me]; this is the knowledge that removes curses. (46)
O Tārā, O Śivā, O Gaṇeśānā, release me from the curse of Rudra!
O Mahādevī, at the end of the forest [of worldly existence], this is the lore that removes the curse. (47)
O Tāra, O primordial syllable, O oblation, O God, O Lord of the Svacchanda!
Release [me] from the curse of Śiva; may this Vidyā be the remover of the curse. 48.
O Goddess, [the mantra] consisting of Tāra, Kūrca, Parā, Mahākāla, and the Vidhicchala, followed by the two 'Mocaya' and the letter 'Pa', is this Vidyā that removes curses. (49)
Vāgbhava, Kāma-śakti, and Bhairavāṅka—liberate [me]! This Vidyā, consisting of Tāra, Parā, and the primordial seed-syllable, removes all curses. (50)
Now, O Pārvatī, listen with respect to the Vaiṣṇava mantras, which instantly remove curses, since through them the perfection of the mantra is attained. (51)
"Tāram, Ramām, and Lakṣmī—this is the secret of Nārāyaṇa and Śiva;
O Moca, this twofold mantra is a knowledge that removes curses. (52)
*Tāraṃ* is *Śakti*, the supreme; *tāraṃ* is the deception of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa and Brahmā.
O Great Goddess, release me from this! This is the knowledge that removes curses. (53)
Tāraṃ parāṃ ramāṃ viṣṇo, vimocaya rudraśāpam; Tāraṃ with two Ṭhas at the end—this is the Vidyā that removes the curse. (54)
*Tāra*, *parā*, the seed-syllable of man (*nṛbīja*), *narasiṃha*, and the face of Śiva (*śivacchala*);
with the two oceans at the end—this is the Vidyā that removes curses. || 55 ||
"Tāram, Ramām, and Lakṣmī; O Varāha, O you marked by Hari! Release the two at the end with 'āpaḥ'—this is the vidyā that removes curses. (56)
*Tāram*, *kūrcam*, *bhārgava*, and "liberate from Śukra’s curse"—*turagam*, *ṭha* twice; O Goddess, this is the vidyā that removes curses. (57)
Tāraṃ, Ramāṃ, Rāmabhadra, and Guruśāpa-vimocaya;
with Haraṃ and two Ṭha-s at the end—this is the vidyā that removes curses. (58)
*Tāraṃ ramā ramā tāraṃ*—O Janārdana, this is the deception of Brahmā.

"O Great Goddess, release the two waters; this is the knowledge that removes the curse. (59) "Oṃ, Parā, Ramā, Oṃ, Viṣvaksena, followed by the mantra 'manu'—release the two waters; this is the knowledge that removes the curse. (60)
*Tāraṃ ramā ramā lakṣmīvāsudeva śivacchalam | mocaya dvayam āpaś ca*—this is the vidyā that removes curses. (61)
Thus, O Īśānī, this is the supreme reality, the secret, the most excellent essence; it is the hidden treasure of all, to be guarded with special care.
Thus ends the seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Extraction of the Śāpaharī Vidyā," in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*, within the *Śrī Devī Rahasya*.
Now begins the eighth chapter.
The venerable Bhairava said:
Now I shall describe the supreme practice of recitation (japasādhana), by the mere accomplishment of which the attainment of mantra-perfection (mantrasiddhi) arises. || 1 ||
If Śrīvidyā is obtained through the grace of the Guru's feet, one is capable of accomplishing it simply through worship and recitation. (2)
O Goddess, eloquent, wealthy, victorious, heroic, and an enjoyer of pleasures in this world, such a king shall become a practitioner in the hereafter who resembles Bhairava himself.
On an auspicious day and under a favorable constellation, having performed his morning rites and brought his own preceptor to his home, he bowed at the preceptor's feet, O Maheśvarī. (4)
O Śivā, having washed the Śrīcakra in the place of worship, one should worship it;
one should draw a triangle with vermilion and install the Guru there.
O Goddess, one should utter *tāram*, the three *śivas*, and the word for the *guru*;
at the end of *viśvam*, O Great Goddess, is this supreme mantra of the *guru*. (6)
With this root mantra, O Goddess Pārvatī, the wise one should worship the Guru together with the Mātṛkās in their respective places.
O Goddess, one should satisfy the Guru there with fragrances, unbroken grains, flowers, and other substances, as well as with auspicious garments, ritual fees (dakṣiṇā), and the nectar of the Kula.
Then, having received that command upon his head for the purpose of recitation,
O Great Goddess, the excellent practitioner, at sunrise in the morning, should bow to his guru.
Facing the east and bowing down,
the practitioner, O Goddess, having performed the recitation of Śiva and Śakti separately, should recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times.
Then, one should recite the six-limbed mantra ten times for every one hundred recitations of the root mantra;
thereafter, O Goddess, the practitioner of mantra should recite the meters, the sages, and the mantras.
Then, O Goddess, having performed the recitation (japa), one should perform the fire-oblation (homa) with a tenth part [of that number];
having offered libations (tarpaṇa) with a tenth part, one should perform the ritual purification (mārjana) with a tenth part of that.
Having fed [the brahmins], the perfection of the recitation (japa) shall then occur through a tenth part [of that number].
O Maheśvarī, success comes from recitation; success comes from recitation; success comes from recitation! || 13 ||
O Śivā, such perfection as that which belongs to practitioners of mantra through the recitation of the *pārāyaṇa* does not arise from praise, nor from worship, nor from meditation.
The Goddess said:
O Blessed One, O Supreme Lord, out of a desire for the welfare of practitioners, tell me of the recitation of the *pārāyaṇa*, if I am dear to you. (15)
The illustrious Bhairava said:
O Goddess, I shall declare the *pārāyaṇa* for the sake of attaining the fruit of the recitation of the Vidyā.
By means of which the mantra-practitioner becomes endowed with siddhi and resembles Bhairava himself. || 16 ||
O beloved, there are countless renowned recitations of the Pārāyaṇa;
