Having worshipped with: *Namaḥ hrīṃ śrīṃ kālāgnaye namaḥ*, *hrīṃ śrīṃ suptabhairavāya namaḥ*, *hrīṃ śrīṃ unmattabhairavāya namaḥ*; [one should worship] in the hexagon: *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ jayāyai namaḥ*, *oṃ vijayāyai namaḥ*, *oṃ kāntyai namaḥ*, *oṃ ratyai namaḥ*, *oṃ prītyai namaḥ*, *oṃ manonmanāyai namaḥ*.
Having worshipped with flowers, saying "Oṃ namaḥ," one then worships within the triangle, saying: "Oṃ gāṃ, obeisance to Gaṅgā; oṃ yāṃ, obeisance to Yamunā;

oṃ saṃ, obeisance to Sarasvatī. Then, having worshipped in the *bindu* with "Oṃ [mūla-mantra], obeisance to Mahāmāyā," one should thus fully worship and visualize the Śrī Devī there in the form of light, as if she were the *yantra* itself, using cow's ghee.

One should perform worship. Therein, one should worship Bhairava and Bhairavī. Therein, one should worship Vaṭuka along with his Śakti. When the Bhairava Tantra is active, all castes are twice-born; when the Bhairava Tantra has ceased, all castes remain distinct. Having worshipped nine maidens right there—
On the left is a woman skilled in dalliance; on the right is a bowl of wine, and in front are the hand-gestures (mudrās) of chickpeas and cakes,
the warm purification of a pig, a lute, a sweet and melodious stringed instrument, a true guru, and excellent discourses.
The Left-hand Practice (vāmācāra) [or Kaula], which is supremely profound, is inaccessible even to yogins. || 8 ||
Having drunk again and again, and drinking until the consciousness consisting of mind [arises],
if there should be any modification therein, that drinking is like the killing of a Brahmin.
The practitioner, intent on drinking honey-wine, should satisfy the Śakti with sexual union;
he should gratify the Goddess with his semen and satisfy the Śakti with the drink. 10.
One should drink the wine that is the remnant of Śakti, and chew the food that is the remnant of Vīra;
joined with the five "M"s, one should fashion the mandala of the Śrīcakra.
O Śivā, the practitioner, having gratified the other practitioners with devotion through food and drink,
and having gratified his chosen deity with sweet foods and chewables, [should proceed].
One should worship one's own guru with devotion and satisfy him to the utmost according to one's capacity;
having gratified one's own guru with sacrificial fees and prostrations. (13)
Having received that command upon his head— which grants perfection in the daily rites—

he performed them as follows: having worshipped the practitioners there, meditated upon himself as Ānandabhairava, and become filled with supreme bliss, he dismissed the Goddess together with Śiva by means of the *saṃhāramudrā*, prostrating himself like a staff.
One should prostrate.
Thus, the best of practitioners should conceal this secret manual, which consists of both prose and verse, and is enriched with the essence of all the Āgamas. (14)
Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, titled "The Exposition of the Method of Purification," in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*, within the *Śrī Devī Rahasya*.
83) Now begins the nineteenth chapter.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Now, O Goddess, O Maheśvarī, I shall describe the origin of the gods,
by the mere hearing of which one obtains the fruit of initiation.
While the ocean, the best of seas, the Milky Ocean, was being churned,
the goddess Surā was born there, assuming the form of a young maiden.
Naked, resembling the fire of cosmic destruction, her face radiant with a laugh;
divine, possessing eighteen arms, and likewise holding nine jars.
Likewise, she holds a new vessel, her eyes are reddened with wine,
she is richly adorned with various flowers, her hair is loose, and she has three eyes.
Adorned with armlets shining with various jewels and graced by strings of pearl necklaces,
she is enriched by the beauty of red-gemmed finger-rings and endowed with high, full breasts.
Her hips are encircled by a girdle inlaid with various jewels;
seated upon a jeweled lion-throne, she bestows supreme bliss.
Upon seeing her, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara, along with the gods, asuras, and gandharvas, together with Īśvara and Sadāśiva, praised the Goddess.
Then the gods, with serene countenances and intent upon granting boons,
first gave him a divine vessel filled with the essence of bliss.
O Goddess of the gods, having bowed to Sadāśiva, he took up the vessel;
from the vessel a drop fell upon the earth, and from that the guḍa-creeper was born.

From the falling of the drops, grains were produced; from them, by the thousands, arose various kinds of sugarcane, khadira trees, the three pungents (tryūṣaṇa), and white [substances] and so forth. (10)
O Maheśvarī, the betel nut and the betel vine flow [together];
when combined with this, it is called Gauḍī, which bestows the fruit of all goals.
Then, O auspicious one, the gods offered the supreme vessel to the Lord;
from that vessel, a drop fell upon the earth, and from it the *ahivallarī* creeper was born.
O Great Goddess, from even the falling drops [of that juice], thousands of varieties of grapes, such as the *mṛdvīkā* and others, were born—most purifying indeed. (13)
The honeyed [liquor], proclaimed as the bestower of all perfections in the practice of the Great Vidyā,
was then offered by her to Rudra in a supreme vessel filled with nectar. || 14 ||
A drop fell from the vessel onto the earth, and from it the various kinds of wheat were born;
from its grains, O venerable one, the various species of grain indeed arose.
O Goddess, that which is made from flour is called *surā*, the bestower of supreme bliss;
then she gave that supreme vessel to the powerful Viṣṇu.
O Dear One, a drop fell from the vessel onto the earth, and from that, consciousness was born;
O Goddess of Gods, even from its particles arose gold and other such substances.
And many other varieties have arisen that increase passion;
however, she who is called Vijayā by me is indeed Vaiṣṇavī, the bestower of the supreme goal.
Between consciousness and wine, consciousness alone is more important;
therefore, the venerable Surā gave the supreme vessel to the Supreme Lord (Parameṣṭhin). 19.
A drop fell from the vessel onto the earth and quickly became a *parūṣaka* tree;
from its seeds, too, were born various varieties such as those with honey-like flavor.
O Īśānī, this supreme drink was declared to be common to all;
then she gave the supreme vessel, filled with nectar, to Indra.
(85) A drop fell from the vessel onto the earth, and from that the nutmeg tree was born;
even from its seeds were produced the various species such as the *āmalaka* and others. (22)
That divine beverage is proclaimed to be a supreme elixir (rasāyana);
then the goddess Girijā gave that excellent vessel to her preceptor.
A drop fell from the vessel onto the earth; from that, O Śivā, the guḍapuṣpa was born, and from its fragments arose varieties such as the coconut fruit and others.
O Goddess of the gods, this drink is indeed the supreme elixir;
then she gave Śukra a supreme vessel filled with nectar.
A drop fell from the vessel onto the earth, and from it were born the date-palm trees;
even from its seeds were produced various species, such as the bhādāmaka and others.
That drink was also declared to be divine, a cause of satisfaction;
then he gave the supreme vessel once each to the Sun and the Moon.
A drop fell from the vessel onto the earth, and from it was born the Sañjīvana herb;
O Śivā, even from its fragments various medicinal plants were produced.
That drink is declared to be supreme and common to all;
O Goddess, it bestows the fruit of all goals and grants all eloquence. (29)
Having bestowed that divine nectar, O Goddess, the goddess Surā vanished there;
they all, O Supreme Lady, were filled solely with the singular bliss of wine.
The gods, beginning with Sadāśiva, granted a boon to the goddesses:
"Those who drink the supreme beverage, which is the cause of supreme bliss [shall be blessed]. (31)
All those who worship Śivā, except for liquor made from molasses (gauḍī) and that made from honey (mādhvī), go to the supreme, eternal, and imperishable state. || 32 ||
Whether he be Śiva, Nārāyaṇa, or Rudra, such a person shall become an inhabitant of hell;
O Goddess, one who is uninitiated is a bound soul (paśu), and even one who is initiated remains a bound soul if he is an asura.
Therefore, having worshipped Surā to Śiva during the ritual of worship, the best of Vaiṣṇavas should drink Gauḍī, Mādhvī, Paiṣṭī, and the excellent Āsava. (34)
And all auspicious drinks [are accepted], each subsequent one in the absence of the preceding;
this is the supreme reality, the secret of the Kaulikas, the entire essence of Ānandeśvara, which should be guarded like one's own womb. (35)
Thus ends the nineteenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Origin of the Gods," in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*, within the *Śrī Devī Rahasya*.
Now begins the twentieth chapter.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Now, O Goddess, O Sovereign, I shall describe the salutation to the vessel (pātravandana),
at which time the vessel of bliss is worshipped by the gods.
O Supreme Goddess, during the worship, one should honor the vessel filled with bliss given by the Guru and then bow to it with the head.
It is drenched by the nectar of the moon shining from the crest of the glorious Bhairava, and it is worshipped by the hosts of Kṣetrādhīśvara, Yoginīs, and Mahāsiddhas.

I bow to this great-souled vessel that brings about bliss, the manifest nectar of the three sections, the first glorious one held in the lotus-hand, which bestows purity. [This is your vessel, O Indra;
drink the Soma with its wealth, O Śatakratu.]
Full is the vessel of the intoxicating sweet mead, which all the gods indeed desire.
This supreme nectar, produced from the *idam* vessel,
I offer into the supreme fire, the carrier (*vahni*), who is of the nature of Śiva.
I drink this purifying nectar, the medicine for existence,
which was proclaimed by Bhairava as the cause for severing the bonds of the bound soul.
Because consciousness has autonomy as its essence, because it consists of bliss,
and because all entities are composed of that [consciousness], entities are submerged within the aesthetic flavor (rasa).
The innate essence is drunk by oneself for the sake of expanding one's own freedom; therefore, I drink this fullness of "I-ness," which is the nature of nectar.

"Situated in the triangle which is one's own self, possessing a radiance equal to ten million suns, and having the form of consciousness in the shape of Kuṇḍalinī— one should offer the substance accompanied by the mantra. [This reading is an addition found in manuscript *gh* and has been omitted.]
This golden vessel was brought by me, and it was filled with drinks and other offerings by my beloved;
moreover, she gazed upon it joyfully with her eyes like trembling red lotuses.
Having placed in my own left hand the vessel of pure nectar purified by its own essence, I now worship this second vessel, which increases sole bliss. || 4 ||
It is endowed with the entire collection of the arts of all traditions, illuminated by curiosity, and served by Candra, Upendra, Mahendra, Śambhu, Varuṇa, Brahmā, and others;
it is always meditated upon by hosts of gods and groups of sages seeking liberation.
Now I salute the third vessel, which is capable of awakening one's own self. || 5 ||
Wine, which brings forth the essence of fish, is filled by Hari, Hara, Brahmā, and the others;
it is devoted to the practices of mudrā, sexual union, and ritual action, and is the basis for salty, sour, and bitter flavors;
it is thoroughly purified by the placement of the eight Ācāryas, the Siddhas, Bhairava, and the Kalās.
May he protect us; we bow to the fourth vessel, which is the abode of the reality of the five aspects.
Upon the base, which is the circle of the king of serpents, the vessel is the orb of the earth;
the wine is the water of the seven oceans, and the meat consists of the eight elephants of the quarters.
Thus, worshipping Bhairava daily with clusters of stars as unbroken offerings, he was served by the hosts of gods and demons headed by Āditya, who acted as his obedient servants and attendants.
It brings about the arising of supreme bliss through the beautiful, stainless, and auspicious throne with its parasol;
it is delightful, provides a kingdom, and always bestows happiness.

We bow to the sixth vessel, which bestows the imperial sovereignty of union (sāyujya), dispels the darkness born of various diseases, destroys rebirth, and is most dear to the illustrious Bhairava and Bhairavī. || 8 ||
Beyond waking, dreaming, deep sleep, and the fourth state, it bestows the witness-consciousness;
it is pervaded by the particles of light of lightning, the sun, fire, the moon, and the rainbow.
May she who dwells between the *iḍā* and *piṅgalā*, the triple-coiled one whose excellent *kuṇḍalinī* moves upward—
may she protect us, she who is the vessel for awakening and who bestows youthful bliss through the filling of the seventh crucible.
Indeed, by keeping the sword, the bowl, the cloth-fragment, the sandals, the sectarian mark, and the pill— belonging to Sarasvatī—
around one's neck, the power of speech, valor, and the activities of an enemy residing within the body are destroyed.
It is the cause,
the fulfiller of desires, the stabilizer of the mind, the subduer, and the attractor of the women of the world.
And I worship the eighth vessel, which brings about the eight supernatural powers and is maturely gracious.
It bestows the state of Sadāśiva which grants all bliss, provides the attainment of all goals,
brings about imperial sovereignty, grants all happiness, and destroys ignorance;
it increases longevity, beauty, and fame, and cuts through the delusion of saṃsāra.
I worship the ninth [form], the vessel consisting of a hundred thousand qualities, possessed of mature majesty. || 11 ||
I bow down to the tenth vessel, which is especially difficult to obtain and purifying even for the gods Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa.
I bow to the eleventh vessel, which destroys evil, bestows peace and auspiciousness, is divine, sweet, and an abode of happiness, attained through the bliss of service to the Guru. (13)
Having placed the vessel in his hand, the practitioner of mantra shall happily attain all accomplishments;
having enjoyed prosperity in this world, he shall become Bhairava at the end of his body.
May all the deities residing in the body, the elephant-faced ones, the lords of the sacred fields (kṣetrapālas), the Bhairavas, the Yoginīs, the Vaṭukas,
the Yakṣas, the Pitṛs, the Paiśācas, the servants (ceṭakas),
and others who move on earth or in the sky— the Vetālas, Bhūtas, and Grahas— be satisfied by this son of noble family (kulaputraka).
They drink the beverage together with the lamp and the sacrificial oblation (caru), which contains honey. || 15 ||
In his hand is a rosary, in his mouth wine, and on his left side is the very tender Rāmā;
in his heart is the youthful Tripurā—[thus he dwells] in every house as a hall of sacrifice.
The vessel is the vessel of Bhairava; the lineage is the lineage of the sandals of Śrīnātha.
The scripture is the scripture of consciousness; knowledge is the knowledge that awakens one to reality.
(17) On the left is the woman, skilled in dalliance; on the right is the vessel of wine; in front are the mudrās, chickpeas, and cakes.
The purification of a pig is by heat.
On the shoulder [is] the lute with its strings; the lute is sweet and melodious, as is the excellent discourse of the true Guru. And the Kaula path is most profound.
It is inaccessible even to yogins. || 18 ||
I am devoted to the enjoyment and worship of wine, meat, and women; I am honored by the undertaking of the manifold paths of the Kula;
I am averse to the vulgar folk; I have taken refuge in Bhairavī; I am intent upon the feet of the Guru; I am Bhairava; I am Śiva. (19)
The bowl is in my hand, the hymn of praise is in my mouth, and bliss is within my heart;
devotion to the lotus feet of the Guru—what refuge could there be beyond this? (20)
With a single dry piece of bread, I drink from a jar; with salted radish, I suddenly drink from a pond.
Having tasted a piece of the head of a mottled Rohita fish, I drink from the Gaṅgā along with the Yamunā.
By Sāgara. || 21 ||

In the left hand is Candramukhī, and in the mouth is the vessel of wine; with the lotus-hand [held] at the head, the mind is the locus for meditation on the Blessed Lady and the contemplation of the venerable Guru;
on the tongue is the practice of recitation—those virtuous ones who, through the practice of the Kaula lineage, constantly drink this transformation.
For you, enjoyment and liberation have become most delicious. || 22 ||
Having drunk again and again, and drinking yet more until one falls to the ground,
and rising once more to drink, there is no further rebirth.
In the fire of my own self, kindled by the oblations of dharma and adharma, I constantly offer the functions of the senses with the mind as the ladle, by way of the path of the *suṣumṇā*. 24.
Holding the ladle of *unmanī* with my hands of light and space,
I offer into the fire that which is filled with the oil of the portions of merit and demerit.
As long as the gaze does not waver and as long as the mind does not waver, so long should one drink; beyond this is the drinking of the Paśu.
Thus ends the twentieth chapter, titled "The Description of the Ritual for Saluting the Vessel," in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*, within the *Śrī Devī Rahasya*.
(p. 91) Now begins the twenty-first chapter.
Śrī Bhairava said:
O Goddess, I shall declare at the conclusion of the worship the unsurpassed Peace Hymn (śāntistotra),
by which heroes, free from desire, will attain the state of supreme bliss.
I bow my head to the Lord Bhairava, the beloved of Bhairavī, who stands in the midst of the circle of Yoginīs and is surrounded by the mandala of Mothers.
Homage to the venerable Lord-Physician, the sole cause for destroying the terrible disease of beginningless saṃsāra, who bestows the medicine of the Kula.
Calamities, misfortunes, and diseases arise from the transgression of conventional conduct;
may all of these be dispelled here by the union with the divine wheel. (4)
May there be long life, health, sovereignty, fame, gain, happiness, and victory; may there be beauty and the fulfillment of desires, and may all the deities protect [us]. (5)

May it grant perpetual peace to those who worship and protect the lords of ascetics, the lords of yogis, and those whose wealth is penance, as well as to the region, the kingdom, the family, and the king.
The Blessed One is the Lord of the Family. || 6 ||
May those who reveal the lineage of the assembly of practitioners rejoice— those who belong to the four great lineages beginning with Sṛṣṭi and ending with Anākhyā;
may all those who delight in the Kula and Kaula traditions rejoice, as well as others, even the most supreme.
Those who belong to the Śāmbhava [tradition], which distinguishes the various specific words.
May the Siddha-gurus, the lineages of one’s own gurus, the Jyeṣṭhas, the Anugas, the Samayins, the Vaṭukas, and the Kumāris rejoice!
May the lords of the earth, cattle, the twice-born, and the virtuous people rejoice—those born of the noble lineage of heroes of the six Yoginīs. || 8 ||

May those who are skilled in policy, established in faultless conduct, free from envy, incomparable, and free from affliction; who are eternal, constantly devoted, stainless, desireless, empowered by Śakti, peaceful-minded, and whose sorrow and doubt have been removed—may they all rejoice! (9)
May those devoted to yoga rejoice, as do those joined with the Kula-yoga, along with the teachers, the initiates bound by the samaya, the practitioners, and the spiritual sons.
May cows, brahmins, young women, ascetics, and maidens be intent upon dharma and endowed with devotion to the guru.
May the lineages of practitioners who have attained the powers such as *aṇimā* rejoice; may the curses of the family *yoginīs* fall upon their enemies!
May that indescribable state of Śambhu manifest within me as well, in which there is only the lotus feet of the Guru.
It is obtainable. || 11 ||
Those goddesses who dwell in the stages of the sequence of the wheels (*cakra*), those who reside within the channels (*nāḍī*),
those who inhabit the pores of the tree of the body, those who abide in the elements (*dhātu*),
those who dwell in the waves of the wind of the breaths of inhalation, and those whose abode is the exhalation— those are the goddesses.
May those who are intent on the effort of devouring their enemies, being worshipped according to the Kaula tradition, be satisfied. || 12 ||
Those who protect the divine path on earth, those deities dwelling in the waters, those of eternally renowned splendor residing in fire, those who take refuge in the wind,
those consisting of the nectar of the lunar orb in the sky, and those who are always omnipresent— all of them [are here].
May those devoted to preserving the family path grant me peace. || 13 ||
Above the cosmic egg, or in heaven, in the subterranean realms, on the surface of the earth, or in the formless void;

Whether in the sky or on the ground, whether situated in the wind or in the water, or wherever else they may dwell— in sacred fields, *pīṭhas*, *upapīṭhas*, and so forth— may those goddesses, who are worshipped by the lords of yogis, always protect you with their favor through the rite of auspicious offerings (*bali*) consisting of incense, lamps, meat, and other such substances. (14)

Brahmā, Śrī, Śeṣa, Durgā, Guha, the Gaṇas, the Bhairavas, the Kṣetrapālas, Vetālas, Ādityas, Rudras, the Planets, Vasus, Manus, Siddhas, Apsarases, Guhyakas, and others; Bhūtas, Gandharvas, Vidyādharas, Ṛṣis, Pitṛs, Yakṣas, Asuras, Serpents, and the many other beings.
May all the lords of yogis, the cāraṇas, the kimpuruṣas, the sages, the gods, and those who dwell on the Cakra mountain protect us. || 15 ||

If the word of the Guru is indeed the truth, if the ancestors and the gods [are the authority], if there is the favor of the Yoginīs, if she is the supreme deity, and if the Vedas are indeed the valid means of knowledge;
If this Śākta philosophy exists, if this Command (ājñā) is present, if there are Kaulikas here as well—if all these should be so, may I always be victorious. || 16 ||
May all the Mothers, the oceans, and the lords of their hosts, as well as the Yoginīs and the Kṣetrapālas who are established within my body, be satisfied. (17)
May the universe— from Śiva down to the earth, including everything from Brahmā to a blade of grass,
and from the Fire of Time up to Śiva— be satisfied by this sacrifice.

Thus ends the Śāntistotra. Now begins the Vīravandanastotra: Homage again and again to the leaders of practitioners, whose teachings are honored throughout the three worlds, who are skilled in accomplishing the welfare of others, and who have uprooted the great serpents of the afflictions (kleśas). (20)
To those who have abandoned all latent impressions (*vāsanā*) of the outflows (*āsrava*),
and who have accomplished the means for the arising of the reality of all objects;
Homage again and again to the leaders of practitioners who are intent on uplifting all living beings. || 21 ||

Salutations again and again to the leaders of practitioners, who have crossed the great ocean of saṃsāra, who are intent upon uprooting the creeper of craving, and who ward off old age, disease, and death. || 22 ||

Homage again and again to the leaders of practitioners, who are vessels for the jewel-mine of the true Dharma, who teach the supreme path to nirvāṇa, and whose aspirations are entirely fulfilled in every respect. (23)

Homage again and again to the leaders of practitioners, who have arisen with reverence out of compassion for the world, who are permeated by mercy and loving-kindness, and who fulfill the practice of benefiting all beings. || 24 ||

Homage again and again to the leaders of practitioners, who have utterly destroyed all evil garments, whose fuel of impurities has been consumed by the fire of knowledge, and who fulfill the vow of wisdom. (25)

Homage again and again to those leaders of practitioners, who fulfill the hopes of all seekers, who awaken the lotus-ponds of those to be trained, and who are vast mines of all meaningful qualities. (26)

Homage again and again to the leaders of practitioners, who have acquired their teachings through infinite karma, who are saluted by Brahmā, Indra, Rudra, and others, and who act for the mutual benefit of one another. (27)

Salutations again and again to the Lords of Causes, who protect from the great terrors such as the dissolution of the elements and the like, who are devoted to the conduct of the fivefold path, and who are the source of all the arts of good fortune. || 28 ||

Salutations again and again to those who have become Śambhu and Śambhavī, who have completely exhausted the latent impressions born of their divided evil karma, who are endowed with great renown on all sides, and who have established the abode of stainless, attainable knowledge.
[Kh, g: va | Likewise in the case of fire as well. || 29 ||

Homage again and again to those who are born of Śambhu and belong to Śambhu, who are great rafts upon the ocean of all scriptures, who are solely devoted to the purpose of the worship of the Śrīcakra, and who are capable of practicing the conduct of the venerable Vīras. 30.

Salutations again and again to those who belong to Śambhu and are born of Śambhu, who are adorned with the splendor of ten million glorious mantras, who transcend the state of the twenty-two manifestations, and who are vessels for the nectar of the non-dual reality.

Homage again and again to those who are Śambhu and the source of Śambhu, who are adorned with the thirty-six marks, whose eyes are like pools of blooming lotuses, and whose bodies are like refined gold.
To those who are well-established in the equipment for perfect enlightenment, and who demonstrate both saṃsāra and nirvāṇa; [k, ṅ: who show the vision of nirvāṇa].
Homage again and again to those who are born of Śambhu and are possessed of minds enveloped in great compassion. || 33 ||

Salutations again and again to those who belong to Śambhu and Śambhavī, who are immersed in the essence of the realization of the identity of the Supreme and the Individual, who are terrifying due to their conduct based on the Vāmā path, and who have destroyed the darkness of the world through their absolute sovereignty.

Homage again and again to those who have attained the great fruit through the practice of the charnel ground, who are capable of removing the darkness of delusion, who observe one another’s commands, and who are both Śambhu and beyond Śambhu.
Homage again and again to the attendants of Śambhu, who have disheveled hair and earrings, whose eyes are reddened by the intoxication of wine, and who are intent upon fresh amorous dalliance.

Salutations, salutations to the Bhairavas and Bhairavīs, whose limbs are smeared with ashes, who are clad in the directions as their garments, who are terrifying with the wreaths of smoke from funeral pyres, and who drink the thick nectar from skull-cups! || 37 ||

Homage again and again to the Bhairavas and Bhairavīs, who have established the eight supernatural powers (*siddhyaṣṭaka*), who show reverence for the practice of Śrī Bhairava, who have taken up their residence [therein], and who have surpassed the immortals (*nirjara*) by their own mastery. || 38 ||

Homage, repeated homage, to those who are Bhairavas and Bhairavīs— those who investigate the meaning of the scriptures with perfect tranquility, who have desisted from poetry of manifold sentiments, and whose conceptual constructions have been entirely cast away. (39)

Salutations again and again to Bhairava and Bhairavī, whose forms are the glorious embodiment of existence, consciousness, and bliss, who are mines of the happiness of the sovereign kingdom of union (sāyujya), and whose intentions are veiled by the realization of identity with their own self. || 40 ||

Salutations again and again to those Bhairavas and Bhairavis, whose minds are the abode of supreme grace, who are overflowing with the essence of the non-dual knowledge of Brahman, and whose consciousness has taken refuge in the thought, "I am Śiva. 41.
In every way and at all times, I know this entire world— including everything from pots to cloth— to be the blissful Brahman that has brought forth this vast expansion.
I alone am the supreme *haṃsa*, Śiva, the ultimate cause;
he is merged within my life-force, my very self, having attained a state of equal flavor (*samarasī*).
We meditate upon that dark abode, the dwelling place of truth, consciousness, and bliss, the supreme and non-supreme cause, enriched by the light of the non-dual Śiva. 44.
By this recitation of the *Vīrastava*, having thoroughly cleansed my afflictions, may I rescue the world as it sinks into this great ocean of the wilderness of saṃsāra. (45)
Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, titled "The Description of the Peace Hymn and the Salutation to the Heroes," within the *Śrī Devīrahasya* of the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*.
(p. 98) Now begins the twenty-second chapter.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the supreme procedure for the purification of liquor,
by performing which the practitioner in the Kali age will become a vessel for liberation.
O Goddess, by those very same materials through which a practitioner becomes a sinner due to their improper accumulation,
by those same materials, when pure, one partakes in both worldly enjoyment and liberation through worship.
O Goddess, from the moment that liquor first attained renown in this world, all the gods—Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Hara, and the others—became known as *surās*. (3)
Asuras, rākṣasas, yakṣas, gandharvas, humans, and others, their inner minds were filled with the intense bliss arising from that association. (4)
And they partook of divine liquor consecrated by the performance of mantras.
In due time, that goddess of liquor, O Sovereign of the Gods, became established within the jar.
O beloved Goddess of the gods, when the world was afflicted by Kali in the form of Time,
she was cursed by Śukra for the murder of Kaca.
Due to the power of Śukra’s curse, the gods— Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the others—
as well as the Brahman-sages, bestowed curses upon Surādevī in due order.
O Maheśvarī, the killing of a Brāhmaṇa and the drinking of liquor should be known as equal;
when the liquor was cursed by the gods, then the Daityas rejoiced.
O Goddess, having drunk the *surā* liquor, the gods were deprived of their strength by the sons of Diti and expelled from heaven, with Purandara at their head.
Then, O Goddess, placing Jiṣṇu at their head, the gods performed a sacrifice;
Sadāśiva and the others manifested at that supreme sacrifice. (10)
"Choose now a boon as you desire, O leader of the gods;
we shall grant it to you immediately, and then we shall go to our own abode. (11)
Then Śakra, O auspicious Goddess, placing his preceptor at the forefront, said:
"By consuming even as much as a drop on the tip of a blade of grass of this liquor... (12)
That satisfaction which arises within us cannot be attained even by hundreds of jars of nectar;
yet that very goddess has been cursed by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śaṅkara. (13)
Without her, they became powerless and were defeated by their enemies, including Śakra and the others. Then all the gods [approached] the god Śiva, the Lord, the imperishable one. || 14 ||
Having prostrated again and again with supreme devotion,
they praised the one-syllabled Rudra, who is the letter 'A' and whose form is the Self.
Salutations indeed to the primordial god represented by the syllable *U*, whose body is knowledge;
salutations to the third, the syllable *Ma*, who is Śiva, the Supreme Self.
Salutations indeed to the Sun, who possesses the luster of the moon, the sacrificer;
salutations to you, O Blessed Rudra, the Sun of immeasurable splendor. (17)
Homage to Bhava, the god, and to Śarva with matted hair;
homage to Śiva, who takes the form of the earth, and who is ever the destroyer of the fear of the Asuras. 18.
Salutations to you, O Īśāna; salutations again and again to Saṃsparśa;
and to Paśupati, the purifier of immeasurable splendor. || 19 ||
Salutation indeed to Bhīma, whose form is space and who consists of sound alone;
salutation again and again to Mahādeva, to Soma, and to the Immortal. || 20 ||
"Homage to you, the fierce one, for the sake of the sacrificer; homage to you, the master of ritual yoga"—having thus praised the supreme god Bhairava, Śiva, the Lord. (21)
(100) Then all the gods, beginning with Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Hara, prostrated themselves;
at that moment, a voice arose from the sky of those whose bodies are the five voids.
This [teaching] should always be practiced by all those seeking liberation, through this method, in its proper context, according to the rules, and in due sequence. (23)
I am the fourfold form of the Vedas, possessing the nature of Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman;
I am Atharvan, the essence of the mantras, the Supreme Self, Śiva, the imperishable.
Having churned the Vedas and formulated the meaning of the Vedas in the form of mantras,
O Sadāśiva, reveal the great vidyā of Kurukullā.
The supreme scripture known as Āgama consists of sixty-four [parts]; in it, the purification of the gods and others was revealed by the most excellent Manus. (26)
When the supreme speech born of Śiva had thus ceased,
the gods, bowing down, praised Sadāśiva, the Great Lord.
O God, salutations to you whose form is the syllable Oṃ, salutations to you whose form is the universe;
salutations to the god of gods, and indeed salutations to Mahādeva.
Salutations again and again to the eternal one, whose body is half-female, who is the originator of Sāṃkhya and Yoga, and who is to be understood through the meaning of the Vedas and Śāstras.
Salutations to you, the protector of the distressed and the afflicted, and to you who possess divine vision;
salutations to the thousand-headed one, and salutations to the one with a thousand feet.
"Salutation to the Mantra, who dwells in the expanse of consciousness, the Supreme Self.
Having thus praised him, the great-souled Mahādeva, the illustrious Sadāśiva, [remained there]. || 31 ||
She, the goddess who is known as Devī, the Goddess of Gods, and as Bhavānī, proclaimed the scripture of the Āgamas, which is the path to liberation for the high-souled ones.
Having quickly prostrated before Sadāśiva, he spoke with gentle words:
"O Lord, tell me the scripture concerning the arrival of the gods, which is a supreme and most wonderful secret."
(101) By the mere utterance of which even a goddess becomes free from the curse.
Śrī Śiva said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall explain the purification of the intoxicants in their proper order—
the cleansing of all things beginning with the letter 'M', which increases spiritual accomplishment.
The Veda is indeed the word "niṣkala" (partless), and the meaning of the Veda is the Āgama concerning Śiva.
The gods should be served by those seeking liberation who know the true essence of the Veda, its meaning, and the Āgamas. (35)
O Supreme Goddess, it is certain that there is no absolute difference between the Vedas and the Āgamas;
therefore, O Kaulikas, you must not entertain any delusion regarding the scriptures. (36)
Now listen, O Goddess of gods, to the supreme purification of liquor, by which, through mere purification, all success is produced. (37)
Having prepared a mandala to the left, either with water or with colored powders,
or with saffron, the eight fragrances, or in every case with the ashes of a hero (vīrabhasman).
O beautiful lady of the Kula, having quickly sprinkled the triangle joined with the bindu, the circle, and the square with the water of the general arghya, [one should proceed].
Having established the support there, one should worship the fire-mandala;
having worshipped the digits (kalās) of the fire as they are described by me, it is performed correctly.
One should worship with the mantra: "The syllable *ra* joined with the *bindu*, the orb of fire, ending in *ṅe*, [and] 'to the one whose self is the ten kalās, the universe (*viśva*)'. (41)
Dhūmrā, Nīlavarṇā, Kapilā, Visphuliṅginī, Jvālā, Haimavatī, Kavyavāhanī, and Havyavāhanī. || 42 ||
Having worshipped Raudrī, Saṅkarṣaṇī, and the ten digits of Vaiśvānara according to the prescribed rule with perfumes, unbroken grains, and flowers, || 43 ||
One should place a large, divine water-pot (kalaśa), adorned with flower garlands and the like,
made of gold, silver, or clay, using the Vīra-mudrā.
O Goddess, just as [you were established] by Śambhu and Viṣṇu in the past,
and just as [you were established] by Brahmā in former times, so do I establish you now. (45)
Having thus established the pitcher there, one should worship the Sun;
O Maheśvarī, having uttered the name of the Sun, one should recite the Jīva-mantra. (46)
And entering the solar disc, which consists of the glorious twelve kalās,
one should worship with this mantra, employing the Viśva-mantra at the end.
One should worship the twelve digits (kalās) of the Sun; they are declared by me as follows:
Tapinī, Tāpinī, Bodhinī, and Rodhinī. || 48 ||
Kaliṇī, Śoṣaṇī, Vareṇyā, Ākarṣaṇī, Māyā, Viśvāvatī, and Hemaprabhā—these are the digits of the Sun. (49)
O Goddess, having worshipped the jar for the sake of attaining the Kula-siddhi,
the Kaulika should fill the vessel with wine while reciting the letters of the Mātṛkā in reverse order.
One should contemplate this very nectar as being directly in the form of the moon;
having worshipped the lunar disc with this mantra, O Pārvatī. (51)
Having uttered the Śakti, O Goddess of gods, [one should worship] that which is joined with the lunar mandala;
for Viśvāñcala, O Goddess of gods, who is the essence of the sixteen glorious digits (kalās). 52.
Having thus worshipped [the Sun], one should worship the sixteen digits (kalās) of the Moon:
Amṛtā, Mānadā, Tuṣṭi, Puṣṭi, Prīti, and likewise Rati. (53)
Śrī, Hrī, Svadhā, Rātri, Jyotsnā, Haimavatī, as well as Chāyā, Pūrṇimā, Nityā, and the sixteenth, Amāvāsyā. (54)
Having worshipped these with mantras, one should sacrifice to the goddess Bhairavī;
there, upon the water-pot, one should visualize a triangle by means of the root mantra.
Having meditated upon the Supreme Goddess within the circle of the Bindu, one should worship one's chosen deity;
O Goddess, one should worship Śiva with the Praṇava, with fragrance, and with the wind. 56.
In that [mantra], one should extract *tāra* (oṃ) and *māyā* (hrīṃ), O Supreme Sovereign;
and one should extract *paramākāśaśūnya* (haḥ) and *vāhinī* (svāhā). (57)
One should say, "O devourer of the moon, sun, and fire,
enter the vessel," and recite this mantra, ending with two *ṭha*s, ten times over the jar.
In that very place, at the end of the Mātṛkā, O beloved, one should recite this most purifying Ṛc known by the name "Ā kṛṣṇena rajasa" (RV 1.35.2).
O Goddess, one should recite this verse known as *madhuvātā ṛtāya* ten times; therein, O Beloved, one should chant the *ānandeśa-gāyatrī* ten times.
Having uttered the *vāṅmāyā* [mantras], one should likewise say "to Ānandeśvara," and then recite: "vidmahe śrīsurādevyai dhīmahī. (61)
May that Ardhanārīśvara inspire us;
having extracted [the mantra] and recited the Gāyatrī ten times, one should worship with "haṃsaḥ śuciṣat. (62)
The Kaulika, having recited three times the mantra "agnim īḷe purohitam," should thereafter utter the letter *va* preceded by the six long vowels.
For Surādevī, who has been liberated from the curse of Brahmā, one should mutter the *Kuṭāntaka* mantra ten times and recite the Ṛgvedic verse beginning with "iṣe tvorje tvā. (64)
Having uttered "Tāram" (Om), the syllable of Māyā (Hrīm), and the six long vowels, then [the word] "sudhe," one should recite the mantra ending with "mocaya" twice followed by "vanāntam" (svāhā). 65.
O beloved, one should mutter ten times the verse beginning with "agna āyāhi";
this is said to be the knowledge that removes the curse of Śukra, as it is described by me.
O Goddess, born from the solar disc, born from the abode of Varuṇa, composed of the seed-syllable Amā— may [this person] be liberated from the curse of Śukra.
If the Praṇava is the seed-syllable of the gods (or the Vedas), consisting of the bliss of Brahman, by that truth, O Goddess of Gods, may the sin of killing a Brahmin be dispelled. 68.
The Supreme Brahman alone is the ultimate reality, consisting of both the gross and the subtle;
by that [power], I destroy for you the sin of killing a Brahmin born from a mere thought. (69)
Released from the curse of Brahmā, released from the curse of Viṣṇu,
and liberated from the curse of Rudra, become pure now.
O Śivā, having worshipped with these mantras three times,
the Kaulika should recite the verse "śanno devīḥ" ten times over the water-jar.
Then, O Goddess, having uttered *māyā*, *ramā*, *paṅgu*, and that which is divided by six long vowels, one should say "śobhinī" after [the word] "churikākāriṇī". (72)
One should take away the vikāra-s of this substance, as well as the pair of *y* and the two *ṭha*-s;
one should recite the mantra known as Churikā ten times over the water-pot.
One should recite the verse beginning with "yo viśvacakṣuḥ" ten times,
while meditating upon the Guru in the thousand-petaled lotus of the heart, as well as one's chosen deity.
Having prostrated, the Kaulika should meditate upon and recite the mantra of Śrītiraskaraṇī—[the goddess] who resembles a dark blue cloud and is adorned with dark blue locks of hair. (75)
The goddess, wearing blue garments, with eyes like blue lotuses, enriched with ornaments of blue flowers, and adorned with blue jewels. || 76 ||
She was draped in blue body-unguents, wearing a garland of blue lapis lazuli,
and adorned with highly precious jewels whose brilliance was fixed like sapphire.
Mounted upon a blue horse, bearing a blue sword as her weapon, she is supreme;
with a blue cloth of sleep, she covers the fourteen worlds.
She who deludes those in the Mahāyāna, who devours those who revile material substances, and who protects from all sides the heroes devoted to the drinking of the hero’s draught (vīrapāna). || 79 ||
Covering the divine maṇḍala of the convention with their own garments, [they worship] Paramānandabhairavī, whose body is supreme bliss. 80.
"I bow to Parāmbikā, the progenitress of supreme bliss.
Having thus meditated, one should recite the Vidyā as it is described by me. (81)
One should utter "Vāk-kāma-maṭha-māyā" and "tiraskaraṇī," then, having pronounced "sakalajanaṃ," one should say "vāgvādini. (82)
One should speak of the entire multitude of bound beings as being the state of the mind;
likewise, one should disregard the eyes, ears, tongue, nose, and so forth.
Then, one should utter *tiraskuru*, followed by the three *padma* syllables and the two *ṭha*s;
one should recite this *Śrītiraskaraṇī* mantra ten times over the water-pot.
The Pāvamānī verses are the Supreme Brahman, the pure, eternal light;
they attend upon the ancestors with milk, clarified butter, honey, and water.
One should first recite this Ṛgvedic verse three times, and then recite it three times again.
The Pāvamānī is the supreme Brahman; the Pāvamānīs are the supreme essence. || 86 ||
"The Pāvamānī is supreme knowledge; by means of it, I purify you.
Having thus recited this and meditated upon the Guru, one should mutter the Varuṇa-bīja.
One should meditate on the solar mantra "Haṃsa" and upon the goddess Kuṇḍalinī, who is auspicious, coiled three and a half times, and shaped like a sleeping serpent. (88)
She possesses a splendor as formidable as ten million suns, yet is as cool as ten million moons; she is as unassailable as ten million fires, yet more subtle than a lotus fiber.
Having swiftly pierced the six chakras, one should lead [the breath] through the path of the suṣumnā;
having bowed to the God residing in the thousand-petaled lotus, one should dissolve [it] into the state of Śiva. 90.
Having meditated on the great light of Śiva and Śakti, one should draw forth the nectar flowing from the digit of the moon through the tip of the left nostril and pour it into the jar.
Having consecrated that substance as nectar, one should display the dhenumudrā [cow-seal]. One should recite:
"Māyā, Ramā, Kāmakalā; O Nectar, O Source of Nectar! (92)
Having uttered *amṛtavarṣiṇī*, one should utter "make [it] flow with nectar" twice; and at the end of the *viṣṇukalā* mantra, O Pārvatī, the Kaulika should recite *aṃ āṃ*. (93)
Having meditated upon the substance consisting of nectar, well-perfumed with camphor and other fragrances, one should recite this mantra ending in *viśva* for Amṛteśvarī over the jar. (94)
Having prepared a mixture of cardamom, cloves, musk, sandalwood, and uśīra grass,
one should invoke the sacred waters into the jar while reciting the root mantra.
One should extract this root mantra: "Tāraṃ Śivaṃ Śivodbhūtim.
Then [the following names]: "Gaṅge ca Yamune caiva Godāvari Sarasvati" (96).
"O Narmadā, Sindhu, and Kāverī, be present within this substance!"—having thus invoked [the deities], O Great Goddess, with the mudrā in the form of a goad (aṅkuśa). 97.
One should meditate on the substance consisting of all sacred fords (tīrthas), which is supremely purifying;
in the midst of that substance, one should visualize a triangle marked with a drop (bindu).
Having quickly bound the *yonimudrā*, one should meditate upon Ānandabhairava, who resembles ten million suns in brilliance and is as cool as ten million moons. 99.
The god has eighteen arms, five faces, and three eyes;
he stands in the midst of the ocean of nectar, seated upon a Brahma-lotus.
Mounted upon a bull, blue-throated, adorned with all ornaments, bearing a skull-cup and a khaṭvāṅga staff, and sounding a bell and a ḍamaru drum. || 101 ||
The god holds a noose and a goad, and bears a mace and a club;
he carries a sword, a shield, a paṭṭiśa, a mallet, a trident, and a spear.

The best of practitioners should meditate upon the Lord of the gods, who is red in color, holding a variegated staff, a severed head, and displaying the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness with his hands. (103)
Having offered a handful of flowers into the jar, one should recite the mantra of Ānandabhairava:
the syllable *ha*, the god Bhṛgu, Maṇḍūka, and then Dharaṇī. (104)
(Likewise, one should extract the seed-syllable of Jīmūta and the seed-syllable of Hutabhuj;
then Vāyu and Keśa for Ānandabhairava, and [the seed-syllable] at the hem. 105.
Having recited the *vikuṭa* mantra ten times, one should worship Bhairavī.
O Śivā, one should meditate upon Ānandabhairavī exactly as she is described. (106)
While the ocean, the best of seas, the milk-ocean, was being churned,
the goddess Surā was born there, assuming the form of a young maiden.
And one should meditate upon the goddess Surā, possessing the radiance of ten million times ten thousand moons, white as snow, kunda flowers, and the moon, with five faces and three eyes. 108.
Endowed with eighteen arms, intent on bestowing all bliss,
smiling, large-eyed, and facing the God of gods.
One should extract Śakti, Śiva, Nirjara, Bhekī, and the seed-syllable of the Earth (Bhū-bīja), as well as Megha, Vahni, the letter of the Wind (Samīrārṇa), and Keśa. (110)
O Pārvatī, having worshipped Bhairava and Bhairavī, the Kaulika should recite the *kuṭa* for Surādevī at the end and repeat the Vidyā ten times.
One should display the Mahāmudrā, the Dhenumudrā, the Yoni, and the Matsya;
and having again bound the mudrā called Lelihānā, [one displays] Kuṇḍalinī.

O Dear One, having risen from the *mūlādhāra* by way of the *suṣumnā* path and established [the consciousness] at the *dvādaśānta*, one should contemplate "I am He" (*so'ham*) as "He is I" (*haṃsa*). || 113 ||
Having united [the self] with Śiva, one should become filled with supreme bliss;
then, one should release a rain of nectar produced from that through the left nostril.
And with the syllable *praṇava*, O Goddess of gods, one should employ it for the supreme substance;
one should meditate upon the excellent jar as being directly enriched by the principle of nectar (*amṛtatattva*). || 115 ||
Having uttered the seed-syllable of Varuṇa,
one should recite the root mantra ten times, O Goddess, preceded by perfumes and unbroken rice grains (akṣata).
Having worshipped the divine pitcher with various kinds of celestial flowers, garlands, and diverse ornaments, preceded by the ringing of a bell; || 117 ||
Having worshipped with incense, lamps, great splendors, and various supreme medicinal herbs, with supreme devotion, prostrations, and preceded by hymns of praise; || 118 ||
O Goddess of the gods, the practitioner should meditate upon the jar as consisting of all the deities;
that which is the liquor is the goddess Umā, and that which is the substance is Maheśvara. (119)
That which is fragrance is Brahmā; that which is delusion is Janārdana. Soma is established in taste, and Fire is established in foam.
In desire, the god Manmatha resides; in vomiting, Ucchiṣṭabhairava;
in liquefaction, O Goddess, Gaṅgā is stationed; and the seven oceans are situated within the jar. 121.
It is a substance consisting entirely of splendor, overflowing with supreme bliss,
completely liberated from all curses, and well-consecrated by all mantras.
One should worship Bhairava and Bhairavī with the nature of supreme nectar,
together with the great heroes of Maheśvara who abide in the state of Mahācīna.
O beloved, this substance, consisting of great power and worthy of honor,
should be used after having fully gratified one's chosen deity and the assembly of divine Yoginīs.
[He should worship] Vaṭuka and the Kṣetrapālas, the thirty-three crores of deities (the reading *tritriṃśat* is correct),
all the Mothers and their hosts, together with the Bhūtas, Pretas, and others. || 125 ||

O Goddess, having duly gratified the Guru and the excellent Gurus, one should meditate upon the Guru and then meditate upon the Supreme [Deity], after worshipping the Vīras according to one's capacity. (126)
"One endowed with Śakti should worship the worthy recipient"—this is the supreme command of the Lord.
A drinking vessel devoid of Śakti is in vain, and worship devoid of Śiva is in vain. (127)
In the union of Śiva and Śakti, the hero’s worship bestows liberation;
such is this divine purification regarding wine, difficult even for the gods to attain. 128.
Out of affection for you, I have determined this; listen to something else as well, O beloved:
liquor, meat, fish, mudrā, and sexual union. (129)
The fivefold group beginning with the letter *ma* is to be worshipped during the union of Śiva and Śakti;
whatever is brought for the worship—whether it be food to be chewed, food to be eaten, or food to be licked—[should be offered]. (130)
(109) One should consecrate with the mantra everything that is to be drunk, sucked, or [eaten as] fruit and flower.
O Śivā, he who out of delusion should consume these without having consecrated them— || 131 ||
O Goddess of the gods, even that practitioner of mantras would suddenly fall into hell;
one should draw a square diagram and place fish within it.
O Goddess Śivā, one should dry, burn, and flood [the body] with the mantra, using respectively the seed-syllables of Vāyu, Agni, and Varuṇa. (133)
One should display the Dhenu, Yoni, and Mahāmatsya mudrās,
and recite the mantra of Ānandeśvarabhairava ten times.
O Mistress of the Kaulas, having recited [the mantra], one should chant the Vidyā as it has been described;
for the world, oppressed by Kali, was brought down [to earth] by Hari. 135.
And, desiring the welfare of the fishermen, Hari himself became a fish, seized by Bālin for the sake of pleasing Bhairavī. (136)
Then he should recite the *māyā* [the syllable *hrīṃ*, as found in the reading of all manuscripts] for Hari, followed by the *viśva* verse (*viśvam*).
Thereafter, the wise man should mutter three times the mantra: "We worship Tryambaka. (137)
Having worshipped with perfumes and flowers, one should prostrate before the supreme deity;
O Great Goddess, one should place the vessel of meat within the square.
O Kulasaundari, having dried, burnt, and soaked the *pala*, the Kaulika should quickly display the three mudras and recite the mantra. (139)

I take refuge in that imperishable Viṣṇu, who has assumed a form within the goat’s fat and human entrails for the sake of the mantra’s purpose, and who exists for the sake of the sacrificial offering (bali) to Śiva and Śakti. || 140 ||
"I satisfy you for the sake of the offering; become purified now.
Having recited this verse three times, O Goddess, the best of Kaulikas should perform the silent recitation (japa). || 141 ||
Recalling the mantra "pra tad viṣṇuḥ," one should prostrate with the yoni-mudrā;
having brought the vessel for the mudrā, one should place it within the square area.
One should perform the drying, burning, and flooding as before;
having displayed the three mudrās, one should recite the ritual procedure like the Vedas. (143)
Those fragrant substances which are currently used in the worship of the deities shall now serve as pure offerings for the sake of success in the ritual for the God and Goddess.
Having recited the root mantra ten times, one should then recite the unsurpassed Ṛc;
the Kaulika, having repeatedly recited that supreme mantra of Viṣṇu, [should proceed]. (145)
Having prostrated with a spirit of devotion, one should purify the *kuṇḍagola*;
having established it within a square [mandala], the wise man should dry it and burn it. (146)
One should flood it with other seed-syllables and protect it with mudrās;
having recited the root mantra ten times, one should then recite the verse that follows.
Having recollected the mantra "Viṣṇur yonim" and recited it, one should then prostrate;
this is done when all the materials for the deity have been brought together by the Kaulikas.
One should mutter this verse correctly and extract this mantra:
"Glūṃ mlūṃ slūṃ plūṃ nlūṃ, O Goddess of Gods, [the syllable] Svānta, Khaṃ, and Kāmakālika. (149)
"Amṛte, amṛtodbhūte, amṛteśvari, and amṛtam;
having extracted these two [phrases], one should then extract the two Ṭha-sounds. (150)
O Maheśvarī, this lore that removes the curse consists of the five 'ma' syllables; it is to be remembered during the ritual of worship for the five kalpas.
Having purified the Śiva-substances with mantras and mudrās,
one should sprinkle them in due order with the Ṛg-verses and the root-mantra according to the sequence.
O Kuleśvarī, having thus purified the supreme substances with drops of nectar from jars filled with the essence of bliss; 153.
One should worship Bhairava and the goddess Bhairavī in the assembly of heroes;
for without having worshipped the god Bhairava and without having performed the adoration of the deities, [one should not proceed]. (154)
Even a hero, having drunk according to the rite of drinking the *paśu*, would go to hell;
O Goddess of Gods, having thus consecrated [the substance] preceded by devotion to the Guru... (155)
Whoever drinks this supreme beverage shall attain union with Śiva;
thus, this is the supreme secret, the secret among secrets. (156)
This reality, consisting of the eight siddhis, must be guarded like one's own private parts.
Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, titled "The Description of the Method for Purifying Liquor," in the *Śrī Devī Rahasya* of the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*.
Now begins the twenty-third chapter.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Now listen, O Goddess of gods, to the supreme purification of Śakti,
by the mere hearing of which one dissolves into the state of Parāśakti.
From association with families that have not received initiation, the loss of spiritual accomplishment arises;
this is also the case if one should listen to their talk or go to their bedchamber. (2)
The Goddess said: "O God, how should one who is of noble family (kulīna) and desires success in the worship according to the sequence of the Kula practice worship a woman of the Kula?"
The illustrious Bhairava said: "If a Kaulika, without having performed purification, engages with women or in wines,
even if [the rite] is performed, there will be a loss of accomplishment, and Caṇḍikā becomes enraged."
Success arises from consecration, and auspicious [success] comes from the recitation of the mantra;
at the time of sexual union she is the Great Mistress (Maheśānī), and at the time of initiation she is the Virgin (Kanyakā). (5)
Whether by force, with effort, or through cunning, one should cause another's wife to drink either liquor,
semen, water, or honey.

One should consecrate a woman in union— [the reading "one should consecrate her in sexual enjoyment" (saṃbhoge 'bhiṣicet) occurs everywhere in the text]— whether she be a Caṇḍālī or one devoid of mantras,
whether she be one's own or another's, and whether she be proud of her beauty and youth.
The Goddess said: O Blessed One, Lord of the Gods of gods, for the sole purpose of accomplishing the Kula practice, how should a Kula-yogin perform the purification of Kula women? (8)
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Upon seeing a young woman born of a noble family, the Lord of the Kula should offer salutation;
having performed mental worship, the yogi should recite the mantra. (9)
Whether she be a young girl, one intoxicated by youth, an old woman, or beautiful; whether she be contemptible or exceedingly wicked—one should meditate upon her after having paid homage.
One must never, under any circumstances, commit an assault, verbal abuse, deceit, or anything unpleasant toward them; otherwise, it will create obstacles to success. (11)
Women are gods; women are life-breaths; indeed, women alone are the ornament. One must always behave as one would toward the wives of others even toward one's own wife. (12)
Even she, though delighting in the contrary, will be upon the heart;
she shall quickly become for the practitioner like another wish-fulfilling cow.
By that, no unrighteousness arises, nor does anyone become a destroyer of dharma;
devoted to that, one is absorbed into the supreme reality of those whose bodies are dependent on another. 14.
An actress, a Kāpālikī, a prostitute, a washerwoman, a barber’s wife,
a Brāhmaṇa woman, a Śūdra girl, and likewise a cowherd’s daughter— 15.
The daughter of a garland-maker is also proclaimed as one of the nine maidens;
having brought any one of these, he should then perform the purification. (16)
O Goddess, the Kaulika should perform worship as it is correctly described by me:
Sadāśiva is declared to be the seer (ṛṣi) of the mantra for the purification of Śakti. || 17 ||
The meter is known as Triṣṭubh, and the deity is Parāmbikā;
O Īśānī, the seed-syllable is Vāk, and the power is said to be Śakti. (18)
O Goddess, Kāmeśa is the *kīlaka*; O Īśvarī, the binding of the directions is Hara;
O Maheśvarī, the *viniyoga* is for the sake of attaining both worldly enjoyment and liberation. (19)
O Kaulikeśvarī, at the dead of night, the Kaulika brings nine maidens and eleven, nine, or eight Bhairavas.
The best of Kaulikas should purify with nine mantras and perform worship;
the practitioner should first touch [the seat] after having performed the purification of the *viṣṭara*.
Even after performing the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi), one should carry out the rite of offering the vital breaths (prāṇārpaṇa);
having performed the mental resolve for the mantra, one should perform the Nyāsa of the sages and so forth.
Having performed the Mātṛkā-nyāsa preceded by the Kara-nyāsa and Aṅga-nyāsa,
and having then performed the worship of the Heart-Pīṭha, one should carry out the worship of the Śrīcakra.

Having purified the substances belonging to the deity, as well as those from the *kuṇḍa* and *goḷa*, one performs the worship of the Hero (*vīra*) and the service of the Hero’s beloved, which is difficult even for the gods to attain. (24)
Having worshipped the Goddess Śrī Parāmbikā according to the prescribed rite,
one should establish the Śakti on the left and worship her as it is described.
O Maheśvarī, [the mandala] may be a triangle or a hexagon; then the oblation (outside), the triangle of Śiva, the triangle of Kāma, and the triangle of the weapon.
One should visualize a triangle within a triangle and a nine-pointed star using vermilion;
for, within the Śrīcakras, one should contemplate [the deities] beginning with Naṭī and ending with Mālinī.
114) Whatever [kula] of these maidens the Kaulika may bring forth, having drawn their respective yantra, he should worship that very [maiden] therein. || 28 ||
One should place on the left side of the Śrīcakra a maiden beloved of Bhairava—her hair loose, free from shame, and adorned with all ornaments. (29)
Abounding in the splendor of every kind of erotic grace, proud with the intoxication of youth, her heart dissolved in bliss, and exceedingly captivating in her beauty. (30)
One should purify [it] with the purification mantra using the nectar-water of divine bliss;
O Goddess, having first uttered the three seed-syllables of Bālā, immediately thereafter— || 31 ||
Then, for Tripurā, one should utter "Viśvam" followed by the name at the end of the universe;
then, one should extract the pair: "Imām śaktim pavitrī kuru. (32)
O Goddess of the Gods, one should extract the pair *mama śaktiṃ* followed by the wife of Fire (*svāhā*) with this mantra; with this mantra, one should consecrate the Kāminī.
Having consecrated that young girl, one should duly install the network of nyāsas;
O Great Goddess, just as in the case of the Mātṛkās, one should then install the arrows of Kāma.
O Goddess, one should duly place the two moon-seeds, the Kāmarāja which is deluding, and then the Śakti-seed, O beloved. (35)

Having placed [the first] on the forehead and the face, and [the second] on the heart and the circle of the womb, [one employs] the arrow that agitates all, as well as that which puts all to flight. (36)
Then [he drew] the arrow of universal attraction, followed by the one that completely deludes,
and the arrow of subjugation— these are the five arrows of the Five-Arrowed One.
Having performed the placement, O Goddess, one should display these five arrow-mudrās; one should then recite the mantras over the womb-image (yonibimba), nine of which I shall now describe.
One should then utter the seed-syllable of Speech (Vāgbīja), which is Tāra (Om) and Candra (Aim), followed by Kāma (Klīm) and Śakti (Hrīm).
Then one should say "Naṭinī," and then the pair [of words] "Mahāsiddhiṃ mama dehi. (39)
One should utter the two syllables "ṭha" at the end; this mantra is dear to Naṭinī. [The sequence is:
Kālī, Kūrca, Parāśakti, Kāma, and "O beloved Kapālinī! (40).
"Release the semen; say 'yuga' at the end—this is the beloved of Fire (Svāhā).
O Goddess, this is the mantra of Kāpālikī, which brings the God of Love under control. (41)

The pair of *tāra*s (OM), green in color, the seed-syllable of the six-long-clouds (*megha-ṣaḍdīrgha-bīja*), "O you who grant desires, O courtesan, release the semen! and the beloved of the pair of fires (SVĀHĀ). 42.
This is the mantra for purifying a courtesan, beloved by all Kaulikas;
one should contemplate the Vāgbhava, Kāma, Śakti, Lakṣmī, and Parā, which begin with the Vedas. (43)
O Washerwoman, grant me the great siddhi; remove the two syllables *ṭha*.
This is the mantra for the purification of the washerwoman, which brings women of noble family under one's control. (44)
One should utter "Tāram," followed by three "Tāras," then "Vastram," and then "Nāpitāṅgane.
Then one should say "Hara" twice, "Me vighnān," and finally "Turagam" with two "Ṭhas. (45)
This mantra for the purification of a barber’s wife bestows great auspiciousness;
it consists of the beginning of the Veda, the seed-syllable of prosperity, the Tāra, Māyā, and Dhanurdhara. (46)
"O Brāhmaṇī, remember! Release, release your seed! "Grant me success, grant it! Thus did the beloved of Agni always address Hara. (47)
This is the mantra for the purification of Brāhmaṇīs, which bestows great siddhi:
Tāra, Ramā, Ramā, Tāra, and Śūdrāṇi, O you who are fond of pleasure (ratapriye). 48.
"Stop my semen and grant me success; then go to the forest.
This is the purification mantra for a Śūdra woman, which deludes women filled with desire. (49)

One should extract the two syllables "drāvaya" [from the mantra]: the *tāraka* (OM) joined with the six long vowels of Śiva, followed by the seed-syllable *maṭha*, then "gopāli," and finally the "staff of the Siddhas" (*me siddhadaṇḍam*). 50.
The great mantra ending with two *ṭha*s is the means for purifying the cowherdesses;
it consists of the grape (*mṛdvīkā*) joined with the long vowel, encapsulated by two *tāra*s (the syllable *oṃ*). || 51 ||
Having extracted [the seed-syllables] from the *Mālinī*, one should remember: "O Mālinī, bestow love upon me, [and then] the pair.
At the end, the horse and the two *ṭha*s; this is the mantra beloved by Mālinī. (52)
Thus have those purificatory mantras been described by me individually;
the Kaulika should recite them over the vulva of young girls using his hand as a rosary.
Having muttered [the mantra], one should recite the root-mantra three times into the right ear;
O Goddess of Gods, even though she is uninitiated, she then becomes as if initiated.
A hero should enjoy a consecrated and purified woman for the sake of accomplishing all goals.
[He should worship] the Self-Existent One with the mantra: "Tāraṃ vyoṣam auṣmakaṃ ca śivāya. (55)
Having worshipped the Śiva-mantra and stabilized the male organ (puṃdhvaja), one should mutter it;
then, having muttered it, one should restrain that staff (daṇḍa) by means of the mudrā known as Karabhītuṇḍa.
There, in the assembly of heroes within the Śrīcakra, the hero—whose very body is his own bliss—should satisfy his beloved, who is nourished by joy, with sexual union. 57.
O Kuleśvarī, having extracted the Praṇava while reciting the King of Mantras,
one should offer the oblation of dharma and adharma into the fire of one's own self, which is kindled by them, using the mind as the sacrificial ladle.
Reciting the mantra ending with "svāhā" and remembering the supreme Root [Mantra], I constantly offer the functions of the senses into the path of the Suṣumṇā while muttering it. (59)
The practitioner of mantra should engage in sexual union and shall attain the perfection of the mantra;
at the conclusion of the act, he should mutter the root mantra and recite this mantra once again.
Situated between two *tāras* (oṃkāras), the cause of supreme bliss,
one should grasp the sacrificial ladle of *unmanī* with the hands of light and space.
O Pārvatī, taking up the semen with the mantra ending in *svāhā*, I quickly offer it into the fire that is filled with the oil of the portions of dharma and adharma. 62.
One should satisfy the Goddess within the Śrīcakra; then one shall attain success.
Having worshipped the beloved, satisfied her, praised her, and bowed to one another, [one should proceed]. (63)
With the *saṃhāramudrā*, the mantra-practitioner should dismiss the *śaktis* and the heroes.
This is the supreme, divine, and most excellent purification of the *śaktis*. (64)
Out of affection for you, that which must be concealed from those seeking liberation has been revealed.
Thus ends the twenty-third chapter, titled "The Description of the Method for Purifying the Śakti," in the *Śrī Devī Rahasya* within the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*.
Now begins the twenty-fourth chapter.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Listen with focused attention to this supreme purification of the rosary, by which, through mere purification, the rosary becomes perfected and yields excellent results. (1)
The Goddess said:
O Lord, of what kind is the rosary made by the best of the Kaulas? What is its fruit, and how many beads does it have? You should tell me all of this.
Śrī Bhairava said:
The number ending in nine has been described; this duration extends up to twelve [repetitions].
O Goddess of the Gods, this is the secret of the Lord regarding the rosary recitation.
Savitṛ is declared to be the soul of time, O beloved, and the deity of recitation;
that Savitṛ consists of twelve aspects, and its repetition at the end [of the mantra] is prescribed.
O Mistress of the Kaulikas, the rosary is said to consist of *raviphala* [seeds] in number;
one should rotate that very rosary nine times for the sake of accomplishing the recitation (*japa*).
(p. 118) Now, O Pārvatī, out of affection for you, I shall explain the inner secret—
the entire essence of the mystery of the garland— which must not be told to just anyone.
Having fashioned one hundred and one Rudras joined with the eight Bhairavas to form the great Meru, the rosary for recitation (japamālā) is thus constructed.
One should not slay the Bhairavas with the Rudras, nor likewise the Rudras with the Bhairavas;
otherwise, there would be a loss of the recitation, according to the word of Rudra.
O Goddess, one should bind one hundred and eight superior *golaka* beads together, mouth to mouth and anus to anus, using a thread while recollecting the mantra.
O Kulasaundarī, having bound the great banner Meru above,
[one should fashion it] from conch, pearl, coral, sun-crystal, rudrākṣa, and excellent creepers.
One should regard the *meru* bead as being made of gems, gold, lotus seeds, human teeth, and all types of spherical beads (*golaka*), respectively, according to their order. || 11 ||
One should perform the purification of *naradantavirodhas* [the correct reading is *nṛdantavīrudhām*] and *meru* on a horse's tooth;
the practitioner should perform the purification of rosaries (*akṣasūtra*) over the course of six months. 12.
Then the Kaulika should recite the Great Vidyā with his rosary,
repeating it three times through each of the three strands, thus completing thirty-six spheres of the principles (tattvas).
The Kaulika should place Tāra and Meru within the garlands of principles (tattvas). O Goddess, this mature Mālā, consisting of one hundred and eight supreme [syllables], is difficult to obtain.

O Goddess, the letters of the Mātṛkā-garland, interspersed with the Praṇava [Om] in both direct and reverse order, have been described as resting upon the sacrificial oblation of the Vedas and other scriptures. (15)
One should place two *tāra*s at the end of the vowels in direct and reverse order;
likewise, one should place two *tāra*s at the end of each consonant group (*varga*) and at the beginning and end of each individual letter.
Having established Meru as the horse, one should recite with a rosary of beads numbering sixty-four;
this mālā-mantra, encapsulated by the *tāraka* [oṃ], is beloved by the Guru. (17)
O Goddess of the gods, the six Tārās born from the six-faced one [Kārttikeya] indicate the six Āmnāyas of the independent Great Lord, the God of gods. (18)
One should fashion a rosary from the seeds of the four classes of Rudrākṣas— those resembling a conch, the sun, an excellent creeper, or [the lotus]— which grants the accomplishment of all goals.
One should fashion a rosary according to the sequence of the various divisions of the Pūrvāmnāya and other traditions, adorned with pearls, coral, excellent gems, gold, and lotus seeds.

O Śivā, having joined the two hundred most excellent syllables of the *lāmānuloma* sequence with the *tāraka*, one should then join the two hundred most excellent syllables of the *brahma* sequence, O Śivā.

O Supreme Goddess, having first joined the letter *kṣa* with Sumeru according to the sequence of the letters and the hair-pores (*lomānuloma*), one should join the vowels, the consonant groups, and the letters from *ya* to *la*.
O Pārvatī, having received it from my venerable gurus of the Śrī Mahāṣoḍaśī Vidyā, I have affectionately described this garland of the syllables of Śrī Śiva.
One should join this with the thirty-six principles and the seven planets;
this is declared to be the Śivāmālā for the sake of attaining union (sāyujya) with Śiva.
One should join sixty-five syllables with forty-three Bhairavas; this is declared to be the Bhairavī Mālā.
Starting from the two ring fingers and proceeding in order through the little finger and so on,
up to the base of the index fingers— this is called the "garland of hands" (karamālā), which one should recite over its twelve joints.
O Goddess, one should mutter the mantra ten times for each [recitation] using only the hand-garland;
[the counting is done] by the two joints of the ring finger, proceeding in order from the little finger.
One should recite [the mantra] over twelve joints, from the base of the index finger to its tip;
likewise, over the four joints of the little finger and the three joints of the ring finger. (28)
Joining the single middle joint of the goddess [the ring finger] with the four [joints] of the forefinger,
the mantra-practitioner should recite the Vidyā over twelve joints.
p.
120) O Goddess, having omitted four festival days, this Śaktimālā has been described;
one should recite it according to the ritual of Durgā, from a thousand up to ten thousand times.
The world-protectors and the eight houses are present during the sixteen parvans;
in the three Pralamba mountains, three deities are concentrated.
The two cruel planets are Saturn and Mars; the two guardians of the directions are Yama and Nirṛti;
and he who is known as Kulika is considered to cause the destruction of the recitation. || 32 ||
O Goddess, the practitioner of mantra should always avoid the *kulika* during finger-recitation (*karajāpa*).
The deities residing in the hands follow the sequence beginning from the first joint of the little finger. (33)
Listen to them, O Great Goddess, as they are described by me exactly as they are:
Īśāna, Agni, Nirṛti, Vāyu, Indra, and likewise Yama. (34)
Varuṇa, Kubera, Sūrya, Soma, Budha, Guru, and those ending with Śukra, Rāhu, and Śani; and Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara. || 35 ||
O Goddess, all the deities of the hands bring about the perfection of recitation;
however, for the sake of one's own accomplishment during the time of recitation, O Goddess, one should abandon the Kulika. (36)
The Mudgara is to be known as belonging to Kulika; in the Mudgara, however, there is great danger.
Only Mahārudra possesses the power to leap over the Mudgara. (37)
One must not overstep the Kulika, Mahāketu, or Merurūpa;
otherwise, O Goddess, the practitioner of mantra incurs the curse of the deity. (38)
Now, O Goddess, I shall tell you of the purification of garlands that occurs every six months, by which even for the gods success becomes difficult to attain. (39)
At the time of purifying the rosary, the wise practitioner should go to a cremation ground and perform a bath with either ashes or water consecrated by mantras.
Having bathed there and sat down, and having performed the purification of the seat (viṣṭara-śodhana),
he then performed the rite of offering his vital breaths (prāṇārpaṇa) accompanied by the sequence of the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi).
(p. 121) Having performed the purification of the body, one should then carry out the ritual intention (*saṅkalpa*) regarding the mantra.
For the mantra used for purifying the rosary, the seer (*ṛṣi*) is Kālāgnirudra. (42)
O Great Goddess, the meter is Anuṣṭubh; the goddess is Śmaśānabhairavī, renowned as Kālarātri, who sports with a garland of severed heads.
The green seed-syllable is proclaimed, Nalinī is said to be the Śakti, and that which is called Sūrya is the Kīlaka; this is the application for the purification of the rosary.
One who knows the meaning of the Kula should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the seers, meters, deities, and so forth;
then, having performed the placement on the limbs (aṅganyāsa), preceded by the placement on the hands (karanyāsa) and other rites. (45)
Having performed the purification of the seat, one should carry out the sequence of the purification of the elements;
then, O Goddess, having established the vital breaths, one should perform the worship of the Śrīcakra.
Having performed the worship of the Yoga-pīṭha, one should purify the ritual substances and other items;
O Kulasaundari, having gratified the Lord of the Field (Kṣetreśa) and the assembly of Yoginīs.
O Goddess, one should worship the limb of dissolution at the end of the ritual;
O Mistress of the Gods, one should then mutter the mantra with the rosary according to tradition and according to the prescribed rule.
Having placed it upon the Śrīcakra, the practitioner, O Goddess of the Gods, should purify it with the nectar from the jar using the root mantra and the root of the garland mantra. 49.
I shall proclaim the garland-mantras; listen attentively, O beloved!
One should utter the syllable *tāra*, then *ramā*, then *ramā*, then *tāra*, and then the word *śaṅkhinī*. (50)
*Tāraṃ mā tāram ante'po*—this mantra is the *śaṅkhamālikā*.
*Tāraṃ lajjā yugaṃ tāraṃ muktāmālini mā yugam*. (51)
This king of mantras consists of two *ṭha* syllables; it purifies a string of pearls.
[It is joined with] the *Tāra*, the *Vadhū*, and the first of the Vedas, [and addressed] to Raudrī and Rodhramālinī. (52)
The seed-syllable of the ocean (vaṃ) and the two syllables ṭha-ṭha constitute this mantra of the Raudhra-ālikā.
Having uttered the Tāra (oṃ), the first measure, and the pair of seed-syllables known as Sūrya (raṃ-raṃ). || 53 ||
The mantra for the *arkamālā* (sun-garland) is "Haraṃ nīraṃ," which effects purification like crystal.
For the *rudrākṣamālā*, the mantra is "Tāram abdhiramāmāyāḥ sindhum. (p. 122)
"Be pure, O Goddess; the mantra for purifying the forest of rudrākṣas is:
the Tāra, the three Tāras, the Tāra, Vadhū, Tulasī, and Vaiṣṇavī. (55)
Vauṣaṭ, Vana—this is the great mantra known as the purification of Tulasī.
O Maṇimālā, enchanting one! [The mantra consists of] Tāra, Tārā, and Mṛdvīkā.
This king of mantras consists of two *ṭha* letters; it purifies the garland of jewels.
It begins with the Veda (Oṃ), followed by Kamalā (Śrīṃ), Kuntī (Hrīṃ), the seed-syllable of speech (Aiṃ), and the power of desire (Klīṃ). || 57 ||
"Suvarṇamāle śaktyāpaḥ"—this mantra is for the purification of gold.
Then "Tāraṃ," followed by "Vāyupūjyā," then "Tāraṃ," and "Padmākṣamālini. (58)
O Goddess, the green mantra consists of two *ṭha*s; it is the purifier of the lotus-seeds (*padmākṣa*).
O Śivā, there are three *tāra*s, three *mā*s, and three *kāmarāja*s.
Śiva, Śakti, a row of teeth, a garland of skulls, a snare, a bride, a garment, a forest, and a mantra—these are for the purification of human teeth. (60)
O Maheśvarī, having purified and worshipped the rosary situated upon the Śrīcakra with the individual great mantras separately, one should mutter the root mantra ten times its length.
The best of Kaulikas should worship with perfumes, unbroken grains, and flowers, [reciting]:
"Oṃ, Māle, Māle, Mahāmāle, you whose nature is the essence of all principles (sarvatattva)! [Variant readings: sarvaśakti; parāśakti]. 62.
"The fourfold goals have been entrusted to you; therefore, grant me success.
This great mantra, ending with 'svāhā', is the purifier of all rosaries. (63)
Having uttered the seed-syllable of Śiva, one should then remember: "Perform this without obstacle.
The great mantra "Me Ṭha" twice is always the purifier of the entire rosary.
Having thus purified, consecrated, and worshipped [the rosary], O beautiful lady of the family, one should take up the garland, O Goddess of gods, and recite [the mantra] at midnight. (65)
The Śrīdevī said: (p.
123) You have described many types of rosaries and their purification.
