The illustrious Bhairava said:
Now I shall proclaim for you the thousand-name Vidyā of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, which bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation in this world.
Śrī Bhairavī said:
O Blessed One, ocean of compassion, please tell me the divine thousand names of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, which bestow both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
The reality consisting of all mantras, which bestows the fruit of all worship; rich with the secrets of all scriptures, it is uniquely venerated by all the gods. (3)
The illustrious Bhairava said:
This supreme secret, this thousand names of the mantra, is the beloved of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa; in truth, it is my very essence.
O Goddess, this is a secret, most to be guarded, bestowing happiness, increasing righteousness,
enchanting Lakṣmī in this world, and granting the supreme goal in the hereafter.
It bestows the desired fruits upon the Kaulikas who abide in the Great Chinese Seat;
it pacifies the sins of minor transgressions and acts as a subduer.
It surpasses the fruits of all holy fords, bestows the fruit of all sacrifices,
is praised by all the gods, is to be accomplished, and grants the fruits of the four aims of life.
It is unspeakable for those devoid of the path and unfit to be heard by those of wicked mind;
yet the best of the Vaiṣṇavas and Kaulas may recite this Thousand Names.
O Goddess, through the instruction of the Guru, one shall attain all perfections.

For this recitation of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa Sahasranāma*, Śrī Śiva is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Triṣṭubh is the meter (*chandaḥ*), Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa is the deity (*devatā*), *Śrīṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), *Hrīṃ* is the power (*śakti*), and *Oṃ* is the pin (*kīlaka*). Its application (*viniyoga*) is for the sake of virtue, wealth, desire, and liberation during the recitation of the thousand names. The meditation (*dhyāna*):
To him who recovers the Vedas, sustains the worlds, upholds the terrestrial globe, shatters the Daityas, deceives Bali, effects the destruction of the Kṣatriyas,
conquers Rāvaṇa, wields the plow, extends compassion, and stupefies the Mlecchas.
Salutations to you, Kṛṣṇa, who possesses ten forms.
Oṃ! Lakṣmī, Viṣṇu, Īśāna, the beloved of Lakṣmī, Vināyaka, the sustainer of the universe, the lord of the universe, the progenitor of the universe, and the destroyer of the universe. || 1 ||
The noble-souled Lakṣmīrāja is the supreme self, both transcendent and immanent; he is of boundless glory, auspicious, composed of the prosperity of existence, and the source of being. || 2 ||
The great husband of Lakṣmī, the god Lakṣmī, the supreme source of Lakṣmī;
the supporter of Lakṣmī, possessing a splendor equal to that of the cloud-bearer (Indra) who holds the stream of Lakṣmī. || 3 ||
He is renowned, versatile, and alert; [here, it should be understood that only one name is marked with a line];
he is playful, fond of song, beloved by the Vidyādharas, a proponent of knowledge, and an expert in learning. || 4 ||
Wearing a silken cloth, radiant as a trumpet-flower, the fortunate Bhaga wears yellow silk;
he is the bestower of fortune, the source of splendor, and the increaser of the state of Bhṛgu. || 5 ||
Lakṣmīkauleśvara, Lakṣmīguhya, Lakṣmīvibhāvasu, Lakṣmīvīreśvara, Lakṣmīdhanya, and Lakṣmīvibhākara. || 6 ||
He is inconceivable, eternally united [with his consort], self-controlled, and the remover of fear;
he is the beloved maker of night, the destroyer of Rāhu, and the dispeller of poison.
He is steadfast, the remover of delusion, formidable, with a fearsome face, and the beloved of Bhīmā;
he is enriched by ornaments such as necklaces and bracelets, adorned with a crown, and graced by anklets.
Satisfied by the sound of tinkling bells, intent on playing the flute,
possessing a form as firm as a pillar yet moving with a graceful gait, he is beautiful-faced, victorious, and wise.
Possessing modesty and fortune, victorious over Lakṣmī, of graceful form, he is one who has brought Lakṣmī’s eyes under his control;
he is subject to the smiles of Lakṣmī and is a dancer.

He was fond of drama, a dancer, and a source of joy; he was all-knowing and possessed the essence of all things. He was like Indra, beloved by the Gopīs, and devoted to the conduct of a Vaiṣṇava. || 11 ||
He is the Self, the Supreme Self, the Self of knowledge, the Overseer of the world, and the Lord of the gods;
he is truth, the one worthy of praise, pure, eternal, the eternal Self, and the eternal Seer.
He consists of the five sounds, he is infinite, he is fond of the fivefold conduct;
his song is the fifth note, he bestows fame, and he is the destroyer of delusion. || 13 ||
The Supreme Person devoted to Lakṣmī, the bearer of the power of Lakṣmī, gratified by devotion;
the Lord of Yogis of Lakṣmī, the master of the yoga of Lakṣmī, the leader of the enjoyers. || 14 ||
The Lord of Lakṣmī, the World-Lord, Lakṣmī-possessing, and captivating to Lakṣmī;
he of inconceivable majesty, of inconceivable weightiness, and of terrible roar. || 15 ||
He is blissful, the bestower of bliss, possessing a divine form, the Lord of the lords of gods;
he is the god of love, the physician of physicians, the physician of the universe, the knower of the Vedas, and the leader of the Vedas.

He whose form is the Rigveda, who knows the chanting of the Samaveda, who is the Lord of those who enjoy the Yajurveda sacrifices, the performer of sacrifices, the protector of the self-controlled, the progenitor of the three worlds, and the undecaying one. (17)
The bestower of desires, the most excellent of those who grant wishes, he of lovely form, the Kuru;
he who is broad with prosperity, pleased by wealth, the giver of fortune and glory, the Lord of Śrī. || 118 ||
He is Lakṣmīkāma, Lakṣmaṇeśa, and Lakṣmīrāma, who is exceedingly beautiful;
he is one who does not turn back, who is free from attachment, fearless, and free from affliction.
He is without appearance, without support, untainted, and free from egoism;
he is without refuge, devoid of qualities, transcending all attributes, and the Lord of the hosts.
He whose nature is Brahman, the knower of Brahman, the nourisher, the increaser of Brahman;
the great sacrifice, the embodiment of sacrifice, the Boar, and the leader of sacrifice.
Mahārudra, Mahādeva, Mādhava, Madhusūdana; Lakṣmīnirañjana, Lakṣmīsiddhida, Siddhivardhana. || 22 ||
He whose chest bears the Śrīvatsa mark and the goddess Lakṣmī, who is adorned by Lakṣmī and the Kaustubha gem;
he who sustains all the worlds, who is self-controlled, whose weapon is the tusk of an elephant, and who is the subduer of the senses.

He whose course is immeasurable, the peaceful one, the tranquilizer, the one who possesses desire, the one who has accomplished the scriptures; he of great deeds, the great ascetic, worshipped by the auspicious Ma. || 24 ||

Excessive in his delight for the left-hand path (*vāmamārga*), he stands at the center of all modes of conduct; he is a consumer of meat, ever devoted to sensual union, and immersed in the flavors of fish and wine. (25)
He who is fond of mudrās, who delights in the bliss of union, and who is dear to the Lord of Rati;
he who is the god Aghora, the enemy of the Daityas, the conqueror of gods, and the maker of day. || 26 ||
He is the lord of the night, composed of nectar, worshipped by the nine planets;
he is the true essence, the three-eyed one, possessing the splendor of a hundred suns.
The subduer, the combative one, the left-handed, the dweller in the ocean;
he with thick arms, stout feet, long eyes, and extended forearms. || 28 ||
He who has transcended the sequence of the measure of feet, who is true to his promise, and who is eternal;
he who is the eternal source of Lakṣmī, the presiding deity of the dharma of Lakṣmī, and the lord of wealth. || 29 ||
The bestower of fortune and wealth (200), the partaker of fortune and dharma, the possessor of dharma;
the destroyer of heroes, the lotus-eyed one, the lotus-navelled one, the Lord of the world. || 30 ||
Seated upon a lotus, consisting of Brahman, filled with wonder yet free from pride; equal and possessing equal vision, yet appearing uneven with his piercing gaze.
The Lord of Ciñciṇī is meditated upon as having four forms and three forms;
he is the thousand-armed Kṣatreśa, the Brāhmaṇa, and the lord of merchants.
Pervading all, facing all directions, situated in the center of all, he is a friend;
honored by the discus, lord of crocodiles, Varuṇa, the brother of Śakra.
The destroyer of pride, he who reclines upon the serpent-bed, the bestower of boons upon the serpent-eater;
free from ego, the giver of honor, the one worthy of honor, the lord of men, and the supreme Manu.
He who is subject to Manu, the presiding lord of the immortals, the one to be perceived, the sole protector of the world;
the destroyer of grief, the unassailable, the proud, the slayer of Bali, and the annihilator of the Kali age. || 35 ||
He has auspicious limbs, eyes like wine, is a doer of good, and possesses a beautiful form;
he is the guest, the lord of the lunar days (tithis), and the one who moves within the halo of the stars.
He has four arms and four ears, he is Viśravas, the bestower of dissolution;
he brings about the end of the cosmic destruction, he is abundant, and he is dear to his mother and father. || 37 ||

He is renowned, the bearer of fortune, peaceful, and the destroyer of hundreds of doubts; he is the granter of boons to Akrūra, yet fierce, possessing the speech of a parrot, and the leader of the hosts. || 38 ||
Māra wears a golden crown and is adorned with the jewels of Māra;
he is a charming master of mantras, a counselor who grants the desired boons to those who practice mantra. || 39 ||
Lakṣmīvitarka, Lakṣmīsundara, Bandhura, Abhaya, Arjita, Sukhita, Tāra, Tārtīya, and Kārtavīryaka. || 40 ||
The bearer of the lotus of Lakṣmī, whose smile is like the moon for Lakṣmī, the boastful one, the upholder of Govardhana for Lakṣmī, the bearer of the conch for Lakṣmī, the sovereign. 41.
The refuge of the Skandas, the destroyer of enemies, the leader of the divine army;
he who is favorable, the one without a peak, the mountainous one, and the one as beautiful as the moon. (42)
Tāmasa, Sāttvika, Sabhya, (300) Somarāja, Marīcimān, Arciṣmān, Vikala, Kulyakalpa, and Sajjanapoṣaka [Ṅ: Pūjaka]. || 43 ||
Virāja, Vāmana, Veṇu, Vānara, Vārivāhana, Vālmīki, Varada, Vandī, the one worthy of praise, and he who resembles the Bandhūka flower. || 44 ||
The Lord of the castes, garlanded with letters, most beautiful with a forest garland;
Bhṛgu, the radiant-bodied one, the enjoyer, the agent, the destroyer, and the performer of a hundred sacrifices. || 45 ||
Incomparable, tender, yet fierce, he is the lover adorned with jeweled earrings; he wears Lakṣmī’s armlets and is resplendent with Lakṣmī’s jewel-garland.
Adorned with Lakṣmī’s anklets, decorated with Lakṣmī’s pearl garlands, protected by Lakṣmī’s lizard-skin finger-guards, and wearing Lakṣmī’s golden bracelets. || 47 ||
Adorned with Lakṣmī, resplendent with various ornaments of fortune,
he is decorated with the ornaments of the sciences beginning with the letter *ka* and ending with the letter *kṣa*. (48)
He is expanded by the letters beginning with 'a', adorned with the entire circle of vowels, honored among phonemes, and possessing the reality of the letters of the Mātṛkā, the Great Vidyā. (49)
The Lord of Lakṣmī and Kāma, the lover of Lakṣmī, the Lord of the immortals, the possessor of arts, the possessor of fame, the peak, and the one who took the life of Kumbhāṇḍa. || 50 ||
Keśāntaka, Kālasūtra, Kāraka, Kaṣṭahā, Kaṭhī, Krīta, Kubja, Kambudhara, Kalakaṇṭha, and Kulālaka. || 51 ||
The presiding lord of the family, the observer of family conduct, honored by the station of both Kula and Akula;
Karañjaka, Kartarīśa, Kanaka, and Kartarīkara. || 52 ||
He who is free from blemish, the ruddy goose, the dispeller of the grief of the ruddy goose;
he who is tawny, the jar, the boar, the dark-hued one, and whose mind is fixed on the lineage.
He who is surrounded by the lineage of Lakṣmī, born from the lineage of Lakṣmī, the increaser of karma;
the Lord of Kāśī of Lakṣmī, the Vināyaka of the new lord of Lakṣmī. || 54 ||
The youngest of Lakṣmī, the one who has crushed [all foes], the bestower of yoga upon the lords of yogis who possess Lakṣmī;
he whose supreme state is the void, the sky-walker, the planet, the one who moves through the sky, and the destroyer of the wicked.
He whose nature is space, who has the form of a bird, the digger, the leader of the celestial chariot;
he whose weapon is the sky, the bearer of the sword, and the destroyer of the Khañjana-bird’s gaze.
The destroyer of asses, with the braying sound of an ass, terrifying with the appearance of a *kharkhurā* bird;
he who has a hollow skull, whose gait is like that of a bird, and who is served by the lords of the sky-dwellers.

He is served by the hosts of Khecarīs, restrained by the Khaṇḍamudrā; he holds a sword in his hand, protects with a sword, is a rider [or wielder of a shield], and is adorned with ornaments of the color of the sky. (400) 58.
The Lord of Lakṣmī, whose form is the void (kha), possessing a body as radiant as Lakṣmī;
the bearer of the khaṭvāṅga of Lakṣmī, moving through the void (khecara) of Lakṣmī, anointed with the stone (aśman) of the void (kha).
He whose abode is the funeral pyre of Lakṣmī; he who is the fire that reduced Lakṣmī to ashes;
he who bestows the prosperity of Lakṣmī; he who is radiant with the light of Lakṣmī; he who is adorned by the syllable *ga*. (60)
The song of Lakṣmī, the one who utters melodies, the lord of cows, the sovereign of Gokula, the beloved of Gaṅgādhara, the assembly, the cowherd, and the increaser of fragrance. || 61 ||
He is beloved by the wind, he is sung of, he knows song, and he is fond of singing;
he is fond of garlands of *guñjā* berries, he is the teacher, he has the bull as his vehicle, and he is free from disease.
Possessing profundity, most venerable, increasing the sound of "Guru," fond of devotion to the Guru, the Gola, he who dwells upon the boulder-like rock (gaṇḍaśaila). || 63 ||
Roaring with a great sound, lord of the lineage, fond of the path of the celestial sphere, possessed of limbs;
yet bodiless, the lord of the elephant-faced one, the leader of the leaders of the Gaṇas. (64)

The bestower of boons to the lords of the Gandharvas, worshipped by those who move through the sky; free from the womb yet the carrier of the embryo, he who is to be praised and an ocean of virtues. || 65 ||
He whose body transcends all qualities, who is worthy of virtues, who sets forth the secret path;
he who is fond of secret mantras, who is to be protected, who is hidden, and who is beloved by the Guhyakas. || 66 ||
The protector of the cowherd women, the lord of the mountain, the bearer of the mountain, the treasure-trove of the world;
the beloved of Lakṣmī, the dear one, the gratified one, he whose vehicle is Lakṣmī and Garuḍa. || 67 ||
The sun is the abode of the dove of Lakṣmī, the wish-fulfilling tree of Lakṣmī, the essence of the lineage of Lakṣmī, the core of Lakṣmī, and the lord of the creeper of Lakṣmī. 68.
He is graspable by Lakṣmī, yet possesses auspicious marks; he is the son of Lakṣmī and the Ocean;
he is compassionate, composed of compassion, the one who is rubbed [with sandalwood paste], the Lord who is red with saffron (ghusṛṇa), and the Sovereign.
Consisting of compassion, the remover of sin, the compassionate Lord, the possessor of the letter *gha*;
the wish-fulfilling gem for Lakṣmī, the virtuous one, the hero of Lakṣmī, and the most excellent of men. || 70 ||
Lakṣmī, Caturbhuja, Lakṣmīviśvanātha, Vināyaka, the letter Ṅa, Anantarūpa, Jānujña, Ṅāntarūpa, Ṅāṇajña, and Ṅoṇarūpavān. || 71 ||
The Lord of the Universe, whose form is the letter *ṅa*, adorned with the syllable *ṅa*;
served by Lakṣmī, whose nature is beyond qualities (*nirguṇa*); the Sovereign of Lakṣmī, worshipped by Śivā. (72)
He is of beautiful form, beautiful gait, and beautiful appearance;
he is a source of wonder, with beautiful eyes, a beautiful face, and beautiful arms—the four-armed one.
The lord of the earth has beautiful hands, beautiful nails, and beautiful hair;
he dwells upon the funeral pyre, he is a wanderer, he is without clothing, yet the infallible one wears garments of fine Chinese silk.
He of the beautiful smile, the one with the beautiful staff, the immovable one, the one perfumed by the moon;
the moon, the lord of the digits of the moon, the one with beautiful feet, and the one who traverses the four states of existence. || 75 ||
He whose self is fourfold, whose fourth self is the Supreme, who supports the four mountain ranges;
he who reclines upon the four oceans and who has leaped across the four seas. || 76 ||
He possesses four splendors, four beds, and is the most excellent among the four heroes;
he is composed of the four Vedas, a physician, one with beautiful limbs, and one of pleasing speech.
The Supreme Lord has four faces and is worshipped by the four-faced one;
he is enriched by the splendor of the moving moon and resounds with the tinkling of moving anklets.
Resembling a moving cloud, with eyes like shimmering water-lilies, with a face like a drifting rain-cloud, and graced by the splendor of a moving cloud. || 79 ||
His golden armlets were swaying, his golden earrings were swaying;
he shone like a moving golden peak, and his golden crest was swaying.
The Lord of the Discus (Viṣṇu) has the form of the letter Ca;
he is adorned with the syllable Ca, is the end of Lakṣmī (the letter Śa), is the Great Dakṣa, is Lakṣmī-Pītāmbara (the letter Ra), and is the Thunderbolt (the letter Pa). || 81 ||
He who possesses the parasol, the bearer of the parasol, the peaceful one, the father dear to Chinnamastā,
the cutter of what is concealed, the one with a severed face, and he whose form consists of the letter 'Cha'. || 82 ||
The beloved of Lakṣmī, endowed with splendor, the lord who accomplishes prosperity;
the Lord of the World, the sustainer of the world, the creator of the world, and the abode of the world. (83)
The destroyer of the world, the conqueror, the supreme lord of the worlds;
the master of the world, the creator of the world, and the agent of the world’s dissolution. (84)
The individual soul and the supreme soul, the source of the world's prosperity, the possessor of all qualities, the one praised by the world, and the bestower of bliss upon the world. (85)
The self who is the source of the world’s contentment, endowed with compassion even toward the world’s anger, the illuminator of the world, worshipped by the Vedas, the Lord of the World. || 86 ||
Swift, accompanied by speed, the lover who bestows the grandeur of the universe;
served by the world, beloved by the world, desired by the world, and consisting of the world. || 87 ||
The yawner, the matted-haired one, the living soul, the bestower of boons upon the enemy of Jambha;
the son-in-law of the ocean, the destroyer of evil, adorned with a crown of matted locks. || 88 ||
The conqueror of enemies, the bestower of victory, the unconquerable, the maker of victory, and the scorcher of heroes;
seated upon the slopes of Lakṣmī’s breasts, he is the object of Lakṣmī’s gaze. || 89 ||
He who is adorned with tinkling ornaments, the destroyer of the wicked, the banner of victory, the scorcher of the impure,
the one who makes a ringing sound, the humming of bees, the chirping of crickets, and whose anklets produce a resonant jingling.
Lakṣmīvara (600), served by Mahālakṣmī and worshipped by the gods; he is the letter Ña, the one who delights in Ñāra, the Lord Ñeśa, possessing the form of the nectar of the syllable Ña. || 91 ||
The source of Lakṣmī’s own being, the lord of heaven, he who is worshipped by Lakṣmī, the devourer of the moon; the letter *ṭa*, the wielder of a chisel in his hand,
ending with *ṭa*, and emitting the sound *ṭīṭ*.
The god of gods, Lakṣmīdeva, whose end is Lakṣmī, the ocean of compassion;
Ṭhakura, Ṭhālaka, Ṭhāsya, the treasury of the beauty of the letter Ṭha. || 93 ||
The one joined with the syllable *ḍa* is Lakṣmīvidhu, known as Vitarka, whose banner is Vainateya; he is the banner, the ḍamaru-drum, and the lord of the terrible (*ḍāmara*).
The Lord of Lakṣmī, whose body is pure, the foremost leader of the leaders of Lakṣmī;
he who possesses speech beginning with the letter *ḍa*, who is to be pierced by the *ḍhakka* drum, and the slayer of the demon *Ḍhakka*. (95)
The conqueror of Lakṣmī, the granter of victory, the Lord of Lakṣmī, he whose hair hangs down;
the stability of the world for Lakṣmī, the friend of Lakṣmī, and the wielder of the mace for Lakṣmī. || 96 ||
He whose end is the letter *ṇa*, who is adorned with the color *ṇa*, whose lord is *ṇa*, and who is perfected by the nectar of the *ṇa*-syllable;
he is Lakṣmī-Dāmodara, the life-breath of Lakṣmī, and the bearer of the lotus (the wheel) of Lakṣmī.
He is the equal, the unequal, and the greatly incomparable one; his mind is adorned with a multitude of stars;
he is the lord of Tulasī, the knower of Tantra, and the leader of Mantras. || 98 ||
He who bestows the fruit of austerity, whose form is copper-colored, and who possesses incomparable valor;
he who is the essence of the *tuṭi* moment, whose movement is the *tuṭi*, the ascetic, and the lover of ascetics. || 99 ||
He is the cool-rayed moon, born from the cold, adorned with frost-like rays;
he is served by the fourth [state], possesses the splendor of a balance, and is adorned with the letter 'ta'.
The Lord of Lakṣmī, whose weapon is the conch, whose hair is adorned by Lakṣmī, who bears your color;
the ancient one, with stout limbs, served by Sthāṇu, and the maker of the sound "stha. || 101 ||
The one who loves the essence of the cooking pot, the massive one, the Lord of Sthakāra, the Sovereign;
the Lord of Lakṣmī and Jīva, the Bearer of Lakṣmī, and Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha. || 102 ||
Compassionate, lord of heaven, skillful, celestial, and free from deceit;
the destroyer of poverty, the remover of suffering, the one who brings an end to misfortune, and the merciful. 102.
The humble one, the lord of the humble, the guileless, the one who desires the rise of his beloved;
the giver of gifts, the bestower of the fruits of giving, the destroyer of the lords of the Danujas. || 103 ||
The slayer of the Daityas, the destroyer of the pride of the Daityas, the one who brings about the destruction of the arrogant and their followers,
he who is fond of his wife, the long-nailed one, and the annihilator of the wicked Asuras.
The God of gods, worthy of praise through his glory, adorned with the syllable *da*;
he who bestows fortune and mercy, the God of fortune, and the treasure-house of fortune and mercy. (105)
The giver of wealth, the creator of wealth, the praiseworthy, the region of wealth, the bestower of wealth;
he who possesses fortitude, who possesses righteousness, who is righteous, and who is skilled in the performance of righteous deeds. || 106 ||
The overseer of Dharma, the overseer of wealth, white-complexioned, steadfast, and wealthy;
wise, the bestower of fortitude, expert in righteousness, and honored by the Giver of Wealth (Kubera). || 107 ||
The possessor of Lakṣmī, the husband of Mahālakṣmī, the mind-born child of Lakṣmī;
the ever-new, the fresh, the humble, the dancer, and he who is pleased by the dance. || 108 ||
The Elephant, the best of elephants and mountains, accessible to men, the ornament of the Nagas;
the Man-Lion, the best of men, the Infinite, Nara-Narayana, the Ever-New. 109.
The king of serpents, the lord of serpents, the fire that is the banner of the end of serpents, mounted upon a mountain, possessing a deep navel, served by Nandin, and the lord of dancers. || 110 ||
The lotus-eyed one, though worthy of praise by men, is the leader and the lord of serpents;
he sports on the banks of the Narmadā, his eyes like the petals of a lotus.
The lord of men, worshiped by kings, reclining on the serpent, the best of mountains;
Nārāyaṇa, the stainless, whose form consists of nine syllables, the self-possessed one.
Lakṣmīnāga, Nagadhara, Lakṣmīnātha, Narūpavān, Puṣpapriya, Puṣpaśayyāśayāna, and Puṣpaśekhara. || 113 ||
Puṣpadhanvā, Pradyumna, Puṣpeṣu, and Puṣpapūjita;
he who is worthy of worship, the supreme purifier, Parameṣṭhī, and Pitāmaha. || 114 ||
The supreme state, the supreme merit, the supreme lifespan, higher than the highest;
the husband of the daughter of the ocean and the shore, the Supreme Lord, the supreme light. (115)
Bestower of merit, performer of merit, purified, honored by the Purāṇas and Āgamas;
the Ancient Person, full-bodied, broad-chested, and one who has conquered the senses. || 116 ||
Clad in yellow garments, wearing a yellow garland, yellow in color, Parāṅkuśa;
Patraga, the renowned, the traveler, the wayfarer, the one who delights travelers. (117)
The ancient one praised by the citizens, adorned with the syllable *pa*, whose yellow garment is Lakṣmī, who is yellowed by Lakṣmī, and who is supremely devoted to Lakṣmī. 118.

The fruit, the excellent serpent, the prosperous one, the maker of fruit, the giver of fruit, the serpent reclining upon a bed of serpents, and the ornament of the nectar-syllable *pha*—(800)—these are the meanings of the syllable *pha*. (119)
He is a child, the wise one, the follower of Buddha, a kinsman, a relative, and the Lord;
he is the kinsman of Lakṣmī, the kinsman of Mahālakṣmī, and endowed with auspicious marks.

Bhadrapada, Bhāsvarāṅga, Bhāskara, Bhānu, the Imperishable (Avyaya), the Treasure of Light (Bhānidhi), the Blessed Lord (Bhagavān), the Fearful (Bhīta), the Destroyer of Fear (Bhītihā), and the Bestower of Fearlessness (Abhayadāyaka). || 121 ||
He who removes the fear of Lakṣmī, he who bestows the fear of Lakṣmī, the destroyer of fear;
the Great Lord, the highly honored, the great minister, the one who delights the mind.
Manohārī, Mahāśānta, Mahātejā, Manojava, Mahotsāhī, Mādhava, Māyādhārī, and Manonmana. || 123 ||
He is the destroyer of pride, the slayer of Mura, and the bestower of the fruits desired by men; he rejoices in the fragrance of wine and is entirely free from the delusion of Māra.
The great rise of Lakṣmī, the one honored by Lakṣmī, the one languid from the intoxication of Lakṣmī;
the delighter of Yaśodā, the one going, the illustrious, and the warrior-soldier. || 125 ||
Yaśodhara, Yama, the Yogin who bestows yoga upon yogins, the Lord of Yoga, worshipful through sacrifice, the Yādava, and the Sovereign of the Yādavas. || 126 ||
He who is pleased by sacrifice, the treasury of sacrifice, the officiating priest, and the beloved of those who perform sacrifices;
he who is the sacrificer, the sacrifice itself, born of glory, and possessing the form of the syllable "Ya."
The performer of Lakṣmī’s sacrifice, the one who commands Lakṣmī, he who is served by the sacrifice;
the King, the Lord of Ramā, the Divine, Rāma, the King, the dust of passion.
He who creates the night, who is dark-hued, who bestows joy upon Rāma;
the lover of Revatī, the lord of the full moon, the possessor of all arts. (129)
Lakṣmīrāma, Mahālakṣmīrāja, Lakṣmītrivikrama, Lākṣāruṇa, Lītarākṣa, Lalajjihva, and Latāpati. || 130 ||

The Lord is the lord of Laṅkā, the dancer, the one who has transcended *la*, the beloved of Lambodara, the supreme, the one merged with Lakṣmī, the color of a bee, the letter *la* in form, and the Sovereign. || 131 ||
The one who has vomited out the host of enemies, the boar, the embodied one, the sovereign, Viṣṇu, the lord of the earth, the giver of wealth, and the ruler of the world. || 132 ||
Vāgīśvara, Veṇuhasta, Vetāla, Virasa, Viyat, Vidvān, Viśālanayana, Vikāra, Avikṛti, and Pumān. (133)
Reflective, disciplined, honored as the king of vidyās, and discerning;
eloquent, rooted in the reed-thicket, talkative, and the leader of heroes. || 134 ||
Lakṣmīvarāha, Vīreśa, Lakṣmīvīra, Vanecara, Śaṅkara, Śrīdhara, Śrīla, Śramī, and Śītāṃśuśītala. || 135 ||
The moon-crested one, the autumnal elephant, Śambhu, the destroyer of Śaṅkha;
Śakra, the destroyer of enemies, the bringer of death to his foes, the auspicious Śiva. (136)
Lakṣmīśiva, Śrīpati, Śrīvara, the bestower of Lakṣmī and Śiva;
he whose form is the sixteen vowels and who is adorned with sixteen syllables. || 137 ||
He is the knower of the six-limbed science, adorned with the syllable *ṣa*;
he bears the six limbs of Lakṣmī and sustains the sixteen syllables of Lakṣmī. || 138 ||
He is the beautiful one, whose dwelling is heaven, the Lord of all, facing every direction;
he who possesses seven horses, whose conduct is ever-righteous, the virtuous one, beloved by holy men. || 139 ||
Sarama, Sarala, Sāla, Sukhī,
Sukhavirdhana,
Lord of the earth consisting of seven islands, and Leader of the seven oceans. 140.
Consisting of the seven musical notes, dwelling in the depths of the seven netherworlds, endowed with the quality of goodness (sattva), possessed of being, and the remover of all evils. (141)
The destroyer of all enemies, the slayer of all asuras, the destroyer of all sins, and the one worshipped by all the gods. || 142 ||
The eternal Lakṣmī, the source of Lakṣmī, worshipped by the virtuous;
Hari, Hara, Hari-Hara, the Lord of Gold (Hāṭakeśa), and the remover of obstinacy (Haṭāpaha). || 143 ||
He is turmeric-colored, smiling, charming, and has green eyes;
he is Lakṣmī’s Hari, Hṛṣīkeśa, the wearer of Lakṣmī’s necklace, and the sinless one.
He is the patient one, the lord of patience, the protector, the master of forbearance, and the possessor of the syllable *kṣa*.
He is the creator of moments, the lord of the night, the one endowed with forgiveness, and the one who agitated the asuras.
Endowed with fortune and forbearance, the protector of fortune, bearing the color of the lord of fortune;
infinite and worshipped by the infinite, he is also the primordial source, resplendent like the sun. (146)
The Lord who is the beloved of Indirā, the Sovereign of formidable form, radiant with heat, the destroyer of debt, whose alphabet is resplendent with the letter *Ṛ*. || 147 ||
The letter *ḷ* is the color [of the syllable], while the vowel *ḹ* is endowed with the sound *e*;
it is accompanied by sovereignty (*aiśvarya*) and likewise honored by the mad-sounding vowel (*au*). || 148 ||
The syllable *Aṃ* and likewise the syllable *Aḥ*, whose nature is adorned with vowels;
*Oṃ hrīṃ hasauḥ hrīṃ śrīṃ*—the Lord Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa is Śiva. (1000) || 149 ||
Thus, O Goddess, this thousand names consisting of mantra is the supreme reality,
the abode of knowledge extending from the letter 'A' to the letter 'Kṣa'.
It embodies all sacred fords and is worshipped by all gods and dānavas;
it is equal to thousands of horse sacrifices and tens of millions of vājapeya sacrifices.
O Goddess, ten thousand cāndrāyaṇa fasts and numerous great gifts do not equal even a sixteenth part of the thousand names of the mantra. (152)
At midnight, the hero, seated upon the chest of the Śakti, should recite [the mantra] softly;
he too beholds in a dream the God who is dear to Lakṣmī and the granter of boons.
Having performed the Mahācīna worship, one should recite [the mantra] once during the Vīrārcana;
one shall obtain the fruit of a hundred thousand years of worship. || 154 ||
Whoever recites this once, having performed worship in the presence of the Guru, shall become a glorious adept and in the next world shall go to heaven. || 155 ||
It bestows merit, grants boons, is worthy of praise, and is the supreme means for attaining the sacred ford;
it grants yoga to yogins and is worshipful, increasing the enjoyments of those who seek enjoyment. || 156 ||
It pacifies the diseases of the sick, destroys all evil deeds,
is most dear to the Vaiṣṇavas, and bestows the supreme goal upon those who are liberated.
O Pārvatī, it must not be given nor heard by one who is not a disciple;
one should not accept without a gift, nor should one give without a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
By giving this away or by taking it [from another], the loss of spiritual accomplishment for both is certain.
This thousand names of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa has been recounted to you by me out of devotion to you; it must be guarded like one's own private organ. 159.
Thus ends the thirty-ninth chapter, titled "The Description of the Thousand Names of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa," in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*, within the *Śrī Devī Rahasya*.
(p. 239) Now begins the fortieth chapter.
Śrī Bhairava said:
Today I shall proclaim to you the mantra and hymn of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, which is the very essence of all reality, a secret that bestows the supreme goal.
O Great Goddess, this fifth limb reveals the ultimate truth;
it is praised by the scriptures of the four Vedas and is the sole cause of both worldly enjoyment and liberation. || 2 ||
O Pārvatī, this is the secret, most guarded reality of the King of Mantras;
it is the constant cause of the essence of the bliss of consciousness for the Kaulikas.

Of this King of Hymns, the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa Mantra, Śiva is the Seer (ṛṣi), Triṣṭubh is the Meter (chandaḥ), Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa is the Deity (devatā), Śrīṃ is the Seed-syllable (bīja), Hrīṃ is the Power (śakti), and Oṃ is the Bolt (kīlaka). Its application (viniyoga) is for the purpose of attaining worldly enjoyment and liberation through recitation. The Meditation (dhyāna):
I worship Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, whose face is like the full moon, who wears yellow garments, who is seated upon a lotus, who is embraced by Lakṣmī, and who possesses four arms.

I worship the Lord, the ancient Puruṣa, the all-pervading one— wearing a crown, adorned with earrings and necklaces, seated upon a lotus, with a dark-blue countenance and four arms, clad in yellow garments, holding a conch, mace, lotus, and discus in his hands. || 5 ||
If a human being, intent on serving the lotus feet of Hari, should chant the *praṇava*,
he will surely go to the abode of the Destroyer of Danujas, filled with supreme bliss and free from pride.
If a person, overcome by passion and casting off fear of the crooked paths of the Smṛtis and Āgamas, mutters the seed-syllable of Parā on the ground for recitation;
May he become the Lord of Kaula, a rain-cloud to the forest fire of all enemies, and rejoice together with celestial women in groves of divine trees. || 7 ||
He who, filled with bliss, recites this seedless great mantra shall become one whose very nature is bliss, beloved by Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa.
If the lord of the Kaulas recites at the conclusion of his worship the mantra-king, the reality that is the seed of all manifestations,
he— whose feet are worshipped by gods and asuras— goes to the supreme state unattainable by any of the deities.
He who mentally recites the seedless mantra, which is the ultimate reality and whose sole nature is pure being,
becomes skilled in the destruction of the desires of lustful women and the remover of the great pride of his enemies.
He who, with his mind fixed upon the lotus feet of Hari, recites before the yantra the mantra that is the seed-syllable of Ramā and consists of the words of his own name as its crown,
shall have his feet radiant with the mass of rays from the rows of jewels shimmering on the crests of kings.
The lord of the mountain-keepers is victorious. || 11 ||

He who recites at night and at dawn the mantra "Nārāyaṇāya," which is the seed of the supreme reality, becomes like a rain-cloud to the forest-fire of his enemies; he shall be one who removes the heavy pride of the learned with his words.

He who, intent on meditating upon Viśvaṃbhara, recites the Viśvasāra mantra within his heart at dawn, shall conquer his enemies and attain the fortune of universal sovereignty on earth; thereafter, when his life has departed, he shall attain heaven.

I worship the Infinite Lord, who is composed of supreme bliss, seated upon a lotus within a dot, [surrounded by] a square, a circle, a sixteen-spoked wheel, an eight-petaled lotus, and a thousand-spoked wheel. (14)
Whoever recites this mantra-filled hymn, dear to Nārāyaṇa, in the heart at dawn, Lakṣmī will certainly come under the sway of that pure-minded person who is devoted to sacred learning. 15.
Thus, O Īśānī, this supreme hymn consisting of the root mantra has been declared by me through devotion to you; it must not be disclosed to those who merely seek liberation.
This five-limbed [hymn] of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, from beginning to end, has been described to you; it is rich in worshipful forms, secret, and must be guarded like one's own womb.
The Goddess said:
"O Blessed One, knower of all principles, devoted to the welfare of all the worlds!
O Śaṅkara, I have been purchased by you with this narration."
Having today heard this supreme five-limbed [ritual] of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, I have attained supreme bliss; I am your servant—what more can I say? (19)
The illustrious Bhairava said:
"O Goddess, having churned through the Vedas and the Tantras, I have told you this entire secret that is concealed within all the Tantras."
O Pārvatī, this five-limbed reality, which is difficult even for the gods to attain and is worshipped by the Vaiṣṇavas, is a secret of all the worlds and my very own essence.
This must not be disclosed, it must not be spoken, and it must not be given to a wicked person;
it should be given to a disciple who is peaceful and devoted to the guru.
To one who is charitable and virtuous, devoted, and delighting in the Kaula path;
to one established in the state of Mahācīna, a high-souled Vaiṣṇava. (23)
"By giving this, O Goddess, one obtains liberation, which bestows happiness upon devotees.
242) Thus, this is the supreme reality—the reality beyond all realities, higher than the highest. (24)
"It is to be guarded, it is secret, and it is to be concealed; such is the command of the Supreme Lord.
Thus ends the fortieth chapter, titled "The Narrative of the Hymn to Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa," in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*, within the *Śrī Devī Rahasya*. 40.
The *Lakṣmīnārāyaṇapañcāṅga* is completed.
Now begins the forty-first chapter.
The Five-Limbed Ritual Manual (Pañcāṅga) of Mṛtyuñjaya.
Śrī Bhairava said:
On the delightful peak of Kailāsa, resplendent with garlands of jewels...
It was filled with various trees and creepers, and adorned with various flowers.
Adorned with stone pavilions inlaid with various jewels, its quarters made resonant by the sweet singing of kinnarīs. || 2 ||
He beheld the Blessed Lord Umānātha seated, attended by Umā,
and accompanied by Brahmā, Upendra, Indra, Candra, Ārka, Guru, and Śukra.
Served by hosts of Brahman-sages, Vasus, Siddhas, Gaṇas, and Gandharvas,
he is adorned with a crescent moon upon his crown and bears a trident and a khaṭvāṅga staff. (4)
He is peaceful, with hands granting boons and fearlessness, and is equipped with a spear, arrows, and a sword;
he holds a scimitar and a shield, and possesses weapons such as a noose and a tomara.
He held a *bhiṇḍipāla* weapon and carried spears and iron clubs;
he had maces and hand-drums in his hands, and was equipped with *śataghnīs* and discuses.
The god has eighteen arms, his body adorned with ashes;
he is sky-clad, large-eyed, three-eyed, and five-faced.
The universe is blissful and joyful, and the Lord is the leader of the universe;
his form is embraced by Gaurī as he chants and laughs.
Mahādeva Maheśvara, adorned with serpent ornaments,
Śambhu seated in the lotus posture, who is compassionate toward those who have come for refuge.
Seeing his serene countenance, Pārvatī bowed down, rose up,
and addressed the Supreme Lord, the God, with sweet words.
The Śrī Devī said:
O Blessed One, he who is the god Śiva, the supreme Mahāmṛtyuñjaya, the Primordial Lord (Ādinātha), the protector of the world, the leader of initiation, and the Sovereign (Īśvara). || 11 ||
Previously, you described Mahādeva, the Lord of Consciousness who transcends all attributes;
now [describe] that very God, whose nature is the Supreme Brahman.
"I wish to hear the five-limbed [mantra]; you should speak it to me, O Lord.
Śrī Bhairava said:
"Of the Supreme Lord, the Divine Mahāmṛtyuñjaya, for you..."
Out of devotion, I shall describe the five-limbed [rite]; it must not be told to just anyone.
He who guards the Paṭala, the Paddhati, the Varma, the Sahasranāman-mantra, and the Stotra—these five constituent parts—is a true practitioner (sādhaka). || 14 ||
Therein, first I shall speak of the chapter (*paṭala*) which is dear to the leader of initiation (*dīkṣānāyaka*);
it is secret, supremely secret, and must be guarded by those seeking liberation. (15)
O Great Goddess, for the sake of increasing the fruit of initiation,
I shall explain the extraction of the mantra— which is divine, brings happiness, and is to be accomplished— so that it may be perfected.

The Tāra (Oṃ), the Hṛdaya (Namaḥ), Bhavānī-tika (Śivāyai), the Śiva-śara (Hrīṃ), the Maṇḍūka-bīja (Hūṃ), then "Pālaya Pālaya" (Protect, Protect), again the Śakti (Aiṃ), Śiva (Hrīṃ), and the Śāktika (Klīṃ),
followed by the Hṛdaya (Namaḥ) adorned with the Tāraka (Oṃ)— this has been declared by me for the sake of devotion to You.
This mantra, beloved by the leader of initiation, is the wish-fulfilling gem of the three worlds. || 17 ||

For him there is no abundance of obstacles, nor any impairment by accomplished practitioners, those yet to be accomplished, or enemies; there is no physical exhaustion or weakness, nor any confusion regarding conduct or observances. (18)
There is not even the slightest suspicion of the five defects, nor are there creditor and debtor;
it is solely the increaser of supreme bliss and the crusher of enemies. (119)
This mantra is the king of mantra-kings, a celestial tree that yields the fruit of initiation;
yet this king of mantras does not attain success without the performance of preliminary rites (puraskriyā).
Therefore, for the sake of performing the preliminary consecration (*puraścaraṇa*), one should petition the Guru regarding Śiva;
he who performs the preliminary consecration of this mantra by means of the Guru’s hand [is empowered]. (21)
O Maheśvarī, for him this king of mantra-kings shall be like a wish-fulfilling tree; he should perform the preliminary rite (puraścaryā) one hundred thousand times, or half of that.
One should set a limit of one hundred thousand [recitations], never less than that;
from ten parts of the recitation comes the fire-oblation (homa), and from ten parts of that comes the libation (tarpaṇa).
The cleansing [of the mantra] should be performed with a tenth part of that, and the feeding [of Brahmins] with a tenth part of that;
having thus completed the preparatory rite (puraścaryā) of the mantra, the practitioner— || 24 ||
O Goddess, having given a sacrificial fee to the guru according to one's means, O Mistress, then the recitation (japa) shall become the bestower of all perfections. || 25 ||
Otherwise, even for one with a virtuous mind, there would be no accomplishment of initiation.
O Pārvatī, I shall now describe the procedure for drawing the yantra of the God of gods. (26)
It is divine, enchanting all, and the fulfiller of all hopes;
it is adorned with a point, a triangle, a hexagon, a circle, and an eight-petaled lotus.
The Śaiva Śrīcakra is said to consist of three circles and the abode of the Earth;
O Pārvatī, I shall now describe the limb of dissolution belonging to this king of yantras.
Merely by hearing which, one obtains the fruit of initiation;
there, in the auspicious subterranean chamber, are the ten guardians of the directions, beginning with Indra, equipped with their weapons.
In the three Āraṇas, there are also the Gurus of the divine, perfected, and human lineages:
Asitāṅga, Ruru, Caṇḍa, Krodheśa, and Unmattabhairava. (30)
O Śivā, Kapālīśa, the one named Bhīṣaṇa, and Saṃhāreśa as the eighth—
these are to be worshipped on the eight petals by practitioners seeking liberation.
One should worship Kālāgnirudra, Netreśa, Viśvanātha, Maheśvara, Sadyojāta, and Vāmadeva within the wombs of desire (kāmayoni).
O Goddess, one should worship Kāmeśvara, Mahākāla, and the god Svacchandabhairava within the triangle, starting from the southeast, east, and northeast corners.
Within the Bindu, O Śivā, one should meditate upon the god Mṛtyuñjaya together with his own Śakti,
as well as Amṛteśvara, Īśāna, Īśvara, and Bhuvaneśvara.
O Īśānī, the best of practitioners should worship the three-sectioned noose, the excellent vessel of nectar, and the pearl rosary upon the body of the Goddess. (35)

Having worshipped according to the prescribed rites, O Goddess, with perfumes, unbroken grains, and flowers, as well as with incense, lamps, food offerings, betel leaves, umbrellas, and chowries; || 36 ||
This limb of dissolution has been declared; it is hidden in all tantras.
O Goddess, it bestows all accomplishments and must be kept especially secret. (37)
O Great Goddess, for this mantra, the seer is Sakahola, the metre is Gāyatrī, and the deity is likewise Mahācamasapadādika. (38)
Rudra, the Great God Mahādeva, is the presiding deity;
O Goddess, the seed-syllable is the Praṇava, and the power is the seed-syllable known as Hṛjjā.

O Goddess, the Kīlaka is in the autumn, the Diśbandha is in the northeast, and the Astra is in the northeast; thus the application of this Vidyā among the four aims of life has been proclaimed. || 40 ||

The best of practitioners should perform the placement of the vital breath (prāṇanyāsa) using the six long vowels together with the seed-syllables of Tāra (oṃ), hṛdaya (namaḥ), jaḥ, śara (vauṣaṭ), and bīja (huṃ) upon the two hands and the limbs beginning with the heart. 41.

One should perform three breath-control exercises (prāṇāyāma) using only the root and other seed-syllables; and one should perform the ritual sipping of water (ācamana) by means of the three principles (tattva), beginning with Ātman, Vidyā, and Śiva.
Now I shall indeed proclaim the meditation upon the Lord of the Gods of gods, by which mere meditation the practitioner of mantra attains the state of Śiva. (43)
[One should meditate upon the deity] whose eyes are the moon, sun, and fire; whose face is smiling; who is situated within a pair of lotuses;
whose hands shine with the *mudrā* (known as the *trikhaṇḍā*), a noose, nectar, and a rosary; and who possesses the luster of the moon.

One should meditate upon Paśupati, the conqueror of death, whose body is bathed in nectar flowing from ten million moons, who is resplendent with ornaments such as necklaces, and who deludes the entire universe with his beauty. (44)

One should meditate upon the person to be protected (sādhya) as situated there, within the exceedingly vast forehead of Rudra, which rests in the center of the lunar disc; even one who has encountered death lives on.
Thus, O Īśānī, this object of accomplishment, adorned with the seed-syllable and mantra-parts of the Supreme, resides on the forehead of Rudra; it must be kept especially secret.
I shall describe the eight applications which are difficult to obtain and bestow the ultimate goal; by performing these, the practitioner of mantra becomes like Bhairava himself. (47)

Stambhana (paralysis), mohana (delusion), as well as māraṇa (killing) and ākarṣaṇa (attraction); likewise vaśīkāra (subjugation), uccāṭana (eradication), śāntika (pacification), and pauṣṭika (nourishment). || 48 ||
(247) I shall describe the means for accomplishing these, which is the sole cause of all happiness;
by the mere accomplishment of which, every success shall be attained in the Kali age. (49)
Having bathed in the Ravau [Tīrtha] and performed his daily rites at Śiva,
he should recite the mantra ten thousand times, preceded by the formal vow (saṃkalpa).
By offering ten parts of ghee, barley, and gold seeds,
the immobilization of speakers, thieves, and even the sun occurs.
Having worshipped the Lord of Gods under the moon, one should recite the mantra ten thousand times;
the fire-oblation (homa) should be performed with ghee, barley, rice, and vegetable leaves, consisting of one-tenth of that number.
By means of that very ash-mark (tilaka), the enchantment of the worlds shall occur.
Having bathed for auspiciousness, the practitioner should go to the cremation ground circle. (53)
One should recite the mantra ten thousand times; the fire-oblation (homa) is performed with ghee, along with bilva fruits mixed with śrīparṇī and madhuka, and with ciñcinī fruits.
O Goddess, within ten days the enemy, though equal to me, shall meet his death.
Having bathed on a Wednesday, one should worship the Lord before the Śrīcakra and recite the mantra.
One should offer ten thousand oblations with clarified butter, *śatāvarī*, *trikaṇṭaka*, and *bilvaka* as the tenth part; this will result in the attraction of women.
Having bathed in the Guru [tīrtha], one should recite the supreme Vidyā ten thousand times;
a fire sacrifice (homa) should then be performed with ghee, lotus seeds, and sandalwood in a tenth part of that number.
O Śivā, by means of Āragvadha, Kaṇā, Varā, and Amṛtā, the enemy—
whether he be a king, wealthy, or a heroic conqueror— shall fall into servitude.
In the Śukra cremation ground, Vīreśa should recite the mantra ten thousand times;
at the edge of the funeral pyre, he should recite the root-vidyā and offer clarified butter as its tenth part as an oblation.
One will certainly cause the eradication of enemies, including the maṇḍūka and śambhūka,
by bathing on a Saturday, performing worship, and likewise reciting the vidyā ten thousand times.
By offering honey, clarified butter, milk, clay, eggplant, tender śādvala grass, and dhattūra flowers, complete pacification of all evils arises. (61)
At all times and on every occasion, one should recite [the mantra] ten thousand times;
the fire-oblation (homa) should be performed with ghee, milk-rice, and lotuses, numbering one-tenth of that amount.
With the meat of goats, deer, tortoises, and boars, along with cooked rice,
for the ancestors, the deities, the kings, and likewise for the sick; || 63 ||
By offering a tenth part according to the prescribed rule, great nourishment is produced.
Thus, this supreme reality of this mantra has been declared by me;
it must not be given to those who are not devotees, but should be guarded like one's own private parts. 64.
Thus ends the forty-first chapter, the description of the Mṛtyuñjaya-paṭala, in the Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra, within the Śrī Devī-rahasya.
Now begins the forty-second chapter.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Now, O Goddess, I shall describe the supreme manual of worship, which consists of both prose and verse, is divine, and bestows the fruit of ten million sacrifices. (1)
If one worships Śiva with devotion without first performing the morning rites,
that worship is fruitless, just like a ritual action devoid of purity.
Having risen during the *brāhmī* hour, and having assumed the bound lotus posture (*baddhapadmāsana*),
one should meditate upon one’s own Guru situated within the pericarp of a thousand-petaled, downward-facing lotus located at the crown of one's head.

I bow to the glorious Guru, supreme bliss, whose form is his own inherent joy; by whose mere presence the body becomes one with the bliss of consciousness. Having thus prostrated before the glorious Guru—two-armed, peaceful, with lotus-hands granting boons and fearlessness—
His lotus-face is like the full moon; he is smiling and joined with Śakti.
One should meditate upon the God, who is clothed in white garments, adorned with various ornaments, joyful and delighted, and seated upon a lotus throne.

Having meditated thus and prostrated like a staff, one should recite the *haṃsa* mantra twenty-one thousand six hundred times as the root *ajāpī* recitation, and having recited the root mantra according to one's capacity,
one should offer the recitation to the Guru. Having received his permission and come outside, one should discard impurities and so forth, and [perform] what is prescribed for one's caste.

Having taken up purification materials, one should go to a river or similar place and clean the teeth with the mantra: *oṃ klīṃ kāmadevāya sarvajanamanoharāya namaḥ*. Then, performing three mouthfuls of water (gaṇḍūṣa) with the mantra: *gaṃ glauṃ dantaśodhanaśaktyai namaḥ*, one should fetch earth, divide it into three portions, and [apply the first portion] with the mantra: *oṃ prīṃ mṛttikāyai namaḥ*.

Having thus consecrated [the deity] and empowered [it] with the root mantra, and having performed the bathing that removes impurities, one should invoke the sacred waters from the solar orb using the *aṅkuśa-mudrā* with the following: "Oṃ gāṃ gīṃ! O Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Godāvarī, Sarasvatī, Narmadā, Sindhu, and Kāverī—be present in these waters! Then, having thrown earth into the water, [one proceeds].

"Furthermore, O Lord of Devas, Bhairava, who is easily accessible through devotion along with your retinue: O Deva, as long as I shall offer libations to you, so long remain here. Having thus visualized a triangle in the water, having invoked the Deity there with clay, and having displayed the mudrās, one should perform *prāṇāyāma* with the root mantra and emerge three times from head to foot. Then—

One should offer three *arghya* libations to the Sun: "Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ, this *arghya* is for the venerable Sun, accompanied by the Power of Radiance (*prakāśāśakti*); obeisance. Having offered the three *arghya*s and then having provided another garment, one should perform three *prāṇāyāma*s preceded by the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) on the hands and limbs. As follows:
Drink the breath through the *iḍā* for sixty-four [cycles] plus sixteen;
exhale it slowly through the *piṅgalā*, ten by ten, ten by ten, and two more.

Having performed inhalation (pūraka) sixteen times, retention (kumbhaka) sixty-four times, and exhalation (recaka) thirty-two times—repeating this three times—one should sip water while reciting: "Oṃ juṃ saḥ, I purify the principle of the self (ātmatattva), svāhā! Oṃ juṃ saḥ, I purify the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva), svāhā! Oṃ juṃ saḥ, I purify the principle of Śiva (śivatattva), svāhā! Then, having performed the six-limbed ritual (ṣaḍaṅga), one should place water in the left hand.
Having held it with the *tattvamudrā* and covered it, one should empower it seven times with the mantra of the five elements— *yaṃ raṃ vaṃ laṃ haṃ*— and then hold it in the right hand.

Joining the left ring finger with the thumb, one should sprinkle one's own head ten times (or seventeen times, according to manuscript Ṅ) while reciting the root mantra, using water droplets drawn up by that [thumb]. Then, placing it again in the left hand,
one draws it inward through the *iḍā* [left nostril], washes away all evil within the body, and [expels] that water through the *piṅgalā* [right nostril].

Holding the turbid water in his right hand, he should strike it against the vajra-stone prepared on his left side; having thus performed the *aghamarṣaṇa*, he should perform the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) as before, reciting: *oṃ juṃ saḥ paramahaṃsāya vidmahe so haṃ saḥ*.

"Let us meditate upon Mṛtyuñjaya; Oṃ, may Amṛteśvara, who is *juṃ*, inspire us. Having thus recited this ten times and having recited the root mantra (*mūlamantra*) as many times as possible, one should offer three *arghya* oblations to the Goddess and the God with the Gāyatrī:
"Oṃ juṃ saḥ, this is your *arghya*, salutation to Mṛtyuñjaya together with his limbs and accompanied by Amṛteśvarī."

Likewise, as before, having offered three *arghya* oblations to the Sun, one should visualize a square and a triangle within the water; while reciting the root mantra seven times (or seventeen times, according to manuscript Ṅ), one should offer libations (*tarpaṇa*) to the Lord together with the Goddess.
[The formula is: "O Mṛtyuñjaya, together with your limbs, vehicles, weapons, retinue, and the Goddess..."
Having satisfied [the deity] with the words "May the Blessed One be satisfied," having satisfied each member of the retinue with a single handful [of water],

and having satisfied all beings from Brahmā down to the smallest insect, he should perform the libation for his ancestors and others; then, as before, he should withdraw the deity into his own heart by means of the *saṃhāra-mudrā*, while contemplating, "I am Śiva."
"He shall come to the sacrificial pavilion"—this is the rule for the twilight ritual (saṃdhyā).

Then, having returned home and washed one's feet, one should worship the deities of the doorway. Having cleansed the door with "Hūṃ Phaṭ," one should worship as follows: at the top, "Oṃ Gāṃ Gaṇeśāya Namaḥ"; then on the left and right in sequence, "Mahālakṣmyai Namaḥ," "Sarasvatyai Namaḥ," "Gaṅgāyai Namaḥ," "Yamunāyai Namaḥ," and "Dhātre Namaḥ."

Having worshipped with the words, "Homage to Vidhātṛ; homage to Nanda; homage to Sunanda; homage to Pracaṇḍa; homage to Caṇḍa; homage to Kṣetrapāla; homage to Vetāla; homage to Agnivetāla," one should offer a flower upon that seat with the mantra for the seat: "To Anantāsana..."

Salutations to the one on the stainless seat; salutations to the one on the lotus seat. Oṃ! O Earth, by you the worlds are supported; O Goddess, you are supported by Viṣṇu. You, in turn, support me in this world; make my seat pure. Having struck the ground three times with the left heel, [one should say]: "May those beings depart who are here."

"May those beings established on the earth who create obstacles perish by the command of Śiva. Having thus dispelled the obstacles and bound the ten directions with "HŪM AGHORĀYA PHAṬ," one should perform the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi).
Having made the formal resolve (saṅkalpa), "Today I shall perform the purification of the elements," [one should place] "Obeisance to the Gurus" on the left and on the right...

Having offered salutations, saying "Salutation to Gaṇeśa in front; salutation to Śiva at the back; salutation to Kṣetrapāla," and having performed three breath-controls (prāṇāyāma) with the Praṇava, [one should recite] "Hūṃ" from the Mūlādhāra...

Having raised Kuṇḍalinī by way of the path of Suṣumṇā, and having taken up the life-force (jīva) residing in the heart, one should visualize it as having reached the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra); then, with the mantra "Haṃsa," one should unite it with Brahman. Thereafter, one should contemplate the earth from the feet up to the knees, and water from the knees up to the navel.

Having dissolved fire from the navel to the heart, air from the heart to the space between the eyebrows, and space from the space between the eyebrows to the dvādaśānta, each into the next; then dissolve space into the ego-principle (ahaṅkāra), the ego-principle into the Great Principle (mahattattva), and that into primordial nature (prakṛti).
Having dissolved my own self into Brahman, whose nature is Being-Consciousness-Bliss, and having contemplated myself as consisting of Brahman:
"I am the Divine; there is no other. I am indeed Brahman, not subject to sorrow.
I am the form of Being-Consciousness-Bliss, possessing a nature that is eternally liberated."
Having meditated thus, one should visualize the Person of Sin (pāpapuruṣa) within the right thigh of one's own body:
having the murder of a Brahmin for its head, the theft of gold for its two arms,
the drinking of intoxicants associated with its heart, and the violation of the Guru’s bed for its two hips.
The pair of words associated with that [term] causes the downfall of limbs and minor members;
it has the down of secondary sins and blood-red beard and eyes.
One should contemplate the black sin within the belly as holding a sword and a shield.

Having thus meditated and visualized the body as defiled and impure, one should render it free from sin by means of the mantras of the five elements preceded by breath control (prāṇāyāma). [One should do so] from the heart and other centers up to the space between the eyebrows by means of the seed-syllable *yaṃ*.
Having filled the breath with air recited sixteen times, one should dry up the sin;

then, having kindled the fire located within from the navel to the heart by means of the fire-seed syllable (*raṃ*) recited sixty-four times, one should burn away the sin; and [one should fill] the water from the knees to the navel with the Varuṇa-seed syllable *vaṃ*.

Having taken up the sins with water over which the mantra has been recited thirty-two times, and having dissolved them by reciting the earth-seed syllable *laṃ* sixteen times while contemplating the earth from the feet up to the knees, one should meditate on it as having become a solid mass identical to oneself; then, having manifested consciousness by reciting the space-seed syllable *haṃ* once, one should contemplate [the self] as consisting of consciousness and bliss.
Having generated one's own body, one should sustain the vital breaths; this is the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi).
"Oṃ juṃ saḥ, salutation to Śiva, the self of the vital breaths"—having thus offered a flower upon one's own heart, [one recites]:
"Āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ yaṃ raṃ vaṃ laṃ haṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ haṃsaḥ so 'haṃ juṃ saḥ oṃ.
My vital breaths are here, my vital breaths; my life-force is established here; all my senses [are here]."

Having retained the vital breaths with the mantra: "May my speech, mind, eyes, ears, tongue, nose, and life-breaths come right here and remain happily for a long time, Svāhā," and having inscribed the root mantra in his own heart, worshipped Śiva along with Śivā, and contemplated "I am Śiva," he should perform the ritual resolve (*mantra-saṅkalpa*) for this [rite]. Of this—
For the mantra of the worship of Śrī Mahāmṛtyuñjaya (p.
the seer is Mahācamasakahola, the meter is Devīgāyatrī, and the deity is the Great God, Śrī Mṛtyuñjaya Rudra.

The deity is Oṃ, the seed-syllable (bīja) is Juṃ, the power (śakti) is Saḥ, and the pin (kīlaka) is the purpose of dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa; this is the application (viniyoga) for the worship. Now, the ritual placement (nyāsa): salutation to the sage Mahācamasakahola on the head;
salutation to the divine Gāyatrī metre on the face.
Salutation to the deity Śrī Mṛtyuñjaya Rudra Mahādeva at the heart; Oṃ, salutation to the seed-syllable at the navel;
Juṃ, salutation to the power (śakti) at the secret place; Saḥ, salutation to the pin (kīlaka) at the feet;
salutation to the application (viniyoga) for recitation (or worship) at all limbs. Now, the ritual placement on the hands (karanyāsa): Oṃ, salutation to both thumbs.
*Juṃ* to the two index fingers, *namaḥ*; *saḥ* to the two middle fingers, *namaḥ*; *oṃ* to the two ring fingers, *namaḥ*;

*juṃ* to the two little fingers, *namaḥ*; *saḥ* to the palms and backs of the hands, *namaḥ*. Thus is the ritual placement on the hands (*karanyāsa*). Now follows the ritual placement of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*): *oṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*; *juṃ* to the head, *svāhā*; *saḥ* [to the crown].
Vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock; Oṃ, Huṃ to the armor; Vauṣaṭ to the eyes; Saḥ, Phaṭ to the weapon.

Now, the Mātṛkā-nyāsa: Aṃ, salutation to the head. Āṃ, salutation to the circumference of the mouth. Iṃ, salutation to the right eye. Īṃ, to the left eye. Uṃ, to the right ear. Ūṃ, to the left ear. Ṛṃ, to the right nostril. Ṝṃ, to the left nostril. Ḷṃ, to the right cheek. Ḹṃ, to the left cheek. Eṃ, to the upper lip.

Aiṃ on the lower lip; Oṃ on the upper row of teeth; Auṃ on the lower row of teeth; Aṃ on the forehead; Aḥ on the tongue [Aṃ on the head, Aḥ within the mouth]; Kaṃ at the root of the right arm; Khaṃ at the elbow; Gaṃ at the wrist; Ghaṃ at the base of the fingers; Ṅaṃ at the tips of the fingers; Caṃ...

*Chaṃ* at the base of the left arm; *jaṃ* at the elbow; *jhaṃ* at the wrist; *ñaṃ* at the base of the fingers; *ñam* at the tips of the fingers. *Ṭaṃ* at the base of the right foot; *ṭhaṃ* at the knee; *ḍaṃ* at the ankle; *ḍhaṃ* at the base of the toes; *ṇaṃ* at the tips of the toes. *Taṃ* at the base of the left foot; *thaṃ* at the knee; *daṃ* at the ankle; *dhaṃ*.

Aṃ at the base of the fingers; Naṃ at the tips of the fingers; Paṃ on the right side; Phaṃ on the left side; Baṃ on the back; Bhaṃ at the navel; Maṃ in the abdomen; Yaṃ in the heart; Raṃ on the right shoulder; Laṃ at the crown of the head; Vaṃ on the left shoulder; Śaṃ from the heart to the tips of the right hand; Ṣaṃ.

From the heart to the tips of the left hand: *saṃ*; from the heart to the tips of the right foot: *haṃ*; from the heart to the tips of the left foot: *laṃ*; from the feet to the top of the head: *kṣaṃ namaḥ*. Thus one should perform the pervasion three times; this is the Mātṛkā-nyāsa.

Oṃ hsauḥ aṃ, salutation to Śrīkaṇṭha and Pūrṇodarī on the head. Oṃ hsauḥ āṃ, salutation to Ananteśa and Virajā on the face. Oṃ hsauḥ iṃ, salutation to Sūkṣmeśa and Śālmalī on the right eye. Oṃ hsauḥ īṃ, salutation to Trimūrtīśa and Lolākṣī on the left eye.
p. 253) Oṃ hsauḥ uṃ, obeisance to Amareśa and Vartulākṣī on the right ear. Oṃ hsauḥ ūṃ, obeisance to Arghyeśa and Dīrghaghoṇā on the left ear. Oṃ hsauḥ ṛṃ...
Oṃ hsauḥ ṛṃ; salutations to Bhāvabhūti and Dīrghamukhī in the right nostril. Oṃ hsauḥ ṝṃ; salutations to Tithīśa and Gomukhī in the left nostril. Oṃ hsauḥ ḷṃ;
salutations to Sthāṇukeśa and Dīrghajihvā on the right cheek. Oṃ hsauḥ ḹṃ...
Oṃ hsauḥ aiṃ: Homage to Hareśa and Kuṇḍodarī on the left cheek. Oṃ hsauḥ eṃ:
Homage to Jhiṇṭhīśa and Ūrdhvakeśī on the upper lip. Oṃ hsauḥ aiṃ:
Homage to Bhautikeśa and Vikṛtamukhī on the lower lip. Oṃ hsauḥ oṃ.

*Oṃ hsauḥ auṃ*, obeisance to Sadyojāteśa and Jvālāmukhī on the upper row of teeth. *Oṃ hsauḥ auṃ*, obeisance to Anugraheśa and Ulkāmukhī on the lower row of teeth. *Oṃ hsauḥ aṃ*, obeisance to Akrūreśa and Śrīmukhī on the forehead (or the head).
Oṃ hsauḥ aḥ, salutation to Mahāseneśa and Vidyāmukhī on the tongue [in the interior of the mouth]. Oṃ hsauḥ kaṃ, salutation to Krodhīśa and Mahākālī at the base of the right arm.
Oṃ hsauḥ khaṃ, salutation to Caṇḍīśa and Sarasvatī at the elbow. Oṃ hsauḥ gaṃ...
Salutation to Pañcānaneśa and Sarvasiddhi at the wrist;
Oṃ hsauḥ ghaṃ, salutation to Śivottameśa and Trilokavidyā at the base of the fingers; Oṃ hsauḥ ṅaṃ, salutation to Ekarudreśa and Mantraśakti at the tips of the fingers.

Oṃ hsauḥ caṃ, salutation to Kūrmeśa and Ātmaśakti at the base of the left arm; oṃ hsauḥ chaṃ, salutation to Ekanetreśa and Bhūtamātṛ at the elbow; oṃ hsauḥ jaṃ, salutation to Caturānaneśa and Lambodarī at the wrist; oṃ hsauḥ jhaṃ...

*Oṃ* Ajeśa-Drāviṇībhyāṃ namaḥ, on the base of the fingers. *Oṃ* Ñaṃ Śarveśa-Nāgarībhyāṃ namaḥ, on the tips of the fingers. *Oṃ* Ṭaṃ Someśa-Khecarībhyāṃ namaḥ, on the base of the right foot. *Oṃ* Ṭhaṃ Lāṅgalīśa-Mañjarībhyāṃ namaḥ, on the knee. *Oṃ* Ḍaṃ Dāhakeśa-Rūpiṇībhyāṃ [namaḥ].

[Ṅ: Dārukeśa] *Namaḥ* to the ankles. 2. *Ḍhaṃ*, *namaḥ* to Ardhanārīśa and Vīriṇī at the bases of the toes. 2. *Ṇaṃ*, *namaḥ* to Umākānteśa and Kākodarī at the tips of the toes. 2. *Taṃ*, *namaḥ* to Āṣāḍhīśa and Pūtanā at the base of the left foot. 2. *Thaṃ*...

*Daṃ* to Daṇḍīśa and Bhadrakālī, salutation to the knees; *2*. *Dhaṃ* to Adrīśa and Yoginī, salutation to the ankles; *2*. *Naṃ* to Mīneśa and Śaṅkhinī, salutation to the bases of the fingers; *2*. *Paṃ* to Lohiteśa and Kālarātri, salutation to the tips of the fingers; *2*.
On the right side: 2. Phaṃ, salutation to Śikhīśa and Kubjinī.
On the left side: 2. Baṃ, salutation to Chagalāṇḍeśa and Kapardinī. On the back: 2.
Bhaṃ, salutation to Dviraṇḍeśa and Vajriṇī.
At the navel: *namaḥ* to Maṃ Mahākāleśa and Jayā. At the belly: *namaḥ* to Yaṃ Tvagātman and Kapālīśa-Sumukhī. At the heart: *namaḥ* to Raṃ Asṛgātman...

Salutation to Bhujaṅgeśa and Revatī on the right shoulder. 2. Laṃ, salutation to Pinākīśa and Mādhavī, the essences of flesh, on the crown of the head. 2. Vaṃ, salutation to Khaḍgīśa and Vāruṇī, the essences of fat, on the left shoulder. 2. Śaṃ, [salutation] to the essences of bone...

*Vakeśavāyavībhyāṃ namaḥ*—from the heart to the tips of the right hand. 2. *Ṣaṃ majjātmabhyāṃ śveteśarakṣobandhinībhyāṃ namaḥ*—from the heart to the tips of the left hand. 2. *Saṃ śukrātmabhyāṃ bhṛgvīśasahajābhyāṃ namaḥ*—from the heart to the tips of the right foot. 2.

Haṃ, salutation to the Prāṇa and Ātman, Nakulīśa and Lakṣmī, from the heart to the tips of the left feet. Laṃ, salutation to the Śakti and Ātman, Śiva and Vyāpinī, from the feet to the top of the head. Kṣaḥ, salutation to the Krodha and Ātman, Saṃvarteśa and Mahāmāyā, from the head...
"Up to the feet" refers to the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the *mātṛkā* beginning with Śrīkaṇṭha.

Now, the ritual placement of the digits (*kalānyāsa*): Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ hsauḥ, salutation to the All-Knowing One with both thumbs. 4. Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ hsauḥ, salutation to the one garlanded with nectar-flames with both index fingers. 4. Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ hsauḥ, salutation to the one with a blazing crest of fire with both middle fingers. 4. Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ hsauḥ, salutation to the wielder of the thunderbolt, whose hand holds the thunderbolt, with both ring fingers. 4. Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ hsauḥ, salutation to the one with a blazing crest of fire with both middle fingers. 4. Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ hsauḥ, salutation to the wielder of the thunderbolt, whose hand holds the thunderbolt, with both ring fingers. 4. Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ hsauḥ, salutation to the one garlanded with nectar-flames with both index fingers. 4. Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ hsauḥ, salutation to the All-Knowing One with both thumbs.
To Aluptaśakti, salutation with both little fingers; to Paśupati, salutation with the palms and backs of the hands. Thus is the ritual placement on the hands (karanyāsa).

Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ sauḥ, salutation to the Heart, the Omniscient One. 4. Svāhā to the Head, garlanded with nectar-flames. 4. Vaṣaṭ to the Crest, possessing flaming crests of fire. 4. Huṃ to the Armor, the wielder of the thunderbolt with the thunderbolt in hand. 4. Vauṣaṭ to the Two Eyes, whose power is undiminished. 4. Phaṭ to the Weapon, the Lord of Beasts (Paśupati). Thus.
The ritual placement (nyāsa) of the heart and other [limbs].

Oṃ juṃ saḥ, to Śiva, whose essence is the Nivṛtti-kalā, [I offer] salutation with both thumbs. 3. To Sadāśiva, whose essence is the Pratiṣṭhā-kalā, [I offer] salutation with both index fingers. 3. To Īśvara, whose essence is the Vidyā-kalā, [I offer] salutation with both middle fingers. 3. To Mahārudra, whose essence is the Śānti-kalā, [I offer] salutation with both ring fingers. 3.

Salutation to Viṣṇu, whose self is the Śāntyatīta-kalā, with both little fingers (kaniṣṭhikā). Salutation to the Supreme Brahman, whose self is the Jyotis-kalā, with both palms and backs of the hands. Thus is the ritual placement on the hands (karanyāsa).
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, salutation to Śiva, the essence of the Nivṛtti-kalā, for the heart;
svāhā to Sadāśiva, the essence of the Pratiṣṭhā-kalā, for the head; vaṣaṭ to Īśvara, the essence of the Vidyā-kalā, for the crest-lock (śikhā). 3. 3. 3.

To Mahārudra, the self of the Śāntikā-kalā, for the armor (kavaca), *huṃ*. To Viṣṇu, the self of the Śāntyatītā-kalā, for the two eyes, *vauṣaṭ*. To the Supreme Brahman, the self of the Jyotis-kalā, for the weapon (astra), *phaṭ*. Thus ends the ritual placement of the kalās (*kalānyāsa*).

Oṃ juṃ saḥ, salutation to Netranātha with the two thumbs (aṅguṣṭha). Haṃ saḥ, salutation to Bhagavannetra with the two index fingers (tarjanī). Māṃ pālaya pālaya, salutation to Somasūryāgninetra with the two middle fingers (madhyamā). So haṃ saḥ, salutation to Netranātha with the two ring fingers (anāmikā). Juṃ oṃ, salutation to Bhagavannetra.

To the two little fingers, *namaḥ*. *Oṃ juṃ saḥ haṃsaḥ māṃ pālaya pālaya sohaṃ saḥ juṃ oṃ*, to the one whose eyes are the Moon, Sun, and Fire, to the palms and backs of the hands, *namaḥ*. Thus is the six-limbed assignment (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*). This concludes the assignment of the eyes (*netranyāsa*).

Oṃ, salutation to the head; Juṃ, between the eyebrows; Saḥ, to the mouth; Haṃ, to the throat; Saḥ, to the heart; Māṃ, to the two hands; Pāṃ, to the two breasts; Laṃ, to the belly; Yaṃ, to the two sides; Pāṃ, to the back; Laṃ, to the navel; Yaṃ, to the penis; Soṃ, to the two knees; Haṃ, to the two shanks; Saḥ, to the two feet; Juṃ.
From the feet up to the head, and from the head down to the feet—thus one should perform the pervasion three times;
this is the placement of the root mantra (*mūlamantranyāsa*).
One should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) of Īśāna and Tatpuruṣa, whose natures are joined with Aghora, together with Sadyojāta, Īśa, and Vāmeśa.

Thus is the teaching of Śiva. *Oṃ* at the *mūlādhāra*; *juṃ* between the eyebrows; *saḥ* at the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*). Having performed this ritual placement (*nyāsa*) according to one’s capacity and having meditated upon the divine body, one should offer salutation at the heart with *oṃ juṃ saḥ amṛteśvarapīṭhāya namaḥ*. Having worshipped in the heart with perfumes, unbroken rice, and flowers, [one recites] *oṃ juṃ saḥ*.

"Hamsa! Salutation to the Yoga-pīṭha [consisting of] Śrī Kālāgnirudra, Mūlaprakṛti, Kūrma, Ananta, Varāha, Pṛthivī, Sudhārṇava, and the rest. Having thus worshipped within one's own heart and having formed the Amṛtīkaraṇa-mudrā, one places the flower contained within the Padma-mudrā and [visualizes] Kuṇḍalinī from the Mūlādhāra.

Having raised [the consciousness]— which flashes like ten million lightning bolts, shines like ten million suns, is as invincible as ten million fires, and is as cool as ten million moons— and which is shaped like the flame of a lamp, along the path of the *suṣumṇā* into the immortal Lord (*amṛteśvara*) situated within the path of Brahman (*brahmapatha*), one should unite it with Him.

Having satiated [the deity] with a stream of nectar falling from the lunar maṇḍala, and having brought [the deity] back into one's own heart and restored him to his own place, one should meditate upon the Lord while contemplating, "I am Śiva," having become one whose body is composed of nectar.
May he whose crest-jewel is the moon, who carries a jar of nectar in his palm,
who is enclosed within the embrace of the nectar-like radiance [of Lakṣmī], who bears streams of nectar,
whose beautiful body is composed of nectar-rays, and who is the companion of the Fortune of Nectar, protect me.
May the Conqueror of Death, who rains down a stream of nectar, gladden us day after day.
Having thus meditated upon the Deity and worshipped with mental offerings, one should perform the installation of the water-pot (*kalaśa*).

Having drawn a triangle, a hexagon, a circle, and a square on one's left, and having displayed the conch-gesture (*śaṅkhamudrā*), one should worship it with the root mantra, saying: "Oṃ *raṃ*, obeisance to the fire-mandala consisting of ten kalās."

Having worshipped the support (*ādhāra*) and established it, and having placed the vessel upon that support, one worships within the vessel with the mantra: "Oṃ, obeisance to the solar orb (*arkamaṇḍala*), consisting of twelve digits (*kalā*). Then, having filled it with water, one worships it with the mantra: "Sauḥ, obeisance to the lunar orb (*somamaṇḍala*), consisting of sixteen digits. There, [one should invoke] with the hook-gesture (*aṅkuśamudrā*).

Having invoked the sacred waters (*tīrtha*) with the mantra beginning, "Oṃ gāṃ gīṃ Gaṅge ca Yamune caiva Godāvari Sarasvati | Narmade Sindhu Kāveri, be present in this water," and having consecrated it eight times with the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*),
he should display the cow-mudrā (*dhenumudrā*), the womb-mudrā (*yonimudrā*), and the vase-mudrā (*kalaśamudrā*), and protect it by snapping his fingers while reciting "phaṭ."

Having veiled [the deity] with "Hūṃ" and displayed the conch, discus, and womb mudrās, one should prostrate. By the mere sight of the conch, what need is there to mention its touch? Sins go to dissolution like snow at the rising of the sun.
Thus ends the procedure for the general *arghya*.
To the right of the general *arghya*, having fashioned a mandala consisting of a dot (*bindu*), a triangle, a hexagon, a circle, and a square,
one should worship the four squares with the mantra "Salutation to Kāmarūpa, Uḍḍīyāna, Jālandhara, and Pūrṇagiri-pīṭha. Then,
having worshipped the six-limbed mantras (*ṣaḍaṅga-mantra*) in the hexagons, and having worshipped the three seed-syllables (*bīja*) in the triangle.

Having worshipped the *bindu* with the root mantra, one should place the washed base (*ādhāra*) while reciting: "Oṃ raṃ, obeisance to the solar disc consisting of ten digits. Then, having placed the jar (*kalaśa*) with the *kumbha-mudrā* while reciting: "Aṃ, obeisance to the lunar disc consisting of twelve digits," one should [place] therein [the fire] while reciting: "Oṃ jvāṃ jvīṃ jvūṃ jvaiṃ jvauṃ jvaḥ saḥ."

Having filled the jar with the substance of supreme bliss (*paramānanda-dravya*) and so forth by pouring a stream [of liquid] while reciting "Salutation to Amṛteśvarabhairava, the Conqueror of Death" (*mṛtyuñjaya*) either with the root mantra (*mūla*) or the root-vidyā (*mūlavidyā*) using the *tattvamudrā*,
one should worship it with perfumes, unbroken rice, and flowers, reciting: "Oṃ sauḥ, salutation to the lunar mandala (*somamaṇḍala*), whose essence consists of sixteen digits."
Having bound the ten directions with the mantra "haṃsaḥ," protected them with finger-snaps,
veiled [the area] with "hūṃ," sprinkled [it] with "namaḥ," and recited the root mantra ten times, one should display the Amṛta-mudrā while reciting:
"Oṃ aṃ āṃ īṃ oṃ juṃ saḥ, O Immortal One, O Source of Immortality, O Showerer of Nectar!"
"Amṛtaṃ srāvaya 2 oṃ juṃ saḥ amṛteśvaryai namaḥ"— having recited this ten times,
[then] oṃ juṃ saḥ (p. 257).

O Goddess, born from the solar disc, born from the abode of Varuṇa, whose essence is the seed-syllable *Amā*—may [this person] be released from the curse of Śukra. Oṃ juṃ saḥ! If the *praṇava*, the seed-syllable of the gods, consists of the bliss of Brahman, by that truth, O Queen of Gods, may the sin of killing a Brahmin be dispelled.

Oṃ juṃ saḥ. The Supreme Brahman alone is eternal, consisting of both the gross and the subtle. By that [power], I destroy for you the sin of Brahmin-slaughter arising from the *kaca* [hair]. Oṃ juṃ saḥ. You are liberated from the curse of Brahmā;
you are released from the curse of Viṣṇu; you are freed from the curse of Rudra—be pure now! 3.

"Pavamāna is supreme bliss; Pavamāna is the supreme essence; Pavamāna is supreme knowledge—with that, I purify you. Having recited this three times, and having recited "Oṃ hasakṣamalavarayūṃ ānandeśvarabhairavāya vauṣaṭ" ten times, [one recites] "sahakṣamalavarayūṃ".

Having recited "surādevyai vauṣaṭ" ten times and having recited the root mantra three times, one should invoke the sacred waters (*tīrthas*) with the *aṅkuśa* mudrā while reciting "Oṃ, Gaṅge ca Yamune caiva... and so forth; then, having raised Kuṇḍalinī in the form of light, pierced the six wheels (*ṣaṭcakra*), and united her with the venerable Lord Paramaśiva residing at the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*).

Having joined them together and contemplated "Haṃsaḥ So'haṃ Svāhā," one should fill the flask with the stream of nectar issuing from the nostrils— which carries the nectar of bliss arising from their state of aesthetic fusion (sāmarasya)— and, having meditated upon it as consisting of nectar, worship it with perfumes, unbroken rice grains, and flowers.
Having displayed the mudrās of the cow-source and the fish, one should prostrate; this is the purification of the substances.
Then, reciting "Oṃ juṃ saḥ haṃsaḥ,

vauṣaṭ to the worship materials of the Great Mṛtyuñjaya, the Lord Śrī Amṛteśvarī, and the Supreme Lord of Nectar," one takes nectar from the *kalaśa* vessel; then [recites] "Oṃ juṃ saḥ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ saḥ juṃ oṃ."
