One should cremate it with [the mantra] recited sixteen times. One should flood it with a shower of nectar from the moon dripping down, using "vaṃ," the seed-syllable of nectar, recited sixteen times. And using "laṃ," the seed-syllable of Indra, recited sixteen times.

Having meditated upon one's own self as a condensed mass, and having performed the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*) by contemplating one's own self as a divine body through the single recitation of the space-seed syllable *haṃ*, one should perform the consecration of the vital breaths (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*).
*Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ āṃ kroṃ sohaṃ haṃsaḥ mama prāṇā iha prāṇāḥ.* (Thus nine times.)
"May my life-force remain here. May all my senses remain here.
May my speech, mind, eyes, skin, ears, tongue, nose, and breath come to this very place and remain happily for a long time.
Svāhā! This is the procedure for the installation of the vital breaths (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*). Having thus established the vital breaths, as before...

Having performed the six-limbed ritual (ṣaḍaṅga) and sipped water for purification, one should meditate upon the Root Goddess: "I worship Durgā, the three-eyed Bhavānī, who stands upon a seat consisting of a buffalo situated on a drop (bindu), surrounded by a lotus, the six flavors, the six seasons, and the eight serpents; her arms are adorned with a complexion like the tips of durvā grass leaves."
The seed-syllable of Vilāsī.

Having meditated thus, performed the root and limb nyāsas, and having either visualized or drawn with eight kinds of fragrant paste the Śrīcakra—consisting of four gates, three circles, an eight-petaled lotus, a circle, a hexagon, a triangle, and a bindu—one should perform the worship of the pedestal (pīṭhapūjā) as follows: "Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Maṇḍūka. (2)

Salutation to Kālāgnirudra. 2. Salutation to Mūlaprakṛti. 2. Salutation to Ādhāraśakti. 2. Salutation to Kūrma. 2. To Ananta. 2. To Varāha. 2. To Pṛthivī. Having thus worshipped each one above the other, [one should worship] 2. to Sudhārṇava in the center. 2.

Salutation to the island consisting of nine regions, resplendent with the nine gems. Salutation to the region of rubies. Salutation to the Golden Mountain. Salutation to the Nandana garden. Salutation to the Kalpa forest. Salutation to the Lotus forest. Salutation to the ground inlaid with various jewels. Salutation to the pavilion of wish-fulfilling gems. Salutation.

To the jeweled altar (*vedikā*) inlaid with nine gems; 2. To the lion-throne (*siṃhāsana*) of jewels; in its center: 2. To the thousand-petaled lotus (*sahasrārapadma*); 2. To the petals consisting of *prakṛti*; 2. To the filaments (*kesara*) consisting of *vikṛti*; in its center: 2. To the pericarp (*karṇikā*) adorned with the eight seed-syllables; at its side: 2. To Dharma; 2. [To Artha].
To Jñāna (Knowledge) 2; to Vairāgya (Dispassion) 2; to Aiśvarya (Sovereignty) 2. To the left: to Adharma (Unrighteousness) 2; to Ajñāna (Ignorance) 2;
to Avairāgya (Lack of Dispassion) 2; to Anaiśvarya (Lack of Sovereignty) 2. In the center: *saṃ* to Sattva (Purity) 2; *raṃ* to Rajas (Passion) 2.
Having recited "taṃ tamase" and having uttered the root-mantra (mūlavidyā), [one says] "salutation to the one seated upon the buffalo" (mahiṣāsanāya namaḥ).

Having recited the root-mantra and having uttered the Mātṛkās, [one says] "salutation to the venerable Yogapīṭha" (śrīyogapīṭhāya namaḥ); having thus worshipped, one should perform the worship of the vessel (pātrārcana).

Then, having worshipped one's own body with perfumes and other offerings, one should fashion there on one's left a circular, triangular, and square mandala; having honored it with the root mantra, [one recites]: "Oṃ, obeisance to the root mantra for the general *arghya* of Durgā. Raṃ, obeisance to the fire-mandala consisting of ten kalās."

Having thus worshipped that mandala on the support with the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga), and having placed there a conch washed with the weapon-mantra (astra), one worships the conch with: "Oṃ, obeisance to the solar mandala consisting of twelve kalās. Then, having filled it with the reverse-order Mātṛkā, [one worships] with: "Sauḥ, obeisance to the lunar mandala consisting of sixteen kalās."

Having thus worshipped and consecrated [the water] eight times with the root mantra, one should invoke the sacred ford (tīrtha) with the verse beginning "O Gaṅgā and Yamunā," and contemplate it as pure; this is the general procedure for the arghya offering.

To the left of the general *arghya*, having fashioned a mandala consisting of a triangle, hexagon, circle, and square, one should worship that mandala with the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*). Then, reciting the root mantra, [one says]: "Obeisance to the mandala of the auspicious Durgā’s pitcher. Thereafter, having worshipped it as before with the root mantra, one should place a tripod (*tripādikā*) washed with the weapon-mantra (*astra*) therein.
Having worshipped with "Raṃ, obeisance to the fire-maṇḍala consisting of ten kalās," and having placed there the pitcher washed with the weapon-mantra (astra),

one worships it with unbroken rice and flowers, saying "Aṃ, obeisance to the sun-maṇḍala consisting of twelve kalās," and then [offers] from there a stream of nectar using the ring finger and the thumb.
Having filled the *kalaśa*, worship it with: "Oṃ *sauḥ*, obeisance to the lunar maṇḍala consisting of sixteen digits.
Then recite: "Oṃ hrīṃ dāṃ dīṃ dūṃ daiṃ dauṃ daḥ duṃ aṃ, O nectar! O source of nectar! O showerer of nectar!
Cause the nectar to flow forth! Release the curse of Śukra! Release it! Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ, to the Goddess Surā, vauṣaṭ!"

Having consecrated it seven times with "vaṣaṭ," and having worshipped with "duṃ hrīṃ oṃ hasakṣamalavarayū~— salutation to the sandals of Ānandabhairava and Surādevī," and having displayed the Dhenu and Yoni mudrās, [one recites]: "O Goddess, born from the solar orb, arisen from the abode of Varuṇa, consisting of the seed-syllable Amā!"

May you be liberated from the curse of Śukra. The Supreme Brahman alone is eternal, consisting of both the gross and the subtle; by that, I destroy the sin of Brahmin-slaughter arising from your hair. Pavamāna is supreme bliss;
Pavamāna is the supreme essence; Pavamāna is supreme knowledge; by that, I purify you.

If the *praṇava* is the seed of the Vedas and consists of the bliss of Brahman, by that truth, O Goddess, may your sin of killing a Brahmin be removed. Released from the curse of Kṛṣṇa, released from the curse of Brahmā, and released from the curse of the sage, become pure.
"Always [now]. Having thus fully worshipped the flask, having displayed the cow, womb, and fish mudrās, one should cover it with the Garuḍa mudrā; this is the purification of the substances.

Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ. Having descended as an incarnation by Hari, for the sake of the welfare of the Kaulikas and because the world was oppressed by the powerful Kali, the Lord himself became a Fish in order to please Śrī Durgā. Having thus displayed the three mudrās, one should purify the purification. Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ.

"Salutations indeed to the one who has assumed the forms of the goat and so forth, ending with the cow; for the sake of the offering to the God and Goddess, become purified now. Having recited the root mantra three times, one should display the three mudrās.
"Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ! At the time of the worship of Śrī Durgā, whatever fragrant substances are here at present..."

"These purifiers are to be offered to the gods here for the sake of accomplishment. Reciting this root mantra three times, one should display the three mudrās over everything; such is the procedure for the flask and other vessels.

Then, having meditated upon the Śrī Devī Nīlakaṇṭheśī seated on the lap of Ānandabhairava by means of the root mantra (mūla), and having invoked her with the root mantra, one should worship the Śrīcakra. There, one should offer water for the feet (pādya), the respectful offering (arghya), water for sipping (ācamanīya), and so forth, using the root mantra.
One should present the honey-mixture (madhuparka), water for sipping, and other offerings to the God and Goddess by means of the root mantra.

One should perform the visualization. Having offered the food offering (*naivedya*) with the root mantra, having offered the water for sipping (*ācamanīya*) with "Namaḥ," and having offered three mouthfuls of water (*gaṇḍūṣa*), one should present betel leaves and other items with the root mantra. Then, having performed the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) upon the root mantra, one should worship the square [mandala] with: "Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ, obeisance to the wheel that bestows all accomplishments (*sarvasiddhiprada-cakra*)."

Having offered a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*), one should worship the first enclosure with scents, unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), and flowers, reciting: "Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ gaṃ, obeisance to Gaṇeśa" in the east; "Hauṃ, obeisance to Kumāra" in the south; "Prīṃ, obeisance to Puṣpadanta" in the west; and "Vaiṃ, obeisance to Vikartana" in the north. Thus ends the first enclosure.
To the venerable sandals of Brāhmī, accompanied by Asitāṅga Bhairava; 3. To the venerable sandals of Nārāyaṇī, accompanied by Ruru Bhairava;

3. To the venerable sandals of Cāmuṇḍā, accompanied by Caṇḍa Bhairava; 3. To the venerable sandals of Aparājitā, accompanied by Krodheśa Bhairava; 3. To the venerable sandals of Māheśvarī, accompanied by Unmatta Bhairava; 3. To the venerable sandals of Kaumārī, accompanied by Kapālin Bhairava.

3/ To the venerable feet (śrīpāda) of Vārāhī accompanied by Bhīṣaṇabhairava; 3/ To the venerable sandals (śrīpāduka) of Nārasiṃhī accompanied by Saṃhārabhairava—one should worship in this manner with perfumes, unbroken rice, and flowers, moving counter-clockwise.
This is the second enclosure. *Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ*, obeisance to the wheel that fulfills all desires (*sarvāśāpūrakacakra*); thus, [one should offer] a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*).

Having offered [the oblation], one should worship the hexagon: *oṃ hrīṃ duṃ śailaputrī-śrī-pādukāṃ pūjayāmi*. 3. *brahmacāriṇī-śrī-pādukāṃ pūjayāmi*. 3. *caṇḍaghaṇṭā-śrī-pādukāṃ pūjayāmi*. 3. *kūṣmāṇḍā-śrī-pādukāṃ pūjayāmi*. 3. *skandamātṛ-śrī-pādukāṃ pūjayāmi*.
3. *kātyāyanī-śrī-pādukāṃ pūjayāmi*. Thus one should worship, moving counter-clockwise. This is the third enclosure. *oṃ hrīṃ duṃ*.
Having offered a handful of flowers with the mantra, "Obeisance to the wheel that bestows good fortune," one should worship the triangle: "3.
Obeisance to the venerable Kālarātrī; 3. Obeisance to the venerable Mahāgaurī.
3/ Devadūtīśrī... Thus one should worship [the goddesses] starting from the southeast, proceeding to the northeast and the southeast. This is the fourth enclosure (caturthāvaraṇa).
Reciting "Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ, obeisance to the wheel that bestows the eight supernatural powers (aṣṭasiddhi)," offer a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*).
Then, uttering the root mantra (*mūla*), worship [the deity] seven times within the *bindu* with the formula: "Śrī Nīlakaṇṭha Śrī Durgā Śrī-pādukāṃ.
This concludes the fifth enclosure (*pañcamāvaraṇa*). Above the *bindu*, worship with the root mantra: "Ambikā Śrī-pādukāṃ" and three times "Aṣṭākṣarā Śrī-pādukāṃ."

3/ One should worship with: "Obeisance to the Eight-Armed Śrī... / 3/ "Obeisance to the Blue-Throated Śrī... / 3/ "Obeisance to the Mother of the World Śrī...". Thus ends the sixth enclosure. Above the *bindu*, one should worship with the root mantra: "Obeisance to the Conch," "to the Lotus," "to the Sword," "to the Arrows," "to the Bow," "to the Shield," "to the Trident," and "obeisance to the Threatening Finger. [Then recite] the root-vidyā.

Having recited "Śrī Nīlakaṇṭha Śrī Durgā Śrī Pādukāṃ Pūjayāmi Namaskaromi" three times, and having offered perfume, unbroken rice, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, water for sipping, betel, an umbrella, a fly-whisk, and a mirror with the root mantra;
and having presented the *bali* offering there with the root mantra: "Sauḥ, obeisance and *svāhā* to all spirits who create obstacles."

*yāṃyīṃyūṃ yoginīgaṇebhyo namaḥ svāhā |* *vāṃvīṃ devīputravaṭukanātha kapilajaṭābhārabhāsvara trinetra jvālāmukha ehyehi imaṃ baliṃ yathopacitaṃ gṛhṇa 2 svāhā |* *kṣāṃkṣīṃ kṣetrapālāya namaḥ |* Having thus offered the *bali*:
Having first performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) and other rites, including meditation, and having taken up the rosary before the Goddess,

one should recite the root-mantra (*mūlavidyā*) as many times as possible; then, having offered the recitation with the words "O Secret One," and having performed the recitation of the armor (*kavaca*), the thousand names, and the hymn before the Goddess, one should offer that too to the God and Goddess from the time of dawn onwards.

"O Mother of the World, whatever I do from evening until morning and from morning until evening, may that be an act of worship unto You. Having thus offered a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*), having prostrated with the *yonimudrā*, and having dismissed the God and Goddess into his own heart with the *saṃhāramudrā*,
he himself becomes Sadāśiva and, together with his own Śakti, performs the offering of the vessel (*pātrārpaṇa*).
May he dwell in happiness.
Thus, O Mistress of practitioners, one should conceal this manual of the daily worship, which is secretly guarded and born from the essence of Śrī Durgā.
Thus ends the forty-seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Śrī Durgā Paddhati," in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*, within the *Śrī Devī Rahasya*.
p. 294) Now begins the forty-eighth chapter.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Now, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the armor (kavaca) which contains the essence of the mantra—
the very quintessence of Durgā known as Kavaceśvara.
It bestows the ultimate truth, is divine, and destroys great sins;
it is dear to yogis, accessible through yoga, and difficult even for the gods to attain. (2)
"O Goddess, without this [mantra], there can be no accomplishment of mantra in the Kali age;
by the wearing of this, O Mistress of the Gods, Śiva becomes the leader of the three worlds. (3)
Bhairava, the Lord of Bhairavas; the powerful Viṣṇu, Nārāyaṇa;
Brahmā, O Pārvatī, the Lord of the World; and the elephant-faced one, the destroyer of obstacles. || 4 ||
O beloved, he is the commander of the great army, the victorious one, the bull among men;
he is the sun that dispels darkness, and likewise the moon, the storehouse of nectar.
O Goddess, what is the use of saying much? By wearing the Durgā-kavaca, even a mortal becomes immortal—a practitioner who has mastered the mantra.
O Goddess of the gods, Maheśvara is declared to be the seer (ṛṣi) of this armor-mantra;
its meter (chandas), O beloved, is Anuṣṭubh, and Durgā is remembered as the deity of these eight syllables.
The seed-syllable *cakri* is the seed; *māyā* is said to be the power (*śakti*). *Tāra* is the pin (*kīlaka*), O Īśānī; the binding of the directions (*digbandha*) is described as the *aśmarī*.
For the sake of virtue, wealth, desire, and liberation, this is remembered as the application (*viniyoga*). || 8 ||

Of this Śrī Durgā-kavaca, Maheśvara is the seer (ṛṣi), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chanda), Śrī Durgā is the deity (devatā), Duṃ is the seed-syllable (bīja), Hrīṃ is the power (śakti), Oṃ is the pin (kīlaka); its application (viniyoga) is for the attainment of the four aims of life (caturvarga) during recitation.
"Namaḥ" is the ritual binding of the directions (digbandha). The visualization (dhyāna) is as follows:
[I meditate upon her] who resembles the color of dūrvā grass, who has three eyes, whose crown is radiant, and who holds a conch, a lotus, a sword, arrows, a shield, a trident, and a bow.
I worship Durgā, who holds the threatening gesture (saṃtarjanī), is seated upon a buffalo throne, and resides on the sacred seat (pīṭha) of the nine families (navārakula).
Oṃ, may Durgā protect my head; Hrīṃ, may she protect my forehead;
Duṃ, may the eight-syllabled goddess protect my eyes; and may Cakrī protect my ears. (9)
May the Goddess of the gods, Raktakuṇḍalā, protect my monastery and my two cheeks;
may Raktabījanisūdinī always protect my nose from the wind.
May Lavarṇā protect my lips, and may Cāmuṇḍā, the slayer of the fierce, protect them;
may Bhekībīja always protect my teeth, and Raktadantikā protect them as well. (11)
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ: May she who dwells upon the lap of Nīlakaṇṭha protect my throat.
Oṃ aiṃ klīṃ: May Maheśvarī, the mother of Skanda, protect my shoulders. (12)
Oṃ sauḥ klīṃ; may the Goddess Bagalāmukhī protect my arms.
Aiṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ; may Śivā, who resounds with a hundred [thunderous] roars, protect my hands.
Sauḥ Aiṃ Hrīṃ: may the deity Vindhyavāsinī protect my chest.
Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ: may the supreme Mātaṅginī protect my belly.
Śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ: May she who dwells on the Himālaya protect my two sides. Oṃ strīṃ hūṃ aiṃ: May she who removes misfortune protect my back.
Oṃ krīṃ hūṃ: may the goddess Nārāyaṇī always protect my navel.
Oṃ aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ: may Kātyāyanī always protect my hips.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ; may the goddess Śrībhagamālinī protect the penis. Aiṃ sauḥ klīṃ sauḥ; may she who is worshipped by Guhyakeśvara protect the private parts. 17.
Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsauḥ! May Manonmanā protect my thighs.
Oṃ juṃ saḥ sauḥ! May she who is worshipped by the Lord of the Universe protect my knees. (18)
Oṃ aiṃ klīṃ; may she who dwells on Mount Meru protect my shanks.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ gīṃ; may Gaṇeśvarī always protect my ankles. (19)
Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ: may Pārvatī, the sixteen-syllabled [mantra], protect my feet.
May Brahmāṇī protect me in the east, and likewise may Vaiṣṇavī protect me in the southeast.
May Caṇḍikā protect [me] in the south, and Nārasiṃhikā in the southwest;
may Vārāhī protect [me] in the west, and Aparājitā in the northwest.
May Kaumārī protect [me] in the north, and likewise Śāmbhavī in the northeast;
may Durgā always protect [me] from above, and may Śivā always protect [me] from below.
May Tripurā protect me at dawn, may Maheśvarī protect me at midday;
may Sarasvatī protect me in the evening, and may Chinnamastakā protect me at midnight.
May Bhairavī protect me at the end of night, and may Bhadrakālī always protect me;
may Ambā protect me from fire, and may Jagadambikā protect me from water.

May the Goddess of Speech protect me from the wind; may she whose eyes are like lotuses protect me from the forest; may she who sits upon a lion-throne protect me from the lion; and may she whose seat is the destroyer of serpents protect me from the serpent. 25.
May Rājamātaṅgī protect me from disease; may Bhūteśavallabhā protect me from spirits; may Yakṣiṇī protect me from yakṣas; and may Rākṣasāntakā protect me from demons. (26)
May Sumukhī protect me always from ghosts, spirits, and demons;
may the nine-syllabled Durgā, Oṃ Hrīṃ, protect me everywhere and at all times. (27)
Thus, O Great Goddess, this secret armor is the supreme essence of all Durgā; containing the heart of the mantra, it is known as Kavaceśvara.

It bestows wealth, it bestows merit, it is merit itself, and it is the armor that grants success in the Kali age; it grants the eight supernatural powers, it is to be kept secret, and it is the supreme and inferior mystery. (29)
It brings about the highest good, consists of the Manu-mantra, is the supreme destroyer of disease, the eradicator of millions of great sins, bestows honor, and confers glory. (30)

O Goddess of the gods, this armor (kavaca), which yields the fruit of a thousand horse-sacrifices and bestows the supreme goal, is to be kept strictly secret; it grants the perfection of mantras. (31)
O Śivā, reciting this grants success in the world, while wearing it grants liberation;
O Beloved, having performed his daily rites, the wise man should write it on birch bark during the sun's transit.
For the sake of attaining mantra-siddhi, the practitioner should write the Śrīcakra with the eight fragrances at its center and wear it on his arm as a merit-increasing pill.
What in this world would it not accomplish? The pill of Varmā quickly achieves everything; by wearing the pill on the head, one brings even a king under one's control.
One who desires wealth should wear it on the neck; one who desires a son should wear it on the region of the belly.
O Goddess, having written it thus upon birch bark, one should wear it in this manner. (35)
Having wrapped it with a white thread, one should encircle it with lac;
then, having wrapped it with gold, one should wear it with a red cord.
O Goddess, this pill grants all desires and is difficult even for the gods to obtain;
when this pill of the armor is worn, it bestows liberation.
O Goddess of the gods, the majesty of this armor cannot be described even by hundreds of millions of tongues, O Great Goddess. (38)
This armor, containing the essence of mantras and secret, must not be given away;
it is not to be spoken of, yet it is of great merit and bestows all eloquence. (39)

One should not give [this] to one who is uninitiated, nor to one with tattered clothes, nor to one of evil nature, nor to the disciple of another, nor to the wicked, nor to a slanderer of those who seek the Kula.
To one who has been initiated, who is of noble birth, who is devoted to the Guru, who is peaceful, who is attached to the Kula, who is a devotee of Śakti, and who is a lover of the Kula; || 41 ||
By bestowing this armor upon a virtuous person, a man shall become a partaker of his lineage. This is the supreme secret, the most excellent armor of Durgā.
It is a secret, most to be guarded, to be concealed, and to be hidden like one's own birth.
Thus ends the forty-eighth chapter, titled "The Description of the Durgā-Kavaca," in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*, within the *Śrī Devī Rahasya*.
Now begins the forty-ninth chapter.
The venerable Bhairava said:
Now listen, O Goddess; I shall declare the entire essence of Durgā, a secret that is difficult even for all the gods and for living beings to attain.
The essence of the truth of Śrī Durgā has been declared, which is the cause of the three worlds;
and the thousand names of Durgā, which bestow supreme merit.

Having recited and retained this *Devīnāmasahasraka* for the sake of auspiciousness, a man shall enjoy worldly pleasures in this life and become liberated while living (jīvanmukta) in the hereafter as well. || 3 ||
This thousand names of yours, containing the essence of mantras and kept secret, yields merit greater than ten thousand horse-sacrifices and increases good fortune in the world. (4)
O Goddess, it brings about the highest good, is worshipped by the universe, and is saluted by all the gods; it is secret, most worthy of being guarded, and bestows perfection through its recitation.

For this recitation of the *Śrī Durgā Nāmasahasra*, the seer (*ṛṣi*) is Śrī Maheśvara, the meter (*chandaḥ*) is Anuṣṭubh, the deity (*devatā*) is Śrī Durgā, the seed-syllable (*bīja*) is *duṃ*, the power (*śakti*) is *hrīṃ*, and the pin (*kīlaka*) is *oṃ*; it is for the sake of virtue, wealth, desire, and liberation. (p.
The application (*viniyoga*) is for the recitation of the Thousand Names (*sahasranāma*). The meditation (*dhyāna*):
[I meditate upon her] who resembles the color of *dūrvā* grass, who has three eyes, who wears a shimmering crown, and who holds a conch, a lotus, a sword, an arrow, a shield, a trident, and a bow.
I worship Durgā, who holds the threatening gesture (saṃtarjanī), who is seated upon a buffalo throne, and who resides on the sacred seat of the nine-fold lineage (navārakulapīṭha).
Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ! Jagadambā, Bhā, Bhadrikā, Bhadrakālikā, Pracaṇḍā, Caṇḍikā, Caṇḍī, the slayer of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa. || 6 ||
Anasūyā, Tuṣṭi, Tārā, Kṛttikā, Kubjikā, Layā, Pralayā, Sthiti, Saṃbhūti, Vibhūti, and Bhayanāśinī. || 7 ||
Mahāmāyā, Mahāvidyā, Mūlavidyā, Cidīśvarī—[Cide is a name distinct from Namaḥ]—Madālasā, Madottuṅgā, Madirā, and Madanapriyā. || 8 ||
Āli, the mother of serpents, the meritorious, the purifier, the Supreme Goddess;
the Primordial Goddess, the digit, the beloved, Tripurā, the Sovereign of the Universe. (9)
Manonmanā, Mahālakṣmī, Siddhalakṣmī, Sarasvatī, Saritkādambarī, Godhā, Guhyakālī, and Gaṇeśvarī. || 10 ||
Gaṇāmbikā, Jayā, Tāpī, Tapanā, and Tāpahāriṇī;
she who consists of austerity, who is difficult to grasp, and who wards off evil planets. || 11 ||
She is the destroyer of suffering, the bestower of happiness, the virtuous one, the mother of supreme nectar, and the goddess.
She is the ambrosia, the abode of the moon, and resembles the fire of universal destruction. 12.
She is the abode of all prosperity, residing in the pericarp;
she is the Mistress of Knowledge, consisting of the universe, the Virāj, the meter, the goal, and the intellect.
Bestowing fortitude, free from hypocrisy, a swing, Lopāmudrā, most skillful, the destroyer of the heaviest misfortunes, faultless, compassionate, Kāśī, who is both noble and unconfined. 14.
Akulasthā, Padanyāsā, Nyāsarūpā, Virūpiṇī,
Virūpākṣī, Koṭarākṣī, Kulakāntā, and Aparājitā. (15)
Ajitā, Kulikā, Lampā, Lampaṭā, Tripureśvarī, Tritayī, Vedavinyāsā, Saṃnyāsā, Sumati, and Bhayā. (100) 16.
Abhayā, Svarmukhā, the goddess Mahauṣadhī, Alambuṣā, Capalā, Candrikā, Caṇḍā, and Caṇḍamuṇḍanisūdinī. || 17 ||
She is the one with restless eyes, possessed by passion, her eyes reddened by wine;
she is the city of Tripura, the goddess Sūrā, the essence, the beautiful woman, and the enchanting one.
She is the twilight, she whose nature is like the twilight clouds, the hall, she with dark breasts, she who has the moon as her crown, the dark-complexioned one, the goddess with beautiful eyes. (19)
Viṣamākṣī, Viśālākṣī, Vāśā, Vāgīśvarī, Śilā, Manaḥśilā, Kastūrī, Mṛganābhi, and Mṛgekṣaṇā. || 20 ||
She whose vehicle is the enemy of deer (the lion), the honey-like one, the bestower of honor, she who speaks with intoxication;
she who is the Man-lion, the goddess Vāmadevī, the leftward-moving one, and she who is fond of the Vedic revelation that flows from the left.
She is the meritorious one, the path of merit, the virtuous daughter, and beloved by the Puṇyajanas;
she is Cāmuṇḍā, Ugracaṇḍā, Mahācaṇḍā, and the darkness beyond all darkness.
She is the night, the ascetic woman, the great radiance, the moonlight, and the embodiment of the supreme light;
she is beautiful in form, the true goal, the virtuous wife, and she is resplendent with both the forms of existence and non-existence.

She is creation and sustenance, the bringer of security, the patient earth; she has full and elevated breasts, she is the ground that causes destruction, she is diminished, she dwells in Śarva, and she is the beloved of Śiva.
She has prominent teeth, she delights in pomegranates, she is compassion itself, and she is the destroyer of the hypocritical.
She is the Rākṣasī, the Ḍākinī, the one worthy of union, the Yoginī, and the beloved of Yoga. (25)
Kabandhā, Kandharā, Kṛṣṇā, Vidyā, Kṛttikā, Kaṇṭhakāntakā, Kalaṅkarahitā, Kālī, Kampā, and Kāśmīravallabhā. || 26 ||
Kāśī, the bestower of fame; Kāñcī; Kāśmīrī, whose voice is like the cuckoo;
Prabhāvatī (200); Mahāraudrī; the consort of Rudra; the remover of disease. || 27 ||
Rati, Stuti, Tarī, Turyā, Totilā, Atalavāsinī, Tapahpriyā, Śaracchreṣṭhā, Paṅguputrī, and Yamasvasṛ. || 28 ||
Yāmī, Yamāntakā, Yāmyā, Yamunā, Svarnadī, Taḍit, Nārāyaṇī, Viśvamātā, Bhavānī, and Pāpanāśinī. || 29 ||
She who is free from [defilement], she whose questions have vanished, the dark one, the wielder of the drawn sword;
the water, the best of women, the bearer of boons, the giver of boons, the destroyer of the sons of heroes. || 30 ||
She who gives birth to heroes, whose form is speech, who is slow in action, compassionate, a cave,
a bestower of wealth, the supporter, the creeper that nourishes, and she of the vast belly.
Gaṇeśvarī, Gayā, Kāñcī, Kāñcīkiṅkiṇighaṇṭikā, Māyā, Māyāvatī, Mattā, Pramattā, and Pravareśvarī. || 32 ||
Śacī, the daughter of Puraṃdara, is cool by nature, produced from the qualities of both cold and heat;
her natural virtues are to be counted, and she is adorned with the quality of profundity.
She is the birth-giver, a digit of the Sun, who slumbers in the form of the seven-horsed chariot;
she is radiant, eternally blissful, and the one who increases the joy of the assembly.
Tarpaṇā, Karṣaṇā, Hotā, Saṅkalpā, Śubhamantrikā, Darbhā, Droṇikalā, Śrāntā, Samiddhā, and Suravedikā. || 35 ||
Dhūmrāhuti, Caramati, Amīkararuci, Citā, Cintānaleśvarī, Nelākārā, and Nīlasarasvatī. || 36 ||
Aparṇā, Suphalā, Yajñā, Sabhayā, Nirbhayā, Abhayā, Bhīmasvanā, Bhargaśikhā, Bhāsvatī, Bhākarā, and Vibhā. (37)
The river Vibhāvarī flows with joy from Nandī as the Nandyāvarta;
she is Pṛthvīdharā, the sustainer of the universe (or, according to manuscripts gh and ṅ, the sustainer of poison).
She who contains the universe within her womb; she who sets all things in motion. || 38 ||

She is the universal illusion, the forehead-mark of the universe, the playful consort of Viśvambhara; she is the mistress of serpents, the lotus-serpent, and the progeny born from the navel-lotus of Padmanābha.
Toraṇā, Tulasī, Dīkṣā, Dakṣā, Dākṣāyaṇī, Dyuti; Saṃpuṭā, Śayanā, Śayyā, Śāsanā, and Śamanāntakā.

She who is the color of śyāmāka grain, the tigress, the lightning flash, beloved by the rays of the moon; she who is worthy of praise, the well-guided, destiny, the trembling one, and the remover of tremors. 41.

Resplendent as the campaka flower, she moves through the lands of China and other regions; she is dear to the lowly people, the supporter of the earth, the dweller in the abode of Indra, the mistress of wealth, and the sovereign of the banyan tree.
She is the ocean, the confluence, the full one, she whose interior is shimmering, and she who dwells in the trees;
she is Pārvatī, the lowly woman, the venerable one, the one worthy of honor, and the beloved of Madhu. || 43 ||
Mādhavī, Madhupānasthā, Mandirā, Mandurā, Mṛgī, Momuṣā, Ruruṣā, Revā, Revatī, Ramaṇī, and Ramā. (44)
She who has supernatural power in her hand, she who has accomplishment in her hand, Maheśvarī who is full of food;
she who is the form of food, the light of the world, the destroyer of all demons. || 45 ||
She is the daughter of Garuḍa, supported by the sky, fond of her hanging locks of hair;
she wears yellow garments, adorns herself with yellow flowers, is the destroyer of Putana, and is beloved of song. || 46 ||
Balākā, Jagadantā, Jarā, Jayavarapradā, Prīti, Kaṭhoravadanā, Karālaradanā, and Rasā. (47)
She is the tongue and the hand, Bagalā, affection and the bestower of discipline; she is the crest, the one with a formidable body, intelligence, the fly, and the ink.
She who has crossed over, the one who causes to cross, the sharp, the gentle, the Mistress of Desire, the Auspicious One;
the Consort of Śiva, the lotus-eyed, the lotus-handed, Sarasvatī. (400) || 49 ||
She who has lotus-like eyes, she who was born from the lotus, she who sports with the sword;
she who is worshipped by poets, she who is the goal of poets, she who is the form of the poet, and she who is dear to the poet. (50)
She is the plantain tree, she has the form of the plantain tree, and she dwells in the plantain forest;
she delights in the sweet voice, she bestows strife, she is strife itself, and she is afflicted by strife.
She is established in the form of the musk deer, she possesses the appearance of the musk deer;
she is firm, she holds a rosary of beads, and she bears full, firm breasts.
She is the mother of sacrifice, the enjoyer of sacrifice, the mistress of sacrifice, and the source of sacrifice;
she is the perfection of sacrifice, the perfection of ritual action, the possessor of the limbs of sacrifice, and the protector of sacrifice.
She is Vaiṣṇavī, possessing the form of Viṣṇu, and having the nature of the mother of Viṣṇu;
she is the Māyā of Viṣṇu, the large-eyed one, radiant with expansive eyes.
She is the mother of Śiva, known as Śivā, the giver of auspiciousness, and the embodiment of Śiva;
she is Gāyatrī and Sāvitrī, Brahmāṇī, and the very form of Brahman.
Durgasthā, Durgarūpā, Durgā, Durgatināśinī, Māheśvarī, Sarvādyā, Śarvāṇī, and Sarvamaṅgalā. || 56 ||
She possesses the radiance of thousands of millions of suns, a face resembling ten million moons,
a depth like ten million oceans, and a great strength like ten million winds.
She dwells in the midst of the moon, sun, and fire; she resides within the circle of jewels;
she abides upon the twelve-petaled lotus; and she dwells within the solar disc. || 58 ||
Possessing the luster of the stainless moon, she dwells within the sixteen-spoked [lotus];
her abode is the heart-lotus, she is fearless, and she resounds as the Great Bhairava.
Rich in color yet devoid of color, she who transcends the fifty letters;
Bhavānī, the bestower of prosperity, prosperity itself, the giver of prosperity, and Bhairavī.
Devoted to the practice of Bhairava, served by the Bhairavas and spirits, she is the Mistress of Desire, whose form is desire, and who liberates from the fever of passion. 61.

The goddess who is the mother of Gaṇeśa, the bestower of boons upon Gaṇeśa; she who grants the ultimate goal and removes the cycle of rebirth; she who is praised in song, the daughter of Gautama, and she who is served by her gurus. || 62 ||
She removes the suffering of the wretched and eradicates the torment of the distressed;
she is of a compassionate nature, whose essence is compassion, and who abides in an ocean of compassion. (63)
She who delights in dance, who is devoted to dance, the dancer, she who loves dancers;
she who belongs to Nārāyaṇa, who resides among kings, and who wears a garland of human skulls and bones. || 64 ||
Bhairavī, worshipped by Bhairava, Bhīmā, the bestower of formidable boons;
(500) Bhuvanā, worshipped by the world, Bhavānī, the increaser of prosperity. || 65 ||
She is the slayer of the demon Mahiṣāsura and the destroyer of Raktabīja;
she eternally bears the bow and arrow and is the annihilator of Dhūmralocana.
Noble, abiding on the path of the noble, illuminating the path of the noble;
enriched with the seed-syllables of the fifty letters, she wears a garland of fifty severed heads.
She is to be worshipped as the maiden of the six limbs, yet she is devoid of the form of the six limbs;
she is Kālamātā, Kālarātri, Kālī, and the dweller in the lotus. (68)
She is Kamalā, Kāntirūpā, Kāmarājeśvarī, and Kriyā;
she is Māyā, Mati, Mahāmāyā, Bhayadā, and Bhayahārikā. (69)
She is to be counted as a woman, yet she is Nārāyaṇī; she is the beloved of Nārāyaṇa’s abode, satisfied by the drinking of wine, and bearing the fragrance of wine.

She is the truth, the wholesome, the skillful, the thoroughfare, she who stands upon the chariot, she whose voice is far-reaching, the great one, the passionate, the daughter of Bhṛgu, she of pure laughter, and the sovereign of the monkeys.
She who is radiant with the rays of emerald gems, the beautiful consort of the Lord of Lakṣmī, the Mother Ambālikā, the Sovereign Goddess, the sinless one, the crest of fire, and the Veda itself. 72.
Alasā has a slow gait and is the final one; she is the abode of infinite, endless qualities. Ādyā is radiant like the sun, the beautiful lady of the Solar lineage (Ādityakula). || 73 ||
She is the primordial goddess who pacifies the superimposition of the nature of the self;
she is the progenitor of Indra, radiant as a river, and has eyes like the moon and fire.
She is praised by the younger brother of Indra; she is Ilā, who is fond of sugarcane juice;
she is the Sovereign Lady, the consort of Īśa; she is Īśā, the beloved of Keśava. (75)
Umā, Urvī, Urubhujā, Uttaṅgā, Cokṣavāhanā, Uttaṅkā, Uttamā, Ullāsā, and Corugarviṇī are to be meditated upon. || 76 ||
She is heat (*ūṣmā*), she is woolen (*ūṇā*), she has heavy limbs, her eyes are upturned, and her head is raised.
She is supernatural power (*ṛddhi*), she is the *ṛc* verse, the mistress of the vowel *ṛ*, the remover of debt (*ṛṇahartrī*), and the destroyer of the *ṛ* sound (*ṛvāntakī*).
Ṛḍhijā, Cāruvastrā, Ṛṇivāsā,
Mahālayā, Ḷkārā, Ḷkkurā, Līnā, and Ḷḹkārā Varadhāriṇī. (600) || 78 ||

She who wears a crown marked by the deer, she whose beautiful crescent moon is her digit, she whose movement is the syllable *Ai*, she who bestows sovereignty, and she who is the path of Īśvara. || 79 ||
She is the form of the syllable Oṃ, the seed-syllable, the mother of the three Vedas, and the bearer of the cane-staff;
she is Ambikā, Lampikā, and Pampā, whose nature is the utterance of the vowel Aḥ.
She is Kālī and Bhadrakālī, Kālikā, the beloved of Time;
she dwells in the Kadamba tree, she is the patched garment (kanthā), and she is adorned with the jewel-girdle of Kāñcī. || 81 ||
Free from blemish, she is like a tortoise, possessing the luster of gold and a body as delicate as a young elephant;
she dwells upon the Golden Mountain, her mind overflowing with compassion.
Kulasthā, Kaulinī, Kulyā, Kurukullā, Kapālinī, Kapālakulanirviṇṇā, Klīṃkārā, and Kañjalocanā. || 83 ||
She has eyes like a wagtail, she wields a sword, and is adorned with a shield as her weapon;
she is richly endowed with a skull-bowl, the destroyer of the wicked, the bearer of a shield, the sky-walker, and the bird-like one.

She whose weapon is the thunderbolt, whose gait is like that of a bird, who is adorned with the letter 'Kha', the presiding deity of the Gaṇas, whose movement is like that of an elephant, the mother of Gaṇeśa, and the mace. 85.
Godhā, Gadādharā, Prājyā, Gaganeshī, Mahī, Malā, Ghurghurā, Ghaṭabhū, Ghūkā, Ghusṛṇābhā, and Gaṇeśvarī.
She is equal to musk and her beloved;
she is adorned with the letter *gha* and has the letter *ṅa* as her crown-ornament; she is decorated with the *ka*-group of consonants. || 87 ||
The goddess is lunar, praised by the Moon, beautiful, moonlight, possessing fierce sounds,
sounding like a bee, and adorned with shimmering golden armlets.
Chatrikā, Churikā, Chañchā, adorned with umbrellas and chowries, Jraṃkārī, Jalajihvā, Jṛmbhikā, and Jalayoginī. || 89 ||
She who wears a mass of matted hair, she who belongs to the Jāti class, whose face resembles the Jātī flower;
the Mistress of the Waters, the object of meditation for the world, the progenitor, the Mother, and the Matted One. (90)
She is the tempestuous torrent, the one who resounds with the tinkling of her girdle and small bells;
she is the Jhintika flower, the one who performs the leap, the leap itself, and the one who wards off those terrified by the leap.
She whose form is knowledge, whose hand holds a fish, who is praised by the syllable *ña* (or the letter *ña*),
who has a *ṭaṅka* as her weapon, who is the great truth, whose compassion resounds like a *ṭaṅka*, and who is *ṭasī*. 92.
The venerable one (ṭhakurā), the one who stands firm (ṭhatkarā), the one who abides (ṭhānī), she whose garment is foam (ḍiṇḍīravasanā), the one who flows (ḍhalā);
she who consists of the wind that stirs (ḍhaṇḍhānilamayī), the one who is free from worldly attachment (ḍhaṇḍā), she who makes the sound "ḍhaṇat" (ḍhaṇatkārakarā), and she who bestows (ḍhasā). 93.

She whose end is the letter *ṇa*, who wields the blue weapon (*nīlāyudhā*), who is humble, who is adorned with the letters of the nine colors, who is youthful, who has a protruding belly, who is corpulent, who belongs to darkness (*tāmasī*), and who is dear to those of a dark nature (*tāmasapriyā*). || 94 ||
Tāmrānanā has a copper-colored face; Tāmrakarā wears copper-colored garments; Tulā removes the three types of suffering; Tāpī is devoted to oil; and Tilottamā is most excellent. || 95 ||
The consort of Sthāṇu, the ground, the vast one, stability, the bearer of steadfastness, the great one;
she who possesses tusks, the jagged one, the wood-apple tree, Devakī, and the leader of the gods. || 96 ||
She who tames, she who pacifies, she who is to be punished, she who holds a staff in her hand, she who is difficult to bow down to;
she who is irresistible, she who is a difficult path, she who sees instantly, she who is the grape, and she who dwells in Draviḍa. 97.
She whose sound is like that of a distant drum, who destroys fear, who removes suffering, who moves swiftly, who is faultless, who is compassion itself, and who destroys hypocrisy. 98.
Righteous, the source of Dharma, preeminent, the giver of wealth, beloved of the Creator;
the wielder of the bow, the bow-creeper, the bestower of boons upon the archers. || 99 ||
Dhūmālī, Dhūmravadanā, Dhūmaśrī, Dhūmralocanā, Nalinī, Nartakī, Nāntā, Naṅgā, and Nalinalocanā. || 100 ||
She is stainless, the conduct of the Vedas, a river, the daughter of the mountain, Nimi;
she has a blue throat, is free from desire, and dwells in groves of nīpa trees.
Nirañjanā, Janī, Janyā (800), Nidrālur, Nīravāsinī, Naṭinī, Nāṭyaniratā, Navanītapriyā, and Anilā. || 102 ||
Nārāyaṇī is formless, untainted, and eternally beloved;
she is Padmāvatī, lotus-handed, the giver of sons, and affectionate toward her children. 103.
She is the supreme city, the sacred Pāṭhā, she whose ears are full, the daughter of Puloman;
she is the flowering one, holding a book in her hand, the clever one, whose vehicle is the pāṭhīna fish. 104.
The destroyer of sin, the bestower of peace, the protectress, the village-dweller, the supremely beautiful one;
the female piśāca, the slayer of piśācas, the bearer of the drinking vessel, and the one with joined palms.
She is the full moon, the fifth lunar day, the granddaughter, and the bestower of boons upon Purūravas;
she is the five sacrifices, the five-arrowed one, and the beloved of the fiftieth Manu.
She is the princess of Pañcāla, she who possesses the five mudrās, worship, and the fulfillment of all desires;
she is the fruitful one, the bestower of fruit, the one with a swift hand, and the beloved of the serpent-king. || 107 ||
Phiraṅgahā, Sphītamati, Sphīti, Spītimatī, Sphurā, Balamāyā, Balastutyā, Bilvasenā, and Balābalā. (108)
She is the one worthy of worship by Bagalā, the powerful one who increases strength;
she is the mother of the Buddha, the intellect of the Buddhists, the one bound [to her devotees], and the liberator from bondage. 109.
Bhaginī, Bhagamālā, and she whose essence is the flowing nectar of the *bhaga* and *liṅga*;
Bhīmeśvarī, Bheruṇḍā, Bhageśī, and Bhagasarpiṇī. (110)

She who resides in the *bhaga* and the *liṅga*, the fortunate one, the giver of fortune, the garlanded with *bhagas*; she who is intoxicated, the heart-stealing one, the fish, the mother of Maināka, and the destroyer of Mura.

She is the flute-player, the human-like priestess, rejoicing in the company of the radiant ones; she moves with the gait of an elephant in rut, is the daughter of Mādrī, possesses the stride of a swan, and is unwavering.

She is the sovereign of the lords of Yakṣas, the sacrifice itself, and she who rests upon those dear to the Yajurveda; she is Yaśovatī, the abode of ascetics, the self-restrained, and the beloved of ascetics.
She is the Yavana woman, established in youth, and the barley-grains that are the refuge of the Yakṣa folk;
she is the giver of the sacrificial thread, the eldest, the sacrificial ground, and she whose root is the sacrificial post.
Rañjitā, Rājapatnī, and Rājasūyaphalapradā; Rajovatī, Rajaścitrā, Rājyadā, and Rājyavardhinī. || 115 ||
The Queen, the Mistress of the Night-walkers, the Destroyer of Disease, the Sovereign of Gṛhapura;
she who is agitated, the Creeper, she who is to be praised, the Eraser, and she who is intensely devoted to women. 116.
Lanka, the abode of sandalwood trees, where sandalwood trees dwell, was surpassed by her who possessed a trembling mass of matted locks and who was more beautiful than the world. 117.
The bestower of boons to Lokeśa, she who causes absorption, the great absorption;
the altar, the clinging one, speech, the lute, the flute, and the mistress of the forest. || 118 ||
Vandamānā, Vavarṇāḍhyā, Vārāhī, Vīramātṛkā, Śaṅkhinī, Śaṅkhavalayā, Śaṅkhāyudhadharā, and Śamā. 119.
She dwells in the center of the lunar disc, residing in cool waters;
she stays in the cremation ground, the most formidable one, the mistress of the cremation ground and the wind.
Sindhu is the bearer of the thread, ever moving through all families;
she is the seventh, characterized by goodness (sāttvikī), full of being (sattvā), established in truth, and the slayer of the Asuras.
The Sovereign Goddess of the gods, the source of all prosperity, she who moves through all things both stationary and moving;
she who is full of equanimity, the perfect measurement, the honor, the sacrificial ground, and the mistress of the sacrifice. (122)
Haṃsī, Harapriyā, Hāsyā, Harinetra, Harāmbikā;
Heṣā, Haṭeśvarī, Herā, Halinī, and Haladāyinī. || 123 ||
She who utters the cries of "hehā" and "hāhā," she who is the intoxicating liquor (hālā), she whose heart is struck by the poison hālāhala;
she who is patience (kṣamā), the bestower of security (kṣemapradā), she who is emaciated (kṣāmā), she who wears linen garments (kṣaumāmbaradharā), and she who is destruction (kṣayā).

The earth, Lakṣmī who loves milk, the daughter of the mountain-king, hunger, the Kṣatriya woman, the Brāhmaṇa woman, the field, the night, and she who is adorned with the seed of the letter *kṣa*. (124)
She whose essential nature is the seed-syllable *laṃ*, she who is the letter *kṣa* among the letters of the alphabet;
she who destroys foul odors, she who is the *dūrvā* grass, she who is difficult to attain, and she who dwells in the inaccessible. 125.
Durgā, the pacifier of the suffering of distress, adorned with the seed-syllables *oṃ hrīṃ duṃ*—this thousand-name hymn contains the essence of mantras and yields great fruit. (126)
It removes the distress of Durgā, is saluted by all the gods,
consists of all mantras, is divine, and is worshipped by both gods and demons.
Whoever reads or causes it to be read, or hears or causes it to be heard—this brings about the highest good, yields great merit, and destroys even the most heinous sins. (128)
Freed from great sins and served by gods and dānavas, he shall enjoy prosperity in this world and go to heaven in the next. || 129 ||
The Thousand Names of Durgā is the sole means for accomplishing the root mantra;
at midnight, the hero, attended by sweet smiles, should recite it. (130)
O Goddess, he who recites this three times at midday, preceded by the armor-mantra (varma), with his hair loosened and accompanied by his wife, shall become equal to the Lord of Speech (Vāgīśa).
O Goddess, slayer of the Daityas, the family of his enemies shall tremble at the mere sight of him, just as the host of moths does at fire, O Daughter of the Mountain. (132)
Whoever, having worshipped Bhairava in the evening at the root of a reed-tree (vetasī), should recite [this],
from the cavity of his mouth shall issue speech endowed with prose and verse.
O Goddess, he who constantly recites this while lying down, though agitated by the pleasures of women, shall become a destroyer of his enemies and equal to Kubera in wealth. (134)
In speech he was like the Lord of Speech (Bṛhaspati), in poetic talent he was like Śukra;
in splendor he resembled the sun, and in fame he was like the moon. || 135 ||
In strength he is equal to the wind, and in fortune he is the leader of the gods; O Goddess, what need is there for much speaking? He would become like Bhairava himself. (136)

O Goddess, one capable of performing the rites of paralyzing, attracting, expelling, and subjugating should write [the mantra] on birch bark at midnight during the sun's transit, using the eight fragrant substances.
O Īśvarī, having written [the mantra] with the sixteenth, the semen, and the menstrual blood, the practitioner of the mantra should wrap the name within a thousand-beaded rosary.
Having wrapped it with a white thread, one should encircle it with lac;
then one should wrap it with gold, silver, and so forth, using yellow threads.
O Goddess, on an auspicious day, the best of practitioners, having worshipped the pill, should wear that desire-granting pill either upon his head or on his arm. (140)
Having quickly conquered her enemies in battle, the auspicious woman should enter her home;
having performed the worship of the practitioner, she who is barren should hold [the image] on her left arm. 141.
O Great Goddess, one shall obtain sons who are truly like Vaiśravaṇa himself; this pill is most divine, to be kept secret, and it bestows the fruit of all desires. 142.
She, who is the very embodiment of Durgā, must be constantly worshipped by practitioners.
O beloved, the practitioner who worships Durgā should wear this pill.
O Śivā, one should recite the supreme *Mantranāmasāhasrikā*, which is the armor;
O Goddess, listen as I now describe the fruit of that *Aṅgastotra*. (144)
Whether in a forest or a royal palace, during a famine or in the peril of enemies, in a wilderness, a desert, a fortress, a cremation ground, or in the danger of a river; || 145 ||
O Goddess, in a whirlwind, or in fear of yakṣas, piśācas, and other spirits or ghosts, the hero who is free from fear shall be victorious everywhere. (146)
The supreme practitioner may paralyze the wind, the sun, water, the moon, and so forth;
he may instantly delude the three worlds and certainly attract women. 147.
O Śivā, it slays all enemies, drives away adversaries, and instantly brings even the deities under control; how much more so, then, human beings? (148)
He shall pacify all diseases, great portents, and calamities;
what indeed does the hero not obtain from the five-limbed worship of Durgā? (149)
O Maheśvarī, this is the secret of the eight-syllabled mantra of Durgā; it is her entire essence, the core reality, and the supreme embodiment of the root-vidyā. 150.
One should recite and worship this Thousand Names of the Goddess, which brings glory to practitioners established in the Great Cīna-krama. 151.
This indeed is the essence of all tantras, the supreme reality among all realities;
this Thousand Names of Durgā has been revealed through devotion to you. 152.
It must not be given to one who is not a devotee; it should be guarded against the presence of cattle (or, according to manuscript *kh*, against the proximity of animals).
Even by giving it to sons who are not devotees, one would attain hell. 153.
This Thousand Names should be given to one who has been initiated, who is of noble birth, who is devoted to the guru, who is peaceful, and who is endowed with devotion. 154.
One should not accept without having given, nor should one give without a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
By giving or accepting in such a manner, the loss of accomplishment for both is certain. || 155 ||
O Śivā, this thousand names of yours is secret and most to be guarded;
out of devotion, I have declared this reality to you, yet it must be kept hidden like one's own womb. (156)
Thus ends the forty-ninth chapter, titled "The Description of the Thousand Names of Durgā," in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*, within the *Śrī Devī Rahasya*.
Now begins the fiftieth chapter.
The venerable Bhairava said:
Now, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the enchanting hymn to Durgā, which consists of the root mantra, is divine, and bestows all eloquence. (1)
This supreme and most excellent King of Hymns is a limb of Durgā; it is meritorious, pacifies the suffering of affliction, and bestows victory upon practitioners. (2)
O Śivā, for this King of Hymns to Śrī Durgā, the seer is the Lord Maheśvara, the meter is Anuṣṭubh, and the deity is the eight-syllabled Śrī Durgā. (3)
The seed-syllable *duṃ*, the Supreme Power (*parā śaktiḥ*), and the universe (*viśvam*) are the *kīlaka*;
O Daughter of the Mountain, their application (*viniyoga*) is proclaimed for the sake of dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa. || 4 ||

Of this King of Hymns to Śrī Durgā, the seer (ṛṣi) is Śrī Maheśvara, the meter (chandaḥ) is Anuṣṭubh, the deity (devatā) is Śrī Durgāṣṭākṣarā, the seed-syllable (bīja) is *duṃ*, the power (śakti) is *hrīṃ*, the pin (kīlaka) is *namaḥ*. Its application (viniyoga) is for the sake of virtue, wealth, desire, and liberation during recitation. The meditation (dhyāna):
Resembling the color of dūrvā grass, possessing three eyes, and adorned with a shimmering crown,
she holds a conch, a lotus, a sword, an arrow, a shield, a trident, and a bow.
I worship Durgā, who holds a threatening gesture, who is seated upon a buffalo throne, and who resides on the sacred seat of the nine-fold lineage. || 5 ||
O Mother, he who meditates within his heart upon the radiant pearl necklace— the seed-syllable amidst the strings of mantra—
while his beautiful locks hang down, for him Rambhā, having gone to heaven and being subject to desire, quickly comes to his two feet as he remembers her again and again.
O Durgā, he who, weary from the exhaustion of misfortune, constantly recites your mantra within the midst of the *māyā* [syllable],
shall have his lotus-feet rubbed by the rubies in the garlands upon the crowns of kings on this earth.
O Mother, O Sovereign of the Lords, if one recites the *cākrika* mantra while situated in the center of the wheel,
the practitioner becomes a leader of universal emperors, skilled in the art of political strategy.
O Śivā, a man who remembers another seed-mantra, the *cakri-bīja*, when afflicted by the harm inflicted by a host of enemies,
shall conquer his foes while situated within the circle of battle, mounted upon horses, elephants, or chariots.

O Goddess, he who, having smeared his body with the ashes of *māyā*, recites the seed-syllable of *dūrvā* at twilight in a cremation ground, becomes a master of speech and arrows; having become a mantra-practitioner, he brings about a kingdom that is abundant and prosperous.
O Pārvatī, if a practitioner recites the seed-syllable of Vāyu, he will become capable of crushing the pair of breasts of beloved women;
he shall become a swan sporting within the snares of the eyes of all beautiful women.

O Sovereign of the Universe, if one recites the *viśva* mantra at the conclusion of the arts of amorous play during the night, performing the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) that shines with the syllables of the *mātrās*, he shall surely become the abode of the Goddess;
his lotus-face will be smiling, the splendor of his limbs will be radiant, and he will be brought under control.
She is Urvaśī, who forms a garland for the heads of the celestial damsels of the city of the gods. 12.

O Consort of Śarva, that practitioner who meditates in his mind upon you— resplendent in the corner of fire, adorned with two fires, graced by the circle of the serpent’s abode within the circle of fire curved by the earth-house— he shall become equal to Smara among women on earth and in heaven. 13.
If one recites this hymn to Durgā— which consists of mantras, which is the crest-jewel upon the crown of the king of mantras, and which is the supreme secret of the limbs of Śivā—
at the time of morning prayers, during silent recitation, or during worship, he shall become a lord of men on earth and a lord of gods in heaven.
Whoever recites this highly meritorious hymn— the unique crest-jewel of the five limbs— at midnight, the three worlds shall come under his control.
This entire five-limbed secret of Śrī Durgā bestows all accomplishments, is a profound mystery, and fulfills every aspiration. || 16 ||
This secret, the mystery of the mantra, has been revealed to you out of devotion;
it must not be given to one who lacks devotion—such is the command of the Supreme Lord. (17)
The Goddess said:
O Blessed One, O Maheśvara, by this discourse of yours regarding the glorious five-limbed [ritual] of Durgā, I have indeed been purchased today for a supreme price. (18)
Śrī Bhairava said:
This supreme secret, the most excellent essence of Durgā, consisting of five parts, has been described; it is to be guarded and hidden like one's own private parts.
Thus ends the fiftieth chapter, titled "The Description of the Durgā Hymn," in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*, within the *Śrī Devī Rahasya*.
The Śrī Durgā-pañcāṅga is completed. (p.
The fifty-first chapter:
Now, the secret doctrine of Durgā.
On the peak of the King of Mountains, Śrīśaila, which is densely covered with various kinds of trees...
[He saw] the Lord of Umā seated in the abode of the splendor of spring. || 1 ||
Once, [he beheld] the god Īśāna, the Lord whose crest is the moon,
whose body is half-occupied by Umā, and who is served by gods and dānavas.
His three eyes are absorbed in meditation; his matted locks are reddish like creeping vines;
he is white with ashes as body-unguent; and he is saluted by Nārāyaṇa.
He who is bowed to by the gods beginning with Brahmā, honored by the hosts of Gandharvas, and worshipped by the lords of Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Nāgas, and the race of mountain kings. || 4 ||
Rising up and bowing low before the formidable Bhairava, who is the Lord of Mountains and the Supreme Sovereign, Pārvatī questioned him.
O Blessed One, Lord of all worlds, honored by all the world; O You who transcend qualities, supervisor of qualities, Lord of beings, Great Lord! || 6 ||
O Lord, you alone create, sustain, and at the end of time, withdraw this infinite world of moving and non-moving beings; why then do you mutter prayers? (7)
"What are you meditating upon, O Mahādeva, who are ever affectionate toward your devotees?
Speak quickly, O ocean of compassion, if I am dear to you. (8)
The illustrious Bhairava said:
O Goddess, what shall I tell you of this wonderful secret?
It is my entire being, the very essence of all things, and the supreme reality of everything.
O Great Goddess, though you have been restrained hundreds of thousands of times again and again, you ask once more due to the nature of women.
Today, out of devotion and affection for you, O Maheśvarī, I shall speak of the most wonderful King of Tantras known as the Devīrahasyatantra.
It is the sole crown of all scriptures, eternally composed of the essence of all things,
divine, consisting of all mantras, and endowed with ten chapters.
O Pārvatī, listen to the divine table of contents of this tantra, by the mere hearing of which one obtains the fruit of ten million worship-rites. (13)
O Goddess, the *Śrīvidyānirṇaya* is another [treatise] concerning the practice of mantra;
and the *Śivamantraprakāśa* is the unsurpassed ritual for initiation (*dīkṣā*). || 14 ||

O Goddess, [this is] the procedure for the preliminary rite (puraścaryā), the sequence of the Pañcaratneśvarī, the means for the fire-oblation (homa), and the supreme procedure for the worship of the wheel (cakrapūjā). || 15 ||
O Goddess, this is the tenth chapter, the determination of conduct, which is the procedure for the tenth day.
Therein, O Goddess, I shall first describe the wonderful world of Durgā. (16)
It was a great divine city named Jaya, vast and extensive, strewn with various jewels, and possessing a splendor equal to ten million suns. || 17 ||
It has the color of a cochineal insect and is as enchanting as ten million moons;
it is immeasurable, incalculable, and inaccessible to all disputants.
O Supreme Goddess, this divine world is named Jaya;
it is there that the supreme Durgā dwells, consisting of nine forms.
She who is the goddess of gods, the bestower of boons, and the sole beauty of all the worlds;
she who is known in the world as Durgā, abiding within the interior of the cosmic egg.
Having previously propitiated the Supreme Goddess through austerity,
Viṣṇu caused her to descend for the purpose of slaying Mahiṣa, the lord of the Asuras. (21)
Yogamāyā, Mahāmāyā, the Supreme Goddess who is ever-present—
I meditate upon her alone day and night, and I chant the supreme Śrīvidyā.
Today I shall proclaim that [mantra] which bestows both knowledge and conduct;
having heard it, Śiva became the auspicious one whose essence consists of the five sounds (pañcanāda).
When she was bereft of Hari, that Durgā existed in a form devoid of parts;
though she was the manifest form of the universe, she was of the nature of the great light.
Then, O Maheśvarī, at that very moment,
Śiva— the pervasive Lord who is of the nature of light— emerged from the circle of radiance as one devoid of consciousness.
He heard a voice, the support of the worlds and the supreme seed:
"Remember even Māyā; you have been created as the foremost leader by the Anu. (26)
Having heard that supreme sound, which is called *tāra*, Śiva suddenly muttered the seed-syllable (*bīja*) of the three worlds, O Śivā. (27)
Then he heard from the sky this word "Māyā":
"O Great Lord, resort to Māyā, the supreme abode of eternal bliss. (28)
The Lord Śiva, the Supreme Sovereign, became composed of the Bindu and the Nāda;
then he heard that Nāda, which was devoid of all harsh syllables.
"Devote yourself to Durgā"—saying this, Śiva became composed of the fivefold sound (pañcanāda).
Then, O Mother of the Universe, having recited the supreme Vidyā, he created the world.
In the beginning, Śiva created the wind, and from that, creation proceeded according to his will;
for in Śiva, the Lord of the Universe, the entire world of moving and unmoving beings exists as mere will.
"Śiva, the blue-throated one, emitted a mere fragment [of it] into Śivā.
Having thus obtained this secret lore through the worship of the Guru's feet, (32) p. 318).
What in this world cannot the practitioner who masters the mantra accomplish?
The practitioner can achieve clothing, fire, desire, wealth, and conduct. (33)
One should bring it under control according to one's intellect, by which the fourth state (turya) becomes manifest;
this Śrīcakra is the support and the cause of the Goddess’s manifestation.
This secret, the very essence of the Mother, is to be worshipped by the best of practitioners;
O Great Goddess, one should draw the wheel to be worshipped with petals representing the lotus and the sun. (35)
By means of which the goddess Mahāmāyā Śrī Durgā quickly becomes pleased—he who worships the wheel that possesses a blue luster and a burning radiance. (36)
One should worship the mandala-shaped form born from fire, moon, sun, and space;
that best of practitioners shall become radiant with a shimmering crown.
His fame, resembling a conch shell, wanders through the three worlds;
O Maheśvarī, together with the gods, asuras, and gandharvas, it comes under his control, and great siddhi falls into the hands of the virtuous. 38.
Becoming filled with the bliss of the supreme essence of the flowery liquor (śarāsava), one should recite the mantra;
the Kheṭakas are pleased with that practitioner through the worship of their limbs. (39)
All his diseases, such as colic and others, perish without delay;
even by merely seeing his forefinger, enemies flee in utter panic. (40)
In his house there was wealth, cows, buffaloes, seats, and elephants; his land was filled with jewels and difficult to traverse, and his throne was enchanting.
Through such extensive worship, the practitioner shall indeed attain manifold prosperity.
In this manner, one should meditate upon the Great Goddess Durgā, the destroyer of misfortune.
"By means of which meditation one shall indeed become a practitioner [and] a Lord of the Gods—this most wonderful reality, O Goddess, has been told to you.
It is not to be spoken, it is not to be given away, and it must be guarded like one's own womb. (43)
Thus ends the fifty-first chapter, titled "The Exposition of Mantra-Vidyās," in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*, within the *Śrī Devī Rahasya*. 51.
Now begins the fifty-second chapter.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
I shall now declare the secret of all practitioners of mantras, which is the means for accomplishing mantras;
by the mere performance of this practice, the mantra will attain success.
O Śivā, without the mantra for uprooting, a mantra does not bestow accomplishment;
nor does it do so without the life-restoring mantra, nor without the encapsulation.
One should place the *viśva* at the beginning of the *manu*, and likewise place the *tāra* at the end;
this is called the *utkīlana-manu*, O Śivā, which bestows all accomplishments (*siddhi*).
O Śivā, one should first place the seed-syllable called *cākrika* at the beginning of the mantra;
then, having placed the name before that, one should place the *tāra* and *māyā* syllables after it.
At the end of the mantra, one should utter the mantra named Sañjīvana;
thereafter, O Goddess, the best of mantra-practitioners should recite the perfected mantra.

Then, according to his capacity, the best of practitioners should offer the *saṃpuṭa* (encasement): he should place the *tāra* (oṃ), the *parā* mantra, the seed-syllable of the Wheel-Bearer (cakribīja), and finally the name of the object at the end. 6.
(320) This mantra known as the *saṃpuṭa* is remembered as the fulfiller of all desires. O Īśānī, having thus consecrated it, one should always recite this mantra of the Goddess.
The practitioner who accomplishes the mantra attains all supernatural powers (*siddhi*).
Thus, O Maheśvarī, this reality of the mantra called "the means of accomplishment" (*sādhana*) is more secret than the most secret; it must be guarded and kept hidden by the best of practitioners.
Thus ends the fifty-second chapter, titled "The Description of the Practice of Mantras," in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*, within the *Śrī Devī Rahasya*.
Now begins the fifty-third chapter.
The venerable Bhairava said:
Now I shall declare to you the Śiva-vidyā, which bestows the supreme goal,
which consists of all vidyās, which is to be accomplished, and which is hidden in all tantras.
If one should recite only a Śākta mantra and not a Śaiva mantra,
that mantra will not yield success (or grant its fruit), even if recited for ten million lifetimes.
Whichever deity is the consort of whichever god, for her, Śiva becomes auspicious;
by means of that, O Great Goddess, the Vidyā is swiftly accomplished in the Kali age. (3)
O Īśvarī, Mahākāla is the consort of Kālikā, Amṛteśvara is the consort of Sumukhī,
Kāmeśvara is the consort of Trikūṭā, and Śiva is likewise [the consort] of [Śivā].
O Īśvarī, for Chinnā the Lord is Kālarudra; for Śāradā, Śiva is Śiva;
for Kālarātri, the Lord is Śrībhairava—thus it is. (p. 321)
Mahādeva is the lord of Jvālāmukhī; Vijayeśvara is the lord of Vāgdevī;
and Śiva is the lord of Bhuvaneśvarī—thus it is, O Īśvarī.
O Goddess, Viśvanātha is Śiva, the Lord of Beings (Bhūteśvara), with Queen Pārvatī;
and Virūpākṣa is Śiva with Bhīḍā. Thus it is said.
O Goddess, Śiva is thus called Nīlakaṇṭha in relation to Durgā;
O Sovereign of the Gods, he is declared to be Vāmadeva in relation to the stone.
O Goddess, Sadyojāta is for Tārā and Śiva is likewise;
today, first of all, I shall declare the supreme root mantra of Durgā-Śiva.
O Supreme Goddess, by reciting which this Vidyā is quickly perfected:
Dakṣiṇāmūrti is the Lord of the Śrī Nīlakaṇṭha mantra. (10)
O Goddess praised by heroes, I have described the seer as Anuṣṭubh, and the deity as Nīlakaṇṭha, the Lord of Durgā, as declared by me. (11)
O Īśānī, the green seed-syllable is known as Tāra, and Śakti is remembered, O Śivā; the Kīlaka is declared to be Viśva, and the Niyoga is for the sake of the perfection of the mantra. 12.
One should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) with Tāra, Candra, Kaḍimba, and so forth, along with the six long vowels.
Having first heard this meditation on Śiva, keep it most secret. 13.

[I bow] to the illustrious Nīlakaṇṭha together with Umā— he who resembles the Bandhūka flower and gold, who holds a beautiful rosary, a noose, a goad, and the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness in his hands, who is adorned with the crescent moon, and who possesses three eyes.
I take refuge in that which is resorted to. || 14 ||
I shall proclaim the extraction of the mantra, which is supreme and consists of all accomplishments;
it is the secret of Durgā—listen quickly, O Pārvatī! (15)
The *praṇava*, *harita*, *vyoṣa*, and [the word] for Nīlakaṇṭha are for the stone-disease (*aśmarī*).
(p. 322) The extraction of the ten-syllable mantra of Durgeśa-Nīlakaṇṭha is as follows: || 16 ||
O Pārvatī, by the mere recitation of this king of mantras, the supreme vidyā of Durgā is swiftly accomplished in the Kali age. (17)
Thus, O Sovereign, this is the secret more secret than the secret, the very essence of all;
it is the mystery of Nīlakaṇṭha, which must be concealed by those seeking liberation.
Thus ends the fifty-third chapter, titled "The Description of the Knowledge of Śiva," in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*, within the *Śrī Devī Rahasya*.
Now begins the fifty-fourth chapter.
The venerable Bhairava said:
I shall proclaim the ritual of initiation out of a desire for the welfare of practitioners;
having performed the initiation according to the rules, one is liberated from the state of being a bound soul (paśu). || 1 ||
Supreme perfection is bestowed, the latent impressions of karma are destroyed, and the supreme abode is attained; for this reason, O Śivā, it is known as *dīkṣā*.
O Maheśvarī, the entire universe, from Brahmā down to a mere insect, is deluded by its state as a bound soul (paśu) due to the Goddess; therefore, one should practice initiation in the Kali age.
O Goddess, by means of service to the Śrī-Devī, preceded by the worship of the Cakra,
the practitioner, liberated from the state of a bound soul (paśubhāva), shall thereafter attain knowledge.
One who is initiated attains the state of *caraṇa*; one devoid of initiation remains a bound soul (*paśu*).
But the initiated becomes a knower, liberated from the condition of being a bound soul, and is all-pervading.
Indeed, one who has not received initiation into Śiva until the end of his life remains bound by birth; yet he who is freed from all sins shall attain the supreme goal.
O Goddess, such a person shall never at any time cross over the ocean of hell— neither one devoid of initiation, O Mistress of Gods, nor a bound soul (paśu) of contemptible birth.
A flood of evil approaches, while merit flees far away;
therefore, this initiation should be received with effort by the most excellent of the wise.
O Goddess of the Gods, whether in childhood, youth, or even old age,
a sinner who acts otherwise will go to hell and lead his own ancestors to hell as well.
O Śivā, having previously been a human being, one may enter the womb of an animal;
yet, having attained the latent impression (vāsanā) earned through former merit which bestows the ultimate truth, one proceeds.
Having found a guru who is of noble birth, knowledgeable in the tantras, and pleasing in all his limbs,
one should first bow with devotion and especially satisfy him.
O Goddess, with prostrations and salutations, preceded by the offering of sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā),
[he received] from the Goddess initiation as determined for the Siddhas, Sādhyas, and Aris, according to the prescribed rite.
With supreme devotion, the practitioner should accept [the disciple], by which the Guru [obtains] a disciple of beautiful limbs, enchanting in all his features. (13)
A youth devoted to devotion for the Guru, of noble birth, initiated from the womb, devoted to the Goddess, a true devotee, fearful of sin, and self-disciplined. || 14 ||
Having seen [this], one should bestow the supreme initiation; thereby, one becomes a partaker of the ritual portion.
The Śrī Devī said:
O Blessed One, ocean of compassion, out of a desire for the welfare of practitioners...
Tell me, when should the supreme initiation be received by practitioners? || 15 ||
Śrī Bhairava said:
On an auspicious day, under a favorable lunar mansion, during a solar transit, or at either of the two solstices.
On the day of Navarātra, during the Śrāddha for one's parents, or on the anniversary of one's own birth.
O Goddess, on the day of the New Year, during an eclipse of the moon or sun,
on Śivarātri, or on one's own birth asterism, the wise practitioner should perform initiation.
There, at the outset, having bathed under an auspicious constellation and having worshipped Bhairava,
one should go, O Goddess, to a riverbank or to some temple.
Having bowed again and again before the Guru in the presence of the deity for the sake of satisfaction,
one should quickly reach and prostrate at a sacred island, a supreme grove, or even a temple of the gods— places difficult even for the gods to attain. (19)
Therein, O Goddess, having first purified the seat, one should worship the Guru.
O Goddess of the gods, having extracted [the elements] from the [disciples'] bodies, one should then perform the placement on one's own limbs (svāṅganyāsa).
Then, the Guru, seated and facing east, [should place them] upon the disciple who faces north.
O Goddess, having installed [the image] according to the rules and having meditated upon the Supreme Goddess,
the one free from affliction should bestow initiation according to the prescribed rite before the deity for the sake of supreme satisfaction.
The lord of practitioners, his heart absorbed in bliss, should slowly offer the Great Vidyā, the Śrīvidyā, three times each at the base of the ear.
Then [one should offer] to Gaṇeśa, to the Gāyatrī, and to Mṛtyuñjaya;
then to one's chosen deity and to Śiva, and thereafter one should offer the Vidyā.
Having received initiation, the disciple should worship the guru according to his ability, pleasing him with prostrations, sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā), and auspicious garments. (25)

Then, O Supreme Goddess, having suddenly received His command for the sake of worship—[or recitation]—one should take up the yantra, the mantra, the rosary, and the five ancillaries, O Supreme Goddess. (26)
(325) Never at any time should a disciple show disrespect even toward his guru;
this is the secret, the most profound mystery, which constitutes the very essence of the ritual of initiation.
But that which is protected as the secret beyond secrets must not be revealed by those seeking liberation. || 27 ||
Thus ends the fifty-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of Initiation," in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*, within the *Śrī Devī Rahasya*. 54.
Now begins the fifty-fifth chapter.
The venerable Bhairava said:
Now I shall describe the supreme preliminary practice (puraścaraṇa) of the King of Mantras,
by which the mantra becomes a wish-fulfilling tree that bestows accomplishment.
O Goddess, on a certain auspicious day, under a favorable constellation and at a sacred festival,
the best of practitioners should commence the preliminary rites (puraścaraṇa) and other such activities.
O Maheśvarī (or Sureśvarī), one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times, or half of that;
one should perform it up to the limit of one hundred thousand, but never less than that.
If it is not possible for practitioners to perform the recitation numbering one hundred thousand, then one hundred thousand must be recited; it should never be less than that.
The Goddess said:
O Lord, if a mantra recited one hundred thousand times becomes a wish-fulfilling tree (kalpadruma), [then what need is there for others?
Then, O practitioner, tell me what the principle of the *lakṣa* is in this world. || 5 ||
In whose hand should the practitioner have the rite of *puraścaraṇa* for a mantra performed? O Dhūrjaṭi, please dispel this doubt.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
"Well asked by you, O Goddess; listen, O Pārvatī, I shall speak. One should never perform the preliminary consecration of a mantra oneself at the outset."
O Goddess of Gods, one should perform the rite of *puraścaraṇa* for this supreme mantra either by the hand of the Guru or by the hand of the practitioner himself.
Just as a body devoid of life is incapable of any action,
so too a mantra devoid of *puraścaraṇa* does not bestow its fruit.
From the japa, the homa is performed with a tenth part; the tarpaṇa with a tenth part of that;
the mārjana with a tenth part of that; and the feeding [of Brahmins] with a tenth part of that. || 10 ||

If, at the beginning of the mantra, one should perform the preliminary service (puraskriyā) oneself through negligence, then the recitation (jāpya) would be as futile as ghee poured upon barren fields. || 11 ||
Therefore, the best of practitioners should perform the preliminary rite (puraścaryā) of his own mantra either by the hand of the guru or with his own hand.
O Śivā, O beloved, having first given the formal vow (saṅkalpa) for the preliminary rite (puraścaraṇa) to the Guru,
the Guru should perform the recitation (japa) of the Kula-mantra according to the prescribed rule.
O Śivā, O Goddess, by the grace of the Guru’s feet, the practitioner shall obtain the fruit of the *puraścaryā*;
therefore, he should satisfy the Guru.
By means of which the mantra shall quickly bestow the desired accomplishment in the Kali age;
[one should worship] with sacrificial fees and auspicious garments according to one's own means. (15)
Then the practitioner himself should perform many preliminary rites (puraścaryā) on a mountain peak, by a riverbank, or likewise in a temple of the deity.
In a solitary and pure place, one should recite [the mantra] with a disciplined mind;
being a hero who observes celibacy, eats moderately, and has conquered the senses. (17)
One should abandon falsehood, envy, hypocrisy, as well as the acceptance of gifts, during the period of preparatory rites (puraścaraṇa) and likewise at the time of the fire-oblation (homa). || 18 ||
Having recited the root mantra one hundred thousand times and performed the fire-oblation (homa) with a tenth part of that number,
the practitioners— and even by a Kṣatriya— should likewise perform the homa with a tenth part.
Being well-satisfied, one should gratify the Goddess and then feed the practitioners;
this procedure for the preliminary rite (puraścaryā) has been described, O Kulasundarī. (20)
Alternatively, the preliminary rite (puraścaraṇa) is desired in another manner:
on the eighth or the fourteenth day of both fortnights.
Beginning from sunrise until the next sunrise,
by reciting [the mantra] during that time, the mantra becomes free from obstacles and like a wish-fulfilling tree.
During an eclipse of the moon or the sun, from the moment of the first grasping until liberation,
one should perform the fire oblation and other rites as many times as the mantra has been recited.
O Goddess, praised by practitioners, this mantra shall become the sovereign of all accomplishments;
one should recite the mantra according to the prescribed rite during the autumn season when the sun is in its course.
At midnight, one should perform the fire-oblation (homa) for Śivā, offering oblations with the hand placed over a Kṣatriya;
at that very moment, O Goddess, even a Kṣatriya practitioner shall obtain auspiciousness.
Alternatively, the preliminary rite (puraścaraṇa) is desired in another manner:
having brought and established the Guru, one should perform the worship of the deity.
Having gratified the preceptor with garments, ornaments, gold, and other gifts,
as well as his son, his daughter, and likewise his wife.
Having performed worship and recited the mantra, one becomes a master of all supernatural powers (siddhis).
Alternatively, the preliminary rite (puraścaraṇa) is desired in another manner.
Having meditated upon the lotus feet of the Guru within the thousand-spoked [cakra] and having worshipped them with a purely divine disposition,
one shall become a master of all siddhis. (29)
One should give a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) to the guru according to one's own means;
by the mere permission of the guru, even a flawed mantra becomes effective.
Thus, this secret chapter, which consists of the essence of mantra and is eternal, must not be disclosed, must not be given away, and must not be told by those who proclaim the Brahman. || 31 ||
Thus ends the fifty-fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the Rules for Puraścaryā," in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*, within the *Śrī Devī Rahasya*.
Now begins the fifty-sixth chapter.
The venerable Bhairava said:
