Now, O Goddess, I shall declare the ritual procedure for Pañcaratneśvarī, by the mere hearing of which this Vidyā is swiftly accomplished. (1)
Without the recitation of the mantra of Pañcaratneśvarī, success shall not be attained even by the most excellent practitioner;
therefore, O Goddess of gods, the initiated one should worship his own venerable Guru, the lord of all eight supernatural powers.
Listen attentively to the supreme reality of Durgā, which consists of the Mistress of the Five Jewels, by means of which liberation shall be attained in the Kali age.
Śrīdurgā, Śāradā, Śārī, Sumukhī, and Bhagalāmukhī—
this Vidyā of Pañcaratneśvarī has been described by me as belonging to Durgā. (329) || 4 ||

On an auspicious day, O Goddess, the practitioner should recite the *Pañcaratneśvarī* mantra of Durgā; he thereby obtains the fruit of the preliminary rite (*puraścaryā*) consisting of one hundred thousand recitations of the syllables. || 5 ||
O Śivā, among these four types of practitioners, the practitioner of the Śrī Durgā mantra should likewise satisfy the venerable Guru with prostrations, hymns of praise, and even with wealth.
The most excellent practitioner should cause other disciples to receive initiation, by which the mantra of Durgā indeed causes the Goddess of Speech to manifest instantly. (7)
O Great Goddess, even among five practitioners in the Kali age, by giving [this] Pañcaratneśvarī, one obtains the fruit of the preliminary rite (puraścaryā). || 8 ||
O Śivā, one was a devotee of Śrī Durgā, another a devotee of Śāradā, yet another a devotee of Śārikā, and another a devotee of Mātaṅgī.
O Goddess, when these five, including Bagalāmukhī, have gathered together in one place, they should worship the Guru and recite the mantra of Pañcaratneśvarī.
O Śivā, the five practitioners, having performed their mutual [ceremonies], should then pray before the venerable Guru for the attainment of the fruit of the *puraścaryā*.

Thus, when accomplished in this world, the mantra bestows all success. O Bhavānī, it consists of Tāra, Māyā, the Discus, the Holder of the Discus, Dūrvā, and the syllable of Vāyu, with Viśva at the end.
The extraction of the root-mantra of Durgā has been described to you; this eight-syllabled [mantra] is a secret.

*Tāra*, *māyā*, *kāmarāja*, and *śakti* [are the first four syllables]; then *stambham*, followed by *bhagavatyai* and the name; then *bhūtiḥ*, and finally two *ṭha*s at the end (*añcale*). This is declared to be the *śāradā* mantra for the sake of liberation. (13)
*Tāra*, *parā*, *mātaṭa*, *sindhura*, *arṇa*, *kha*, and *śarma*— with the name situated in the middle of those.
O Pārvatī, before this is the thirteen-syllable mantra of Śārikā, which must be kept secret. (14)

Having visualized speech as the goddess Caṇḍālinī— whose feet are at will left over— and who is Sumukhī and Mahāpiśācī, the mantra for the entire triad of lotuses and the forest is "Sumukhī-priya. (15)
*Tāram maṭham bagalāmukhi sarvaduṣṭānāṃ vācaṃ mukhaṃ stambhaya* twice;
*padam jihvāṃ kīlaya* twice; or *maṭham vā tāram nīram*. This is the Astra-vidyā of Brahmā.
Thus, this secret lore, endowed with power in the Kali age, is the Mistress of the Five Jewels; she should be grasped for the sake of accomplishing the preliminary rite (puraścaraṇa).
Thus, O Īśānī, this is the reality, the secret of the preliminary practice (puraścaryā);
it yields infinite fruit, is esoteric, and must be guarded by those seeking liberation. 18.
Thus ends the fifty-sixth chapter, titled "The Exposition of the Pañcaratneśvarī-vidyā," in the *Śrīrudrayāmala-tantra*, within the *Śrīdevī-rahasya*.
331) Now begins the fifty-seventh chapter.
Śrī Bhairava said:
Now I shall describe the procedure for the fire sacrifice (homa), which is concealed in all tantras,
the secret essence of Durgā, and the core of the king of mantras, O Pārvatī.
O Sovereign Lady, having meditated upon the supreme goddess Durgā and having meditated upon the Guru together with his Śakti,
one should recite the mantra at midnight before the Śrīcakra.
O beautiful goddess, for a mantra that has been recited ten million or one hundred thousand times, one should perform a fire sacrifice (homa) consisting of one-tenth of that number.
Without performing the homa ten times [the number of mantras recited], one shall not obtain that fruit;
likewise, without going to the cremation ground, the daily homas, japa, and other rites [yield no result].
O lady of excellent hips, they do not succeed in the Kali age due to the curse of Bhairava;
[yet they do succeed] with ghee, milk-rice, grapes, molasses, flowers, sugar, and arrows.
O Goddess worshipped by the gods, a human [image] should be fashioned from one-tenth of the number of recitations;
O Queen of the Gods, one should satisfy it with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta) using one-tenth of that amount.
Having satisfied [the deity] with a tenth part [of the offering], the wise one, O Goddess of gods, should cleanse the face of the five nectars with a tenth part of that, using the eight fragrances.
Having fed the initiated and most excellent of the twice-born with a tenth part [of the offerings],
O Goddess, the practitioner thereafter obtains the fruit of the *puraścaryā*.
Otherwise, there would always be a loss of accomplishment even for a mantra that has been recited.
The Illustrious Goddess said:
O Maheśvara, tell us how one who does not possess such power as to perform the *homa* ten times over [the number of recitations] should nevertheless perform the *homa*. (9)
The illustrious Bhairava said:
O Śivā, for one who lacks the capacity to perform the fire-oblation (homa) with its full ten-fold portion,
I shall today declare a method for the benefit of the Kaulikas.
On an auspicious day, O Goddess of gods, having gone to a grove at evening,
one should place the cremation ground either in front or behind oneself, O Supreme Goddess.
The practitioner, together with other practitioners, should prostrate with devotion to the cremation ground, [addressing it as]:
"O you whose face is formidable with flames, O beloved of the fire at the end of the aeon! (11)

"O Great Goddess, bestow your grace upon my consciousness, which has arisen from the abode of the life-breaths of all living beings. Having spoken thus and bowed down, he recognized the Bhairavas who had become the directions.
One should dwell there at night and perform the fire-oblation (homa), O Mistress of the Kula;
and in the northeastern direction, O Goddess of the Gods, one should visualize the Śrīcakra.
O Pārvatī, having worshipped the guardians of the directions there according to the rules with mantras,
one should worship Gaṇeśa there and worship the Kula-yoginīs.
To the east of that, one should dig a sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) and offer clarified butter with the Vidyā;
O Īśānī, daughter of the Mountain, the pit should be triangular and one cubit deep.
One should visualize a wheel extending one cubit in all directions upon that [ground]:
a dot, a triangle, a hexagon, an eight-petaled lotus, and three circles.
O worshiper of the Kula, I have described the fire-wheel (vahnicakra) marked by the earth-cave;
following that are Gaṇeśa, Dharma, Varuṇa, and Kubera.
The Mothers, beginning with Brāhmī, and the Bhairavas, beginning with Asita, should be especially worshipped with perfumes, unbroken grains, and flowers. (19)
O Maheśvarī, one should worship [the goddesses] upon the eight petals in the fire-wheel:
Māyā, Mohinī, and the third, Manonmanā.
Muktakeśī, Mātaṅgī, and Madirākṣī are to be worshipped in the hexagon;
and Yamunā, Gaṅgā, and Sarasvatī are to be worshipped in the triangle. (21)
O Śivā, Durgā should be worshipped in the *bindu* with perfumes, flowers, and unbroken rice grains;
then the practitioner of mantras should invoke the enclosure (*āvaraṇī*) within the *bindu* using the root mantra.
O Goddess of the Gods, having invoked the Fire with the root mantra using the invocation mudrā, one should do so with the mantra: "Oṃ rūṃ rāṃ agnaye svāhā. (23)
Having consecrated the fire with the root mantra and prepared the clarified butter (ājya-ghṛta), O Īśvarī,
the practitioner should perform the formal resolve for the ten-part oblation (daśāṃśa-homa) of the mantra.
He should offer three hundred oblations into the fire using the rosary.
O beloved, one should offer oblations deposited by a Kṣatriya into the fire there.
Then, O Dear One, one should offer the bali-oblation with flowers and fruits mixed with clarified butter;
O Goddess, having again recited [the mantra] as before with the five "ma" syllables. (26)
One should offer one hundred and eight oblations while facing downwards;
then, O Pārvatī, [one should do so] for the circle of practitioners and for the Kṣatriya.
Having performed worship upon this discus, one should satisfy the Guru with hymns of praise;
one should cause him to increase the power of the Kṣatriyas with blessings, by which he may quickly become a lord of the earth. || 28 ||
There, even a Kṣatriya may declare the fruit of the mantra's preliminary service (puraścaryā):
"Obtain it, O best of practitioners! Then he should offer the final oblation (pūrṇāhuti).
Then, O Goddess, one should recite the armor-mantra (varma), by which one becomes identical with the Goddess.
Then, the mantra-practitioner [should dissolve] the Goddess together with Śiva using the withdrawal-mudrā (saṃhāramudrā).
O Dear One, having first gratified the practitioners with food, drink, and other offerings,
one should dismiss the practitioners and the Goddess, together with Śiva and her retinue.
Having obtained the fruit of the preliminary practice (*puraścaryā*), the practitioner shall become a partaker of liberation.
Thus concludes this divine chapter, which consists of the worship of mantras and is eternal.
The abode of all reality, it should be kept secret by those seeking liberation. || 32 ||
Thus ends the fifty-seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Ritual of Homa," in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*, within the *Śrī Devī Rahasya*.
Now begins the fifty-eighth chapter.
The venerable Bhairava said:
Now, O daughter of the mountain, I shall describe to you the worship of the wheel (cakrapūjā),
by which Durgā quickly becomes a granter of boons in the Kali age, O beloved.
O Goddess, up to eleven, the practitioners bestow the supreme goal;
indeed, all eleven practitioners have been described as auspicious within the wheel. || 2 ||
O Goddess of the gods, nine are superior; five practitioners are middling;
but three, O Goddess, are inferior—those situated in the center of the wheel are not to be worshipped.
Without the worship of the Cakra, the daily worship, recitation of mantras, and so forth, yield no fruit due to the curse of the Yoginīs; therefore, one should worship the Cakra. || 4 ||
On the new moon, the full moon, the sun’s transit (saṃkrānti), and on the fourteenth and eighth lunar days,
as well as on the ninth, when Tuesday or Saturday falls, the worship of the Discus bestows auspiciousness.
The practitioners and the excellent disciples gathered together in a temple of Śiva,
or in a shrine of a deity, or even in an empty crossroads.
O Goddess, having visualized the Bhairavas who have become the directions, the practitioner of the rite (purusādhaka),
O Goddess, having sat upon his seat and purified the Vīramaṇḍala, [should proceed]. (7)
Having sat down here, the practitioner should perform the formal resolve (saṃkalpa) with devotion;
having performed the ritual placement (nyāsa) on all his limbs, he should carry out the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) and the other rites.
There, O Śivā, having established the vital breaths, one should worship the Śrīcakra;
between oneself and the Śrīcakra, one should perform the installation of the water-pot (kumbha).
O Śivā, one should worship Gauḍī, Mādhvī, Pauṣṭī, and Āsava;
having taken the essence of these according to reality, they are for the worship of Bhairava.
The Supreme Goddess is pleased by worship with the essence of bliss;
O Pārvatī, Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras are all worthy of worship and are purifiers in acts of worship.
Gauḍī wine brings auspiciousness among Brahmins; Mādhvī is the best among Kṣatriyas;
Paiṣṭī brings auspiciousness among Vaiśyas; and among Śūdras, Āsava brings welfare.
For Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, and Vaiśyas, however, intoxication brings auspicious joy;
yet liquor must be avoided from afar by practitioners who seek liberation. (13)
But in the absence of the juices that delight the gods, O Supreme Goddess, one should worship the god Ānandabhairava with honey, O Goddess. (14)

O Goddess of the gods, having purified the substance, one should purify the five *makāras*; there, at the front of the *śrīcakra*, one should worship the practitioners according to the *Bhairava-āgama*. (15)
There, having fully worshipped the Lord of the Yantra and having invoked the god Bhairava,
one should worship the Yoginīs there, and thereafter worship Vaṭuka.
O Maheśvarī, one should worship Gaṇeśa, the Kṣetrapālas, and the leaders of the circle; having gratified the gods, the ancestors, the sages, and the Vedas.
O Īśvarī, one should recite the root mantra at the center of the Śrīcakra, then read the Kavaca,
and thereafter recite the Thousand Names of the Mantra and the meritorious Stotra. (18)
Then, O Śivā, having offered the bali-oblation to the Goddess, one should satisfy the practitioners;
thereafter, one should satisfy the eight Bhairavas and then satisfy those who have received initiation.
Nine vessels are excellent, five vessels are middling, and three vessels are inferior; however, one should not worship with only a single vessel.
When the Bhairava Tantra is active, all castes are twice-born;
when the Bhairava Tantra has ceased, all castes remain distinct.
Having worshipped nine maidens during the adoration of Bhairava as Vīreśa,
one should satisfy the Goddess with semen and thereby deliver ten million members of one's lineage.
One should drink the substance that is the Śakti’s leavings and chew that which is the Hero’s leavings;
having performed the five [acts] beginning with *ma*, one should fashion the mandala of the Śrīcakra.
There, one should worship one's own guru and satisfy him to the best of one's ability;
O Goddess, having gratified the guru with sacrificial fees and prostrations. (24)
Taking that command upon his head, he should bring joy to himself:
on the left is a woman skilled in dalliance; on the right is a vessel of wine; in front are the mudrā, chickpeas, and *vaṭuka* offerings;
and there is the hot purification of the boar.
The lute of the true guru’s excellent discourse is sweet with melody; yet its contrary conduct is most profound and inaccessible even to yogis. (25)
Thus, this entire essence of the Cakra, secret, supreme, and consisting of reality, has been declared by me out of devotion to you; it should be guarded by those seeking liberation.
Thus ends the fifty-eighth chapter, titled "The Description of the Worship of the Cakra," in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*, within the *Śrī Devī Rahasya*.
337) Now begins the fifty-ninth chapter.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Now, O Goddess, I shall declare the supreme reality of Durgā, the rule for practices by which Durgā becomes pleased in the Kali age. (1)
In the Āgama there are two paths: the Left-hand practice (vāmācāra) and the Right-hand practice (dakṣiṇa). Of these two, the reality is the Kula practice; O Śivā, hear their ritual procedure from me.
Having been initiated, by what means does the practitioner attain accomplishment?
Out of affection for you, I shall tell you; this must not be disclosed to one of evil nature.
There are three seed-mantras (bījas) of Durgā, and their corresponding practices are remembered as three:
the first is the Right-hand Practice (dakṣiṇācāra), and the second is the Left-hand Practice (vāmācāra). || 4 ||
But the third is the family tradition; hear its rule, O beloved:
morning bathing, twilight prayers, and so forth, and at midday, the recitation of mantras, O Goddess. (5)
A woolen seat is prescribed, with milk-rice and sugar as the food;
a rosary made of rudrākṣa beads and a vessel made of stone.

O Goddess, this practice of enjoyment with one's own wives while following the right-hand path (dakṣiṇācāra), when performed with material substances and wine, is considered to cause the destruction of spiritual attainment.
I shall now proclaim the supreme Vāmācāra practice for the sādhana of Śrī Durgā,
by performing which a practitioner of mantras will quickly attain accomplishment in the Kali age.
A garland made from human teeth, a begging bowl of stone or a skull, a seat such as a lion skin, and a bracelet made from a woman's hair—these [are the ornaments]. (9)
O Śivā, food such as meat and other edibles is rich in the reality of substances and fermented liquors;
chewing is the consumption of young fish and the like; the *mudrā* is the sound of the lute; and the discourse is the conversation. (10)
O Śivā, sexual union with excellent beloveds from all castes, practiced with equanimity, is called *vāmācāra*; it bestows all accomplishments.
Otherwise, O Maheśvarī, there would be a loss of the efficacy of this mantra;
therefore, one should always resort to the Vāma, for the Vāma alone is the supreme goal.

O Goddess, in the Kali age, both the Right-hand (dakṣiṇa) and the Family (kula) paths must be abandoned from afar by heroes who are the best of practitioners; rather, one should resort only to the Left-hand (vāma) path in the Kali age.
O Maheśvarī, I shall proclaim the family tradition (kulācāra) which is to be practiced by the most excellent yogis; [it concerns] the woman of the family, the family guru, and the family goddess. 14.
That which one should worship constantly in this manner is called the Kulācāra; O Śivā, having recognized a woman of the Kula, O Maheśvarī, one should praise her again and again. (15)
Having brought her by force, having worshipped her, and likewise having provided enjoyment,
one should satisfy the Goddess Śrī Durgā, the mistress of the wheel, with semen.
One should especially perform the recitation (japa) of Nīlakaṇṭha according to the prescribed rule;
preceded by that, one should perform the fire-oblation (homa) and adorn the beloved of the Kula.
Having gratified the woman of the family with drinks, beverages, and likewise with foods, one should practice this daily; this is known as the Kula-ācāra (family tradition). || 18 ||
Thus, the illustrious practitioner devoted to right conduct, who honors the women of his lineage and his guru, and who is intent on the Vāmācāra path, will certainly partake in liberation. 19.
Thus, this secret chapter, which is dear to the Goddess’s conduct, must not be given to those who lack devotion, nor should it be revealed by those seeking liberation. (20)
Thus ends the fifty-ninth chapter, titled "The Description of Conduct," in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*, within the *Śrī Devī Rahasya*.
(p. 339) Now, [the next section begins].
The Sixtieth Chapter.
Śrī Bhairava said:
Now I shall proclaim the secret doctrine of Śrī Durgā.
O Goddess of the gods, the tenth-day worship is the supreme essence of the mantra. || 1 ||
He who is the initiating guru (dīkṣā-guru) for Śiva is proclaimed as the tenth;
I shall describe his worship, which is concealed in all the tantras.
Having received initiation according to the rules from a guru who is an expert in the Kula tradition,
and having accepted his command upon one's head, one should then practice one's own mantra.
Once, O Goddess of the gods, on an auspicious day and at a favorable moment, having brought the Guru to an empty house or a crossroads, || 4 ||
Whether in a cremation ground, or in a forest, or even in one's own home, O Pārvatī, one should draw the yantra upon the ground there; it is described by me exactly as it is.

O Goddess, I have taught you this Yantra of the Guru, which is to be praised with the fire-measures (tuṭīs): it consists of a point, a triangle, a circle of eight corners, a circle with eight petals, and a circle joined with a flame, along with the abode of earth.
O Īśvarī, having quickly drawn [the diagram] with vermilion, one should worship the cakra;
O Śivā, [worship] Gaṇeśa, Dharma, Varuṇa, and Kubera together.
The door-keepers are to be worshipped with excellent flowers preceded by perfumes and unbroken grains (akṣata):
Asitāṅga, Ruru, Caṇḍa, Krodheśa, and Unmattabhairava. (8)
O Goddess, on the eight petals, Kapālī and Bhīṣaṇa, as well as Saṃhāra, should be worshipped;
[and] Paramānandanātha and Prakāśānandanātha. (9)
And Śrī Bhogānandanātha, Samayānandanātha, Bhuvanānandanātha, and Sumanānandanātha [in Ṅ: Śrī Svātmānanda].
O Goddess, one should worship Gaganānandanātha and Śrī Viśvānandanātha, as well as the eight Kulagurus, upon the eight-petaled lotus.
One should indeed worship Madanānandanātha, Śrīlīlānandanātha,
and Maheśvarānandanātha within the triangle.
Having worshipped the Guru within the *bindu* with perfumes, unbroken rice, and flowers, one should, O Goddess, install the Guru there within the *bindu* with devotion. (13)
One should worship with one's own root mantra and sacrifice to Dakṣiṇakālikā;
there, one should likewise sacrifice to Mahākāla, Kāma, and Kāmeśvarī.
O Goddess, one should worship the Guru as supreme, as well as the Parāpara-guru and the Parameṣṭhi-guru upon the head of one's own Guru.

Having worshipped with various flowers, garlands, and the finest ornaments, O Maheśānī, as well as with sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇās), foods to be chewed, foods to be eaten, and foods to be licked; || 16 ||
O Maheśvarī, having offered the bali-oblation with foods to be sucked, drunk, and eaten, one should satisfy the Guru— who is filled with the essence of bliss— by beholding him with the intellect.
Then, O Goddess, having bowed to the Guru, one should pray for one's own heart's desire.
O Goddess, whoever should thus worship their own Guru on an auspicious day— || 18 ||
He alone is Bhairava manifest, who moves through the three worlds;
the Guru alone is the supreme mantra, and the Guru alone is the supreme recitation.
The Guru alone is the supreme knowledge; there is nothing whatsoever apart from the Guru.
O Goddess, for him with whom the Guru is pleased, Maheśvarī is likewise pleased. (20)
O Goddess, he by whom the Guru is satisfied is indeed Sadāśiva himself.
That which the Guru does not speak even upon seeing it in the Tantra, that the Guru should not practice.
O Īśānī, honored by the Kula, merit as well as demerit must be abandoned or accepted;
the best of practitioners should immediately do whatever the Guru says. 22.
In the Kali age, the *Manu* [scripture] does not attain success without the instruction of a guru;
therefore, one should worship the guru with devotion and constantly satisfy the guru.
Wherever there is slander or censure of the guru, one should cover one's ears or else flee far away. (24)
The Guru is the supreme dharma, O Goddess; the Guru alone is the supreme refuge.
One should constantly worship the Guru, by which the Goddess Durgā is pleased.
Thus, O Goddess, this is the reality of Gaśamī, the secret of all the Āgamas; it is the essence of essences and must be guarded by those seeking liberation.
Thus, this is the supreme reality, the reality that is the highest essence of all;
rich with the core secret of Durgā, it is a mystery to be guarded by practitioners.
Thus, this tantra called the *Devīrahasya* is an ocean of tantras;
it is my all-in-all, my secret, the supreme treasury of all scriptures,
the very essence of Śrī Durgā, consisting of the king of mantras, and eternal.
O Great Goddess, he is the bestower of accomplishment and is to be worshipped by practitioners. || 29 ||
The Goddess said:
O Blessed One, by your devotion you have shown this grace toward me, since you have described the Tantra of Śrī Durgā, O Kuleśvara. (30)
I have been purchased; I am your slave; I am devoted to you, O Destroyer of Tripura!
I must be protected by you in every way—what else shall I say to you? (31)
Śrī Bhairava said:
O Maheśvarī, this king of tantras is known as the *Devīrahasya*.
O Maheśvarī, it must not be given to those who are unworthy or to those who are evil-minded.
This must not be given to one's own sons or to other disciples by those seeking liberation;
for this is the essence of the tantras, the supreme truth, and the highest treasure of all. (33)
"O Goddess, this secret of Durgā must be guarded like one's own womb.
Thus ends the sixtieth chapter, the Description of the Ritual for the Tenth Day, within the *Śrīdevīrahasya*, which is part of the *Śrīrudrayāmalatantra*.
And thus ends this *Devīrahasyatantra*.
In the Vikrama year measured by five, nine, and one (1995), [this work],
which is the essence of all the excellent tantras of the *Devīrahasya*, is complete.
Having refined this highly precious jewel from the great ocean of the Śrī Rudrayāmala by means of textual emendations, the restoration of pure readings, and other such methods; || 1 ||
Having diligently recovered even ancient manuscripts written by the hands of scribes from many worn-out books,
[this work was produced] by the command of King Harisiṃha, the sovereign of kings, whose splendor flashes with the virtues of generosity, heroism, and beauty;
in this composition concerning the office of the learned Śrī Rāmacandra, who belongs to the Kāka lineage and holds a high position of authority.
Having completed it with the assistance of the sage Śivanātha, this work was brought to light by the learned scholar Harabhaṭṭa Śāstrī.
the supplement.
The Five-Limbed Ritual of Jvālāmukhī. Śrī Bhairava said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim it, O Bhairavī, O beloved of the life-force of Bhairava.
This entire chapter concerning Jvālāmukhī is difficult even for the gods to obtain.
The Goddess said:
O Blessed One, O Dhūrjaṭi, you are indeed the knower of everything;
various scriptures have been heard by me from the lotus of your mouth.
O Lord, if I am dear to you, tell me quickly the great mantra of Jvālāmukhī, the yantra, the procedure for worship, and the limbs of dissolution (layāṅga). [The reading "śīghraṃ" is preferred. 3.
Śrī Bhairava said:
Listen, O Goddess, O Sovereign of Bhairava, to the mantra, the yantra, and the limbs of dissolution;
I shall declare the method of practice, which is more secret than the secret among my [teachings]. (4)
"O Maheśvarī, this entire universe is indeed cruel and devoid of devotion;
once, in the form of a swan, I [perceived] the Supreme Reality of the world through the mantra."
O Goddess of gods, by the grace of Jvālāmukhī, he was able to create incessantly;
that mantra of Jvālāmukhī was described by her merely by its name.
From that time forward, by means of that mantra, I create, maintain, and withdraw the world of the moving and the unmoving day and night.
She by whose power of mantra supreme sovereignty was attained—
she alone is Jvālāmukhī, the Mother of the World, who consists of the three qualities (guṇas). (8)
By means of *sattva* she creates the universe, by *rajas* she protects it, and by *tamas* she causes it to decay; thus, through the power of her three qualities, [the world comes to be]. 9.
The Mother, the progenitor of the three worlds, is indeed my own chosen deity;
her yantra, her mantra, and her meditation, together with the limbs of absorption (layāṅga), [are now revealed].
O Supreme Goddess, listen attentively to the ritual applications;
first, however, is the extraction of the mantra, as determined by all the Āgamas. (11)
I shall proclaim it, O Great Goddess; it must not be disclosed to those seeking liberation.
First, having extracted the Praṇava, as well as Māyā and Kamalā— || 12 ||
In the mantra *jvālāmukhi mama*, one should utter "all enemies" (*sarvaśatrūn*);
then, having extracted the pair [of syllables], one adds the *kūrca* (hum) joined with the horse (e). (13)
This mantra of Jvālāmukhī is indeed joined with two *ṭha* syllables;
O Supreme Goddess, this mantra bestows all that is desired in the Kali age. (14)

The killing of a Brahmin, the killing of a guru, the killing of a woman, the eating of forbidden food, the sin of approaching those who should not be approached, and that arising from approaching one's mother or sister; || 15 ||
O Goddess, this mantra washes that away; it is the truth, there is no doubt.
Now listen, O Queen of the Gods, to the extraction of the Yantra, which is higher than the highest.

I shall now describe the extraction of the yantra, which bestows enjoyment and liberation, is to be kept secret, is pleased by song and instrumental music, is beautiful with bliss, and is worthy of praise. (17)
One should not give away one's entire possession; rather, [one should give] that which is the most excellent among the excellent, the very essence of the essence.
First, having drawn a hexagon, one should draw an upward line.
Having drawn the lower line, one should draw it along both sides;
one should extend the lower line upward and the upper line downward.
In the center, one should fashion a single triangle and place a dot as the abode of Śiva;
that which is the triangle in the center is known as the dwelling of Sundarī. (20)
The other [triangle] above is the abode of Dakṣiṇakālikā;
in the center, within the triangle at the point (bindu), is the great abode of Śrījvālāmukhī.
Then, O Pārvatī, having drawn one circle, one should draw an excellent eight-spoked wheel;
having raised up a sixteen-spoked wheel, one should place it upon that single circle.
Having again inscribed three circles, one should then draw a square enclosure;
this is the Yantra of Jvālāmukhī, capable of uplifting the three worlds.
It must not be taught to the disciples of others; by teaching it to them, one becomes a slayer of Brahman (brahmahā).
O Goddess of Gods, listen now to the limb of dissolution (layāṅga), which is worshipped by Brahmā and Viṣṇu. 24.
O Goddess of the gods, the Yantrarāja [is composed] in brief according to its true meaning:
Gaṇeśa, Dharmarāja, Vāsuki, and Narasiṃhaka. (25)
At the four gates, the four door-keepers are to be worshipped:
Gaṇanātha in the east and Dharmarāja in the south.
Vāsuki is to be worshipped in the west, and Narasiṃhaka in the north;
thereafter, on the sixteen petals, the sixteen flames are to be worshipped.
O Goddess, by following the counter-clockwise sequence, one obtains the fruit of various forms of worship:
Vāruṇī, Vātyālī, Vārāhī, and Kulasundarī. (28)
Kūvarī, Kulikā, Kuṇṭhī, Kutsitā, Kuṭilā, Kuhū, Kuntī, Kumbheśvarī, Kuntā, Kūcarī, Kāruṇī, and Kṛti. || 29 ||
Thus there should be sixteen flames extending through all her limbs;
thereafter, the eight young maidens are indeed to be worshipped upon the petals of the eight-petaled lotus.
Māyā, Mohinī, Bālā, Bhagarūpiṇī,
Bhagāvāsā, Bhīruṇḍā, Mṛḍānī, and Baindaveśvarī.
(346) Eight maidens are proclaimed as those to be worshipped upon the eight petals;
thereafter, O Pārvatī, there are the ten Jvālāmukhīs who bestow happiness. 32.
By following the sequence of counter-clockwise rotation alone, the accomplishment of worship will certainly occur:
Brāhmī, Śāmbhavī, Durgā, Vārāhī, and Kulakāminī. (33)
Nārasiṃhī, Kaumārī, Mātaṅgī, Bhadrakālikā,
and Ugratārā— these are declared to be the ten flames and digits (kalās).
The practitioners should worship [the goddesses] upon the ten petals for the sake of perfect accomplishment;
thereafter, having worshipped the goddess Tripurasundarī above that, [they should proceed]. (35)
In the center of that, the goddess Dakṣiṇakālikā, situated below, is to be worshipped;
likewise, in the middle of that, the goddess Jvālāmukhī is to be worshipped.
Jvalinī, Jaṭinī, Jātī, and likewise Jālandharī—these are the supreme goddesses of the Yantra, situated within the triangle at the point of the Bindu. || 37 ||
And one should perform the worship of the Goddess's weapons within a square;
O Goddess, [this is done] within a square situated in the center of the yantra and extending toward the intermediate directions.
The wise one should worship the [deity] holding the gesture of fearlessness, the boon-granting gesture, the lotus, and the noose (or arrow);
likewise, one should worship the weapons in the sequence starting from Īśāna.
Thus has the limb of dissolution been declared to you; now hear of meditation, O Maheśvarī.
By meditating upon the Goddess, O Great Goddess, the practitioner of mantra becomes equal to Bhairava. (40)
She is situated upon a mountain of flames, three-eyed, presiding over the three seats,
adorned with a profusion of fire-flames, beautiful-faced, eternal, and invisible to ordinary people.

I bow to Jvālāmukhī, who resides in the center of the lotuses of the six cakras, who bears the excellent arrow, the lotus, and the gesture of fearlessness, whose nature is consciousness, and who illuminates all objects of knowledge. (41)
She whose face resembles the rising moon, who possesses full and lofty breasts,
and who holds in her left hand a pure noose of a freshly blossomed lotus—

I take refuge in Jvālāmukhī, who holds the gestures of granting fearlessness and boons in her right hands, whose slender body shines with three colors, who is supreme, and who resides in the center of a triangle situated upon a lotus of Rudra.
Resembling the luster of the cool-rayed moon, with the crescent moon as her crest-jewel, three-eyed, auspicious,
seated upon a lotus-throne of twelve syllables, reeling from the nectar of honey-wine,
her creeper-like limbs radiant with the three syllables, and surrounded by the maidens of flame— [or the family of Kālī].
I bow to Jvālāmukhī, the mother of the three worlds, whose pair of feet are radiant. || 43 ||
Thus the three meditations have been declared, as determined by the Tantra and Mantra.
O Goddess of Gods, listen to the ritual applications; having heard them, keep them most secret.
Stambhana (paralysis), mohana (delusion), as well as māraṇa (killing) and ākarṣaṇa (attraction), vidveṣaṇa (enmity), vaśīkāra (subjugation), and thereafter uccāṭana (expulsion). || 45 ||
Listen with focused attention to the pearl-like, peaceful, nourishing, and most wonderful [rite], by which the flame becomes propitious. (46)
Having risen at the hour of Brahmā or at midnight,
one should go to the riverbank and perform the occasional rite as prescribed.
One should perform the ritual of bathing and the twilight prayers (sandhyā), and carry out the recitation (japa) one hundred and eight times;
having recited the mantra of Jvālādevī, one should then proceed to the abode of the deceased (pretālaya).
Then, O Goddess of the gods, having brought a handful of ashes, the practitioner—
the best of practitioners— should bury it in one triangular pit.
O Goddess of the Gods, having thrown a handful of ashes into that sacrificial pit, one should perform the fire-oblation with ghee,
sesame oil, and milk-rice.
One should perform the fire-oblation with the root mantra until midday arrives;
O Supreme Goddess, if it should fall after that, the punishment is the staff of an Āiṣika.
O Goddess of gods, having performed the fire sacrifice (homa), the wise one should perform the supreme rite;
rising at midnight and taking the ashes, he should smear them [upon himself]. 52.
O Goddess of the Gods, on the morning of the lunar day, the wise practitioner, having applied a tilaka on his forehead, should enter the midst of the assembly.
Merely by the sight of him, Indra, Jīva, Pitāmaha, Stambha, Vāk, and the Lord Viṣṇu shall come into being; of this there is no doubt. (54)
Having risen on an auspicious day— at midday or at midnight—
one should bring a new pitcher and fill it with water, O beloved.
In the midst of that, O Maheśvarī, the practitioner of mantra should perform the worship of Jvālāmukhī for eight days with perfumes, water offerings, and flowers.
O Maheśānī, when another auspicious day has arrived, the mantra-practitioner should offer a propitiatory oblation; he should also place a cock and its blood into the jar.
Then, having offered the food offering with the root mantra, the practitioner who accomplishes the mantra should perform the ritual bath with the water from that jar. (58)
"By means of his actions, mind, and speech, he may delude the three worlds;
he will certainly (or swiftly) cause even me, the omniscient one, to be otherwise. [59]
On another occasion, O Śivā, having gone to the abode of the pretas on a Saturday and meditated upon the deity together with Śiva, one should perform the unsurpassed ritual bath.
Then, having recited [the mantra] one hundred and eight times with a rosary and having assumed the form of a woman, he should carefully discharge his semen.
O Sovereign of the Universe, having placed honey above the semen, the wise one should pour wine;
then, having added breast milk, he should place cow’s urine on top.
Having briefly added human urine, one should pour in donkey urine;
likewise, O Maheśvarī, elephant urine and fish meat should be placed in the middle.
Having filled a jar with sesame oil, salt, and *māraṇāla* according to the prescribed rite, the practitioner [should place it] in the abode of the deceased.
Having thrown it upon the ground, one should constantly recite the mantra one hundred and eight times.
Having completed one month, one should offer an oblation of buffalo meat (māhiṣika). 65.
Then one should perform the fire sacrifice with milk-rice and clarified butter;
likewise, having offered the vīrī fruit, one should offer the harītakī.
Then, when a month has passed, O Goddess, the practitioner who accomplishes the mantra should again bow his head to the ground and draw the jar from the earth.
One should recite the root mantra exactly one thousand times according to the true method;
at midnight, having taken the name of the enemy at a crossroads, [one should proceed]. 68.
The practitioner should break the jar, and the enemy will die instantly.
Now I shall describe the rite of attraction to be performed at dawn on a Thursday.
O Goddess, having gone to a secluded place, one should perform the occasional rite;
then, having brought milk, specifically that from a buffalo’s udder. (70)
Having unified them, one should perform the fire-oblation with clarified butter and milk-rice;
and having experienced sexual union, one should cast the semen into the milk.
One should offer oblations of heaps of flowers— yellow, red, and white— and then,
O Goddess of Gods, on another day, one should remove the cooled ashes.
The mantra-practitioner should join [the substance] with his semen and cast it at a crossroads;
even Urvaśī, though dwelling in heaven, will appear in the morning.
Rising on a Monday and going to a cremation ground, the wise man should,
at midday, place the collection of ashes and bones into a new jar.
Having covered the jar with a cloth, the mantra-practitioner should cast it upon the ground and recite [the mantra] for eight days while keeping the root-mantra in mind.
When the eighth day has arrived, the mantra-practitioner should draw out the jar and,
at midnight, slowly break that jar at the enemy's door.
By ten blows with the foot, there shall be enmity toward the enemy.
On a Wednesday, under an auspicious lunar mansion, one should procure the five products of the cow (pañcagavya). (77)
Having smeared the ground and drawn a triangular sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), one should place the great mantra within it;
in the center of that, one should fill in the yantra and perform the fire-oblation (homa) with the syllables born of the root-mantra.
Having offered the bali-oblation to the cat, the practitioner, a man, should recite the root mantra seven thousand times according to the rules, together with its ancillary parts.
By grasping the name of either a woman or a man and reciting it seven times, even the Lord of the Gods becomes subject to one's will; it is not otherwise.
O Goddess of the Gods, by the grace of this mantra, all the immortals beginning with Brahmā, as well as the hosts of Apsarases beginning with Rambhā, come under one's control.
On a Saturday, having gone to a harsh black forest at midnight,
one should worship the yantra and offer an oblation (bali) before it with its own root mantra.
Having performed ten thousand recitations (japa), one should dig a sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) on the path;
one should offer that blood and clarified butter (sarpiḥ) into the fire while pronouncing the name of the enemy.
By that very [means], all enemies undoubtedly go to their destruction.
On an auspicious day and under an auspicious constellation, one should go to a beautiful shore of the ocean.
The practitioner should perform the fire sacrifice (homa) with the root mantra using *śamī* leaves,
breast milk, sugar-cane juice, pieces of sugar, and clarified butter, offering ten parts for every one part [of the mantra recited].
O Goddess of the gods, having completed the homa, one should then offer the final oblation (pūrṇāhuti);
from that, nourishment arises which is difficult even for the gods to attain.
This chapter concerning Jvālā has been declared by me as the most excellent;
it is the supreme secret, O Goddess, the entire essence, and the highest pith.
O Goddess, this is difficult to obtain even in the third heaven; it must not be given to anyone—to a slanderer, a wicked person, a hater, or one devoid of devotion.
It is to be guarded as the most secret thing on earth, bestowing the fruit of all arts. 88.
Thus ends the chapter on Śrī Jvālāmukhī in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*, within the secret doctrine of the ten Vidyās.
Now follows the ritual manual for worship.
O Goddess, I shall now describe the supreme manual for Jvālā, which consists of both prose and verse, is secret, and bestows the fruit of ten million sacrifices. (1)
But whoever worships Śrījvālā without having performed the morning duties,
his worship is as fruitless as a ritual action devoid of purity.
Therein, at the outset, the illustrious practitioner, having risen from his bed during the *brāhma-muhūrta* and having washed his hands, feet, and face, sits upon his own seat;
[he visualizes] within the pericarp of a thousand-petaled white lotus facing downward upon his own head.

Seated upon a lion throne within a lunar disc is one's own Guru, white in color, adorned with white ornaments, his mind delighted by the bliss of primordial wisdom, his form consisting of existence, consciousness, and bliss, four-armed, holding the gesture of knowledge (*jñānamudrā*), a book, and displaying the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, and three-eyed.

Having meditated upon the Lord of all gods, whose face and eyes are serene, who is the very nature of Supreme Śiva, and who is embraced with his right arm by his beloved— who wears red garments and ornaments and holds a lotus in her left hand against his left side— and who is peaceful and most gracious;

Visualizing oneself bathed by the stream of nectar flowing from the pair of his lotus feet, one should worship him with mental offerings (*mānasopacāra*). For example: *Laṃ*, I offer fragrance consisting of the element earth;
*Namaḥ*. *Haṃ*, [I offer] flowers consisting of the element ether. *Yaṃ*, [I offer] incense consisting of the element air. *Raṃ*...

The lamp, whose nature is fire (vahnyātmaka), [I offer]. Vaṃ: the various food offerings, whose nature is nectar (amṛtātmaka), [I offer]. Saṃ: the fruits, roots, and betel leaves, which are all-pervading (sarvātmaka), I present. Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hasa khaphreṃ hasara kṣa mala vaya ūṃ saha khaphreṃ saha kṣa mala vaya ūṃ hasauṃ.

Having contemplated ten times with the mind, "ŚAUṂ! I worship the venerable *śrīpādukā* of the illustrious Śrī-Amukānandanātha and the venerable *śrīpādukā* of Śrī-Amukāmbā; obeisance," one should prostrate like a staff.
Upon a thousand-petaled lotus, he who possesses the luster of the full moon, whose lotus-hands display the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness,
and who is clad in garments of stainless fragrant flowers.
One should remember the Guru, whose face and eyes are serene, who embodies the form of all deities, seated upon a swan at the crown of the head, while first uttering his name.
Having meditated thus, one should recite the mantras of salutation:
"I bow my head to the true Guru, who is peaceful, manifest in the form of Śiva, seated upon the Yoga-pīṭha, for the sake of attaining liberation, desire, and wealth. (2)
I bow to the glorious Guru, supreme bliss, whose very form is bliss;
by his mere presence, the Supreme manifests as the bliss of consciousness.
Salutations to that illustrious Guru, by whom the eye of one blinded by the darkness of ignorance was opened with the salve-stick of knowledge. (4)
Salutation to that venerable Guru by whom that state was revealed—the state which, in its form of an unbroken circle, pervades all that is moving and unmoving. || 5 ||
The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, the Guru is Maheśvara himself;
the Guru alone is the entire universe—salutations to that venerable Guru.
Salutations to you, O Lord, Blessed One, Śiva, who appears in the form of the Guru;
you who have assumed manifold forms for the sake of perfectly accomplishing the descent of knowledge. 7.
Salutations to You, who are ever-new and of ever-new form, whose singular nature is the ultimate reality,
the sun that shatters the darkness of all ignorance, and the mass of pure consciousness.

Salutations to the Supreme Self, who is independent yet assumes a form fashioned out of compassion; who is dependent upon his devotees and those destined for liberation, appearing in forms suited to their welfare.

For the illumination of those who illuminate, for the discernment of the discerning, for the embodiment of knowledge of the wise, and for the reflective awareness of those possessed of awareness. || 10 ||
In front, on both sides, behind, above, and below, may you always accept my prostrations; with the nature of the True Mind, please grant me your seat.
Thus, having prostrated to the glorious Guru and visualized him as being well-pleased, and having mentally received his command,
[one should meditate] upon the *bindu* situated within the triangular wheel (*trikoṇacakra*) inside the pericarp of the four-petalled golden lotus at the *mūlādhāra*.

The supreme Śakti Kuṇḍalinī, resplendent like a thousand rising suns, resembling ten million flashes of lightning, the mother of all mantras, whose body consists of the fifty letters, who takes the form of the thirty-eight kalās, and who is the life-force of all living beings.

Having visualized [the central channel] as the abode of the three abodes, coiled like a serpent with its mouth upward, possessing three and a half coils, thinner than a lotus fiber, and appearing as if asleep; and having rendered it conscious by means of the innate *nāda* taught by the Guru, one should [place the syllables] at the four petals there: *vaṃ namaḥ*, *śaṃ namaḥ*, *ṣaṃ namaḥ*, *saṃ namaḥ*.

Having worshipped [the petals] in the leaves in a clockwise direction and with the root mantra in the center, and having raised [the consciousness] everywhere by means of the mantra *haṃsaḥ*, one should then lead it to the coral-colored *svādhiṣṭhāna* at the base of the *liṅga*, in the six-petaled lotus, and there [worship] with:
*baṃ namaḥ*, *bhaṃ namaḥ*, *maṃ namaḥ*, *yaṃ namaḥ*, *raṃ namaḥ*, *laṃ*.

Having worshipped with "Namaḥ" in the center of the petals using the root mantra, one should then lead [the consciousness] to that blue ten-petaled lotus in the Maṇipūraka at the navel, and there [worship] with: "Ḍaṃ Namaḥ, Ḍhaṃ Namaḥ, Ṇaṃ Namaḥ, Taṃ Namaḥ, Thaṃ Namaḥ, Daṃ Namaḥ,
Dhaṃ Namaḥ, Naṃ Namaḥ, Paṃ Namaḥ, Phaṃ Namaḥ."

Having worshipped [the letters] in the middle of the petals with the root mantra, one should then lead her to the twelve-petaled lotus at the heart in the Anāhata center, which is of a tawny (piṅgala) color; there, [one worships] with: *kaṃ namaḥ*, *khaṃ namaḥ*, *gaṃ namaḥ*, *ghaṃ namaḥ*, *ṅaṃ namaḥ*, *caṃ namaḥ*, *chaṃ namaḥ*, *jaṃ namaḥ*, *jhaṃ namaḥ*, *ñaṃ*.

Having worshipped with "Namaḥ ṭaṃ namaḥ," "Namaḥ ṭhaṃ namaḥ," and so on upon the petals, and with the root mantra in the center, one should then lead her to the Viśuddhi [cakra] at the throat— a sixteen-petaled lotus of smoky color— and there worship with: "Aṃ namaḥ," "Āṃ namaḥ," "Iṃ namaḥ," "Īṃ namaḥ," "Uṃ namaḥ," "Ūṃ namaḥ," "Ṛṃ namaḥ," "Ṝṃ namaḥ."

Having worshipped with "Ḷṃ namaḥ," "Ḹṃ namaḥ," "Eṃ namaḥ," "Aiṃ namaḥ," "Oṃ namaḥ," "Auṃ namaḥ," "Aṃ namaḥ," and "Aḥ namaḥ" upon the petals, and with the root mantra (mūla) in the center, one should then lead her to the *ājñācakra*— the two-petaled lotus between the eyebrows, lightning-colored— and there worship with "Haṃ namaḥ" and "Kṣaṃ namaḥ."

Having worshipped [the deity] between the two petals with the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*), and having then caused [the consciousness] to reach the *dvādaśānta-cakra* located at the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*), one should bring it to oneness there with the Supreme Śiva, who consists of light in the form of a drop (*bindu*) residing within the pericarp of the thousand-petaled lotus; then, having gratified [the deity] there with the supreme nectar (*paramāmṛta*) flowing [from that state], [one should remain] there.
Intent on hearing the *nāda*, having contemplated dissolution for a moment, one then descends through all [the centers] with the mantra "That am I" (*so'ham*).
Being made to descend from lotus to lotus in the sequence beginning with the *ājñācakra*,
she is worshipped in each of those lotuses with their respective syllables, as the respective supports, elements, and colors.

Having satisfied the respective presiding deities and brought [the energy] down to the *mūlādhāra*, one should establish it right there in its own place. Thus, having meditated upon the supreme power, Kuṇḍalinī, through the sequence of ascending and descending, (p.
I take refuge in that Woman who is of the nature of bliss, who shines forth at the first departure, who becomes like nectar upon the return journey, and who moves within the inner path.
Having praised thus:
"I do not exist, nor does another exist; and here, no object of meditation is found.
The mind has become absorbed in the state of bliss, having attained a state of equal flavor."
"I am the Goddess, and there is no other; I am Brahman itself, not a partaker of sorrow.
I am the form of Being-Consciousness-Bliss"—thus one should contemplate one's own Self.

Having thus recollected according to the instructions of the guru, one should perform the gross meditation upon one's chosen deity (iṣṭadevatā) by means of this very subtle meditation. Having contemplated one's own body as pervaded by that light,
and having meditated upon the venerable Supreme Deity within the lotus of one's own heart as non-different from oneself, transformed by that very light—

One should perform three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*). The procedure for this is as follows: having assumed a prescribed posture such as the lotus (*padmāsana*), with the mental fluctuations fixed upon the *mūlādhāra*, one should recite the root mantra or the *praṇava* sixteen times while blocking the right nostril with the right thumb; then, one should fill the air through the left nostril.

Then, reciting that same [mantra] sixty-four times, one should firmly block the left nostril with the right thumb and little finger and perform *kumbhaka* (retention) of the breath with both hands. Then, reciting that same [mantra] thirty-two times, one should likewise block the left nostril and [exhale] through the right nostril.

One should exhale the breath very slowly; this is the first *prāṇāyāma*. This same process performed in reverse is the second. The third is like the first. Having thus contemplated one's own body—its every impurity dispelled by these three *prāṇāyāmas*—as fit for the worship of the Deity, [one should proceed] with one's own root-vidyā.

One should perform the recollection of the seer and so forth. For example: "Of this King of Mantras, the Illustrious Jvālāmukhī, the seer is the Illustrious Vaiśvānara, the meter is Anuṣṭubh, the deity is the Illustrious Jvālāmukhī, the seed-syllable is Hrīṃ, the power is Śrīṃ, the pin is Hūṃ; the application is in the recitation for the sake of accomplishing the four aims of human existence. Having thus recollected, one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa).

Salutation to the Ṛṣi Śrī Vaiśvānara on the head; salutation to the Anuṣṭubh metre on the mouth; salutation to the deity Śrī Jvālāmukhī on the heart; salutation to the seed-syllable Hrīṃ on the private parts; salutation to the power (Śakti) Śrīṃ on the feet; salutation to the pin (Kīlaka) Hūṃ on the navel; salutation to the application (Viniyoga) for recitation on all limbs.
Thus ends the Nyāsa of the Seers and others. Oṃ hrāṃ śrāṃ, salutation to the two thumbs. Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, svāhā to the two index fingers.
Oṃ hrūṃ śrūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the two middle fingers. Oṃ hraiṃ śraiṃ, huṃ to the two ring fingers. Oṃ hrauṃ śrauṃ, vauṣaṭ to the two little fingers. Oṃ hraḥ śraḥ [to the palms].
*Phaṭ* with both the palms and the backs of the hands. Thus is the placement (*nyāsa*) of the heart and the other limbs.

Having thus performed the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) of the hands, one should meditate upon Śrī Bhairava and Bhairavī as non-different from oneself within the lotus of one's own heart. As follows:

I bow to Mahādeva, the Lord of Consciousness, who has three eyes, whose crest-jewel is the crescent moon, whose splendor is like the sun at the end of an aeon, whose smile is like the moon, who is seated upon the bull, and who holds a trident and a skull-cup in his hands. || 1 ||

I bow to her who dwells upon a mountain of flames, who has three eyes, who is established upon the three seats, and who is adorned with a profusion of fire; she of beautiful countenance, eternally invisible to ordinary people,
situated within the lotuses of the six chakras, bearing the gestures of granting boons, the arrow, the lotus, and fearlessness, and whose nature is pure consciousness.
I bow to Jvālāmukhī, who illuminates all objects of knowledge. || 2 ||

Having meditated thus and worshipped with mental offerings, one should place the *setu* (bridge) ten times in the heart with the syllable *oṃ*. Then, having placed the *mahāsetu* (great bridge) ten times in the *viśuddhi* [cakra] and the *sahasrāra* with the syllable *strī*, one should recite from *oṃ aṃ mūlaṃ aiṃ aṃ āṃ* and so forth, ending with *kṣaḥ*. One should then mutter the *nirvāṇa* ten times in the *maṇipūraka* with the syllable *oṃ*. Thereafter—

One should perform the mantra-consecration (*mantra-saṃskāra*). Thus: *Śrīṃ oṃ jvālāmukhi mama sarvaśatrūn bhakṣaya 2 hūṃ phaṭ svāhā hrīṃ*—one should recite this three times; this is the "unbolting" (*utkīlana*). *Hūṃ oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ jvālāmukhi mama sarvaśatrūn bhakṣaya 2 svāhā*—this is the "revivification" (*sañjīvana*), recited three times. *Caṃ chaṃ jaṃ* is the root [mantra].

One should recite "jhaṃ ñaṃ" three times; this is the practice of *tauṭilya*. One should recite the mantra for removing curses, "Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ Jvālāmukhi, release [me] from the curse of Bhairava, hūṃ phaṭ svāhā," ten times. One should recite the mantra for Kurukullā, "Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ Kurukullāyai svāhā," ten times. Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ...

One should recite the weapon-mantra (*astramantra*) three times: *Jvālāmukhyāstrāya daha daha duritaṃ hūṃ phaṭ hana 2 kīlān svāhā jvālāmukhīṃ hrīṃ svāhā*. One should recite the root-mantra (*mūla*), *Oṃ*, seven times for the purpose of warding off the two types of impurity (*aśauca*). [Then recite: *Oṃ jvālāmukhyai vidmahe hrīṃ...*
Having recited the root *gāyatrī* ten times— *jagadbhakṣiṇyai dhīmahi śrīṃ tanno jvāle pracodayāt*—
and having taken up the rosary, one should say: *oṃ māṃ māle mahāmāle sarvaśaktisvarūpiṇi | caturvargastvayi nyastastasmānme siddhidā bhava || oṃ hrīṃ siddhyai namaḥ*.

Having mentally worshipped her with scents and other offerings, [one should recite]: "O *mālā*, you who always remain present in all states, grant me freedom from obstacles. Having thus worshipped her mentally and taken the *mālā* in the right hand, one should meditate on the venerable Guru as white in color upon the head, the root-mantra (*mūlavidyā*) as golden-colored at the throat, and the venerable Supreme Goddess (*śrīparadevī*) in the heart.
Meditating on her in the form described above and having performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's ability, at the conclusion of the recitation, [one should say]:
"O Rosary, you who grant pleasure and auspiciousness to all the gods, be auspicious for me, O blessed one;
always bestow upon me fortune and valor."

Having recited this and placed the rosary upon his head, he should mutter the Bhairava mantra—*oṃ hrāṃ hrauṃ mahādevāya namaḥ*—according to the prescribed rule, and having recited the root mantra three times with the *saṃpuṭa* insertion, [he should do so] once again.

Having performed the breath-control (prāṇāyāma) and the ritual placements (nyāsa), [one should pray: "O You, the protector of that which is most secret among secrets, accept this recitation performed by us!
O Great Goddess, may success be mine through Your grace."
Having thus offered this fire-like recitation (*japa*) into the left hand of the Śrī Devī, one should prostrate with the *yonimudrā*. "From morning until evening, and from evening until morning,
whatever I do, O Source of the Universe, may that be an act of worship unto You."
Thus, having entrusted my own duties to you,

O Sovereign Goddess of the three worlds, whose essence is universal consciousness, O Śrī Jvālikā, I shall rise at dawn and, by your very command, follow the course of worldly existence for the sake of your pleasure.
O Jvālāmukhī, as I continue my journey through saṃsāra, may rivalry, contempt, strife, negligence, and fear no longer overcome me by the command of your feet, O Mother.
I know what is unrighteous, yet I have no inclination toward it; I know what is righteous, yet I have no impulse toward it.
O Hṛṣīkeśa, I act exactly as I am directed by You who dwell within my heart.

Thus, having prayed for the command of the Śrī Devī, and having made a formal resolve (*saṅkalpa*) regarding the *ajapājapa*—which is spontaneously accomplished and known through the instruction of the venerable Guru—to the deities beginning with Mahāgaṇapati who reside within the cakras from the *mūlādhāra* up to the *dvādaśānta*, one should offer it. As follows: "Today..."

The *ajāpājapa*— consisting of inhalation and exhalation performed throughout the day and night on the preceding day, numbering twenty-one thousand six hundred breaths— is [to be contemplated] within the *mūlādhāra*, *svādhiṣṭhāna*, *maṇipūra*, *anāhata*, *viśuddha*, *ājñā*, and *brahmarandhra* chakras, which possess four petals, six petals, [ten petals], twelve petals, sixteen petals, two petals, and [one aperture].

To the Gaṇapati, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, the individual soul (jīvātman), the supreme soul (paramātman), and the sandals of the venerable Guru (śrīgurupādukā), who reside respectively upon the ten-petalled, twelve-petalled, sixteen-petalled, two-petalled, and thousand-petalled lotuses, which are golden, coral-red, blue, tawny, smoke-colored, lightning-bright, and variegated in hue— [to them, I offer salutation] as is fitting.

Recalling, "I offer [the recitations] part by part," one should place them with palms joined in reverence (*kṛtāñjali*), as follows: *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*, I offer six hundred *ajapā* recitations to Śrī Gaṇapati, who resides in the *mūlādhāra-cakra*; obeisance. (4) To Brahmā, who resides in the *svādhiṣṭhāna-cakra*, [I offer] six thousand *ajapā* recitations.

Oblation: 4. To Viṣṇu, residing in the Maṇipūra-cakra, I offer six thousand ajapā-japas. Oblation: 4. To Rudra, residing in the Anāhata-cakra, I offer six thousand ajapā-japas. Oblation: To the Jīvātman, residing in the Viśuddha-cakra, [I offer] one thousand ajapā-japas.

Offering: 4. To the Supreme Self residing in the *ājñācakra*, [I offer] one thousand recitations of the *ajapā*. 4. To Her who dwells in the center of the pericarp of the thousand-petaled lotus (*sahasradalakamala*).

"I offer one thousand repetitions of the *ajapā* to the sandals of the venerable Guru; obeisance. Having thus offered the *ajapā* recitation and performed breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with the *ajapā* mantra, one should make the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*). As follows:
"Oṃ. Of this venerable *Ajapā-Gāyatrī* mantra, Haṃsa is the seer (*ṛṣi*), and the unmanifest Gāyatrī is the meter (*chandaḥ*)."

The venerable Supreme Self, the Paramahaṃsa, is the deity; *haṃ* is the seed-syllable, *saḥ* is the power (*śakti*), *so'haṃ* is the pin (*kīlaka*), the syllable *oṃ* is the essence (*tattva*), the acute (*udātta*) is the accent, the sky is the location, and the golden color is the hue. My application (*viniyoga*) is for the purpose of attaining liberation through the recitation of the *ajapā*. 4. *Haṃsa-ṛṣaye namaḥ* (Salutation to the sage Haṃsa) on the head. 4. [Salutation to the deity] on the head.

Salutation to the unmanifest Gāyatrī metre at the mouth. Salutation to the deity Śrī Paramahaṃsa at the heart. Haṃ, salutation to the seed-syllable at the private parts. Saḥ, salutation to the power (śakti) at the feet. So’haṃ, salutation to the kaulaka at the navel. Oṃkāra-tattva, salutation to the principle of Oṃ at the heart. Udātta-svara, salutation to the acute accent at the throat.
"Obeisance to Nabhase for the location; obeisance to the head. "Obeisance to Haima for the color; obeisance to all the limbs.
Having thus performed the placement (*nyāsa*), one should recite with palms joined: "This is the application (*viniyoga*) for the *ajapājapa* for the sake of my liberation.
This is the placement of the seer and other elements (*ṛṣyādinyāsa*). "Hsāṃ, obeisance to the two thumbs, svāhā to the self of the Sun. "Hsīṃ..."
*Somātmane svāhā* to the two index fingers; *svāhā*. 4. *Hsūṃ nirañjanātmane svāhā* to the two middle fingers; *vaṣaṭ*. 4. *Hsaiṃ nirābhāsātmane svāhā* to the two ring fingers; *huṃ*. 4.
*Hsauṃ anantatanuḥ sūkṣmādevī pracodayāt svāhā* to the two little fingers; *vauṣaṭ*.
4/ *Hsaḥ* svāhā to the unmanifest consciousness-self; *phaṭ* with the palms and backs of the hands. Thus is the placement (*nyāsa*) on the heart and other limbs. Then the meditation (*dhyāna*):
"The wise declare that heaven is his head, the sky indeed is his navel, and the moon and sun are his two eyes."
He whose ears are the quarters and whose feet are the earth—he, the inner self of all beings, is to be meditated upon.

Thus, having meditated upon one's own self as the nature of Virāṭ and contemplated it, and having recited twenty-five times the *ajapā-mantra*— which consists of the inhalation and exhalation of the vital breath (*prāṇavāyu*)— and having offered it, one should proceed according to the path taught by the venerable Guru, preceded by the contemplation of the internal sound (*nāda*).
Having contemplated, "I am proceeding as some manifestation of consciousness, with all limiting adjuncts cast aside," [he addresses:
"O Goddess whose garment is the ocean, whose breasts are the mountains! for the performance of his own duties.
O Consort of Viṣṇu, salutations to you; forgive my touch of your feet.

Having thus requested the ground, and having placed his foot upon it following the movement of his breath while reciting "May all practitioners rejoice" and so forth, he goes outside, performs the purification and sipping of water after voiding urine and excrement, and [recites] *klīṃ*.

One should perform the cleansing of the teeth with the mantra: "Obeisance to Kāmadeva, who captivates the minds of all people" (or "to the Beloved"). Then, having gone to a river or similar place and completed the Vedic bath (*vaidikasnāna*), one should begin the Tantric bath (*tāntrikasnāna*).
As for that, first, having washed the hands, feet, and face with the root-mantra (*mūla*), [one recites]: "Oṃ, O wearer of jewels, wielder of the thunderbolt, Great Protectress..."

Having tied the topknot with "rakṣa 2 hūṃ phaṭ svāhā," and having sipped water three times with the root mantra, and having performed six mouthfuls of rinsing with the root mantra "āṃ hrīṃ," one should say: "hrīṃ, salutations to the sage Vaiśvānara;
be pleased by flowers, arghya, incense, lamps, and so forth; at the time of bathing, ward off obstacles, ward them off, svāhā."

Having sprinkled [the stone] ten times with the root mantra, having taken earth from the bank, and having washed the stone with "svāhā," one should place the earth upon it and perform the bath. Therein, first: "O Root, I purify the *ātmatattva*, svāhā"; O Root, "I purify the *vidyātattva*, svāhā"; O Root, "I purify the *śivatattva*, svāhā."

Having thus sipped water (ācamana) and performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the seers (*ṛṣi*) and so forth upon the hands and the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), one should divide the clay into three portions with the mantra *oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ jvālāmukhi hrīṃ phaṭ svāhā*. Then, one should purify one portion of the clay with *oṃ*. Next, taking another portion of the clay, one should perform the formal resolve (*saṅkalpa*) for the bath, beginning with "Today... and so forth. Then...
Standing in a river with water reaching up to the navel, one should mentally designate a square sacred space (*tīrtha*) measuring one cubit in front of oneself in the water, and recite:
*Oṃ, O Sun, the sacred waters within the belly of the universe have been touched by your rays.*
By that truth, O Lord of Gods, O Maker of Day, grant me sacred fords.
Having thus prayed to the Sūryārtīrtha, one pierces the solar disc with the *krom* syllable and the hook-gesture (*aṅkuśamudrā*), [reciting]:
"Oṃ gāṃ! O Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Godāvarī, Sarasvatī, Narmadā, Sindhu, and Kāverī—be present in this water!"

Thus, having invoked the sacred waters (*tīrthas*) from the solar orb (*sūryamaṇḍala*) and joined them with the previously prepared water, one should again invoke the power of the sacred waters (*tīrthaśakti*) from the solar orb itself with the mantra: *hvāṃ hvīṃ hvūṃ hvaiṃ hvauṃ hvaḥ, O Tīrthaśakti consisting of all bliss, come, come, svāhā*. One should then meditate upon her within that mandala of sacred waters as follows: [as described].
Consisting entirely of bliss, destroying all misfortunes, possessing the luster of the moon,
and three-eyed, she holds in her two upper hands a noose and a goad respectively.

I worship the Śrītīrtha-Śakti, who holds in her two hands a golden pitcher filled with nectar and a white rosary, who is clothed in white garments, and who is accompanied by the two rivers Gaṅgā and Sindhu and others.

Having meditated thus, one should empower that water eight times with the root mantra while in the *yonimudrā*; then, having stirred it with "hrīṃ," transformed it into nectar with "vaṃ" using the *dhenumudrā*, and having projected the three principles (*tattva*) into the water— reciting "oṃ ātmatattvāya namaḥ, oṃ vidyātattvāya namaḥ, oṃ śivatattvāya namaḥ"— one should sprinkle one's own head with it three times.

Having thrown one portion of clay into the water, having purified the limbs with a second portion of clay, and having taken up the third portion, one should perform the invocation of the deity (*devatāvāhana*). As follows:
"O Jvālāmukhī, mounted upon the jackal (*śivā*), endowed with the three seed-syllables *oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*!"
O Goddess, accompanied by your retinue, be present in these waters.

Thus, having invoked the deity with the third *mṛd* (earth/water) and visualized the *yantra* therein in the water, one should consecrate Jvālāmukhī three times with the mantra: *oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ jvālāmukhi mama śatrūn utsāraya 2*. Then, having sipped water (*ācamana*) three times over oneself as before with the root mantra (*mūla*), and while recollecting the root mantra, one should block the seven apertures beginning with the ears.

One should immerse oneself and emerge from the water three times. Then, having offered a handful of water to the Sun with the mantra "Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Saḥ, this handful of water is for Sūrya," and having sipped water (ācamana) three times, one should sprinkle one's own head seven times with the root mantra and mutter the root mantra ten times.
Having ascended to the bank from the water and put on two washed garments, [one should do so] with the root mantra.
One should apply the *tripuṇḍra*, the *ūrdhvapuṇḍra*, or the *tilaka*. This is the procedure for bathing (*snānavidhi*).
Thereafter, having first performed the Vedic *saṃdhyā*, one should begin the Tantric *saṃdhyā*. As follows:
having consecrated the water from a sacred site (*tīrtha*) before oneself with the *dhenumudrā* as nectar, and having empowered it eight times with the root mantra (*mūla*), with that [water]—
Having sprinkled one's own head with water using the Mātṛkā mantra, beginning with *aṃ namaḥ* and ending with *kṣaṃ namaḥ*,
and having sprinkled it three times with the root mantra (*mūla*), one should take water in the left hand, cover it with the right hand,
and consecrate it seven times with the mantras of the five elements— *laṃ vaṃ raṃ yaṃ haṃ*— and with the root mantra.
Having consecrated it three times with the root mantra, one should sprinkle one’s own head three times with drops of that water using the *tattvamudrā*.

Then, placing the remaining water in the right hand, one draws that water—which has taken the form of light—into oneself through the *iḍā* [left nostril], thereby washing away all impurities situated within one's body; then, through the *piṅgalā* [right nostril], one expels that water, which has become black in color.

Thinking that [the impurity] has gone outside, he should again take it in his left hand and, having visualized a blazing vajra-stone on his own left side, should strike it against that stone with the Pāśupatāstra mantra: *oṃ ślīṃ paśu huṃ phaṭ*. Then, taking water with the root mantra (*mūla*), via the flowing channel (*pravahannāḍī*)...

Having visualized [the self] as having become one with the supreme nectar of the thousand-petaled lotus, and having brought it forth, one should sprinkle one’s own head three times with that water using *kuśa* grass while reciting: *oṃ amṛtamālinyai svāhā*. Then, the *ātmatattva*...

"I purify, svāhā! Thus, I purify the *vidyātattva*, the *śivatattva*, the *śivatattva*, the *vidyātattva*, the *ātmatattva*, and the root *sarvatattva*. Having thus sipped water three times, and having likewise sipped it nine times, one should take water in both hands, rise, and [recite]: *oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ*.

Having offered the arghya three times to the Kula-Sūrya with the mantra: *śrīmārtaṇḍabhairavāya prakāśaśaktisahitāya idamarghyaṃ parikalpayāmi svāhā*, one should then lead the Root Goddess from the heart-lotus to the solar orb (*sūryamaṇḍala*), meditate upon her there according to the rules, worship her with mental offerings (*mānasopacāra*), and [recite]: *oṃ jvālārūpiṇyai vidmahe*.

"Let us meditate upon the one who devours the world; may that Jvālā inspire us. Having offered three *arghya* oblations to the venerable Goddess with this root *gāyatrī* during the four *sandhyā*s, and having recited the *gāyatrī* and the root mantra as much as possible, one should again perform the *prāṇāyāma*, the *ṛṣi*-assignment, and so forth, along with the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*), and then perform the libation (*tarpaṇa*) with "O Guhya... and so on.
Having offered the fruit of the recitation (*japa*) and having brought the Śrī Devī into the lotus of the heart, one should dismiss her from the sacred water (*tīrtha*).
This is the procedure for the *sandhyā*. Having thus performed the four *sandhyās*, the practitioner (*sādhaka*) becomes one whose form is that of the Śrī Devī;
therefore, the four *sandhyās* must necessarily be performed. Alternatively, [one may perform] only the morning [sandhyā].
"One should perform the twilight worship alone and must not abandon it"—this is the teaching of Śiva.

Then one should perform the libation (*tarpaṇa*). Having invoked the sacred site (*tīrtha*) as before and rendered it nectarine with the root mantra and the *amṛtamudrā*, one should meditate upon the *yantra* in that water. Then, having brought the Goddess together with her retinue from the heart, one should effect the ritual integration (*sakalīkaraṇa*) by means of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*).

Having consecrated [the disciple] with the nectar through the practice of Kuṇḍalinī and having worshipped according to the rules, one should satisfy [the deities] three times in the northeast with the mantra "May the venerable Śrī Guru Amukānandanātha Bhairava be satisfied," and likewise in the fire [corner, southeast]: "May the Paramaguru be satisfied"; in the southwest: "May the Paramācārya-guru be satisfied"; and in the northwest: "May the [Parama-]guru be satisfied."

"Parameṣṭhiguruḥ"—having thus gratified [the lineage] three times or once, [one says]: "May the gurus of the Divine Current (divyaugha), the Siddha Current (siddhaugha), and the Human Current (mānavaugha) be gratified. Then, within the *bindu*: "May the venerable Goddess Jvālāmukhī, together with Mahādeva Bhairava, along with her retinue, her vehicle, her weapons, and her mudrās, be gratified. Hrīṃ."

Having offered libations with the words, "May the Yoginīs and Mothers who move through the unbroken realms of Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, and Svaḥ be satisfied," and having again offered libations to the Śrī Devī within the *bindu*, he should bring her back into his heart, dismiss the sacred waters (*tīrthas*) to their respective places,
perform *prāṇāyāma* and the other rites once more, and take up a water-pot (*kamaṇḍalu*) filled with water while reciting the root mantra.

Recalling the *mūlamantra*, one should enter the sacrificial hall (*yāgageha*). There, one should worship the deities of the doorway with water and other offerings, as follows: *blūṃ vāsukaye namaḥ* [to Vāsuki] at the top; *narasiṃhāya* [to Narasiṃha]...
Having worshipped thus: "Oṃ, salutation to Sumukhī below; Hrīṃ, salutation to Satyā on the left;
Śrīṃ, salutation to Umā on the right; Hrīṃ, salutation to Dehalī above; Hrīṃ Aṃ, salutation to Alindā below;
Oṃ Hrīṃ Jvāṃ, salutation to Jvālinī; Oṃ Hrīṃ Dvāṃ, salutation to Dvāraśrī. Then [recite] Oṃ.

"Salutation to Vāstupuruṣa," [he says] in the center. Then, entering within by contracting the left limb, he should gaze upon the sacrificial ground with the root mantra and, having spread a seat there, perform the purification of the seat.
As follows: "Of this venerable mantra for the purification of the seat, Merupṛṣṭha is the seer (ṛṣi), Sutala..."

Chanda is Kūrma, the deity; the application (viniyoga) is for the purification of the seat. *Namaḥ* to Merupṛṣṭha, the Ṛṣi, on the head; *namaḥ* to Sutala, the Chanda, on the face; *namaḥ* to Kūrma, the deity, on the heart; *namaḥ* to the application for the purification of the seat on all limbs. *Oṃ prīṃ, O Earth, you are supported by...* [thus [addressing] the earth].

Having worshipped the seat with "Prārthya maṇḍūkāya namaḥ," "Kālāgnirudrāya namaḥ," "Hrīṃ ādhāraśaktikamalāsanāya namaḥ," and "Hrīṃ pīṭhāsanāya namaḥ," one should sit upon it and assume the state of consciousness (saṃvid) according to the mantra.
O Consciousness, born of Brahman, daughter of Brahman, eternally stainless;
for the sake of the satiation of the Brāhmaṇas, be forever purifying.

Oṃ, homage to Brāhmaṇī, svāhā! Oṃ, O Goddess who brings about the root of success, who awakens deficient understanding, who subdues those honored by kings, and who destroys the faction of enemies! Aiṃ, homage to Kṣatriyā, svāhā! O you who are the blazing fire for the fuel of ignorance!

O you who are the form of Brahman, the fire of knowledge! Considering this offering of bliss to be true affection, grant me perfect wisdom. *Hrīṃ*, obeisance to Vaiśyā, *svāhā*. I bow, I bow to you, O revealer of the path of Yoga; O Mother, conqueror of the three worlds, be the bestower of the fruit of samādhi.
*klīṃ śūdrāyai namaḥ svāhā*. *Oṃ amṛte amṛtodbhave amṛtavarṣiṇi amṛtam ākarṣaya 2 siddhiṃ dehi 2 śrījvālāmukhīpadaṃ me vaśyam ānaya 2 svāhā*.
Having thus recited the root mantra seven times over that [liquid] and consecrated it as nectar (*amṛta*) with the *yonimudrā*, [one should proceed].
"Come, come! Be present, be present! Be firmly established, be firmly established! Be restrained, be restrained! Be near, be near!

Accept this worship accompanied by all ritual offerings, svāhā! Having thus displayed the mudrās and performed the binding of the ten directions with finger-snaps, one should [place] the Śrīgurupādukā-vidyā upon one's own head.

Having gratified the lineage of the Śrī-gurus sevenfold or threefold, one should gratify the Śrī-devī within one’s own heart—along with her weapons, her vehicle, her retinue, and Śiva—by means of the root mantra. Then, one should offer oblation into the mouth with this mantra: *aiṃ vada vada vāgvādini mama jihvāgre sthirībhava sarvasattvavaśaṅkari svāhā*.
Then, having become filled with bliss,
[he says]:
"May those beings who dwell upon the earth depart from here."
May those beings who create obstacles perish by the command of Śiva.
May those beings who act as heretics, whether dwelling on the earth, in the intermediate space,
or situated in the heavenly world, perish by the command of Śiva.
Thus, having dispelled the three kinds of obstacles by striking the ground three times with the left heel while giving three upward claps with the index and middle fingers,
and having performed the binding of the ten directions with snapping sounds, one should visualize a wall of fire in the four cardinal directions.
One should perform breath control (prāṇāyāma) as follows:
Inhale through the *iḍā* [left nostril] sixteen times; hold the breath within for four sets of sixty [breaths];
and exhale slowly through the *piṅgalā* [right nostril] in ten, ten, ten, and two [additional] counts.

Thus, having contemplated one’s own body as fit for the worship of the deity—its every impurity having been dispelled by the threefold *prāṇāyāma*—one should perform the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*). As follows:
from the *mūlādhāra*, by means of the mantra "Haṃsa," one [leads] Kuṇḍalinī together with the earth to the *svādhiṣṭhāna*.

Having brought [the earth] there, one should visualize the earth dissolved in that water; then, having brought it from there along with the water to Maṇipūra, one should visualize the water dissolved in that fire; then, having brought it from there along with the fire to Anāhata, one should visualize the fire dissolved in that air; then, having brought it from there along with the air to Viśuddhi—
There, having visualized the wind dissolved in space, one brings it together with that space into the *ājñā-cakra*; then,
having contemplated the space dissolved in the mind situated there, the mind dissolved in the *nāda*, and the *nāda* dissolved in the resonance (*dhvani*).
[One should meditate on the Self] in the form of a radiant drop situated in the center of the lunar disc within the pericarp of the thousand-petaled lotus,
[and visualize] the personification of sin (pāpapuruṣa) residing in the left side of the abdomen, with the luster of collyrium,
having the murder of a Brahmin for its head and the theft of gold for its two arms.

The heart is joined with the drinking of liquor, and the two hips with violating the Guru’s bed; the pair of feet belongs to those who associate with such sinners—this constitutes the sin of the limbs and minor members.
One should visualize the sinner in his belly as having body hair like that of a minor offender, with red beard and eyes, wrathful, and bearing a sword and shield.
