Having thus meditated upon the personification of sin (pāpapuruṣa), one should recite the seed-syllable of air (*vāyubīja*), *yam*, which is smoke-colored, sixteen times according to the rules of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), thereby completely drying up that personification of sin. Then, reciting the seed-syllable of fire (*vahnibīja*), *ram*, which is red-colored, sixty-four times, one should burn that very same [personification] away. [Finally, one should recite] the seed-syllable of nectar (*amṛtabīja*), *vam*...
Having meditated upon the thousand-spoked [wheel],
reciting [the mantra] thirty-two times, one produces a sinless body by means of the stream of nectar arising therefrom.

Having made [the body] firm by means of the yellow-colored seed-syllable *laṃ*, the seed of the earth located at the forehead, one should— by means of the root-seed-syllable *hrīṃ* situated at the base and the mantra *so 'haṃ*— unify the Kuṇḍalinī with nectar and join the five elements and the individual soul (*jīvātman*) to their respective locations on the path of Brahman. This is the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*).
Then, having visualized oneself in the form of the Goddess and placing the hand upon the heart, one should perform the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* (consecration of the vital breaths) as follows:
*oṃ āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ mama prāṇā iha prāṇāḥ 18/ mama jīva iha sthitaḥ 18/ mama sarvendriyāṇi...*

"May my speech, mind, skin, eyes, ears, nose, and vital breaths, which were situated here [in the previous body], come here and remain happily for a long time—svāhā! Having thus performed the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā*, one should perform the recollection of the *ṛṣi* and other components of one's own *mūlamantra*. As follows:

Oṃ. Of this King of Mantras, the Śrījvālāmukhī-mantra-rāja, the Seer (ṛṣi) is the illustrious Vaiśvānara, the Metre (chandaḥ) is Anuṣṭubh, the Deity (devatā) is the illustrious Jvālāmukhī whose form is non-dual, the Seed-syllable (bīja) is Hrīṃ, the Power (śakti) is Śrīṃ, the Pin (kīlaka) is Hūṃ;
my application (viniyoga) is in the recitation for the sake of Dharma, Artha, Kāma, and Mokṣa—thus one should speak with palms joined in reverence.

Salutation to Vaiśvānara the Ṛṣi on the head; salutation to Anuṣṭubh the Chandas on the mouth; salutation to Jvālāmukhī the Devatā on the heart; salutation to the Bīja "hrīṃ" on the private parts; salutation to the Śakti "śrīṃ" on the feet; salutation to the Kīlaka "hūṃ" on the navel; salutation to the Viniyoga for the recitation on all limbs.

Oṃ hrāṃ śrāṃ, salutation to the two thumbs; hrīṃ śrīṃ, [salutation] to the index fingers; hrūṃ śrūṃ, [salutation] to the middle fingers; hraiṃ śraiṃ, [salutation] to the ring fingers; hrauṃ śrauṃ, [salutation] to the little fingers; hraḥ śraḥ, [salutation] to the palms.
In this manner, perform the placement (*nyāsa*) on the heart and other limbs. Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, salutation to the head; Jvālāmukhi, [salutation] to my heart.
"Devour all enemies at the navel! Hūṃ at the genitals! Phaṭ svāhā at the secret place! Namaḥ on all limbs! Thus is the ritual placement of the mantra (mantranyāsa).
Now, the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the *Mātṛkā* with mantras: Oṃ aṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ oṃ, salutation to the head.

Similarly: Āṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ Hrīṃ, on the forehead. Iṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ Śrīṃ, on the two eyes. Īṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ Jvāṃ, on the mouth. Uṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ Lāṃ, on the throat. Ūṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ Śuṃ, on the two shoulders. Ṛṃ raṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ, on the two hands. Ṝṃ laṃ... [continues]

*Ḷaṃ vaṃ* on my two breasts; *ḹṃ śaṃ* [conquer] all enemies in the heart; *eṃ ṣaṃ* devour in the belly; *aiṃ saṃ* devour on the two sides; *oṃ haṃ hūṃ* on the genitals; *auṃ laṃ phaṭ* on the private parts; *aṃ aḥ kṣaṃ svāhā namaḥ* on the feet. Thus is the placement of the Mantra-Mātṛkā (*samantramātṛkānyāsa*).

Now follows the internal placement of the Mātṛkās (Antarmātṛkānyāsa). In this practice, inhalation (*pūraka*) is performed with the vowels; retention (*kumbhaka*) with the consonants from *ka* to *ma*; and exhalation (*recaka*) with the consonants from *ya* onwards. Oṃ. Of this venerable Antarmātṛkānyāsa, Brahmā is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the meter (*chandas*), the venerable Antarmātṛkā-Sarasvatī is the deity (*devatā*), the consonants are the seeds (*bīja*), the vowels are the powers (*śakti*), and the Unmanifest (*avyakta*) is the bolt (*kīlaka*).
Having performed the assignment (*nyāsa*) and application (*viniyoga*), one should place [the mantras] while recollecting them with palms joined:
to the Brahman-seer (*brahmarṣi*) Śi0, to the Gāyatrī metre (*chandas*) in the mouth, and to the goddess Antarmātṛkā-Sarasvatī as the deity (*devatā*) in the heart. (p. 364)

"To the half-seeds, salutation on the secret place; to the vowels, to the Śaktis, and to the feet; to the unmanifest *kīlaka*, to the navel; to the application (*viniyoga*), salutation on all limbs"—thus is the ritual placement of the seers and so forth (*ṛṣyādinyāsa*).

Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aṃ Kaṃ 5 Āṃ, to the two thumbs, *namaḥ*. Likewise [for the other fingers]. Iṃ Caṃ 5 Īṃ, to the two index fingers (*tarjanī*), *namaḥ*. Uṃ Ṭaṃ 5 Ūṃ, to the two middle fingers (*madhyamā*), *namaḥ*. Eṃ Taṃ 5 Aiṃ, to the two ring fingers (*anāmikā*), *namaḥ*. Oṃ Paṃ 5 Auṃ, to the two little fingers (*kaniṣṭhikā*), *namaḥ*. Aṃ Yaṃ 10 Aḥ, to the palms and backs of the hands. Thus is the placement (*nyāsa*) of the heart and other limbs.
Then, for the meditation:
[one should visualize her] resembling pure crystal, adorned with pure silken garments,
with ornaments sparkling with pearls and gems, holding a rosary and a water-pot.

Having thus meditated upon the Supreme Goddess holding a book and a boon-granting gesture within the lotus of the heart, the wise practitioner should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the Mātṛkās.

Having meditated thus, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*). *Aṃ* 16 at the throat; *kaṃ* 12 in the *anāhata*; *ḍaṃ* 10 at the navel; *baṃ* 6 in the *svādhiṣṭhāna*; *vaṃ* 4 in the *mūlādhāra*; and *laṃ-kṣaṃ* between the eyebrows—this is the internal *mātṛkā*. Thereafter, one should perform the external *mātṛkā-nyāsa* as prescribed.

Then follows the placement of the principles (*tattvanyāsa*). Reciting the root mantra: *ātmatattvāya svāhā*, from the feet up to the navel; *vidyātattvāya svāhā*, from the navel up to the space between the eyebrows; *śivatattvāya svāhā*, from the *ājñā* center up to the head;
*sarvatattvebhyaḥ svāhā*, on all the limbs. This is the placement of the principles. Now, [the placement of the letters].
The placement of the root mantra (*mūlamantranyāsa*): *Oṃ namaḥ* on the head; *hrīṃ* on the forehead; *śrīṃ* between the eyebrows.

[Regarding the unlocking (*utkīlana*) and other rites for this mantra: *Śrīṃ mūlaṃ hrīṃ utkīlanāya namaḥ*. *Hūṃ mūlaṃ phaṭ sañjīvanāya namaḥ*. *Oṃ jvālāmukhi mama sarvaśatrūn*... [the rest of the mantra follows].

*Bhakṣaya 2 hūṃ phaṭ svāhā | Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ tauṭilyāya namaḥ.* By which mantra, O Goddess of Devas, the venerable goddess Tvaritā is fully manifested and grants boons—that is proclaimed as *Tauṭilya*. Without the *Tauṭilya* mantra, everything shall become fruitless. *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ jvālāmukhi*...

Release the curse of Bhairava, release it, hūṃ svāhā; obeisance to the remover of curses. Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ, obeisance to Kurukullā. O fair-faced one, she who brings about mental clarity during bathing, recitation, and fire-offerings is renowned as Kurukullā among practitioners. O beloved, he who performs the recitation of the mantra while abandoning Kurukullā—

All recitation and other rites of the practitioner will certainly become fruitless. Now, for the weapon-mantra: *Oṃ strīṃ jvālādevyastrāya hrīṃ mahāstrāya śrīṃ sarvāstrāya hūṃ phaṭ astrāya astravidyāyai namaḥ*. This should be recited three times.
Jvāṃ at the nose; lāṃ at the eyes; muṃ at the mouth; khiṃ at the throat; maṃ at the shoulders; maṃ at the breasts;
saṃ at the chest; rvaṃ at the belly; śaṃ at the sides; trūn at the navel; maṃ at the penis.

*Kṣaṃ* on the back, *yaṃ* on the waist, *bhaṃ* on the anus, *kṣaṃ* on the penis, *yaṃ* on the two thighs, *hūṃ* on the two knees, *phaṭ* on the two shanks, *svāṃ* on the two ankles, *hāṃ* on the two feet, and the root mantra (*mūla*) on all the limbs.
This is the ritual placement of the root mantra (*mūlamantranyāsa*).
Now, the placement of the deities (*daivatanya-āsa*): Oṃ Hrīṃ! Salutation to the goddess Māyā, together with Vāruṇī and Vātyālī, on the head.

Hrīṃ! Salutation to Mohinī, together with Śrīvārāhī and Kulasundarī, on the face. Hrīṃ! Salutation to the goddess Bālā, together with Śrīkūvarī and Kaulinī, on the heart. Śrīṃ! [Salutation] to the goddess Bhagarūpiṇī...

*Oṃ hrīṃ śrīkuṇṭhīkutsitāsahitāyai namaḥ* on the belly. *Hrīṃ bhagāvāsādevyai śrīkuṭilākuhūsahitāyai namaḥ* on the navel. *Hrīṃ bheruṇḍādevyai śrīkuntīkumbheśvarīsahitāyai namaḥ* on the ankle. *Hrīṃ mṛḍānīdevyai*... [on the knee].

"Salutation to Śrī Kuntākūcarī, together with [her attendants], on the two ankles. *Śrīṃ hrīṃ*, salutation to the goddess Baindaveśvarī, together with Śrī Kāruṇīkṛti, on the two feet. Thus is the placement of the deities (*daivatanya*).

As before, one should perform the nyāsa of the Ṛṣis and so forth, as well as the Pīṭha-nyāsa. For example: "Salutation to Maṇḍūka at the Mūlādhāra; salutation to Kālāgnirudra at the Svādhiṣṭhāna; salutation to Ādhāraśakti at the Maṇipūraka; salutation to Prakṛti at the heart; [salutation] to Kamaṭha; [salutation] to Śeṣa."
To the one seated upon the ocean of nectar (sudhārṇavāsana); to the Earth; to the Ocean of Sugarcane Juice;

to the Ocean of Wine; to the Ocean of Clarified Butter; to the Ocean of Milk. To Dharma on the right shoulder; to Jñāna on the left shoulder; to Vairāgya on the left thigh; to Aiśvarya on the right thigh; to Adharma on the face; [and] on the left side.
To Ajñāna (Ignorance) at the navel; to Avairāgya (Non-detachment) on the right side; to Anaiśvarya (Lack of Sovereignty) at the heart.
Again, at the heart: to Māyā; to Vidyā; to Ananta; to Dharma; to Ānandakanda (the Root of Bliss);
to Saṃvinnāla (the Stem of Consciousness); to the petals consisting of Prakṛti; to the filaments consisting of Vikṛti.
To the pericarp, which is enriched with the seed-syllables of the fifty letters and is the form of all principles (tattvas); to the solar mandala (aṃ); to the lunar mandala (soṃ);
to the fiery mandala (raṃ); to the Self (āṃ); to the Inner Self (aṃ);
to the Supreme Self (paṃ); to the Self of Knowledge (hrīṃ); to the seat of the pedestal (hrīṃ); to the seat of the six chakras (hrīṃ).

Having performed the *pīṭhanyāsa* with: "Oṃ hūṃ, obeisance to the pericarp of the thousand-petaled lotus; hrīṃ, obeisance to the corpse-seat; hrīṃ, obeisance to the Veda-seat; hrīṃ, obeisance to the corpse-seat; hrīṃ, obeisance to the Veda-seat; hrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā, obeisance to the Rudra-lotus pedestal," one should meditate upon the goddess Śrī Jvālāmukhī right there as non-different from oneself.
As follows:
[I meditate upon her] who stands upon a mountain of flames, three-eyed, presiding over the three seats,
adorned with a profusion of flames, fair-faced, eternal, and invisible to common people.

I bow to Jvālāmukhī, who dwells in the center of the lotuses of the six chakras, who bears the boon-granting arrow, the lotus, and the gesture of fearlessness, whose nature is consciousness, and who illuminates all objects of knowledge.

Thus, having meditated upon the Śrī Devī within the lotus of the heart and contemplated her as one with oneself, one should offer a handful of flowers to one’s own head with the root mantra (mūlavidyā). Then, having again meditated upon the Goddess in the lotus of the heart in the form described above— along with Her limbs (aṅga), Her attendants (āvaraṇa), and Śiva— one should perform the worship of the pedestal (pīṭhapūjā) according to the method to be explained hereafter.

Having worshipped with mental offerings and presented the food offering (*naivedya*), one should perform the *antarvaiśvadeva* at the time of eating. Therein, having meditated upon the fourfold self— namely the *ātman*, *antarātman*, *paramātman*, and *jñānātman*— as a square sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) blazing with the fire of *kuṇḍalinī* in the *mūlādhāra*, [one should worship] the venerable Supreme Deity there.
Having meditated, at the end of the root-mantra, one offers the ego-sense (*ahaṃtā*) into His mouth with "svāhā.
In this manner, having offered each of the following— egoism, untruth, malice, desire, anger, greed, delusion, pride, and envy—
individually with the ladle of the mind attached to the *suṣumṇā* as the sacrificial spoon, [one offers them] into the blazing fire of merit and demerit.
In the fire of my own self, with the mind as the sacrificial ladle, I perpetually offer the functions of the senses through the path of the *suṣumṇā*;

*svāhā*. Grasping the ladle of *unmanī* with the hands of light and space, I offer into the fire that which is filled with the oil of the portions of merit and demerit; *svāhā*. Having thus offered the oblation,
Or rather—
into the fire of consciousness, which blazes within without external fuel and acts as an adversary to the darkness of illusion;
into that certain ground of wondrously expanding rays, I offer the universe, beginning with the earth and ending with Śiva.
Svāhā!

Having thus offered oblations, one should again meditate upon the Śrī Devī within the heart-lotus, worship her with all the services beginning with the *uttarāpośāna*, and recite the root mantra as much as possible.
Having offered the recitation through breath-control (*prāṇāyāma*) and other means, one should prostrate to the Śrī Guru and [anoint] one's own body with fragrance and other substances.

Having adorned oneself mentally according to one's ability and performed recitation (*japa*), fire-oblation (*homa*), and other rites, one should meditate on one's own body as the form of *Kāmakalā*, thereby making the body fit for worship, and then prepare the ordinary water offering (*sāmānyārghya*).

In that regard, having fashioned a circular diagram with a triangle within it to the right of oneself, one should offer salutation to the Support-Energy (*Ādhāraśakti*) therein: "Salutation to Ādhāraśakti."

Having thus worshipped [the vessel], having placed a tripod upon it, and having worshipped it with "Oṃ *raṃ* obeisance to the fire-maṇḍala consisting of ten kalās," one should place there a washed vessel such as a conch, etc., while reciting "Oṃ *phaṭ* obeisance to the weapon-mantra (*astra*)," and then worship it with "Oṃ *aṃ* obeisance to the sun-maṇḍala consisting of twelve kalās."

Having filled that vessel with pure water and worshipped it with the mantra, "Oṃ, salutation to the lunar disc consisting of sixteen digits," one should invoke the sacred waters (tīrthas) therein with the verse beginning, "O Gaṅgā and Yamunā," and cast upon them perfumes, unbroken rice grains, and flowers. Having thus worshipped the digits of the Sun and the Moon, one should display the *dhenumudrā*.
"One should show [it]"—this is the general rule for the *arghya* offering.

367) Then, having fashioned on one's left a mandala consisting of a circle with an outer perimeter and two triangles within a hexagon, together with a central bindu, one should perform worship there according to the sequence of the pedestal-worship (pīṭhapūjā), beginning with "Obeisance to Maṇḍūkā" and so forth.

One should begin the worship of the *pīṭha*. Then, having washed the base with "Namaḥ" and placed it upon the mandala, one should worship it with "Raṃ, obeisance to the fire-mandala consisting of ten kalās. Having washed the flask with "Phaṭ" and filled it with the causal [liquid], one should adorn it with red cloth, garlands, and so forth, regarding it as the Śrīdevī.
Having established [the vessel] with "Aṃ, obeisance to the solar orb consisting of twelve digits," one worships the jar;

having worshipped the substance with "Soṃ, obeisance to the lunar orb consisting of sixteen digits," one protects it with "Phaṭ," veils it with "Hūṃ," gazes upon it with the root mantra, and smells the fragrance in the jar with the root mantra.
Having offered a flower, one should perform the rite for release from the curse as follows:
Oṃ. The Supreme Brahman alone is eternal, consisting of both the gross and the subtle;
by that [Brahman], I destroy the sin of killing a Brāhmaṇa arising from your hair. (1)
Oṃ! O Goddess, born from the solar disc, arisen from the abode of Varuṇa, composed of the seed-syllable *amā*, may [this] be released from the curse of Śukra. || 2 ||
Oṃ! If the Praṇava is the seed of the Vedas and consists of the bliss of Brahman, by that truth, O Goddess of Gods, may the sin of killing a Brahmin be removed. (3)

Thus three times; then: *vāṃ vīṃ vūṃ vaiṃ vauṃ vaḥ*, "Salutation to Surādevī, who is liberated from the curse of Brahmā," thus three times; and having recited: *hrīṃ śrīṃ krāṃ krīṃ krūṃ kraiṃ krauṃ kraḥ*, "Liberate [her] from the curse of Kṛṣṇa, liberate!
Cause the nectar to flow, cause it to flow! Svāhā! thus also three times: *oṃ hrīṃ*.

Salutations to you, O mass of splendor, who gladdens all beings, peacock-faced one, bestower of unfailing success, cause of great enthusiasm, skull-bearer! Increase, increase! Color, color! Grant me the commitment, grant it twice! O you who possess the liquor of Rudra and Raudra, destroyer of the curse of Śukra, remover of the sin of killing a Brahmin! Hrīṃ hūṃ lāṃ lūṃ!

One should recite ten times the mantra for removing the curse of Śukra: *phaṭ phaṭ svāhā*. One should also recite three times: *oṃ haṃsaḥ śuciṣad vasur antarikṣasadd hotā vedisad atithir duroṇasat | nṛṣad varasad ṛtasad vyomasad abjā gojā ṛtajā adrijā ṛtam*.
Then one should meditate upon Ānandabhairava and Surādevī as follows: "The god has eighteen arms, five faces, and three eyes; he resembles ten million suns and is as cool as ten million moons. (1)
He stands in the midst of the ocean of nectar, seated upon a Brahma-lotus;
he is mounted upon a bull, has a blue throat, and is adorned with all ornaments.
The god holds a skull-cup and a khaṭvāṅga staff, sounds a bell and a ḍamaru drum, and wields a noose and a goad, as well as a mace and a club. || 3 ||
He holds a sword, a shield, a battle-axe, a mallet, a trident, and a spear;
he carries a variegated shield, and his hands display a severed head, the gesture of granting boons, and the gesture of fearlessness.
The best of practitioners should meditate upon Lohita, the Lord of the Gods of gods;
having offered a handful of flowers into the jar, he should recite the mantra of Ānandabhairava.
Having thus meditated upon Ānandabhairava, one should meditate upon Surādevī as follows:
"While the ocean was being churned— the Ocean of Milk, the best of seas—
therein was born Surādevī, assuming the form of a young maiden."
And one should meditate upon the goddess Surā, possessing the radiance of ten million times ten thousand moons,
white as snow, jasmine, and the moon, with five faces and three eyes.
Endowed with eighteen arms, intent on bestowing all bliss,
smiling, large-eyed, and facing the God of gods.

Having thus meditated upon the goddess Surādevī, one should worship the God and Goddess three times with the mantras: *hasarakṣamalavaya-ūṃ ānandabhairavāya vauṣaṭ* and *sahakṣamalavaraya-ūṃ surādevyai vauṣaṭ*.
Then, having recited the root mantra ten times, one should [place] the syllables *aṃ 16*, *kaṃ 16*, and *thaṃ 16* in three rows, rotating clockwise.

Having drawn the wheel of powers beginning with *it* and so forth, and having written *haṃ kṣaṃ* in its center, one should contemplate nectar within the substance through absorption in this [mantra]; then, having rendered it nectar by means of the *dhenumudrā*, and holding the jar while reciting the nectar-seed *vaṃ* and the root-mantra eight times, [one should place it] between oneself and the *śrīcakra*.

Having drawn a triangle, a hexagon, a circle, and a square, one should worship within the square with: "Oṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ! Salutation to Pūrṇagiri-pīṭha! "Oṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ! Salutation to Uḍḍīyāṇa-pīṭha! "Oṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ! Salutation to Kāmarūpa-pīṭha! "Oṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ! Salutation to Jālandhara-pīṭha! Having thus worshipped and having worshipped the hexagon with the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga), [one should proceed].

Having worshipped the triangle with "Oṃ namaḥ" at the front, "Hrīṃ namaḥ" on the right, and "Śrīṃ namaḥ" on the left, and having worshipped the center with "Oṃ Hrīṃ Ādhāraśaktaye namaḥ," one should place the yantra— adorned with a hexagon within the triangle— and, having sprinkled it with water from the general arghya vessel, perform its worship.
For example: *yaṃ* homage to Dhūmrārcis; *raṃ* to Ūṣmā; *laṃ* to Jvalinī;
*vaṃ* to Jvālinī; *śaṃ* to Visphuliṅginī; *ṣaṃ* to Suśrī; *saṃ* to Surūpā; *haṃ* to Kapilā; *laṃ* to Havyavāhā; *kṣaṃ*.

Having worshipped with "Obeisance to Kavyavāhā," and having worshipped in the center with "Obeisance to the Fire-mandala, whose self consists of ten kalās," and having worshipped the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga) in the hexagon, [one should worship] the Goddess in the center with the root mantra (mūla).
Having worshipped [it] with "HŪṂ HŪṂ BRAHMĀṆḌACAṢAKĀYA PHAṬ SVĀHĀ," one should wash a coconut vessel, place it upon the yantra, and [place the syllables] therein: KAṂ BHAṂ TAPINYAI NAMAḤ,
KHAṂ BAṂ TĀPINYAI, GAṂ PHAṂ DHŪMRĀYAI, GHAṂ PAṂ MARĪCYAI, ṄAṂ NAṂ JVALINYAI, CAṂ DHAṂ.

*Rucyai* (to Ruci) *chaṃ*; to Suṣumnā *su*; to Bhogadā *jaṃ thaṃ*; to Viśvā *jhaṃ taṃ*; to Bodhinī *ñaṃ ṇaṃ*; to Kṣamā *ṭaṃ ḍhaṃ*; to Dhāriṇī *ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ*, salutations (*namaḥ*). Having thus worshipped with "Salutation to the solar orb (*arka-maṇḍala*), whose essence consists of twelve digits (*kalā*"), [one worships] the triangle and the hexagon.

Having drawn a square within the vessel, one should worship a triangle with the three seed-syllables (*bīja*), and worship a hexagon with the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*). Then, reciting the *mātṛkā* in reverse order, one should fill the triangle with nectar (*amṛta*) and fill one portion with water; having placed fragrant substances and so forth therein, [one should recite]: "Aṃ, obeisance to Amṛtā; Āṃ..."
To Mānadā—*iṃ*; to Pūṣā—*īṃ*; to Tuṣṭi—*uṃ*; to Puṣṭi—*ūṃ*; to Rati—*ṛṃ*; to Dhṛti—*ṝṃ*; to Śaśinī—*ḷṃ*; to Candrikā—*ḹṃ*; to Kānti—*eṃ*; to Jyotsnā—*aiṃ*; to Śrī—*oṃ*; to Prīti—*auṃ*;
to Aṅgadā—*aṃ*; to Pūrṇā—*aḥ*; to Pūrṇāmṛtā—*soṃ*; [obeisance] to the Self consisting of the sixteen digits (*ṣoḍaśakalātmane*).

Having worshipped with "Oṃ, salutation to the Soma-maṇḍala," one should draw the *yantra* upon the substance as before; having worshipped the triangle with the three seed-syllables (*bīja*) and the hexagon with the six-limbed mantra (*ṣaḍaṅga*), one should invoke the sacred waters (*tīrtha*) with the mantra beginning with "Gaṅge," worship Ānanda-Bhairava and Bhairavī with their respective mantras, and [place] *glūṃ* in the east.
Homage to the Jewels of the Sky (gaganaratna)! To the right: *slūṃ*, homage to the Jewels of Heaven (*svargaratna*). To the north:

*mlūṃ*, homage to the Jewels of Mortals (*martyaratna*). To the west: *plūṃ*, homage to the Jewels of the Netherworld (*pātālaratna*). In the center: *nlūṃ*, homage to the Jewels of the Nagas (*nāgaratna*). Having thus worshipped, one should purify the meat and other offerings as follows: therein—

Having fashioned a square in front of oneself, having placed a vessel for meat and other offerings therein, one should dry it with the syllable *yam*, burn it with *ram*, flood it with nectar using *vam*, and transform it into nectar by means of the *dhenumudrā*. Having recited the root mantra over it ten times, one should purify it in sequence as follows: *Oṃ pra tad viṣṇuḥ stavate*.

"By his vigor, he is like a formidable wild beast that roams the mountains; in whose three wide strides all the worlds abide. Thus is the second purification. *Oṃ*, we worship Tryambaka, the fragrant, the increaser of prosperity; may he release me from death, as a cucumber from its stalk.

"From me, from immortality. Thus is the purification of the fish. With "Oṃ, that supreme step of Viṣṇu," and so forth, is the purification of the mudrās. "Oṃ, may Viṣṇu prepare the womb; may Tvaṣṭṛ fashion the forms; may Prajāpati pour [the seed];
may Dhātṛ place the embryo within you. O Sinīvālī, bestow the embryo; O Sarasvatī, bestow the embryo."
Indeed, the two divine Aśvins, Puṣkara-sraj, have placed the embryo within you.
Thus one should purify the fifth [element]. Then, having veiled it over the vessel with *hūṃ*, rendered it into nectar with *vaṃ*,
and bound the directions with three claps of the hands, one should recite the root mantra seven times over it and form the *yonimudrā*.

One should display it. Then, by means of the application of Kuṇḍalinī through the path of the upper incisor (rājadanta), one should bring forth the stream of nectar that has issued forth; having drawn it with a hand raised by the Yoni-mudrā, [one recites] the root mantra: "Oṃ!
This great vessel, produced from a fragment of the cosmic egg, filled with the entirety of gathered essences, is now full."
"O vessel, bring forth the essence of nectar! Aiṃ! O you who are nectar, born of nectar, Sovereign of Nectar, showerer of nectar, cause the nectar to flow forth, flow forth! Oṃ juṃ saḥ svāhā!
Having thus consecrated it, and having bestowed a state of oneness with that form by means of "Sauḥ," one becomes identical in nature with that [nectar] within the *arghya* vessel.

"O you whose form is supreme nectar, manifest the vibration of consciousness within me! Having consecrated [the vessel] with this mantra and worshipped it with "Hsauṃ Namaḥ," one should display the conch-mudrā, perform the ritual integration (*sakalīkaraṇa*) by means of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), cover the vessel with the fish-mudrā (*matsyamudrā*), recite the root mantra ten times, and contemplate the vessel as being the very form of the Goddess.
The Ritual for the Installation of the Śrīpātra Vessel.

Then, having received the command of the Goddess, one should place near the jar the following vessels: the Guru-vessel, the Śakti-vessel, the Bhoga-vessel, one’s own vessel, the Yoginī-vessel, the Vīra-vessel, the Bali-vessel, the Pādya-vessel, the Arghya-vessel, the Ācamanīya-vessel, and the Madhuparka-vessel; thereafter, by means of the *kāraṇa* accompanied by the chewing of food (*carvaṇa*).

Having lifted drops of nectar from the Śrīpātra with the Tattvamudrā, one should offer libations three times, saying: "Hasarakṣamalavaya-Ūṃ, vauṣaṭ to Surādevī; I satisfy Ānandeśvara Bhairava, obeisance! I satisfy Surādevī, obeisance! Then, with the nectar from the Guru-pātra, having uttered the venerable *śrīpādukā*, [one says] "Śrīmacchrī..."

Having offered libations three times with "I worship the venerable sandals of Amukānandanātha," and having likewise satisfied the Supreme Guru, the Preceptor of the Supreme Teacher, and the Preceptor of the Supreme Abode with the nectar from the venerable *śrīpātra*, one should then [satisfy] the Root [Mantra] along with the venerable Śrī Mahādeva Bhairava, together with his vehicle, using the nectar from the *śrīpātra*.

Having satiated [the deity] within one’s own heart with the mantra, "I satiate Śrī Jvālāmukhī, together with her retinue and her weapons; obeisance," and having placed the *prokṣaṇī* vessel, one should consecrate it with a drop of nectar from the *śrīpātra* and sprinkle oneself with the root mantra. With this very water, one should also sprinkle the sacrificial ground and the ritual materials.
Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the installation of the water jar (kalaśa).
Then, as before, having performed the worship of the seat (*pīṭhapūjā*) upon the seat of the Śrīcakra according to the sequence of the placement of the seats (*pīṭhanyāsa*),
one should take a handful of flowers, meditate upon the Śrīdevī, and— by means of the seed-syllable of air (*vāyubīja*),
*yam*— draw the Śrīdevī, consisting of radiant energy, from one's own heart through the left nostril into that handful of flowers.

Having meditated according to the rules, one should recite: "Oṃ, O Goddess of gods, who are easily accessible through devotion, accompanied by your retinue; as long as I worship you, O Goddess, please come here. Having recited this, one should cast a handful of flowers (*kusumāñjali*) upon the *Śrīcakra*. Then, [one should recite] the root mantra: "O Jvālāmukhī, together with Śrī Mahādeva, come here, come here! Stay here, stay here! (*mūlaṃ śrīmahādevasahite jvālāmukhi ihāgaccha 2 iha saṃtiṣṭha 2*).

"Be present here, be present here! Be firmly established here, be firmly established here! Accept my worship accompanied by all ritual offerings, svāhā!"—thus [one performs] the mudrās for invocation and so forth.
Having displayed [the image] upon the seat of the Śrīcakra and having exhibited the lelihāna-mudrā, one should perform the consecration of the vital breaths (prāṇapratiṣṭhā):

Oṃ āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ. The vital breaths of the venerable Jvālāmukhī are here as her vital breaths. 13 times. Her life-force is established here. 13 times. All her sense-faculties are established here. 13 times.

Having performed the installation of the vital breaths (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*) with the mantra: "Speech, mind, eyes, ears, tongue, nose, and life-breath, having come here, may they remain happily for a long time, svāhā," and having performed the binding of the ten directions,

he should veil [the deity] with the syllable *huṃ*, transform it into nectar with the nectar-gesture (*amṛtamudrā*), and empower it with all its parts (*sakalīkṛtya*) by means of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*).

Having consecrated [the offering] and displayed the *dhenu* and *yoni* mudrās, one should satisfy [the deity] three times with the nectar from the *śrīpātra*, saying: "Obeisance; I satisfy the venerable Jvālāmukhī together with Śrī Mahādeva Bhairava by means of the root mantra. Then, [offering at] the feet [of the deity], one says: "Obeisance; this [is for] the venerable Goddess Jvālāmukhī together with Śrī Mahādeva Bhairava. The root mantra is recited.
"Obeisance! [This is] the water for the feet. Likewise, "Root-mantra: Svāhā! [This is] the water for the respectful offering (arghya). Root-mantra: "Svadhā! This is the water for sipping (ācamanīya).
"Sudhā! This is the honey-mixture (madhuparka). Root-mantra: "Sudhā! This is the water for sipping again. Root-mantra: "Obeisance! This is the water for bathing.
Having thus bathed [the deity] in all limbs with water from the Gaṅgā and other sources, and having wiped the limbs with a clean silk cloth.

[With] various silk cloths, saffron, musk, sandalwood, [and other substances]—then, with the middle, ring, and thumb fingers, one should apply a tilaka on the forehead with the root mantra, saying: "This is fragrance, obeisance. With the thumb and forefinger, [one should apply it] with the root mantra for [the goddess] together with Śrī Mahādeva Bhairava.

Having worshipped with flowers, saying "To Śrījvālāmukhī, *akṣatapuṣpāṇi* vauṣaṭ," and having worshipped the incense vessel with "Phaṭ" and placed it before him, touching it with the left index finger and offering it with the nectar from the *śrīpātra*,
saying "I offer the incense," [one recites] "Oṃ, Mother of the Mantra that Resounds through the World... [Gajadhvani].

[The reading is also seen as follows: Having worshipped the bell with "Svāhā," sounding it with the left hand while holding the vessel with the middle finger, ring finger, and thumb, [one recites] the root mantra: *Oṃ jvālārūpiṇyai vidmahe jagadbhakṣiṇyai dhīmahi tanno jvālāmukhī pracodayāt*. Root mantra.

"Born from the essence of the forest tree, rich in fragrance, this is the most excellent scent; it is to be smelled by all the gods—may this incense be accepted. Having thus raised [the incense] three times, one should fumigate the Goddess. Then, having placed the lamp in front and performed the sprinkling and worship as before, one should [hold] the lamp-vessel with the middle finger of the left hand.

Touching the lamp and saying, "I offer," he offers it as before while ringing the bell; holding the lamp-vessel between his middle and ring fingers with his thumb and showing it while reciting the Gāyatrī and:
*Oṃ suprakāśo mahādīpaḥ sarvatas-tamonāśakaḥ | prasīda mama deveśi* (Oṃ, the great lamp of excellent light, which destroys darkness everywhere; be gracious to me, O Goddess of Gods).

"May this lamp be accepted. Thus one should offer the lamp. Then, having fashioned a *caru* in the form of the moon with eight petals using saffron in a vessel made of gold or other materials, and having established one lamp in the center and eight lamps on the eight petals, [one should worship] with: *Śrīṃ Sauḥ Glūṃ Slūṃ Mlūṃ Plūṃ Nlūṃ Sauḥ Śrīṃ Śrīratneśvaryai*.
Having honored [it] with "Namaḥ" and having honored it again with the root mantra (mūla), one should lift the vessel up to its rim and recite the root mantra nine times.

"O Goddess Navātmikā, joined with all the goddesses who are mistresses of the wheels, accept this *ārātrika* for my spiritual accomplishment. With these words, one should perform the *nīrājana* ritual using the *cakra-mudrā*; such is the procedure for the *nīrājana*.

Then, having placed various food offerings into a golden vessel, having veiled them with "Hūṃ," having rendered them nectar with "Vaṃ," and having recited the root mantra seven times while touching the offering vessel with the left thumb,
[one offers] the divine supreme rice-milk (*paramānna*) contained within the golden vessel at the end of the root mantra.
"O Supreme Goddess, accept this well-prepared offering, fivefold and endowed with the six flavors;

I present it. Having said this, he should offer it with the right ring finger and thumb. Then, having given the *apośāna* water with the root mantra, "You are the spreading of nectar, svāhā," he should perform the five mudrās beginning with *prāṇa*.

Having shown [the offering] so that the Goddess is well-satisfied and having meditated upon her, one should again offer water for sipping (ācamanīya). Then, at the end of the root mantra, saying "I offer betel-leaf (tāmbūla) joined with camphor and other ingredients," one should present the betel-leaf. OṂ AIṂ NAMAḤ UCCHIṢṬACĀṆḌALI MĀTAṄGINI SARVAVAŚAṄKARI SVĀHĀ. I worship the sandals (pādukā) of the venerable Śeṣikā. PŪJAYĀMI.
Having prepared this food of remnants (*ucchiṣṭabhojana*), the Goddess should cast it into the triangle in the northeast.

Then, the ritual dismissal (*utsarga*) of all [the deities] should be performed with the water from the *arghya* vessel. Thereafter, having thrice gratified the Goddess with the nectar from the *śrīpātra* using the *tattvamudrā*, one should contemplate Kṣobhiṇī in the heart, Drāviṇī in the mouth, and Ākarṣiṇī between the eyebrows.
Having displayed the *yonimudrā* consisting of the five seals— namely, *Vaśinī* on the forehead and *Āhlādinī* at the *brahmarandhra*—
and with palms joined in reverence, one should request permission by saying, "O Śrījvālāmukhī, I worship your retinue," and then begin the worship of the retinue (*āvaraṇapūjā*). As follows:

Therein, first, beginning from the east and proceeding clockwise in the Bhūpura (the outer square), one should worship with scents, unbroken rice, and flowers as follows: *Oṃ hrīṃ gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ Gaṇeśa-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi* in the east;
*Oṃ hrīṃ dhaṃ Dharmarāja-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi* in the south; *Oṃ hrīṃ vaṃ Vāsuki-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi* in the west;
and *Oṃ hrīṃ naṃ Narasiṃha-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi* in the north. Thus, having performed the worship in the Bhūpura.
The first enclosure; therein, the worship of the Guru.
Then, one should worship the sixteen flames upon the sixteen petals in counter-clockwise order as follows:

Oṃ śrīṃ vāruṇī-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi | Oṃ hrīṃ vātyālī-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi | Oṃ hrīṃ vārāhī-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi | Oṃ hrīṃ kulasundarī-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi | Oṃ aiṃ klīṃ kūvarī-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi | Oṃ sauḥ klīṃ...

Kulikāśrīpāda | Oṃ krīṃ Kuṇṭhīśrīpāda | Oṃ krīṃ Kutsitāśrīpāda | Oṃ krīṃ hūṃ Kuṭilāśrīpāda | Oṃ hrīṃ krīṃ Kuhūśrīpāda | Oṃ krīṃ Kuntīśrīpāda | Oṃ aiṃ klīṃ Kumbheśvarīśrīpāda | Oṃ krīṃ Kuntāśrīpāda | Oṃ krīṃ Kūcarīśrīpāda | Oṃ krīṃ...

Kāruṇī-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi. Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ Kṛti-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi. Having thus worshipped with sandalwood paste, flowers, and unbroken rice grains, this is the second enclosure on the sixteen petals.
Then, one should worship the eight maidens on the eight petals in counter-clockwise order (*vāmāvartena*), as follows: *hrīṃ* Māyā-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi;
*hrīṃ* Mohinī-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi; *aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ* Bālā-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi; *oṃ hrīṃ bhair*.

Bhagarūpiṇī Śrīpādukāpūjyā | Oṃ hrīṃ bhaiṃ Bhagāvāsā Śrīpādukāpūjyā | Oṃ hrīṃ bhaiṃ Bhīruṇḍā Śrīpādukāpūjyā | Oṃ aiṃ sauḥ Mṛḍānī Śrīpādukāpūjyā | Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aiṃ sauḥ klīṃ blūṃ Bindaveśvarī Śrīpādukāpūjyā. Thus, with sandalwood paste, unbroken rice, and flowers.
Having fully worshipped the third enclosure.

Then, one should worship the ten flames upon the inner ten petals as follows: Oṃ hrīṃ brāṃ, to the venerable Brāhmī (Brāhmī-śrīpādukā). Śāṃ, to the venerable Śāmbhavī (Śāmbhavī-śrīpādukā). Duṃ, to the venerable Durgā (Durgā-śrīpādukā). Vāṃ, to the venerable Vārāhī (Vārāhī-śrīpādukā). Kuṃ, to the venerable Kulakāminī (Kulakāminī-śrīpādukā). Nāṃ, to the venerable Nārasiṃhī (Nārasiṃhī-śrīpādukā). Kauṃ...

Kaumārī-Śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi (2). Māṃ Mātaṅgī-Śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi (2). Bhaiṃ Bhadrakālī-Śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi (2). Strīṃ Ugratārā-Śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi. Having thus worshipped with perfumes, unbroken rice, and flowers, [this concludes] the fourth enclosure.
Then, in the upper triangle: *oṃ śrīṃ* Tripurāsundarī-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi. Then, below: *oṃ krīṃ* Dakṣiṇakālikā-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi. Then, in the center at the *bindu*:
the root mantra (*mūla*)—Śrī Jvālāmukhī together with Mahādeva Bhairava, *śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi*. *Oṃ hrīṃ* Jvālinī-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi. (Twice) Jaṭinī-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi.
2. Jātīśrī; 2. Jālandharīśrī. Having thus worshipped and gratified [the deities] within the *bindu*, one should prostrate with the *yonimudrā*.
This is the fifth enclosure (*pañcamāvaraṇa*).
Then one should worship the four oceans: *oṃ hrīṃ saḥ sudhāsamudra-śrī*. *oṃ kṣāṃ kṣīrasamudra-śrī*. *oṃ drāṃ dadhisamudra-śrī*. *oṃ lūṃ lavaṇasamudra-śrī*.
Having thus worshipped and gratified the four oceans in the square situated at the intermediate directions, one should worship the weapons right here.
Having worshipped and gratified the weapons as follows: *oṃ hrīṃ vaṃ Varaśrī* (twice), *aṃ Abhayaśrī* (twice), *krīṃ Kabalaśrī* (twice), *śrīṃ Śaraśrī*, one should worship the four seats right here.
As follows: *oṃ hrīṃ Śavāsanaśrī* (twice), *Padmāsanaśrī* (twice), *Pīṭhatrayāsanaśrī*.
2. "O Śrī [Goddess] seated upon the Rudra-lotus throne. Having thus worshipped and gratified [Her], one should prostrate with the *yonimudrā*.

This is the sixth enclosure (*āvaraṇa*). Again, having worshipped the Śrī-devī within the *bindu* with the services beginning with *gandha* and ending with *naivedya*, and having gratified Her, one should worship again with three handfuls of flowers. Having worshipped in this manner—
One should perform the daily fire-sacrifice (*nityahoma*). For example:
having drawn or visualized the *śrīcakra* there, either in the fire or in water, one should invoke the Goddess from one's own heart into that [place].

Then, having performed the consecration of the *sruk* and *sruva* ladles, the clarified butter, and the sacrificial porridge (*caru*) with the root mantra, one should perform the sacrifice. As follows:

Having offered five oblations with the mantras: "Svāhā to Prāṇa! Svāhā to Apāna! Svāhā to Samāna! Svāhā to Udāna! Svāhā to Vyāna!", one should then offer the oblations for the six limbs: *oṃ hrāṃ śrāṃ*. (p. 374)

"Oṃ Hṛdayāya Namaḥ Svāhā"—having thus offered the oblations for the six limbs ending with the weapon (astra), and having also offered to the deities of the enclosure, one should dissolve the Goddess into one's own heart and dismiss the fire; such is the procedure for the daily homa.

Then, having drawn a mandala in the northeast, [one should recite]: "Oṃ vāṃ, obeisance to Vaṭuka! Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, come, come, O son of the Goddess, Vaṭukanātha, radiant with the mass of your tawny matted locks, three-eyed, flame-mouthed one! Destroy, destroy all obstacles!
Accept this worship along with all ritual offerings and the bali-oblation, svāhā! Thus.
One should offer the *bali* with the left thumb and ring finger. Then, in the southeast: *yāṃ yoginībhyo namaḥ*.

Whether above the Brahma-egg, or in heaven, in the expanse of the sky, on the surface of the earth, in the formless realm, in the netherworld (*pātāla*), in fire, or in wind and water—wherever they may reside; or those who have taken their stations in the sacred fields (*kṣetra*), seats (*pīṭha*), secondary seats (*upapīṭha*), and so forth.

May the goddesses, who are always pleased by incense, lamps, and meat, and who are worthy of worship by the lords of heroes, protect us through this auspicious rite of bali. With the mantra "Obeisance to the Yoginīs! To all Yogins! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā," one should offer [the oblation] with the left thumb and middle finger. Then, in the southwest, [one offers] to Kṣetrapāla: *Kṣāṃ*.

*Namaḥ oṃ kṣāṃ kṣīṃ kṣūṃ kṣaiṃ kṣauṃ kṣaḥ! O Kṣetrapāla, together with your retinue, accept this offering, accept it, svāhā! May the Kṣetrapāla who dwells in this field, along with his servants, being pleased by this gift of an offering, grant me protection from all [dangers]."* Thus, [one should offer] with the left thumb and forefinger.

"One should offer the bali. Then, in the northwest, one should offer the bali with the left thumb and middle finger, reciting: "Oṃ gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gaṃ, to Gaṇapati, O bestower of boons, bring all people under my control; accept this bali, accept it, svāhā! Then, in the north: "Oṃ, obeisance to all beings! Oṃ hrīṃ..."

One should offer the five-fold bali by uttering: "To all beings who create obstacles, *hūṃ svāhā*, this is the bali, obeisance (*namaḥ*)," while releasing the offering with all the fingers. One who is unable may do so using a single vessel alone.
At this very juncture, one should present the bali of a goat or other animals; therein, having bathed the animal with the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*), [one should proceed].

Having adorned it with perfumes, garlands, and other offerings, and having placed it before the Goddess, one should sprinkle it with water from the *prokṣaṇī* vessel while reciting the root mantra; protect it with "Astrāya Phaṭ"; veil it with "Hūm"; transform it into nectar by means of the *dhenumudrā* while reciting the root mantra; and then [offer it] with: "Obeisance to the one who is the form of all deities, the form of the sacrificial offering, for such-and-such an animal."

Having worshipped him three times with perfumes and other offerings, one should recite the *Paśugāyatrī* three times in his right ear: "Oṃ, may we know the Lord of Beasts (*paśupati*); may we meditate upon the Ear of the Brāhmaṇas; may that Jīva inspire us. Then, having placed a sword before him, one should say: "Oṃ, Kālī, Kālī, Vajreśvarī, homage to Lohadaṇḍā!"

Having worshipped it three times with perfumes and other offerings, one should worship it while holding it in one's fist, saying: "Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Vāgīśvarī and Brahmā" at the center; "obeisance to Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa"; and "obeisance to Umā and Maheśvara.
Having thus worshipped it and held it, one should consecrate it [with the mantra]: "Oṃ, for the sword, for the destruction of the asuras."
O Lord of the Sword, you who are intent upon the purpose of the gods' work, let the sacrificial animal be swiftly slain by you; salutations be unto you!
Having thus consecrated [the materials] by reciting the mantra, and taking scents, unbroken rice, water, and so forth,
one should state the root mantra, the month and other details, and say: "I, of such-and-such lineage, named such-and-such Śarman, desiring such-and-such, [offer this] to the illustrious Jvālāmukhī."

Having recited, "I offer this animal to you; be well-pleased," he should place it upon the head of the animal. Then, holding its head, he should say: "Oṃ, animals were created for the sake of sacrifice; the slaughter of an animal is for the sake of sacrifice.
Therefore, I shall cause you to be slain; thus, killing in a sacrifice is not killing."
"This body is dependent upon Śiva; therefore, you have attained the state of Śiva. Wake up, O bound soul (paśu)!

For you are not non-Śiva; you are indeed Śiva. Having thus awakened him, he should take up a sword and, reciting "sauḥ astrāya phaṭ chindhi 2 svāhā," apply the sword to his shoulder. Then, having himself become the form of the Goddess...

One who is free from conceptual thought (*nirvikalpa*) should cut [the offering] with a single stroke; one who possesses conceptual thought (*savikalpa*) should have it cut by another's hand. In this very context, an offering of one's own blood and so forth should be given by those other than Brahmins. Having thus given the offering (*bali*), having worshipped the Root Goddess (*mūladevī*), and having gratified her with blood, one should transform the water into nectar (*amṛta*), consecrate it three times with the Root Mantra, and [recite] the Root Mantra: *Śrījvālāmukhī*.

Saying, "Accept this water," he should offer water and prostrate with the *yonimudrā*. Then, he should worship the maiden according to the subtle sequence (*sūkṣmakrama*) using the root mantra (*mūla*). Thereafter, having fully worshipped the Root Goddess (*mūladevī*) with the root mantra, and having performed breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), the ritual purification (*arṣya*), and the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) on the hands, he should contemplate himself in the form of the *kāmakalā*.

Meditating and taking up the rosary, one should worship it with the mantra: "Oṃ, O Mālā, O Mālā, O Great Mālā, whose nature is all powers! The four aims of life are entrusted to you; therefore, be the bestower of success upon me. Then, saying "Gaṃ, O Mālā, always grant freedom from obstacles in all circumstances," one should take the rosary with the right hand and place it upon one's own head.

Having meditated on the Śrī Guru at the throat, the root-vidyā of yellow color at the heart, the goddess Jvālāmukhī at the feet of the Śrī Guru, and one's own self [at the feet], and having contemplated the unity of these four in the space between the eyebrows,
one should bring the fourfold group into oneness within the *viśuddhi*-cakra and meditate for a moment upon that in the form of the deity.

Recalling the root mantra, one should perform the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity; at the conclusion of the recitation, one should place the rosary upon one’s own head with the mantra: "O Rosary, you who grant pleasure and auspiciousness to all the gods, be auspicious for me, O Blessed One, and bestow upon me fame and valor. Having thus placed the rosary on one's head, one should once again perform breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), the ritual assignment of mantras to the limbs (*ṛṣyādi*), and the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*).
Saying "Guhyāti," one should offer the fruit of the recitation, consisting of radiant light, into the left hand using the general *arghya* nectar;

then, having worshipped the rosary, one should place it in a secluded spot. Thereafter, having offered a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*) to the Root Goddess, performed the recitation of the armor (*kavaca*), the thousand names, and the hymn of praise, and having satisfied the Śrī Devī with the previously mentioned hymn to the Guru—

"Having praised and bowed to the Śrī Guru, I take refuge in a certain deity of the God, who is the manifestation of all powers, who is distinct from the ego, and whose nature consists of the bliss of consciousness. Having thus bowed, one should ask for forgiveness:
"For those whose feet have stumbled upon the ground, the ground alone is the support."
O Śivā, for those who have committed offenses against you, you alone are their refuge.
A servant indeed commits an offense at every step;
who else in this world, other than a master alone, can endure it?
Thousands of offenses are committed by me day and night;
O Mother, forgive all of this, even as it is done in Your very presence and proximity.

Having thus asked for forgiveness preceded by prostration, and having taken the *arghya* water in his cupped palms, he says: "Oṃ! Whatever [was done] prior to this, through the authority of my vital breaths, intellect, body, and dharmas, in the states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, whether by mind, speech, or action, by my feet, belly, or genitals—whatever was remembered, whatever was spoken, and whatever was performed—all that..."
Having offered oneself by pouring water from the lotus-like feet of the Goddess while reciting "śrīdevyarpaṇamastu svāhā," one should stand with palms joined in reverence.
Whatever flower, leaf, fruit, or water is offered with mere devotion,
and whatever food offering is presented— please accept that out of compassion.
I do not know the invocation, nor do I know the dismissal;
I do not know the portion of the worship—O Supreme Goddess, you are my refuge.
Whether by deed, mind, or speech, there is no other course for me;
O Supreme Goddess, protect me as you move within the hearts of all beings.
In whichever thousands of wombs I may enter, O Acyuta, may my devotion to you, the Acyuta, remain forever undeviating.
The Goddess is both the giver and the enjoyer; the Goddess is this entire world.
The Goddess triumphs everywhere; she who is the Goddess is indeed myself.
O Goddess of gods, you should forgive whatever has slipped from the syllables or words, or whatever is deficient in its prosodic measure; for whose mind has not stumbled?
Forgive me, O Goddess of the lords of gods, Jvālāmukhī, Great Sovereign!
May my devotion remain eternally unwavering at your lotus feet.

Having thus asked for forgiveness with flowers and prostrated with the *yonimudrā*, one should lift up the conch, whirl it above the Goddess, and say: "Whatever action has been performed by me, whether good or bad..."
O Goddess, out of compassion, accept all this as my worship.
Thus, having placed a little water from the conch into the right hand of the Goddess, and having set the conch back in its place,
he places a little of that water in his left hand, consecrates it seven times with the root mantra,
[and sprinkles it] upon himself and others as well.
Having sprinkled those who are present with water according to the ritual convention and having taken a handful of flowers, he says:
"Go, go to the supreme abode, your own place, O Supreme Goddess!"
Wherein the gods, beginning with Brahmā, do not know that supreme state.

Having thus performed the dismissal with the *saṃhāra-mudrā*, taking a flower from the *śrīcakra* and drawing up that splendor, he should smell it, bring it to the heart-lotus by means of the *pūraka* breath-retention,
and meditate there upon her in the form previously described.
Stay, stay, O Supreme Goddess, in that supreme place which is your own abode,
where all the gods beginning with Brahmā abide within my heart.

Having thus established [the deity] within the lotus of the heart and worshipped the *nirmālya* with the mantra "Obeisance to Caṇḍeśvara," one should draw a triangle in the northeast with water and, saying "Obeisance to Nirmālyavāsinī," cast into it a hundredth or a thousandth part of the food offering (*naivedya*) together with the *nirmālya* flowers.
After three claps of the hands, one should dismiss the Nirmālyavāsinī. Then [one should pray]:
"O God, O Lord, O Guru, O Master, O Preceptor, O Leader of my own self!
Save me, save me, O Ocean of Compassion; make this worship most complete."

Thus, having bowed to and petitioned the venerable Guru, having lifted up the *śrīpātra* and offered it to the venerable Guru situated upon his head as far as the crown of his head, and having placed that vessel in his right hand, he should, with the *tattvamudrā* in his left hand, offer libation to the venerable *pādukā* three times with the mantra: "I satisfy the venerable *pādukā*, obeisance (*namaḥ*)."

Having satisfied [the deity] and placed that vessel in its proper position, and having set aside a little of that water in another vessel, one should place the four principles (tattvas) into the water with the mantras: *oṃ ātmatattvāya namaḥ*, *hrīṃ vidyātattvāya namaḥ*, *śrīṃ śivatattvāya namaḥ*, and *mūlaṃ sarvatattvāya namaḥ*. Then, taking that water in the hollow of the cupped hands (*culuka*),...

Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, I purify the gross body, together with the twenty-four impure principles beginning with primordial nature (prakṛti), intellect (buddhi), ego (ahaṅkāra), mind (manas), the sense of hearing (śrotra), the sense of touch (tvak) [and so forth], along with the vowels ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ, and the root mantra (mūlaṃ), which consists of the principle of the self (ātmatattva); svāhā!

Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ! [I purify] the subtle body, which consists of the principles of Māyā, Kalā, Vidya, Rāga, Kāla, Niyati, and Puruṣa, [represented by] jhaṃ ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ klīṃ;
I purify the subtle body consisting of the principle of Vidya-tattva, svāhā!
Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ! Together with the five principles beginning with Śiva, Śakti, Sadāśiva, Īśvara, and Śuddhavidyā—yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaḥ sauḥ—the root mantra;
I purify the supreme body, which consists of the principle of Śiva, svāhā! Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ! Together with the thirty-six principles beginning with Śiva...

From *aṃ āṃ* and so forth up to *kṣaḥ*, followed by *aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ* and the root mantra (*mūla*), [one should worship] the one who identifies with the body known as the gross, subtle, and supreme forms of all the *tattvas*.

Having taken four handfuls [of water] with the mantra "I purify the individual soul, svāhā," and having grasped that vessel with both hands while reciting the root mantra and the lineage of the Guru's sandals (*gurupādukā*), [one should offer it] with the mantra:
"Oṃ, having supported the *unmanī* ladle with hands that are like the space of light."
I offer into the fire that which is filled with the oil of the portions of merit and demerit; svāhā!

Thus, one should consume that water. Then, with both hands, one should touch one's own body from the head down to the feet, contemplating it as consisting of the thirty-six *tattvas*. Thereafter, together with one's fellow initiates (*sāmayika*), one should perform the salutation to the vessel according to the scripture and the procedure taught by the Guru. In that regard, first:

Having raised the Kuṇḍalinī, who is the form of one's chosen deity (iṣṭadevatā), from the Mūlādhāra and brought her to the tip of one's own tongue, one should cover the vessel with the right hand over the three-fold [mudrā] formed by the left hand and recite the verse:
"Now, O Goddess, O Sovereign, I shall describe the salutation to the vessel."
At that time, it was the vessel of supreme bliss, worshipped even by the gods. || 1 ||
O Supreme Goddess, during the worship, one should honor with a prostration of the head that vessel filled with bliss which has been given by the Guru. || 2 ||

This is the nectar of the three sections (*trikhaṇḍāmṛta*), manifest as the Great Self, which drenches all with the nectar of the moon shimmering upon the crest of the glorious Bhairava; it is worshipped by the hosts of Kṣetrādhīśvara, Yoginīs, and Mahāsiddhas, and is the source of the scripture of bliss.
I bow to the venerable first vessel, which rests upon the lotus-hand and bestows purity. || 3 ||
Oṃ, I purify the reality of the self, svāhā!
And the golden vessel containing the deer-essence (musk), offered by his beloved with drinks and other delicacies,
was gazed upon with joy by her whose eyes were like trembling red lotuses.
In my left hand, having placed the fragment of the purity of the essence of sweetness, I now salute this second vessel, which increases singular bliss. || 4 ||
Oṃ, I purify the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva), svāhā! Oṃ, [I praise the one] who is endowed with the collection of all the arts of the traditional lineages, who illuminates curiosity,
and who is served by Candra, Upendra, Mahendra, Śambhu, Varuṇa, Brahmā, and the others.
(379) Meditated upon always by hosts of gods and by groups of sages seeking liberation, I now salute that third vessel which is capable of awakening one’s own self. 5.
Oṃ, I purify the principle of Śiva, svāhā!
Wine brings forth the essence of fish; it is consumed by Hari, Hara, Brahmā, and the others;
it is intent upon the rites of ritual gestures and sexual union; and it abides in the salty, sour, and bitter [flavors].
May that which is honored by the teacher, covered by the deposition of the eight parts of Bhairava, and abiding in the reality of the five *makāras*, protect us; we praise the fourth vessel. 6.
I purify the principle of primordial nature (prakṛti-tattva), svāhā!

In the foundation, which is the circle of the king of serpents, the vessel is the orb of the earth; the substance is the water of the seven oceans, and the meat is the eight elephants of the directions.
Thus, worshipping Bhairava daily with clusters of stars as unbroken grains of rice, and with the hosts of gods and demons headed by the Sun, acting as his obedient servants and attendants; || 7 ||
I purify the principle of the person (puruṣatattva), svāhā! [The parasol],
which brings about the arising of supreme bliss upon a pure, stainless, and auspicious throne, is beautiful, bestows sovereignty, possesses a horse-like gait, and is enchanting.

We praise the sixth vessel, which always bestows happiness, grants the empire of union (sāyujya), dispels the darkness born of various diseases, destroys rebirth, and is most dear to the illustrious Bhairava and Bhairavī.
I purify the principle of the mind, svāhā!
The wind of awakening through the states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, which bestows the witness-consciousness beyond the fourth state (turya),
is pervaded by the digits of light of lightning, the sun, fire, the moon, and the rainbow.

May she protect me—she who resides between the Vāmā and Piṅgalā nerves, possessing three coils, whose vessel is uplifted by awakening through the seventh alchemical elixir (mūṣaṇa), and who bestows the bliss of youth. || 9 ||
I purify the principle of intellect, svāhā!
[I offer] the sword, the sandals of the venerable Guru, the forehead mark, and the Sarasvatī [amulet] upon the neck.
The removal of an enemy’s power of speech, strength, and valor is the cause for remaining embodied;
the accomplishment of desires, the stabilization of the mind, and the subjugation of women— this vessel is the eighth, which brings about the eight siddhis.
I worship the one who is mature and serene. || 10 ||
I purify the principle of ego (ahaṅkāratattva), svāhā!
It is the state of Śiva that eternally bestows all bliss, grants the attainment of all goals, effects sovereign power and prosperity,
confers all happiness, and destroys ignorance.
I worship the ninth vessel, which increases longevity, beauty, and fame, cuts through the delusion of saṃsāra, possesses a hundred thousandfold qualities, and is endowed with mature majesty.
I purify the principle of Śakti, svāhā!
I bow down to the tenth vessel, which is especially difficult to obtain and purifying for the gods Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa. 12.

I purify the principle of Bhairava, svāhā! I salute the eleventh vessel, which destroys sin, bestows peace and auspiciousness, is divine, sweet, and brings happiness, having arrived through the bliss of service to the Guru. 13.

"I purify all reality, svāhā! Having thus performed the salutation to the vessel (*pātravandana*), one should offer praise to the vessel: "The practitioner who holds the vessel in his hand shall happily attain success in all rites.
Having enjoyed prosperity in this world, at the end of the body he shall become Bhairava. (14)
The bowl is in the hand, the hymn is in the mouth, and bliss is in the lotus of the heart;
devotion is in the lotus feet of the Guru—what more than this could there be for remembrance? 15.
With a single parched chickpea I drink from a jar, and suddenly with a salted radish I drink from a pond;
having tasted a piece of meat from the head of a Rohita fish, I drink from the Gaṅgā along with the Yamunā and the ocean. 16.
In her hand is a rosary, in her mouth wine, and on her left side is a very tender woman;
Tripurā is the young maiden in the heart, and the sacrificial hall is in every house. (17)

The vessel is the vessel of Bhairava; the lineage is the lineage of the sandals of Śrīnātha. The scripture is the scripture of consciousness; knowledge is the knowledge that brings about the awakening to reality.
I am devoted to the worship of the enjoyment of wine, meat, and women; I am honored by the undertaking of the manifold paths of the Kula;
I am averse to the world of the fettered (paśu); I have taken refuge in Bhairavī; I am intent upon the feet of the Guru; I am Bhairava; I am Śiva. (19)

In the left hand is Candramukhī, and in the mouth is the vessel of wine; with the lotus-hand upon the head, one contemplates the venerable Guru, while the mind is the locus for meditation on the Goddess;
with the tongue as the means for recitation, those who are virtuous and constant in the practice of the Kaula lineage drink this transformation.
Both worldly enjoyment and liberation have become flavorful for you. || 20 ||
On the left is a woman skilled in dalliance; on the right, a bowl of wine; in front, ritual gestures and chickpea cakes;
the warm, pure flesh of a pig upon his shoulder; a lute [symbolizing] fresh poetry; and the Kaula path within the noble discourse of the True Guru—how profoundly mysterious it is!
It is inaccessible even to yogins. || 21 ||
Having drunk again and again, and having drunk until one falls to the ground,
and rising once more to drink, there is no further rebirth.

With the mind as the sacrificial ladle, I perpetually offer the functions of the senses as oblations into the fire of my own self, which is kindled by the fuel of dharma and adharma, through the path of the *suṣumṇā*. (23)
Holding [the ladle] with the hands of light and space, I offer into the fire the oblation filled with the oil of the portions of merit and demerit by means of the *unmanī* ladle. (24)
As long as the gaze does not waver and as long as the mind does not waver, so long should one drink; beyond this is the drinking of the beast (paśupāna).
Having thus offered praise to the vessel, he then worshipped and gratified his own companions according to the scriptures and the method taught by the Guru; then,
[he took] the food and other offerings contained in the sacrificial vessel previously set out, [placing them] into one [vessel].

Having placed it in a vessel, rising from that house and going outside with the water-vessel in hand, one should prepare a mandala consisting of a square, a circle, and a triangle in a pure place with water, and [place it] there.

Having meditated upon Ucchiṣṭabhairava—“the three-eyed, black-complexioned god Bhairava, who holds a mace, a trident, a *ḍamaru* drum, and a skull-bowl in his hands, and who destroys all obstacles”—and having worshipped him with perfumes and other offerings, [one recites]:
“O Ucchiṣṭabhairava, come, come! Accept the offering (*bali*)! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā! [Thus one offers] that which is in the vessel.
Having offered the bali-offering materials into that maṇḍala, having washed his hands and feet in that vessel and performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana),
having filled that vessel with water, having gone to the door of the worship chamber and entered, having sat down upon his own seat,
and having placed a drop of water from the Śrīpātra into the water contained in that vessel, he sprinkles himself with that water.
One should recite the Śāntistotra. As it is stated in the *Śrīdevīrahasya* (p. 21):
"O Goddess, I shall declare at the conclusion of the worship the unsurpassed Śāntistotra, by which heroes—free from all affliction—shall attain the state of supreme bliss. (1)
I bow my head to the Lord Bhairava, the beloved of Bhairavī, who stands in the midst of the circle of Yoginīs and is surrounded by the mandala of Mothers.
Homage to the illustrious Lord-Physician, who bestows the medicine of the Kula, the sole cause for destroying the terrible disease of beginningless saṃsāra.
Calamities, misfortunes, and diseases arise from the transgression of conventional conduct;
may all these be dispelled here by the union with the divine wheel. (4)
May there be long life, health, sovereignty, fame, gain, happiness, and victory;
may there be beauty and the fulfillment of desires, and may all the deities protect us. (5)

May the Blessed Lord of the Family bestow peace upon those who worship and protect the great ascetics, the lords of yogis, and those whose wealth is penance, as well as upon the country, the kingdom, the lineage, and the kings. (6)

May those who reveal the lineage of the family of practitioners rejoice; may those who possess the fourfold great lineages, beginning with Sṛṣṭi and Anākhyā, rejoice; may those supreme ones who delight in all Kula and Kaula traditions rejoice; and may others as well, who are Śāmbhavas distinguished by various specific stages, rejoice.
May the Siddha-gurus rejoice, along with the multitudes of their own lineages of gurus, the Jyeṣṭhas, the Anugās, the Samayins, the Vaṭukas, and the Kumāris.
May the lords of the earth, cattle, the twice-born, and the virtuous people rejoice—those born of the noble lineage of heroes among the six classes of Yoginīs. || 8 ||

May those who are skilled in ethics, established in faultlessness, free from envy, incomparable, and free from affliction; who are eternal, devoted to the stainless, teachers, desireless, followers of Śakti, peaceful-minded, and whose sorrow and doubt have been removed—may they all rejoice! (9)
May those devoted to yoga rejoice, as well as those established in the family-yoga (kula-yoga), along with the teachers, those bound by the samaya, the practitioners, and the spiritual sons.
May cows, the twice-born, young women, ascetics, and maidens be intent upon dharma and endowed with devotion to the guru.

May the lineages of practitioners who have attained the powers such as *aṇimā* rejoice; may the curses of the Yoginīs fall upon the enemy of the *samaya*. May that indescribable state of Śambhu flash forth within me, in which only the lotus-feet of the Guru are to be found.

Those goddesses who dwell in the stages of the sequence of the wheels (*cakra*), those who reside within the channels (*nāḍī*), those who inhabit the pores of the tree of the body, those who abide in the elements (*dhātu*), those who dwell in the waves of the wind of the breath’s surges, and those whose abode is the exhalation— they are all goddesses.
May those who are devoted to devouring the faction of enemies, being worshipped according to the Kaula tradition, be satisfied. || 12 ||

Those divine guardians of the quarters who dwell upon the earth, those deities who reside in the waters, those of eternally celebrated splendor who abide in the fire, those who take refuge in the wind,
those who consist of nectar and dwell within the orb of the nectar of space, and those who are all-pervading at all times— all of them [are present].
May those devoted to preserving the family path grant me peace. || 13 ||

Whether above the cosmic egg, or in heaven, in the expanse of the sky, on the surface of the earth, in the formless realm, in the subterranean world, or in the depths of water and wind— wherever they may be situated;

May the goddesses, who have taken their seats in the sacred fields, pīṭhas, upapīṭhas, and so forth, and who are ever pleased by incense, lamps, and other offerings, protect us through the rite of the auspicious bali—those goddesses who are worshipped by the lords of heroes (vīrendras). || 14 ||
Brahmā, Śeṣa, all the lords, Durgā, Guha, the Gaṇas, Bhairavas, Kṣetrapālas, Vetālas, Ādityas, Rudras, the planets, Vasus, Manus, Siddhas, Apsarases, Guhyakas, and others;
Bhūtas, Gandharvas, Vidyādharas, Ṛṣis, Pitṛs, Yakṣas, Asuras, Serpents, and many others; the Lords of Yogins and the Cāraṇas.
May all the excellent sages of the Kiṃpuruṣa realm, who move within the discus, protect [us]. || 15 ||

May all the deities residing within the body, the elephant-faced ones, the lords of the sacred fields (kṣetrapālas), the Bhairavas, the Yoginīs, the Vaṭukas, the Yakṣas, the Pitṛs, the Bhūtas, the Piśācas, and the Grahas; as well as others who move on the earth, in the cardinal directions, or through the sky— the Vetālas and the Ceṭakas— be satisfied by this son of noble family.
They drink the beverage and eat the sacrificial oblation together with the lamp.
If the word of the Guru is truth; if the ancestors, the gods, and the Yoginīs are pleased; if the Supreme Deity is present; if the Vedas are authoritative;
if there is the Śākta philosophy; if this Command exists; and if there are Kaulikas here as well—[then this is the case].
If it should ever happen that victory belongs to me. || 17 ||
May all the Mothers, the oceans, the lords of the hosts, the Yoginīs, and the Kṣetrapālas who are established within my body be satisfied. (18)
May the universe— from Śiva down to the earth, including everything from Brahmā to a blade of grass,
and from the Fire of Time up to Śiva— be satisfied by this sacrifice.
Having recited this, one should bow to the heroes and perform the salutation to the heroes; by praising the heroes and bowing to the heroes, the accomplishment of the mantra arises. || 20 ||
Having thus recited the *Śāntistotra*, one should recite the *Vīravandanastotra*:
"To those whose teachings are honored by the three worlds, and who are skilled in accomplishing the welfare of others...
Homage again and again to the leaders of practitioners, from whom the great serpents of the afflictions have been uprooted. || 1 ||

Homage again and again to the leaders of practitioners, who have abandoned all latent predispositions of their bases, whose means for realization have arisen from the reality of all objects, and who are intent upon uplifting all living beings. (2)
Salutations again and again to the attendants of Śambhu, who have disheveled hair and earrings, whose eyes are reddened by wine and spirits, and who are intent upon dalliance with their new consorts.

Salutations again and again to the Bhairavas and Bhairavis, whose limbs are smeared with ashes and who are clothed in the directions; who are terrifying due to the wreaths of smoke from funeral pyres; and who drink the nectar from skull-bowls. || 4 ||

Salutations again and again to the Bhairavas and Bhairavīs, who have established the eight supernatural powers (siddhis) for the great sages; who are honored by Śrī Bhairava for their practice of conduct (ācāra); and who have surpassed the immortals (nirjaras) through their self-mastery. || 5 ||
By this recitation of the *Vīrastava*, may I— having thoroughly uprooted the latent impressions of the afflictions—
rescue the world as it sinks into this great ocean of the wilderness of saṃsāra.

Having recited this *Śāntistotra* and the *Vīravandana*, and having consecrated all the initiates (*sāmayika*), one should lift up the vessel of special offering (*viśeṣārghyapātra*) and offer it to the venerable Guru stationed at the head. Likewise, having worshipped his sandals (*pādukā*) three times with the root mantra and the mantra of the Guru’s sandals, ending with "svāhā," [one should proceed].

With the intention of performing an oblation (*havana*) into the mouth of the Supreme Deity, who is one's own *kuṇḍalinī* at the *mūlādhāra*, one should place that water in another vessel and consume it; the remainder should be given to a beloved disciple.

One should give something with a mind of faith; he too, having placed that water in his own vessel, should drink it—such is the disposal of the *arghya*. Then, one should complete the remaining rites according to the procedure taught by one’s own guru.
Then, having filled a vessel made of copper or similar material with water mixed with scents, flowers, and unbroken grains (*akṣata*), [one recites] "Oṃ namaḥ..."
To Vivasvat, O Brahmin, to the radiant one, to the splendor of Viṣṇu, to the purifier of the world, to the pure one, to Savitṛ, the bestower of action.

Having offered the *arghya* to the Sun with the mantra: "Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ, this is your *arghya*, Svāhā," one should, with palms joined in reverence (*kṛtāñjali*), resolve that the rite is complete by reciting: "Oṃ, whatever flaw there may be in my sacrifice, whatever flaw in my austerity, and whatever flaw in my worship—may all that become flawless through the grace of Bhāskara. Then...
Having performed the breath control (prāṇāyāma), the ritual of the *ṛṣi* and others, and the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) with the root mantra;

having performed the placement of the six seats and the eight goddesses of speech; having recited the previously mentioned hymn to the Guru and bowed to the Śrī Guru; and having placed the remains of the offering (*nirmālya*) upon one's head with the second peak of the root mantra, [one should proceed] with the root mantra itself.

Having accepted the water used for washing the feet and having distributed the consecrated food (naivedya) and other offerings to the devotees of the Supreme Deity, one should eat together with friends and kinsmen; then, contemplating oneself as the form of Kāmakalā,
one should dwell in happiness.
Thus, this manual for the daily worship,
composed in prose and embodying the essence of all flames, should not be given away by those who speak the truth.
This secret manual of Śrījvālā, marked by the sequence of daily worship, is more secret than the secret and rich with mysteries; it must be concealed by those seeking liberation.
Thus ends the Śrījvālāmukhīpaddhati, within the Daśavidyārahasya of the Śrīrudrayāmala Tantra. || 2 ||
(p. 387) Now follows the Śrījvālāmukhī-kavaca.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Listen, O Goddess, Mother of the World; I shall proclaim the armor (kavaca) known as Trailokyavijaya, which contains the essence of the mantra of Jvālāmukhī.
This supreme secret, which must not be disclosed, has not been told by me to anyone;
without this armor (*kavaca*), O Maheśvarī, there can be no accomplishment.
It should not be spoken of nor given to one who is wicked, nor to a non-practitioner; it must never be told to a slanderer or to one who is not a disciple.
The Goddess said:
O Lord of the three worlds, tell me; though I have spoken much, this grace has been bestowed upon me by you yourself out of affection, O Master. (4)
Śrī Bhairava said:
At dawn, at midday, in the evening, and at midnight,
this supreme armor, containing the essence of the mantra, should be recited.
One should worship the deity with honey, fish, meat, and sweetmeats,
and with supreme devotion recite the excellent armor (kavaca).
Oṃ Hrīm, may the two-syllabled Mother of Letters protect my head;
Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, may the three-syllabled Universal Mother descend upon my forehead.
Oṃ aiṃ klīṃ sauṃḥ: may that Goddess Māyā protect my eyebrows. Oṃ aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ hsauṃḥ: may Viśvasundarī protect my eyes.
Oṃ hrīṃ aiṃ sauḥ—may Mohinī protect my nose; uṃ ūṃ—may she protect my ears. Ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ hsauṃḥ—may Bālā protect my cheeks and eyes. (9)
Eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ: may Śrī Bhagarūpiṇī always pervade my mouth.
Aṃ aḥ oṃ hrīṃ klīṃ sauṃḥ: may Bhagadhāriṇī protect my throat.
Kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ hsauṃḥ—may Tripureśvarī protect my shoulders;
ṅaṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ hsauṃḥ—may Baindaveśvarī protect my chest.
May she protect my chest with *jhaṃ ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḥ sauṃḥ aiṃ klīṃ hūṃ*.
May Bhīruṇḍā always protect my breasts with *ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ taṃ*. (12)
May Parā Jayā protect my belly with the mantra *thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*;
may Mṛḍānī always protect my sides with *paṃ phaṃ baṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ sauṃḥ*.
May the Kanyakās protect my navel with the syllables *bhaṃ maṃ yaṃ raṃ śrīṃ hsauṃḥ laṃ vaṃ*; may Guhyakeśvarī always protect my secret place with *śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ*.
Laṃkṣaḥ always protects the *liṅga*; Hrīṃ Śrīṃ is the dweller in the *liṅga*.
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ protect my penis; may Vāruṇī protect my back. (15)
Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ hūṃ hūṃ! May she protect my thighs; may she always protect me!
Oṃ aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ yāṃ! May Vātyālī (Vārāhī) always protect my shanks.
Oṃ śrīṃ sauṃ klīṃ—may Kulasundarī always protect my knees;
oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ—may Kūvarī (or Kulikā) protect my ankles; aiṃ śrīṃ—may she protect me.
Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ iṃ sauṃḥ—may Kuṇṭhī protect my knees; krīṃ hrīṃ hsauṃḥ—may she protect my soles. Oṃ prīṃ śrīṃ—may she protect my feet; hsauṃḥ hrīṃ śrīṃ krīṃ—may Kutsitā protect mine. (18)
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, may Kuṭilā hrīṃ krīṃ protect the backs of my feet;
Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, may she always protect the toes situated on my feet.
Oṃ hrīṃ hsauṃḥ aiṃ kuhūḥ, may she protect my marrow; Oṃ śrīṃ kuntī, may she protect my blood; Kumbheśvarī, aiṃ klīṃ, and Kūcarī, may they protect my semen. || 20 ||
May she protect all my limbs at all times: Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ Aiṃ Hsauḥ.
From the feet up to the head, may Kāruṇī—Hrīṃ Krīṃ Śrīṃ—protect me.
Vāruṇī is always [present]. || 21 ||
May the form *klīṃ śrīṃ* protect me from the crown of my head down to my feet;
may Brāhmī (*brāṃ*) protect my upper body, and Śāmbhavī (*śrīṃ*) protect my lower body.
May Duṃ Durgā protect me in the east; may Vāṃ Vārāhī protect me in the abode of Śiva;
and may Hrīṃ Krīṃ Hūṃ Śrīṃ Kulakāminī protect me in the north.
May Nārasiṃhī, with the mantra *hsauṃḥ aiṃ klīṃ*, protect me always in the northwest;
and may Kaumārī, with *oṃ śrīṃ krīṃ aiṃ*, protect me always in the west. (24)
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ! May Mātaṅgī, the bringer of auspiciousness, protect me in the southwest (Nirṛti).
Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ! May Bhadrakālī always protect me in the south. || 25 ||
Oṃ śrīṃ aiṃ klīṃ, may Ugratārā always protect me in the southeast;
Oṃ vāṃ, may she protect me in the ten directions; Hrīṃ, may Dakṣiṇakālikā protect me. (26)
May Tripurasundarī, [invoked by] Aiṃ Sauḥ, protect [us] at all times, always—in times of fear of pestilence, famine, affliction, and danger from yoginīs. || 27 ||
"Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! May the three-syllabled goddess Jvālāmukhī protect me.
This meritorious armor (kavaca) is difficult to obtain in the three worlds. (28)
O Maheśvarī, this is the mantra-core named Trailokyavijaya;
by its grace, I am the Lord of the Bhairavas in the three worlds. (29)
O Pārvatī, by reciting this, one becomes both the creator and the destroyer;
one should write it on birch bark with saffron mixed with liquor and one's own semen.
One may paralyze all the gods, delude all living beings, slay all enemies, and even bring the deities under one's control. || 31 ||
Holding [the image] by the arm, one should engage in battle; having conquered the enemies, one shall return home.
This applies in a ship, in war, in a dispute, in prison, or when afflicted by disease. (32)
During times of affliction by planetary spirits and the like, one should recite this; everything shall be pacified.
Thus, O Goddess, is this armor (kavaca), which contains the essence of mantras and is worshipped by the gods. (33)
O Pārvatī, this should not be given to anyone at all except for a disciple.
