Within one month, one shall attain that perfection which is difficult even for the gods to obtain;
by reciting it for three months, a mortal shall obtain the vision of the Goddess.
Thus ends the Śrī Jvālāmukhī Kavaca, within the Daśavidyā-rahasya of the Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra. 3.
Now follows the Thousand Names of Śrī Jvālāmukhī.
Śrī Bhairavī said:
O Blessed One, knower of all dharmas, granter of fearlessness to the gods!
That boon which was previously proclaimed by you to me on the peak of Kailāsa— || 1 ||
"O Lord, through supreme compassion, be able to grant that to me.
Śrī Bhairava said:
"What you have spoken is true; choose a boon, O Pārvatī. (2)
"I bestow that upon you for the sake of perfection—whatever is desired by your mind.
Śrī Bhairavī said:
O Lord, you have [manifested] thousands of Jvālāmukhīs in their true essence.
"Tell me these out of devotion, if you have compassion for me.
Śrī Bhairava said:
"O Great Goddess, I shall proclaim the names of the Jvālās according to their true nature."
In the Kali age, thousands of boons are granted to men according to their desires;
however, they must not be given to one who is devoid of devotion, nor to the wicked, nor to one who is not a practitioner.
I shall declare the names of that goddess Jvālāmukhī, who is remembered as the mother of the three worlds; her names are difficult to obtain within the three realms.
Except for the daily offering (nityabali), the hymn of praise (stotra) should not be recited by the best of practitioners;
however, it may be recited during famine, fear of enemies, or for the purposes of killing (māraṇa) and paralyzing (stambhana). || 7 ||
By reciting this hymn of a thousand names of the Goddess, success will be attained immediately,
even without perfumes, unbroken rice, flowers, incense, lamps, or offerings.
The thousand names of the Goddess need not be guarded by the practitioner himself.
Having offered the *bali* oblation, the mantra-reciter should recite the Goddess’s thousand names.
O Goddess, I have spoken the truth; otherwise, there will be a loss of spiritual accomplishment (*siddhi*).

Of this *Śrījvālāmukhīsahasranāmastava*, Bhairava is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (*chandaḥ*), Śrījvālāmukhī is the deity (*devatā*), Hrīṃ is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), Śrīṃ is the power (*śaktiḥ*), Oṃ is the pin (*kīlaka*), and its application (*viniyoga*) is in recitation. Salutation to Bhairava, the seer, upon the head; salutation to Anuṣṭubh, the meter, upon the mouth.

"Salutation to the deity Śrījvālāmukhī in the heart; salutation to the seed-syllable *hrīṃ* at the navel; salutation to the power (*śakti*) *śrīṃ* at the secret place; salutation to the *kīlaka* *oṃ* at the feet; salutation to the application (*viniyoga*) on all limbs. Having thus performed the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) upon the hands with the *māyā* syllable joined with the six long vowels—namely *oṃ hrāṃ* and so forth—one should meditate as follows:
Her face resembles the rays of the rising moon; she stands upon an eleven-petaled lotus, reverently holding in her palms a noose, a lotus, and the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness;
her eyes are fire, the moon, and the sun; she has the crescent moon as her crest-jewel; she is radiant with the three aims of life (trivarga) and stands upon a corpse.
I bow to Jvālāmukhī, whose crest is a circle of blazing fire.
Oṃ hrīṃ Jvālāmukhī, Jaitrī, Śrīṃ Jyotsnā, Jayadā, Jayā,
Audumbarā, Mahānīlā, Śukraluptā, Śacī, Śruti. || 1 ||

She who bestows pride and she who removes pride; she who acts for the pleasure of the Enemy of Smara (Śiva); she who bestows honor, the deluder, the intoxicated, illusion, the young girl, and the sustainer of strength. || 2 ||
She whose form is fortune, whose abode is fortune, the Bhīruṇḍā who destroys fear;
she is fear itself, yet she is the dispeller of fear; she is the one with beautiful brows, the fair-browed, the blissful, and the virtuous.
She who bears the trident, who holds a trident in her hand, who dwells upon the left side of the Trident-bearer;
she who is the mother of the Moon, the cool one, the refreshing one, the parrot-like goddess, and the auspicious one.
She is the small sacrificial ladle, worthy of being honored with honey, and the bestower of the fruits of the three aims of life;
she is Tretā, the three-eyed one, Durgā, the difficult to traverse, and the refuge for those in distress.
The pure one, the leaping one, and the one of discernment (or emission), she is the creator of emanation and the bringer of bliss;
bestowing happiness, dwelling in the center of all, she is Maheśvarī, the Mother of the World.

She is beloved in the worlds, the giver of boons, the one to be praised, praise itself, swift movement, and adoration; she is the bestower of guidance, the eye of vision, and she is served by the nine planets.
Ambā, Varūthinī, Vīrajananī, Vīrasundarī, Vīrasū, Vāruṇī, Vārtā, Varā, Abhayakarā, and Vadhū. || 8 ||
Vānīratalagā resides at the base of the cane grove; Vāmyā bestows the fruits of left-handed practice (vāmācāra);
Vīrā brings about valor; Śāntā is peaceful; and Śarvarī is the skin of a tiger.
She who is like a swarm of locusts, she who is the boundary of the scriptures, the bestower of auspiciousness, the destroyer of Śambara;
she who is dear to the enemy of Śambara, the beloved of Śambhu, and whose face resembles the moon. || 10 ||
She who bears weapons and arms, Peace, Radiance, Splendor, Beloved of the World, Conqueror of the World, She who impels, She who cleanses, and Protectress of Creatures. (100) || 11 ||

(393) Maitrī resides in the center of Meru; she wields the club as her weapon, is worthy of honor, bestows the desired fruits of mantras, is sweet as honey, and is reeling with the nectar of honey. 12.
She whose food consists solely of sweetmeats, who walks with the gait of an elephant in rut, who is beloved by Maheśvara, who is exalted, and who is Dārvī, the crusher of the Daityas. (13)
She is beloved by the gods and beloved by practitioners; she is virtuous, all-pervading, and peerless.
She is like the shade of a Santānaka tree—contented and dispelling the fatigue of the journey.
Śāradā, whose eyes are like autumn lotuses, whose face resembles a boon-granting lotus, who is bowed in body yet firm-limbed, whose limbs are adamantine, and who wields the vajra. || 15 ||
Vajreṣṭā, Vajrakaṅkālā, Vānarī, Vāyuveginī, Varākī, Kulakā, Kāmyā, Kuleṣṭā, and Kulakāminī. || 16 ||
Kuntā, Kāmeśvarī, Krūrā, Kulyā, Kāmāntakāriṇī, Kuntī, Kuntadharā, Kubjā, Kaṣṭahā, and Bagalāmukhī. (17)
Mṛḍānī, Madhurā, Mūkā, Pramattā, Baindaveśvarī, Kumārī, Kulajā, Akāmā, Kūvarī, and Naḍakūvarī. || 18 ||
She is the mistress of the mountains, she whose dwelling is the mountains, the daughter of the mountains, and the destroyer of mountain-enemies;
she is the daughter of the Nāgas, Kuhū, Kuṇṭhī, compassionate, and endowed with mercy.
She is enriched with the form and color of the letter *ka*; she is modesty, shame, fortune, auspiciousness, and inauspiciousness;
she is the sky-farer, the wife of the bird (Garuḍa), the one with eyes like birds, and the sovereign of birds.
She is the well-digger, she who dwells in the sky, she who is to be recited, she who is the recitation, the ageless, and steadfastness;
she is the world, the giver of birth, the shatterer, and she who resides beneath the rose-apple tree.
She is fond of Jāmbūnada gold, truthful, characterized by goodness (sāttvikī), yet transcending the quality of goodness;
she is the mother of all, the light of all, renowned throughout the worlds, and whose nature is dissolution.
Lūtā, Latāratī, Lajjā, Vājigā, Vāruṇī, Vaśā, Kuṭilā, Kutsitā, Brāhmī, Brahmāṇī, and Brahmadāyinī. || 23 ||
She who is beloved in vows, the one with a full bladder, the one with beautiful eyes, the one who brings others under her control;
she who is auspicious, beloved by Śaṅkara, and crowned with the crescent moon. (24)
Kumbheśvarī, Kurughnī, beloved by the Pāṇḍavas, higher than the highest; the destroyer of the demon Mahiṣāsura, she who is worthy of honor and dear to Manu. || 25 ||
She is the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), born of Dakṣa, skillful, the grape, the messenger, splendor, and the supporter.
She is the giver of dharma, beloved by Dharmarāja, established in dharma, and the protector of dharma. || 26 ||
The giver of wealth, the wealthy one, the righteous, the banner, Pārvatī, the progeny;
the mother of progeny, the city, wisdom, the fortress, the daughter, and the bearer of arrows. || 27 ||
Mātaṅgī holds a leaf in her hand; Patrivratā is the bearer of leaves;
Puṣṭi is the Plakṣa tree; and the Goddess dwelling in the cremation ground is served by the Giver of Wealth (Kubera). || 28 ||
Compassionate, she is compassion itself; though far away, her messengers dwell nearby.
She is the Narmadā, yet not merely the Narmadā; she is the source of joy, the celestial one, served by the inhabitants of heaven. || 29 ||
Nāsā, Saṅkrānti, Īḍyā, Bhairavī, Chinnamastakā, Śyāmā, Śyāmāmbarā, Pītā, Pītavastrā, and Kalāvatī. || 30 ||
Curious and following curious practices, she reveals the family dharma;
she is the Śāmbhavī and Gāruḍī vidyā, seated upon the throne of Garuḍa.
Vinatā, beloved of the Vainateyas, Vaiṣṇavī, worshipped by Viṣṇu;
the giver of livelihood (Vārtādā), Vālukā, the attendant (Vetrī), holding a staff in her hand (Vetrahastā), the excellent woman (Varāṅganā). || 32 ||
She is the eye of discernment, the wise one, the vast, the stainless, and indeed the unborn;
she is abundant in discernment, the one who has transcended, the boat, and the one worshipped by Nārāyaṇa.
Nārāyaṇī (300), Sumukhī, Durjayā, Duḥkhahāriṇī, Daurbhāgyahā, Durācārā, Duṣṭahantrī, and Dveṣiṇī. || 34 ||
She is composed of speech, the goddess of eloquence, the language, the ink, and honored by scribes;
she is the writing tablet, the fickle-eyed one, the dancer, the source of laughter, and the bringer of what is dear. || 35 ||
She is the giver of love, the knower of affection, the authoritative witness marked by conviction; she is Vārāhī, Kubjikā, the maker, and the one who grants liberation from the bonds of *kāra*. (36)
Fierce, more fierce than the fiercest, most beloved, honored by men, a lioness among women, praised by Nara and Nārāyaṇa, and worshipped by Naravāhana. || 37 ||
Nṛmuṇḍā, adorned with anklets, Nṛmātā, Tripureśvarī, Divyāyudhā, Ugratārā, Tryakṣā, and Tripuramālinī. || 38 ||
The three-eyed one, the hollow-eyed one, she who resides in the six cakras, the mistress of worms, the destroyer of worms,
the womb of worms, the digit, the digit of the moon, and the army.
Clad in skins, with beautiful limbs and tremulous eyes, she is the bestower of prosperity;
she is Bhadrakālī, Subhadrā, Bhadrāṅgī, and the one who rides upon a corpse.
Suṣamā, Strīpriyā, Kāntā, Kāminī, Kuṭilālakā, Kuśabdā, Kugati, Medhā, Madhyamāṅkā, and Kāśyapī. (41)
She who is the embodiment of the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), Kālī, worshipped by Kālabhairava;
she who is the utterance "klīṃ", she who possesses a subtle intellect, she who is speech, and she who is the slayer of the demon Bāṇāsura. || 42 ||
Free from possessiveness, beloved by those free from possessiveness, without a womb of rebirth, without support,
changeless, effortless, without abode, she is the mother of the king's son.
She is served by kings, desired by Brahmā, preeminent, and the mother of the universe;
her limbs are smeared with the letters of the alphabet, she has bathed in honey, and she flows with honey.
She is beloved by Venus, satisfied by Venus, bathed by Venus, and slender-waisted;
she is the rain, the shower, and the drought, yet she is attainable and free from greed.
She is the ocean (400), the woman to be perceived, Lakṣmī, Rāmā, Ramā, and Rati;
she is the Revā, Rambhā, Urvaśī, the one who brings others under her control, and the one who acts for the pleasure of Vāsuki. || 46 ||
She who delights in all that remains, the most excellent, she who is saluted by the one who reclines upon Śeṣa;
she who is the bed, the beloved of Śarva, the praised, the highly lauded, and she who is served by Śambhu. (47)
She whose eyes are like fire, who dwells for a moment, who is served at every instant,
who is the razor-edged blade, who is the pericarp, who is truth, and who possesses the form of all that is moving and unmoving. || 48 ||
She is the one of good conduct and the supporter of the earth; she is Diti, worshipped by the lords of the Daityas;
she possesses virtues and is the embodiment of virtue; she consists of the three qualities, yet is devoid of qualities; she is compassion itself.
Ghoṣā, beloved of Gajānana, having the form of an elephant, dear to the virtuous;
Gītā, fond of song, truthful, wholesome, the beautiful lady of Tripura.
She has full breasts, she is a delightful woman, desired by lovers, and devoted to sexual union;
she is Padmā, the bearer of the lotus, the offspring, the cow, the sustainer of Meru, and Maghā. || 51 ||
Mālatī, Madhurālāpā, Mātṛjā, and likewise Mālinī;
Vaiśvānarapriyā, Vaidyā, Cikitsā, and Vaidyapūjitā. || 52 ||
Vedikā, Vāraputrī, Vayasyā, Vāgbhavī, Prasū, Krītā, Padmāsanā, Siddhā, Siddhalakṣmī, and Sarasvatī. (53)
She is the most excellent of beings, established in being, common to all, and the source of union;
she is desired by practitioners, the virtuous wife, the mother of virtuous sons, and the refuge of a noble family.
She is both a woman and a non-woman; she is weary, yet her passage to the next world is auspicious.
She is of terrible form and terrible roar, with disheveled hair, yet she bestows liberation.

She is the giver of liberation, the giver of strength, nourishment, and release; she is dear to Bali, the fearless one, she whose nose is like a sesame flower, the flowering one, and the crest of the lineage.
She who causes enmity toward others, the traveler, the daughter of the ocean, the vulva, she who is dear to Bhaga, the crest of Bharga, sport, and the sovereign lady of Himavat. || 57 ||
Herukeṣṭā, Vaṭusthā, Vaṭumātā, Vaṭeśvarī, Naṭinī, Troṭinī, Trātā, Svasā, Sāravatī, and Sabhā. || 58 ||
Saubhāgyā, Bhāgyadā, Bhāgyā, Bhogadā, Bhūḥ, Prabhāvatī, Candrikā, Kālahartrī, Jyotsnolkā, Aśani, and Āhnika. || 59 ||
She possesses heat pertaining to this world and the next, appearing like the radiance of the summer sun;
she has a neck and a face like the summer season, is the protector of the earth, and dwells on Mount Kailāsa. (60)
Mallī, Mārtaṇḍarūpā, Mānahartrī, Manoramā, Māninī, Mānakartrī, Mānasī, Tāpasī, and Tuṭi. || 61 ||
She who abides in milk, she who is praised as the Supreme Brahman, she whose body delights in hymns;
she who is slender, most slender, subtle, gross, dear to the brave, and the lowest. 62.
She is supreme, richly adorned with jewel ornaments, and resides within a pavilion of gems;
she is Māṣā, Tīkṣṇā, Trapā, Cintā, Maṇḍikā, Carcikā, and Calā.
Caṇḍī, Cullī, the performer of wonders, the destroyer, Harīśvarī, she who is served by Hari, the foremost of monkeys, the one worshipped with offerings, and she of beautiful form. || 64 ||
Caṇḍīśvarī, of fierce form, holding a severed head in her hand, she who moves with the speed of thought;
she is the boat, the pure, the purifying, the marrow, the sacrificial essence, and the fragrant one. || 65 ||
Sugandhā, Puṣpiṇī, Puṣpā, Preritā, Pavaneśvarī, Prītā, Krodhākulā, Nyastā, Nyakkārā, and Suravāhinī. (66)
Srotasvatī, Madhumatī, Devamātā, Sudhāmbarā (600), Matsyā, she who resides at the seat of Matsyendra, Vīrapānā, and Madāturā. 67.
She is the earth, she is of the nature of light, she is satisfaction, the root-support, and vast radiance;
she holds the serpent-noose, she is infinite, she carries a noose in her hand, and she is the awakener.
Prasādanā, Kaliṅgā, Madanāśā, Madhudravā, Madhuvīrā, Madāndhā, Pāvanī, Vedanā, and Smṛti. || 69 ||
Bodhikā, Bodhinī, Pūṣā, Kāśī, Vārāṇasī, Gayā, Kauśī, Ujjayinī, Dhārā, Kāśmīrī, and Kuṅkumākulā. (70)
Bhūmi, Sindhu, Prabhāsā, Gaṅgā, Gaurī, Śubhāśrayā, Vetravatī—who consists of various sciences—and Godāvarī, who is the mace (gadā). 71.
The remover of disease, mounted upon an elephant, Indrāṇī, Kulakaulinī;
she who follows the Kula conduct, the ugly one, the beautiful one, and the one devoid of form. (72)
The Candrabhāgā, Yamunā, Yāmī, Yamakṣayaṅkarī, Kāmbhojī, Sarayū, Citrā, Vitastā, Irāvatī, and Jhaṣā. (73)
Caṣikā, Pathikā, Tantrī, Vīṇā, Veṇu, Priyaṃvadā, Kuṇḍalinī, Nirvikalpā (or Nirvikārā), Gāyatrī, and Narakāntakā. || 74 ||
The Kṛṣṇā, the Sarasvatī, the Tāpī, the Payoṇā, the Śatarudrikā,
the Kāverī which has the luster of a hundred lotuses, the Śatabāhu, and the Śatahradā. || 75 ||
Revatī, Rohiṇī, Kṣipyā, Kṣīṇā, Kṣoṇī, Kṣamā, Kṣayā, Kṣānti, Bhrānti, Guru, Gurvī, Gariṣṭhā, Gokulā, and Nadī. (76)
Nādinī, Kṛṣiṇī, Kṛṣyā, Satkuṭī, Bhūmikā, Bhramā, Bibhrājamānā, Tīrthyā, Tīrthā, and Tīrthaphalapradā. (700) || 77 ||
She is youthful, of the nature of darkness (tāmasī), the noose (pāśā), the one who has cast off the noose (vipāśā), and the bearer of the noose (pāśadhāriṇī).
She is satisfied by the offering of bound souls (paśūpahāra), she is the hen (kukkuṭī), and she whose vehicle is the swan (haṃsavāhanā). || 78 ||
Madhurā, Vipulā, Ākāṅkṣā, Vedakāṇḍī, Vicitriṇī, Svapnāvatī, Sarit, Sītādhāriṇī, Matsarī, and Mut. (79)

She is the Śatadrū river, the goddess Bhāratī, Kadrū, and she who possesses infinite, endless branches; she is sensation, the daughter of Vāsava, the courtesan, Pūtanā, and she who smiles with flowers. || 80 ||
She is the triple power, whose form is power, the mother of the imperishable, the razor, and hunger;
she is the slow one, the celestial river, the mudrā, the elemental being, and the beloved of the Lord of Beings.
She is beloved by the elements, the destroyer of the five elements, keen-eyed, and soft-smiling;
she dwells within, she is the secret one, the bestower, she with hanging hair, and she with beautiful hair. 82.
With hair standing erect and large eyes, she is formidable yet beloved by her virtuous husband;
she is dusty, holds an alms-bowl in her hand, and carries a skull-cup as her weapon. (83)
Kekarī, Kākinī, Kumbhī, Suphalā, and she of crooked form;
Viphalā, Vijayā, Śrīdā, she who is served by Śrīda, and Śubhaṅkarī. (84)
Śaityā, Śītālayā, Śīdhupātrahastā, Kṛpāvatī, Kāruṇyā, Viśvasārā, Karuṇā, Kṛpaṇā, and Kṛpā. (85)
She is wisdom and knowledge; she is the sixfold group, the six-faced one, and beloved of the six-faced one;
she is Krauñcī, whose abode is the Krauñca mountain, the self-controlled one, and the destroyer of poverty.
She is the radiant hall, she who is to be accomplished and she who brings about accomplishment;
she is the singer of the *sāman* hymns, possessing the seven musical notes, the seven supports, and eyes numbering forty-nine.
Sthiti, Kṣemaṅkarī, Svāhā, Vācālī (800), Vividhāmbarā, Kalakaṇṭhī, Ghoṣadharā, Sugrīvā, Kandharā, and Ruci. || 88 ||
Śucismitā, Samudreṣṭā, Śaśinī, Vaśinī, Sudṛk, Sarvajñā, Sarvadā, Śārī, Sunāsā, and Surakanyakā. [g: muni] || 89 ||
Senā, Senāsutā, Śṛṅgī, Śṛṅgiṇī, Hāṭakeśvarī, Hoṭikā, Hāriṇī, Liṅgā, and she whose nature is the yoni and the linga. || 90 ||
Bhagamātā, she who is called Liṅga, Liṅgaprīti, Kaliṅgajā, Kumārī, Yuvatī, Prauḍhā, Navoḍhā, and Prauḍharūpiṇī. || 91 ||
Ramya, Rajovatī, Rajju, Rajolī, Rājasī, Ghaṭī, Kaivartī, Rākṣasī, Rātrī, and Rātriñcarakṣayaṅkarī. || 92 ||
Mahogrā, Muditā, Bhillī, Bhallahastā, Bhayaṅkarī, Tilābhā, Dārikā, Dvāḥsthā, Dvārikā, and Madhyadeśagā. 93.
Citralekhā, Casumatī, Sundarāṅgī, Vasundharā, Devatā, Parvatasthā, Parabhū, and Paramākṛti. || 94 ||

She whose supreme form is a garland of severed heads, who wears a sacred thread of serpents, is Kālikā of the cremation ground; she has a beard, is the soul of universal dissolution, and is the devourer. 95.
Prasthasthā, Prasthinī, Prasthā, Dhūmrārcis, Dhūmrarūpiṇī, Dhūmrāṅgī, Dhūmrakeśā, Kapilā, and Kālanāśinī. [Kh: Kali] 96.
Kaṅkālī, Kālarūpā, Kālamātā, Malimlucī, Śarvāṇī, the wife of Rudra, Raudrī, and she who has the very form of Rudra. || 97 ||
The twilight, the triple-twilight, is to be worshipped; she bestows all sovereignty.
She is born of the Kula, the mistress of the world of truth, truthful in speech, and a speaker of truth. 98.
She whose voice is truth, composed of truth, the gateway to Hari, consisting of Hari;
she who is a heap of emerald jewels, the fourfold essence of the Sāman chants, whose body is the planets, stars, and lunar days.
Tumburu, Truṭikā, Troṭī, Bhuvaneśī, Bhayāpahā, Rājñī, Rājyapradā, Yogyā, Yoginī, and Bhuvaneśvarī. (100)
Turī, Tārā, Mahālakṣmī, Bhīḍā, Bhārgī, Bhayānakā, Kālarātri, Mahārātri, Mahāvidyā, and Śivālayā. || 101 ||
She who is united with Śiva, who dwells in Śiva, who is meditative absorption (samādhi), whose vehicle is fire;
she who is the mistress of fire, the great pervasion, the crane (balākā), and she who has the form of a child. 102.
Vaṭukeśī, Vilāsā, Sadasatpurabhairavī, Vighnahā, Khalahā, Gāthā, Kathā, Kanthā, and Śubhāmbarā. (103)
Kratuhā, Kratujā, Krāntā, Mādhavī, Amarāvatī, Aruṇākṣī, Viśālākṣī, Puṇyaśīlā, and Vilāsinī. (104)
Sumātā, Skandamātā, Kṛttikā, Bharaṇī, Bali, Jineśvarī, Sukuśalā, Gopī, and she who is worshipped by the Lord of Cows (Gopatipūjitā). || 105 ||
She is the secret one, the most secret one, the renowned one, the manifest one, and she whose nature is concealed;
she possesses the lineage tradition, she is the pin, she is the full one, and she is eager for the golden armlet.
Utkaṇṭhā, Kalakaṇṭhī, Raktapā, Pānapā, Amalā,
Saṃpūrṇacandravadanā, Yaśodā, and Yaśasvinī. (107)
Ānandā, Sundarī, Sarvānandā, Nandātmajā, Layā, Vidyut, Khadyotarūpā, Sādarā, Javikā, and Javi. (108)
The mother and the destroyer of people, Kharparā, she with eyes like wagtails;
the ancient one, she who is marked by clouds, she with matted hair, and the increaser of victory. || 109 ||
Jalasthā, Jayantī, and likewise Jambhārivaradā—the Goddess who is complete with a thousand names is known as Jvālāmukhī. (110) [1000]
Thus, this thousand names of Jvālāmukhī, spoken by Śiva,
constantly bestows the four aims of human life and is illuminated by the three seed-syllables.
It is the incomparable sole cause of liberation, bestowing both worldly enjoyment and release upon men;
it is praiseworthy, to be practiced, the very essence of all things, and the supreme core.
Consisting of the Great Mantra, consisting of Vidyā, the supreme bestower of Vidyā upon men, it is the very nature of the Supreme Brahman and is the manifest form of immortality. || 113 ||
This thousand names, which is non-dual in nature and proclaimed by Bhairava—whosoever recites it, causes it to be recited, hears it, or causes it to be heard; || 114 ||
O Great Goddess, endowed with devotion, he shall become equal to Bhairava;
[this applies] on Śivarātri, at the transit of the sun (saṃkrānti), during an eclipse, and on one's birthday.

Having offered an oblation to Bhairava [or, according to manuscript kh, to Kukkuta], the mantra-practitioner should recite the Thousand Names of Jvālāmukhī, which is very difficult to obtain, using the root mantra. 116.

The wise person who recites this, which yields infinite fruit and must be kept secret, at the three junctions of the day shall become a master of the supernatural powers such as atomization (aṇimā) and become righteous.
Rising at midnight in a deserted house, the best of practitioners should recite this divine Thousand Names three times. (118)
Through action, mind, and speech, one shall become the son of Jvālāmukhī;
having gone daily at midday to the cremation ground, one who knows the ritual procedure [should perform the rite]. (119)
Having offered an oblation of human flesh, one should recite the Thousand Names;
having assumed a divine body, one shall wander through the three worlds.

On a Saturday, on the eighth lunar day of the waning moon, one should recite the *Nāmasahasraka* while offering a milk-oblation (*kṣīrabali*) to her; thus, all supernatural powers (*siddhis*) will be held within one's hand.

O Goddess, on every Tuesday, a man should always offer a libation of liquor as a bali-offering; otherwise, the protection cannot be ensured by the best of practitioners through mere food offerings alone. (122)
The practitioner who recites this shall quickly obtain the supreme vision;
O Dear One, by always chanting the vidyā on Saturdays and offering the bali oblation.
O Great Goddess, if one recites the *Nāmasahasraka* of Kapota, prosperity will increase in that person's home eternally, like [the abundance at] Gokarṇa. (124)
The practitioner should perform one hundred circumambulations at night and shall obtain a vision [of the deity]. A barren woman or one whose children die in infancy should write this with saffron.
O Dear One, one should daily wear the Thousand Names written on birch bark with one's own breast milk either around the neck or on the left arm.
Even a barren woman obtains sons who are heroic and like unto Vidyādharas;
having fastened this upon her left arm and gone toward the field of battle. (127)
Having conquered the hosts of enemies, he returns happily to his own home;
O Pārvatī, one should recite this constantly three times for the destruction of enemies. (128)

One should recite it twice for the sake of prosperity; for liberation, one should recite it a hundred times. For the purpose of subjugation, one should recite it ten times daily, and for the purpose of killing, twenty times.
For the purpose of immobilization, the best of mantra-practitioners should recite it seven times daily.
O Goddess, for the sake of land, one should recite the Thousand Names thirty times.
If one recites this even once every day, though dead, one shall attain liberation.
This must not be disclosed, nor given, nor spoken to those who lack devotion. (131)

O Pārvatī, [this should not be given] to one who is incapable, to one of ignoble birth, to a wicked son, to one of evil nature, to one devoid of devotion to the Guru, or to one who has not received initiation.
Having given [it] to one who is unfaithful, one becomes afflicted with leprosy in this world and shall go to hell in the next.
But by giving to one endowed with faith, devoted, a practitioner, high-souled, possessed of right conduct, and of virtuous character, one attains liberation.
Thus ends the *Śrījvālāmukhīsahasranāmastotra* within the *Daśavidyārahasya* of the *Śrīrudrayāmala Tantra*. 4.
Now, the Hymn to Śrījvālāmukhī.
Śrī Bhairava said:
O Mother, he who worships your seed-syllable *tāraṃ*, which is like the moon of nectar,
shall have the daughter of the ocean (Lakṣmī) dwell eternally and immovably in his home.

O Bhavānī, O Giver of Boons, the practitioner who meditates within his heart upon the syllable that is void (śū), mounted on fire (ra), stainless (a), attended by the left eye (i), joined with the moon (u),
and endowed with the bindu (m)— then even for one who is mute, the goddess of speech, Bhāratī, will instantly flow like the waters of the ocean of the Lord of Gods, in the form of verses.
O Mother, it remains wide open at your mouth. || 2 ||

O beloved, if Saturn recites this seed-syllable dear to you— which is auspicious, mounted upon fire, joined with *mati*, endowed with the bindu and the moon, and which bestows abundant desired fruits— [he shall attain success].
Then, O Mother, devoted to your worship, he sleeps happily in Indra’s garden, free from the toil of sporting with celestial women. || 3 ||
O Consort of the Lord of the Mountains, the practitioner who recites the syllables of your name, "Jvālāmukhī," preceded by sublime devotion,
causes the pair of his lotus feet to be colored by the rays from the crest-jewels of the courtesans of the Lord of the Gods.
O Daughter of the Mountain, for him who remembers your mantra in the midst of the words "tvaṃ śabdaṃ" while you hold a noose, a lotus, and the gesture of fearlessness,
the falling tears from the eyes of his enemies' wives wash the dust-covered feet of that person.
O Mother, if a practitioner recites these two verses with devotion in his mind,
he shall, by your grace, attain your state day and night, just like the enemy of Smara (Śiva).
O Maheśvarī, if a practitioner meditates upon that sinless seed-syllable of the *kūrca* mantra which is within you,
then all the powers (*siddhis*) equal to those of Tryambaka shall be perfectly under his control through his eight lotus-like hands.
O Goddess, those who recite these two *ṭha* syllables situated above the *manu*, which bestow supreme power— the gods dwelling in heaven, such as Hari, Śaṅkara, and others, worship their feet.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ! O Goddess of three syllables, O destroyer of gods and demons, O Mother who grants fearlessness to the three worlds, O Jvālāmukhī, homage be unto you!
O Lakṣmī, whose splendor is like the rising sun, worshipped by the Lord of Lakṣmī, who holds a choice lotus and the gesture of fearlessness—O Jvālāmukhī, salutations be to you! 10.
O Śarvā, who embodies the essence of all, you who are saluted by all the immortals;
O Jvālāmukhī, while truth and virtuous conduct endure, homage be to you! 11.
She who has the moon upon her head and the three eyes— sun, moon, and fire— within her gaze;
she whose lotus-palms hold the noose, the lotus, the boon-granting gesture, and the gesture of fearlessness, as well as the excellent weapons.
I bow to the Goddess Jvālāmukhī, whose body possesses a luster like saffron, who is adorned with a serpent around her neck, and who resembles ten million rays of light.

O Goddess, when he beholds the blazing flames of the fire of your wrath, then Brahmā loses his sleep, Śiva abandons his auspiciousness, Viṣṇu gives up his fearlessness, and even the lover of the lotus (the Sun) assumes great anxiety. Thus the Lord [acts].
With his two cheeks yellowed by saffron, Saṃkrandana wails. || 13 ||

Having worshipped her day and night with hymns on the banks of the celestial river, the Self-born [Brahmā] attained the status of the eldest among the immortals— [she who is] like the rising, radiant sun; that Goddess,
the mother who is the reviver of the three worlds bitten by the serpent of poverty, I hold in my heart.
I worship her who has the crescent moon as her crest-ornament. || 14 ||

O daughter of the Lord of Mountains, O goddess with beautiful brows like those of the celestial damsels, the practitioner who meditates upon you— bowed by the weight of your swelling breasts and hips, radiant with the pride of Kandarpa, and possessing lovely cheeks marked with loveliness— will find the entire earth under his control. At the soles of your lotus feet, all things shall be submissive to him.
The gods, Gandharvas, Siddhas, and others worship [him]. || 15 ||
O Goddess, having severed the head of Vidhi, she placed it as a vessel in her lotus-hand; she caused Hari, impaled upon the trident, to depart with his true ornaments upon his shoulders;
and at the end of time, O Parvati, she cast the triad into the cavity of Śambhu’s moon-like mouth.
O Pārvatī,
O Mother, O Śivā, I know that everything in your world is wonderful.
O Śivā, that Gāyatrī who is the primordial source was held by Brahmā even at his throat; she, in the form of Śrī, was likewise held by Hari upon his chest as half of his body;
and so too by Śarva, O Goddess Bhavānī—yet we are not able to fully describe your form within our hearts.
For those of dull intellect like me, what talk can there even be of meditating? 17.
He who recites this *Jvālāmukhī-stava*, which contains within it the glorious King of Mantras and is the sole cause of prosperity—
acting as a wish-fulfilling tree (*kalpavṛkṣa*) on earth at the time of granting desired boons— shall go to heaven, attended by the women of the gods.
Thus, O Kulasaundari, the five-limbed Śrī Paramajvālātattva has been declared; it is the supreme secret, the very essence of Śyāmā.
It is to be guarded, the most secret essence, bestowing auspiciousness and increasing merit;
it yields abundant fruit equal to ten million sacrifices and is the sole cause for the preservation of family tradition.
O Pārvatī, O Goddess of the Gods, this secret of mine is worthy of praise, it removes disease, it is divine, it bestows all sovereignty, and it is my very own self. (21)
It must not be given to the disciple of another; by giving it, there would be loss for Manu.
Having first performed worship of the Guru and having diligently satisfied the Guru, [one may proceed]. || 22 ||
O Supreme Goddess, one should receive the entire five-limbed, divine, secret, and supreme deity [of the mantra] of Jvālāmukhī according to the prescribed rite.
"All accomplishments shall be swiftly attained, even those difficult for the gods to obtain.
Śrī Devī said:
"O Maheśvara, I have been purchased by you with this hymn of praise."
"In every way, I shall be your servant by the mere hearing of your five limbs. (24)
Śrī Bhairava said:
This supreme secret has been declared by me to you out of devotion; this entire five-limbed [teaching] of the Goddess must be guarded by those seeking liberation. 25.
Thus ends the Śrī Jvālāmukhī Stotra, within the Daśavidyā Rahasya of the Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra. 5.
The *Śrījvālāmukhīpañcāṅga* is completed. (p.
The Five-Limbed Ritual Manual of Śrī Śārikā.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim this chapter, which is difficult even for the gods to obtain;
it is divine, bestows all perfections, and grants all sovereign powers.
She who is the goddess of gods, the bestower of boons, Śārikā, the sovereign lady of the three cities, the mother of the three worlds, Durgā, the supreme seven-syllabled Vidyā. || 2 ||
She alone is the Mistress of the Seven Vidyās, taking refuge within the seven worlds;
she is the Earth consisting of the seven continents, the Mistress of Kula whose form is emptiness. (3)
The goddess who is consciousness in the world, Śārikā, exists in the form of stone;
she constantly bestows all desired objects and is seated upon the Pradyumna-pīṭha. || 4 ||
I shall speak of her chapter, which reveals the extraction of the mantra;
I shall describe to you, exactly as it is, the construction of the yantra, enriched with the limbs of dissolution.
O Pārvatī, first hear from me the extraction of the mantra, which is a great secret to be kept hidden, bestows all perfections in the Kali age, and is for the benefit of the world. 6.
The syllables *tā-raṃ*, *parā-mā-ta-ṭa-sin-dhu-rār-ṇāḥ*, *khaṃ*, and *śarma* situated in the middle of that,
followed by *aśmarī* at the end— O Pārvatī, this thirteen-syllable mantra of Śārikā is to be kept secret.
O Great Goddess, for this mantra there is neither obstacle nor defect; in this world, there is no fear of reversal, nor any doubt regarding the accomplished, the to-be-accomplished, or the enemy. (8)
It yields no fruit from preliminary rites (puraścaryā), nor does it involve the accumulation of physical hardship;
this mantra directly bestows accomplishment and removes all obstacles. || 9 ||
This mantra quickly washes away the impurity born of the great sins of killing a Brahmin, drinking liquor, and eating forbidden food. (10)
First, one should unlock the mantra; then, one should revive the mantra.
One should recite the perfected mantra in the middle and provide the "encasement" (saṃpuṭa) at the end.
Then, once the mantra is mastered, it certainly becomes effective;
O Goddess of the Gods, by the grace of this mantra, I am Bhairava himself.
O Goddess Pārvatī, this [teaching] concerning Viṣṇu Nārāyaṇa and Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds,
must not be given to the disciple of another, nor to one who is devoid of devotion.
Otherwise, there would be a loss of accomplishment for both due to the curse of Śiva.
O Maheśvarī, Mahādeva is declared to be the seer (ṛṣi) of this mantra. 14.
The Triṣṭubh is declared to be the meter, Śārikā is remembered as the deity;
Śarma is the seed-syllable, Ramā is the power, and Sindhura is remembered as the pin. || 15 ||
The application for the sake of dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa is thus declared; [it is performed] with the seed-syllables of Tāra, Parā, and Māyā, in the form of the six long vowels.

One should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the six limbs and so forth, by which one becomes identical with the Goddess. I shall now describe her meditation, which is the cause of consciousness for the entire universe;
by meditating upon which, O Queen of the Gods, supreme bliss is produced. (17)

I worship in my heart the goddess Śārikeśī, who possesses the brilliance of ten million rising suns, who is crowned with the moon, whose arms hold a supreme sword, a discus, and grant fearlessness, who is seated upon a lion, and who is merged into the left body of Śiva. 18.
I shall now proclaim the extraction of the yantra, which brings auspiciousness to practitioners, accomplishes all aims, is divine, and fulfills every desire. (19)
This yantra, consisting of a triangle, an eight-petaled lotus, a beautiful circle, a radiant eight-petaled lotus, a circle, and a triple mandala,
with a foundation-house adorned by fire, the sun, and the moon, is declared to be the abode of Śiva.
The great yantra of Śārikā, which effects the upliftment of the three worlds, must not be given to the disciples of others; by giving it [to them], one becomes a slayer of a Brahmin. || 21 ||
O Goddess of the gods, I shall now describe the limb of dissolution for this king of yantras, which is worshipped by Brahmā and Viṣṇu and bestows the four aims of human existence.
O Śivā, at the four gates, the practitioners should worship Gaṇeśa, Dharma, Varuṇa, and Kubera with dūrvā grass, unbroken rice grains, and flowers.
And likewise the guardians of the directions beginning with Indra, following the sequence starting from Īśāna;
and the goddesses Brāhmī, Vaiṣṇavī, Caṇḍikā, and Aparājitā.
Kaumārī, Śāmbhavī, Vārāhī, and Nārasiṃhikā—these Mothers situated in the circle of the Mothers are to be worshipped in the leftward order. || 25 ||
In those very three modes of conduct, the gurus are to be worshipped by the practitioners;
and likewise, O Goddess, the supreme guru and the guru of the higher and lower [levels].
O Goddess, having praised the supreme preceptor, the Bhairavas are to be worshipped:
Saṃhāra, Bhīṣaṇa, O Goddess, Kapālī, and Unmattabhairava. (27)
O Maheśvarī, one should worship these Bhairavas—Krodha, Caṇḍa, Ruru, and Asitāṅga—on the eight petals of the lotus, O Goddess. (28)
One should always worship the Mothers, beginning with Brāhmī, where they may be;
the Bhairavas by proceeding clockwise (dakṣiṇāvṛttyā), but the circle of Mothers (mātṛcakra) counter-clockwise (vāmataḥ). || 29 ||
Amā, Kāmā, Cārvaṅgī, the goddess Ṭaṅkadhāriṇī, Tārā, Pārvatī, the goddess Yakṣiṇī, and Śivā are to be worshipped. (30)
O Śivā, in the sequence of counter-clockwise rotation, Kālikā, Tripurā, and Durgā, situated in the eight corners, are to be worshipped; those in the central triangle are also to be worshipped. (31)
By means of the yoga of the Īśāna sequence, they bestow the desired fruits;
in the center is the goddess Śrī Śārikā, seated in the middle of the lap of Vāmadeva.
O Great Goddess, the Kaula practitioner, devoted to the Kaula conduct and seeking to accomplish the mantra, should worship with the five *makāras*.
One should likewise worship the Boon-granting Lord (Vara), the Discus, the Sword, and the Fearless One (Abhaya) with flowers,
unbroken rice grains, incense, lamps, and other offerings at the central point (bindu).
With offerings of food, water for sipping, and well-perfumed betel leaves—this is declared to be the limb of absorption (layāṅga). O Pārvatī, now hear the ritual applications (prayoga). || 35 ||
Stambhana, mohana, as well as māraṇa and ākarṣaṇa; likewise vaśīkāra, uccāṭana, śāntika, and pauṣṭika. || 36 ||
I shall describe their means of accomplishment (*sādhana*), a secret most wonderful, by which, through mere practice, the practitioner becomes Bhairava. (37)
Having bathed in the auspicious well during the sun's transit and likewise performed his daily rites,
he should remain without food at midnight and recite the root mantra at a crossroads.
O Śivā, one should perform the fire-oblation (homa) ten thousand times as a fixed rule,
using ghee, rāsnā, śaṭī, honey, and the flesh of the chameleon and other such creatures.
Brahmā, Hari, Śiva, and Jiṣṇu certainly become paralyzed at the time of midday when [the moon] is in the circle at the root of the reed-plant.
Having fashioned a triangular mandala, one should worship that Śrīcakra; O Goddess of the Suras, one should recite the root mantra ten thousand times according to the rule.
O Goddess of the gods, one should apply a tilaka with ashes extracted while cold from [the fire of] honey, clarified butter, wine, fish, camphor, liquor, and the hair of a tiger. 42.
Merely by the sight of him, the three worlds will fall into a state of delusion.
Having gone to a cremation ground at nightfall on the earth, one should recite [the mantra] ten thousand times. (43)
There, upon a funeral pyre with blazing fire, one should offer oblations of clarified butter mixed with cow dung;
at the root of a *śamī* tree, one should bury human bones while uttering the name of the enemy.
O Goddess, even an enemy equal to a god shall go to the jaws of death; having gone to the forest at the foot of a banyan or an aśvattha tree, one should perform the recitation (japa) there. 45.
O Maheśvarī, one should offer ten thousand roots alone, as well as a heap of white flowers,
along with clarified butter, excellent liquor, blood, and other flowers.
Menakā, with full breasts, will appear at dawn;
having gone to a crossroads where a corpse is seated, one should recite the root mantra while facing the Guru.
One should offer ten thousand or five thousand oblations of milk-rice and liquor;
and one should oneself consume it with eyes longing for the liquor, mixed with clarified butter and betel leaf.
Indra, Agni, Yama, the flesh-eaters, Varuṇa, Anila, and the Giver of Wealth (Kubera),
together with their respective lords, will undoubtedly come swiftly under his control.
O Śivā, having gone alone to a supreme cremation ground at twilight, at midnight, or during the Viṣṭi yoga, and having applied collyrium to his eyes, he should perform the recitation there.

O Goddess, one should offer ten thousand oblations of clarified butter mixed with sour gruel into the fire of a funeral pyre; by this, the eradication of the enemy occurs upon the heap of charcoals from that pyre.
O Goddess, having bathed at the time of midday on a Saturday and performed the daily rites, one should go to the temple and meditate upon the Goddess according to the prescribed rules.
In front of that, one should worship the yantra and recite the root mantra ten thousand times;
there, in a triangular sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), one should offer oblations of clarified butter in equal measure.
O Pārvatī, O Mistress of the Kula, by eating the flesh of a Ruru deer and likewise the head of a cock, there is immediate pacification of all fears. (54)
O Śivā, having gone to the abode of the pretas on the eighth or the fourteenth day,
one should recite the mantra ten thousand times or five thousand, and offer oblations of milk-rice mixed with sugar.
(412) By means of grapes and the three [substances] beginning with liquor, great nourishment is produced.
Thus has this procedure been declared, which is concealed in all the tantras. (56)
It should not be told nor taught by those who worship the circle of Yoginīs.
Thus, this secret chapter contains the essence of all the Āgamas;
O Goddess, being a profound mystery, it must be concealed by those seeking liberation.
Thus ends the first chapter on the Goddess Śārikā in the *Śrīrudrayāmala Tantra*, within the secret doctrine of the ten Vidyās.
Now begins the ritual procedure for the worship of Śrī Śārikā.
The venerable Bhairava said:
Now I shall describe the ritual manual (paddhati) associated with the worship of Śārikā; it consists of both prose and verse, is to be kept secret, and is established according to all the Āgamas. (1)
If one worships the Goddess without having performed the morning duties,
that worship is fruitless, just like a ritual action devoid of purity.

Therein, first, having performed the morning duties during the *brāhma-muhūrta*, and having completed the rites of bathing, the twilight prayers (*saṃdhyā*), and so forth in the river, one should return home and worship the deities of the door of the sacrificial pavilion (*pūjā-maṇḍapa*). As follows: *Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Dvāraśrī* above; *Gaṃ, obeisance to Gaṇapati* on the right; *Kṣāṃ, obeisance to Kṣetrapāla*.
Having worshipped with "Oṃ, obeisance to Vāstu-puruṣa" on the left [side] and "Obeisance" at the threshold, one should enter within, preceded by the left foot.

Having sat upon one’s own seat, [one should recite]: “For this mantra for purifying the seat (*āsana-śodhana-mantra*), Merupṛṣṭha is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Sutala is the meter (*chanda*), Kūrma is the deity (*devatā*), and its application (*viniyoga*) is in the purification of the seat. O Earth, by you the worlds are supported; O Goddess, you are supported by Viṣṇu. Therefore, support me, O Goddess, and make the seat pure. Oṃ.
Having worshipped the seat with "Hrīṃ, obeisance to the lotus-seat of the foundational power (Ādhāraśakti)," one should recite:
"May those beings depart who dwell upon the earth; may those beings who create obstacles perish by the command of Śiva."

May all those beings who cause harm to heretics, whether dwelling on the earth or in the intermediate space, depart; may they all perish by the command of Śiva. May the spirits, the departed, the piśācas, the rākṣasas, and the reptiles—may they all depart, struck by the weapon of the Goddess. (Thus, with three claps of the hands.)
Having dispelled the three kinds of obstacles by snapping the fingers three times upward with the index and middle fingers, by striking the left heel three times, and by means of the divine gaze;
and having performed the binding of the ten directions with ten snaps of the fingers, one should establish a wall of fire in the four directions.

Having reflected thus, one should perform three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*): sixteen *pūraka*s (inhalations), sixty-four *kumbhaka*s (retentions), and thirty-two *recaka*s (exhalations); this constitutes the first cycle.

The second is the reverse order; the third is like the first. Having contemplated one's own body as fit for the worship of the deity, with all impurities dispelled by these three breath-controls, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*).
Of this mantra of the venerable goddess Śārikā, Mahādeva is the seer (ṛṣi), Triṣṭubh is the meter (chandas),

the goddess Śrī-Śārikā is the deity (devatā), *śāṃ* is the seed-syllable (bīja), *śrīṃ* is the power (śakti), and *phrāṃ* is the pin (kīlaka); its application (viniyoga) is for worship for the sake of virtue, wealth, desire, and liberation— thus one should say with palms joined in reverence.

Salutation to the great seer Mahādeva on the head; salutation to the Triṣṭubh metre on the face; salutation to the deity Śrī-Śārikā on the heart; salutation to the seed-syllable *śāṃ* on the private parts; salutation to the power (*śakti*) *śrīṃ* on the feet; salutation to the *kīlaka* *phrāṃ* on the navel; salutation to the application (*viniyoga*) for worship on all limbs. Thus is the ritual placement of the seer and other elements (*ṛṣyādinyāsa*).
Oṃ hrāṃ śrāṃ, salutation to the two thumbs; oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, salutation to the two index fingers;

oṃ hrūṃ śrūṃ, salutation to the two middle fingers; oṃ hraiṃ śraiṃ, salutation to the two ring fingers; oṃ hrauṃ śrauṃ, salutation to the two little fingers; oṃ hraḥ śraḥ, salutation to the palms and backs of the hands.

*Namaḥ*. Thus is the ritual placement on the hands (*karanyāsa*). One should also place *vaṃ* upon the six limbs. Having thus armored the body with these ritual placements, [one should meditate] on the Root-Mantra at the Mūlādhāra, O Dear One, possessing a luster equal to ten million flashes of lightning, resembling ten million suns, and having the brilliance of ten million moons; that [mantra], O Dear One, which is like the fiber of a lotus stalk and consists of a point (*bindu*) and three circles.

"O fair-faced one, by the descent of the upward power (*ūrdhva-śakti*) which is innate (*sahaja*), through the firmness of the root power (*mūla-śakti*) and the awakening of the middle power (*madhya-śakti*), one should contemplate the Supreme (*parā*) who is blissful with the mass of supreme bliss. Having thus performed the internal sacrifice in the *mūlādhāra*..."

Having meditated upon the quadrangular sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*), which consists of the fourfold self— the individual self (*ātmā*), the inner self (*antarātman*), the supreme self (*paramātman*), and the self of knowledge (*jñānātman*)— and which is brilliantly illuminated by the fire of *kuṇḍalinī*, one should [place] the ego-sense (*ahaṃtā*) at its mouth, at the end of the root mantra.

Having offered the end of each with "I sacrifice, Svāhā!", one offers falsehood, backbiting, desire, anger, greed, pride, and envy— having sacrificed each individually with the mind as the ladle resting upon the *suṣumṇā*— or else, with the mind as the ladle, one sacrifices into the blazing fire of one's own self the oblation of dharma and adharma by way of the path of the *suṣumṇā*.

"Forever I offer the functions of the senses. Having thus offered the oblation, one should again meditate upon the Goddess in the lotus of the heart with her form as previously described, worship her with mental offerings (mānasopacāra), and perform recitation, fire-offerings, and so forth, all mentally according to one's capacity;
then, having contemplated one's own self in the form of the Kāmakalā, one should worship one's own body with perfumes and other offerings.

One should perform the installation of the water-pot (*kalaśa*). Therein, having fashioned a triangular circle on one's right side and having worshipped it with "Obeisance to Ādhāraśakti," one places the support (*ādhāra*) there; upon that, [one places the vessel] purified with "Phaṭ! To the Weapon" and "Namaḥ! (to the support).

Having placed a filled vessel or a conch shell there, having invoked the sacred fords (tīrthas) with the mantra beginning "Gaṅge ca Yamune caiva," and having cast in the perfumes and other offerings while reciting "Oṃ," one should worship them with the mantra "Salutation to the digits of Fire, Sun, and Moon," display the cow-mudrā (dhenumudrā), and worship [the deity] with one's own mantra; this is the general arghya.
Having performed [the preliminary rites], then, on one's left, having fashioned a square with a circle outside a triangle situated within a hexagon,

and having sprinkled that mandala with the water of the general *arghya*, one should worship there with "Obeisance to Ādhāraśakti" and, having established the support (*ādhāra*), [worship] with "Raṃ, obeisance to the Fire-mandala consisting of ten kalās."

Having worshipped with "Namaḥ," having washed the water-pot (kalaśa) with "Phaṭ," having filled it with the causal [substance], having adorned it with red cloth, garlands, and so forth, and having established it with the thought that it is the Goddess, one should worship the pot with: "Oṃ, obeisance to the solar orb consisting of twelve kalās. Then, with "Sauṃ, obeisance to the lunar orb..."

Having worshipped the substance with "Salutation to the one whose self consists of sixteen digits," protected it with "phaṭ," veiled it with "hūṃ," inspected it with the root mantra, sprinkled it with "namaḥ," and smelled the fragrance with the root mantra, he should place a flower in the jar and perform the rite of liberation from the curse.

The Supreme Brahman alone is eternal, consisting of both the gross and the subtle; by that [Brahman], I destroy for you the sin of Brahmin-slaughter born from a mere flash of thought. O Goddess, born from the solar orb, born from the abode of Varuṇa, composed of the seed-syllable *Amā*—may you be liberated from the curse of Śukra. The *praṇava* is the seed of the Vedas.
"If [the wine] consists of the bliss of Brahman, by that truth, O Goddess of Gods, may it remove the sin of killing a Brahmin. Having recited this three times,

and then having uttered "Oṃ vāṃ vīṃ vūṃ vaiṃ vauṃ vaḥ, salutation to Surādevī who is liberated from the curse of Brahmā" also three times, one should then recite the mantra beginning with "haṃsaḥ śuciṣat" and ending with "adrijā ṛtam" three times.
Having meditated upon Ānandabhairava, who has eighteen arms, three eyes, and five faces, accompanied by the goddess Surādevī;

having worshipped him three times with "Ānandabhairavāya vauṣaṭ" and "Sahakṣamalavaraya-ūṃ Surādevyai vauṣaṭ," one should [place] "Aṃ" sixteen times and "Kaṃ" sixteen times in three rows, moving clockwise in the center of the substance.
Having written "thaṃ" (16 p. 415), one should contemplate the syllable *haṃsaḥ* in its center; through that immersion, one should visualize nectar (*amṛta*) within the substance.
Having rendered it nectar-like with the Dhenu-mudrā, one should recite the nectar-seed syllable *vaṃ* and the root-mantra eight times.
Between those two, having drawn a triangle, a hexagon, a circle, and a square, one should offer salutations within the square:
"Salutation to Pūrṇagiri-pīṭha; salutation to Uḍḍīyāna-pīṭha; salutation to Kāmarūpa-pīṭha."

Having worshipped with "Oṃ, salutation to Jālandhara-pīṭha," and having worshipped the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga) within the hexagon, and having worshipped the three points of the triangle from right to left using the *trikhaṇḍa* mantra, and having worshipped the center with "Oṃ, salutation to Ādhāra-śakti," one should place the pedestal (*yantrikā*) within the triangle and sprinkle it with the water of the general offering (*sāmānyārghya*) while reciting "Namaḥ."

In the center, having worshipped with "Oṃ raṃ, obeisance to the fire-maṇḍala consisting of ten kalās," and having washed the vessel with "Phaṭ" and placed it upon the tripod (yantrikā), one worships there with "Oṃ aṃ, obeisance to the sun-maṇḍala consisting of twelve kalās," and having drawn a triangle, a circle, and a hexagon within the vessel, [one worships] with the mantra both in its entirety and in its parts.
Having worshipped with *vaṃ* as the root mantra and reciting the reverse Mātṛkā, fill the triangle with nectar;

having placed perfumes and other offerings therein, worship it with "Oṃ *sauṃ*, obeisance to the lunar maṇḍala consisting of sixteen kalās. Then, having drawn the yantra upon the substance as before, [place] *aṃ* sixteen times and *kaṃ* sixteen times on the three lines of the triangle, ending with *thaṃ*.

16. Having thus drawn [the diagram], one should worship the triangle three times with the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*), worship the hexagon with the six-limbed mantra (*ṣaḍaṅga-mantra*), and invoke the sacred ford (*tīrtha*) with the mantra: "O Gaṅgā and Yamunā! Then, having worshipped Ānandabhairava and Bhairavī with their respective mantras, one should worship from the east onwards: *glūṃ* salutation to the jewels of the sky (*gaganaratna*) in the east; *slūṃ* salutation to the jewels of heaven (*svargaratna*)...

"Namaḥ" (obeisance) to the South; "mlūṃ, obeisance to the jewels of the mortal realm" to the West; "plūṃ, obeisance to the jewels of the netherworld" to the North; "nlūṃ, obeisance to the jewels of the serpent realm" in the center. Having thus worshipped, one should purify the meat and other offerings. Taking the vessel of meat, [one recites]: "phaṭ, for the weapon-mantra, phaṭ."

Having sprinkled [the object] with the general *arghya* water, having veiled it with "Hūṃ," and having rendered it nectar with the nectar-mudrā while uttering "Vaṃ," one should purify it by reciting the root mantra seven times and the verse "pra tad viṣṇuḥ stavate. One should purify the fish with the verse "tryambakaṃ yajāmahe. Oṃ.
May Viṣṇu prepare the womb; may Tvaṣṭṛ fashion the forms. May Prajāpati pour [the seed];

may Dhātṛ place the embryo within you. O Sinīvālī, bestow an embryo; O Sarasvatī, bestow an embryo. May the two divine Aśvins, adorned with lotus-garlands, place an embryo within you. Oṃ hsaḥ bhrauṃ juṃsaḥ amṛte.

"O source of nectar, O showerer of nectar, cause the nectar to flow forth, flow forth, svāhā! Having thus purified the *kuṇḍagola* and other substances, veiled them, and rendered them immortal, one should recite the root mantra seven times over them.
Then, having invoked the Goddess therein, performed the binding of the directions with three *tāla* gestures, and displayed the *yonimudrā*, [one should utter] "hsauṃ."

Having honored [the vessel] with "Namaḥ," displayed the conch-mudrā, and performed the ritual integration (*sakalīkaraṇa*) by means of the six limbs, one should cover the vessel with the fish-mudrā while reciting the root mantra and contemplate the vessel as being the form of the Goddess.
Then, near the bell...

One should sequentially arrange the vessels for the Guru, the Śakti, the food offering (bhoga), one's own vessel, the Yoginīs, the heroes (vīra), the water for washing the feet (pādya), the respectful offering (arghya), the water for sipping (ācamanīya), and the honey-mixture (madhuparka).

Then, with the *tattvamudrā* as the means for the enjoyment (*carvaṇa*) [of the nectar], having drawn up drops from the *śrīpātra*, one should satisfy Ānandabhairava three times, saying: "I satisfy [you], obeisance. Then, likewise, one should satisfy the venerable *śrī-amukānandanātha-śrīgurupādukā* three times, saying: "I satisfy [you], obeisance. Thus.

Having gratified the supreme guru, the supreme preceptor, and the others with the nectar from the *śrīpātra*, one should perform the libation with the root mantra, saying: "I satisfy the venerable Goddess, together with her weapons, her vehicle, and her retinue; obeisance.
Thus concludes the installation of the *kalaśa*.

Then one should perform the worship of the pedestal (*pīṭhapūjā*): *Oṃ*, obeisance to Maṇḍūka; obeisance to Kālāgnirudra; to Mūlaprakṛti; to Ādhāraśakti; to Kamaṭha; to Ananta; to Pṛthivī; to Sudhārṇava;
to Ratnadvīpa; to Kalpavana; to Nandanodyāna; to Maṇimaṇḍapa; to Maṇivedikā.

Having worshipped the pedestal with the mantra: "Obeisance to the jeweled lion-throne, to the orbs of the sun, moon, and fire, and to the great corpse-seat of Sadāśiva (hsauḥ)," one should, by means of the seed-syllable of Vāyu through the left nostril, unite the Goddess from one's own heart within a handful of flowers, [reciting]: "O Queen of Gods, easily accessible through devotion, accompanied by Your retinue, as long as I..."

"O Goddess, please come here so that I may worship you. Having recited this, [one should recite] the root mantra followed by: "O Śrī Śārikā Bhagavatī, together with Śrī Vāmadeva, come here, come here! Stay here, stay here! Be present here, be present here! Be firmly established! Accept my worship accompanied by all the ritual offerings! [Then one should perform] the mudrās for invocation and the other rites.
Having performed the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* (consecration of the vital breaths) with the *lelihāna-mudrā*, having effected the binding of the ten directions (*daśadigbandhana*),

and having performed the veiling (*avaguṇṭhana*), one should display the *dhenu-mudrā* and *yoni-mudrā*, as well as the *vara*, *asi*, *cakra*, and *abhaya-mudrās*; and [one should worship] her, together with her weapons, vehicles, retinue, and enclosures, with the nectar from the *śrīpātra*.
"Obeisance, I satiate the venerable sandals of the Blessed Śrī Śārikā"—having thus satiated [her] three times, [one offers]:
"Obeisance, water for the feet to the Blessed Śrī Śārikā together with Vāmadeva"; likewise, "svāhā, the arghya";
"sudhā, the water for sipping"; "sudhā, the honey-mixture"; "obeisance, the bathing water for the sandals in the mouth."

"Then, having put on the two sandals fashioned of jewels, O Śārikā, come to the bathing pavilion situated in the direction of Indra for the purpose of bathing. Having bathed with the root mantra and again having put on the two sandals fashioned of jewels, O Śārikā, come to the beautiful, constructed pavilion of ornaments. Thus, having well-bathed her...

Having wiped the limbs with a clean silk cloth and having offered various ornaments— such as variegated garments, saffron, musk, sandalwood, vermilion, crowns, earrings, necklaces, and so forth— with the root mantra using the tips of the middle, ring, and thumb fingers, [one offers] "Gandho Namaḥ."
Thus, with the thumb and forefinger, one should offer flowers with "Vauṣaṭ! Oṃ jagaddhvanimantramātaḥ svāhā!
Having thus worshipped the bell, while ringing it with the left hand, one should offer incense with the root mantra (mūla).
In the same manner, one should present the lamp, the fly-whisk, the parasol, the banner, the mirror, the food offering (naivedya), and so forth. Then, with the *tattvamudrā*—
Having thrice satiated the Goddess with joined palms, and having obtained permission by saying, "O Blessed Śrī Śārikā, I worship your retinue; obeisance," one should begin the worship of the retinue.

Therein, first is the worship of the four gates: *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ gaṃ*, I worship the *śrīpādukā* of Gaṇapati; I bow and offer libations (*tarpaṇa*), I bow. (3 times) *dhaṃ*, [I worship] Dharmaśrī. (3 times) *vaṃ*, [I worship] Varuṇaśrī. (3 times) *kuṃ*, [I worship] Kuberaśrī. Having offered a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*), one should prostrate with the *yonimudrā*.
On the first line of the four gates, worship is performed in the order starting from the east.

Then, on the second line: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, worship the sandals of Indra (Indra-śrī-pādukāṃ pūjayāmi). 3. [Worship] Agni-śrī. 3. [Worship] Yama-śrī. 3. [Worship] Nirṛti-śrī. 3. [Worship] Varuṇa-śrī. 3. [Worship] Vāyu-śrī. 3. [Worship] Kubera-śrī. 3.

Īśānaśrī0 | 3 | Brahmaśrī0 | 3 | Viṣṇuśrī0 | Having offered a handful of flowers (puṣpāñjali), one should prostrate with the yoni-mudrā. Then, on the third line, one should worship their weapons as follows: 3 | Vajraśrī0 | 3 | Śaktiśrī0.
3. Daṇḍaśrī, 3. Khaḍgaśrī, 3. Pāśaśrī, 3. Dhvajaśrī, 3. Gadāśrī, 3.
Triśūlaśrī, 3. Padmaśrī, 3. Cakraśrī. Having offered a handful of flowers (puṣpāñjali), one should prostrate with the yoni-mudrā; thus ends the first enclosure (prathamāvaraṇa).

Now, the threefold worship (*trivṛttapūjā*). Therein, first, on the first line: *mūlaṃ divyaughaparākhyagurupaṅktiśrīpādukāḥ pūjayāmi*. On the second line: *mūlaṃ siddhaughāparākhyagurupaṅktiśrīpādukāḥ pūjayāmi*. On the third line: *mūlaṃ*... [etc.]

Having offered a handful of flowers (puṣpāñjali) here itself with the words: "To the lineage of gurus known as Mānavaugha, Parāpara, and so forth, [I bow] to the venerable feet of... 3; to my own guru, the venerable... 3; to the supreme guru, the venerable... 3; to the parameṣṭhi-guru, the venerable... 3; to the paramācārya-guru, the venerable...
3," one should prostrate with the *yonimudrā*. This is the second enclosure (*āvaraṇa*).

Then, having offered a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*) upon the eight petals with the root mantra (*mūla*), one should worship the eight Mothers (*mātṛkā*). As follows—the worship begins from the petal in front and proceeds counter-clockwise: 3. Brāhmīśrī 3.
Vaiṣṇavīśrī 3. Caṇḍikāśrī 3. Aparājitāśrī 3. Kaumārīśrī 3. Śāmbhavī 3. Vārāhīśrī
Having thus worshipped and gratified Nārasiṃhikā-Śrī, one should worship the eight Bhairavas on the filaments of the eight-petaled lotus, proceeding in a clockwise direction: 3/ Asitāṅgabhairava-Śrī;
3/ Rurubhairava-Śrī; 3/ Caṇḍabhairava-Śrī; 3/ Krodheśabhairava-Śrī; 3/ [Ugrabhairava-Śrī]; 3/ [Kapālīśabhairava-Śrī]; 3/ [Bhīṣaṇabhairava-Śrī]; 3/ [Saṃhārabhairava-Śrī].
Unmattabhairava-Śrī, 3; Kapālibhairava-Śrī, 3; Bhīṣaṇabhairava-Śrī, 3;

Saṃhārabhairava-Śrī, 3. Having thus worshipped and offered libations, one should prostrate with the Yonimudrā. This is the third enclosure. (In that very place, the worship of Brāhmī and the others should be performed by moving counter-clockwise).

Then, in the northeast corner (vasukoṇa), having offered a handful of flowers with the root mantra: 3/ Amāśrī0 | 3/ Kāmāśrī0 | 3/ Cārvaṅgīśrī0 | 3/ Ṭaṅkadhāriṇīśrī0 | 3/ Tārāśrī0 | 3/ Pārvatīśrī0 | 3/ (p. 418) [End of line].
Having worshipped and gratified Yakṣiṇīśrī and Śivāśrī, one should prostrate with the Yonimudrā;
this is the fourth enclosure (caturthāvaraṇa).
Then, in the triangle, beginning from the eastern corner: 3/ Kālikāśrī; in the northeast (īśāna), 3/ Tripurasundarīśrī.
In the southeast (āgneye), having worshipped and offered libations with "Śrīdurgāśrī," one should prostrate with the *yonimudrā*;
this is the fifth enclosure (*pañcamāvaraṇa*).
Then, having offered a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*) at the *bindu* with the root mantra (*mūla*), one should meditate there upon the Śrī Devī in her form as described.

Having taken a handful of flowers and recited the root mantra seven times, one should worship and satiate [the deity] with: "I worship the venerable sandals of the divine Śārikā together with the venerable Vāmadeva; obeisance, I satiate you, obeisance.
Having thus worshipped and satiated [her], one should worship [her] as before with perfumes, flowers, incense, lamps, parasols, and so forth.
(In that very place, the Varada and Abhaya mudrās, as well as the sword and discus, should be worshipped according to the prescribed ritual.

Thereafter, one should recite the armor-mantras (*kavaca*) and the hymn of a thousand names (*sahasranāmastotra*), and perform the daily fire-oblation (*nityahoma*). Then, having recited the root-mantra (*mūlamantra*) according to one's capacity, one should perform the libation (*tarpaṇa*) with the mantra beginning "O you, the protector of the most secret of secrets," and so forth.
O most auspicious among all that is auspicious, O Śivā, who accomplishes all purposes,
O refuge, O Tryambakā, O Gaurī, O Nārāyaṇī, homage be to you!
Having thus circumambulated [the deity] seven times, together with the initiates, he performs the salutation of the vessel (*pātravandana*) with the root mantra;
then, lifting the vessel and bringing it to the level of his head, he contemplates it as the grace bestowed by the Goddess, and recites: "Root mantra:
I purify the *ātmatattva*, svāhā! Root mantra: I purify the *vidyātattva*, svāhā! Root mantra..."

Having drunk four handfuls [of water] while reciting "I purify the Śiva-principle, svāhā! I purify the root and all principles, svāhā!", one should drink the remainder while reciting the root mantra; and then, having partaken of the chewed offering (carvaṇa).
May all practitioners rejoice; may detractors perish.
May the state of Śambhu be mine, and may the Guru be forever gracious.

Having recited this and other verses of the *Śāntistotra*, having prepared the mandala in the northeast (Īśāna), and having worshipped there with the remains of the offering (*nirmālya*) while reciting "Salutation to Nirmālyavāsinī," and having offered libations, one should take the water from the general *arghya* vessel and [recite]:
"From this time forward, by virtue of my authority over life, intellect, body, and dharma, throughout the states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep..."

"Whatever has been done by mind, speech, action, feet, belly, or genitals—all that which is mine, let it be offered at the feet of the Blessed Śrī Śārikā; svāhā. Having thus offered libations and taken the vessel of general *arghya*, [one should proceed].
Whatever action, whether good or bad, has been performed by me at any time—
O Goddess, out of compassion, accept all of that for my spiritual accomplishment.

Having thus circled three times over the five fingers, one should place water in the hand of the Goddess, hold the remaining water in one's own left hand, and sprinkle oneself seven times with the root mantra while uttering *phaṭ*. Then:
Go, go to the supreme abode, your own station, O Supreme Goddess,
where even the gods beginning with Brahmā do not know the highest state.

Having thus asked the Goddess for forgiveness with a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*), and having taken the flower from the wheel (*cakra*) with the withdrawal gesture (*saṃhāramudrā*) and smelled it,
[one recites]: "Stay, stay, O Supreme Goddess, in the supreme place, your own abode!"
Therein, all the gods beginning with Brahmā abide within my heart.
Thus, having brought the Goddess into one's own heart, one should dwell in happiness.
Thus, this manual for the daily worship,
composed in prose and embodying the essence of all the Śārikās, should not be given away by those who speak the truth.
The Śārikāpaddhati is secret and marked by the sequence of daily worship;
it must be kept hidden from uninitiated persons and from those who are not disciples by the teachers.
Thus ends the second [chapter], the ritual manual (paddhati) of Śrī Śārikā, within the secret doctrine of the Ten Vidyās in the venerable Rudrayāmala Tantra.
Now,
the Śrīśārikā-kavaca. The illustrious Bhairava said:
Now listen, O Goddess of gods, I shall proclaim the supreme armor (*kavaca*) of Śārikā, known as *Trailokyamohana*, which consists of the supreme root mantra. (1)
By the mere hearing of which one obtains the fruit of all sacrifices;
it is divine, the rescuer from all calamities, and the bestower of all accomplishments in the Kali age. (2)
This is my entire being, my secret, most supreme and most wonderful;
by its retention, O Goddess of gods, Viṣṇu [became] that one born from the water.
Just as the lord of the Dānavas, Andhaka, was swiftly slain by the Moon,
so too was the Dānava Bala, the ruler of Tripura, slain by me, the Victorious One (Viṣṇu).
O Goddess, by the power of this armor, Jambha and the asura Vṛtra were [subdued]; O Queen of the Gods, Bhairava is declared to be the seer (ṛṣi) of this armor. || 5 ||

The *triṣṭubh* is the meter and the deity is Trailokyamohaneśvarī; Śārikā is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), Śarma is the power (*śakti*), and Gaja is the pin (*kīlaka*). This application (*viniyoga*) is proclaimed for the sake of the Trailokyamohana-vidyā. || 6 ||

Of this Śrī Śārikā Bhagavatī Kavaca, Śrī Bhairava is the seer (ṛṣi), Triṣṭubh is the meter (chandaḥ), the Goddess Śārikā, the Mistress who Enchants the Three Worlds, is the deity (devatā), *śāṃ* is the seed-syllable (bīja), *śrīṃ* is the power (śakti), *phrāṃ* is the pin (kīlaka),
and its application (viniyoga) is in the recitation of the Kavaca that Enchants the Three Worlds. *Namaḥ* to Bhairava-Ṛṣi on the head.

Salutation to the *triṣṭubh* meter at the mouth; salutation to the deity Śrī-Śārikā at the heart; salutation to the seed-syllable *śāṃ* at the navel; salutation to the power (*śakti*) *śrīṃ* at the secret place; salutation to the *kīlaka* *phrāṃ* at the feet; salutation to the application (*viniyoga*) of the armor (*kavaca*) that fascinates the three worlds at all limbs. *Śāṃ*.
Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) on the hands and the six limbs using the seed-syllables joined with the six long vowels, one should meditate [on her] as follows:
she holds in her four hands the auspicious conch, discus, mace, and pair of lotuses; she wears necklaces, bracelets, and anklets made of lordly serpents, and possesses a white throat and garland.
I meditate in my heart upon the illustrious Śārikā, who has three eyes and whose splendor blazes with the thousand rays of vermilion and saffron.
Oṃ, may Durgā, adorned with the single syllable, protect my head;
Oṃ Hrīṃ, may Caṇḍī, whose form is the delight of the universe, protect my forehead.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ: may Tryakṣarā protect my eyebrows; Bhagamālinī, Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hūṃ, may she protect my eyes—she who is the auspiciousness of all that is auspicious. (8)
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hūṃ phrāṃ! May Śaṅkaravallabhā protect my two ears.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hūṃ phrāṃ āṃ! May Nārāyaṇeśvarī protect my nose. 9.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hūṃ phrāṃ āṃ śāṃ: may Sarasvatī protect my face. Aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ: may Mātṛkāśekhareśvarī protect my teeth. 10.
May Bhavapriyā protect the feet and the lips with the syllables uṃ, ūṃ, ṛṃ, ṝṃ, ḷṃ, ḹṃ, eṃ, aiṃ;
may Nīlakaṇṭhāsaneśvarī protect the throat with oṃ, auṃ, aṃ, aḥ.
May she who is worshipped by Skanda protect my shoulders with *kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ*; may Ambikā, whose beloved is on her left, protect my chest with *caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ*.
May Pārvatī protect my two sides with the syllables *ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ*; may Kulākuleśvarī protect my belly with the syllables *taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ*. (13)
May she who is served by Nārada protect my navel with the syllables *paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ*;
may she who is worshipped by the Lord of the Guhyakas protect the anus with *yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ*. || 14 ||
May the goddess Kātyāyanī always protect the hips;
may she who bestows all eloquence always protect the thighs with the syllables *laṃ* and *kṣaḥ*. 15.
Oṃ śāṃ jānū śivā pātu; Oṃ āṃ, may Umā protect my shanks;
Oṃ phrāṃ, may Rājamātaṅginī always protect my feet. 16.
Oṃ hūṃ! May Kubjikā protect my body from the feet to the head.
Oṃ śrīṃ! May Śāradā protect my body from the head to the feet. (17)
Oṃ Hrīṃ! May the Seven-Syllabled Śārikā protect my entire body.
May Brahmāṇī protect me in the east, and may Vaiṣṇavī always protect me in the southeast.
May Caṇḍī protect me in the south, and Aparājitā in the southwest;
may Kaumārī protect me in the west, and Śāmbhavī in the northwest. (19)
May Vārāhī protect me in the north, and Nārasiṃhikā in the northeast;
may Māmamā protect me at dawn, and may Kāmāvatā protect me in the center. (20)
May Cārvaṅgī protect me at the end of the day; may Ṭaṅkadhāriṇī protect me at the beginning of the night;
may Ugratārā protect me at midnight; and may Pārvatī protect me at the end of the night.
May Yakṣiṇī protect me everywhere; may Śivā protect me at all times.
May Asitāṅga protect me from the earth; may Ruru protect me from water.
May Caṇḍa protect me from the Maruts; may Krodha protect me from the sacrificial fire (Hutāśana);
may Unmatta protect me from Soma; may Kapālī protect me from the Sun.
May Bīṣaṇā protect me from obstacles to sacrifice, Saṃhārā from the void-mandala, Kālikā in battle, and Tripurasundarī in gambling. (24)
May Durgā protect me in dispute; may the Śrīcakra protect me at all times.
May the supreme Goddess Śārikā protect me everywhere and at all times. (25)
May Śiva, the Lord of Consciousness in the form of Vāmadeva, protect each and every thing that is mine—my wealth, my sons, my daughters, my wife, my home, and whatever else belongs to me. (26)
This is that divine armor, difficult to obtain in the three worlds;
it is the secret of Śārikā, named "The Enchanter of the Three Worlds. (27)
O Pārvatī, O Maheśvarī, without this sovereign armor-mantra, there can be no accomplishment for this mantra, even if it has been recited ten million or a hundred thousand times.
Therefore, O Śivā, one should recite at every moment the armor-mantra containing the heart-mantra;
it pacifies all calamities and increases strength and intelligence.
Whoever reads or causes it to be read, or hears or causes it to be heard—this [work] bestows supreme bliss in the world and is the cause of supreme sovereignty. (30)
He alone is the presiding Bhairava, the all-pervading conqueror of the three worlds;
one should write the armor-mantra on birch bark with the juice of the *svayambhū* flower during the sun's transit.
One should wear [the mantra] on the head or on the arm with a flower, the eight fragrances, breast milk, or one's own semen; thus one shall attain the supreme goal. || 32 ||
One desiring wealth shall obtain riches; one desiring a son shall obtain offspring;
and a man, having slain his enemies in battle, shall enter his home auspiciously.
O Goddess of gods, by holding [this] to one's chest, eloquence arises in an instant;
even a barren woman, a woman who bears only one child, or one whose children have died, shall obtain sons.
O Goddess, what may a mortal not obtain by reciting this supreme armor, which bestows the lifespan of Mārkaṇḍeya and makes one truly equal to Vaiśravaṇa? (35)
O Goddess of the Gods, he who recites this at midnight in a cremation ground with his hair disheveled, having drunk spirits, shall obtain a vision of the Goddess.
One may paralyze the sun and the wind, and certainly delude the three worlds;
for what more need be said regarding the wearing of this armor? (37)
By reciting or even by hearing this, O Goddess, one becomes like Bhairava himself;
such is this armor (kavaca), which brings the three worlds under control.
O Goddess of the Gods, that which is named Trailokyamohana must be kept secret;
it should not be given to just anyone, O Pārvatī, except to a disciple.
Having given [this] to one who is initiated and of noble lineage, one shall attain liberation;
one should not accept it without a gift, nor should one give it without a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
Whether one gives it away or receives it, for both there will certainly be success or failure;
otherwise, whoever should receive or give the Lord of Armor (Kavaceśvara), [the result is as stated].
Indeed, O Goddess Śivā, the Yoginīs devour his sons, wives, and daughters if one worships the Śrīśilā without knowing the armor-mantra (kavaca). 42.
O Goddess, O Śivā, that man who, having donned this armor, worships the Śrī-śilā, shall truly become Śiva himself, even if he is beset by all manner of calamities. (43)
He alone attains the supreme accomplishment; there is no doubt about this.
O Goddess, this armor (kavaca) is the essence, the very soul, and the most excellent [teaching]. (44)
This secret, the jewel of Śārikā, is to be guarded like one's own life;
it is divine, the granter of all desires, and is named "The Enchanter of the Three Worlds. (45)
Thus ends the Trailokyamohana-kavaca of Śrī Śārikā, within the Daśavidyā-rahasya of the Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra. 3.
Now follows the Thousand Names of Śrī Śārikā.
The venerable Bhairava said:
That goddess who was previously described as assuming the form of a śārikā bird,
the slayer of the rākṣasa Jālandhara, is stationed upon the peak of Pradyumna.
O Śivā, I shall declare to you that supreme knowledge known by the name "The Thousand," which contains a thousand names, is filled with mantras, and brings victory.
O Goddess, [she is] the embodiment of all other sounds, belonging to the stone known as Śārikā;
[this is so] even without daily rites, without ritual placement (nyāsa), and without worship.
Without formal worship, without recitation, without fire-offerings, worship, or libations;
without going to the cremation ground, and without the worship of the pledges (samaya). || 4 ||
O Pārvatī, listen to that vidyā by which one may obtain every fruit:
it is the goddess who is consciousness in the world, existing in the form of a stone as Śārikā. (5)
She creates, protects, and will indeed withdraw the universe; she is the one characterized by *tamas*, O Goddess, who bestows supreme sovereignty upon those wandering in *saṃsāra*. (6)
The stone whose essence is the Great Vidyā bestows the supreme state;
I shall describe to you its thousand names, which are a secret.
This secret is my all-in-all, the beloved of all conduct;
whoever chants this supreme vidyā or recites the Thousand Names (of the Goddess), [8]
One should wear this divine armor and recite the supreme Lord of Hymns;
O Goddess, what in this world would be difficult for him to obtain that he might not attain? 9.
For this thousand names, Mahādeva is remembered as the seer (ṛṣi); the metre (chandas) is Anuṣṭubh, and the deity (devatā) is proclaimed to be Śārikā. || 10 ||
The seed-syllable is *śarma*, the power (*śakti*) is *ramā*, and the pillar (*kīlaka*) is remembered as *sindhura*;
the application (*viniyoga*) is proclaimed for the sake of dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa. || 11 ||
