I shall proclaim the meditation upon her; listen, O daughter of the mountain!

Of this *Śrīśārikābhagavatīsahasranāmastotra*, the Seer (*ṛṣi*) is Śrī Mahādeva, the Metre (*chanda*) is Anuṣṭubh, the Deity (*devatā*) is Śrī Śārikā Bhagavatī, the Seed-syllable (*bīja*) is Śāṃ, the Power (*śakti*) is Śrīṃ, and the Pin (*kīlaka*) is Phrāṃ.

The application is for the sake of virtue (*dharma*), wealth (*artha*), desire (*kāma*), and liberation (*mokṣa*). Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the sages and so forth, one performs the ritual placement of the hands and limbs with *hrāṃ śrāṃ* and so on. The visualization (*dhyāna*):
[She who is] like ten million rising suns, with the crescent moon as her crest-jewel, and with lotus-like hands...
She holds a lotus, a discus, and the gestures of granting fearlessness and bestowing boons, with a smiling face. || 1 ||
I worship Śārikā in the lotus of my heart— mounted upon a lion, clad in red garments, adorned with red ornaments, and resting in the lap of Vāmadeva.

I worship in my heart Śārikeśī, who possesses the brilliance of ten million rising suns, who is crowned with the moon, whose hands hold the excellent sword, the discus, and the gesture of fearlessness, who is exultant, mounted upon a lion, and merged into the left body of Śiva.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hūṃ phrāṃ āṃ śāṃ! O Śrī Śārikā, Śyāmasundarī, Śilā, Śārī, Śukī, Śāntā, whose sphere of experience is a tranquil mind! || 1 ||
Abiding in peace, bestowing peace, she is peace itself; she is dark-hued with dark breasts.
The Goddess has the luster of the moon’s orb and wears the crescent moon as her crest-ornament.
The Goddess of the Gods possesses a loveliness as radiant as the moon, dwells in the center of the moon,
rides upon a tiger, and is supremely established upon a tiger.
Clad in a tiger skin, she is Śakti whose vehicle is a tiger;
she is Gaurī, Padmāvatī, full-bodied, with bud-like breasts that are full and firm.
Clad in yellow garments, with red teeth resembling the flower of the pomegranate, she is radiant;
her body is composed of a circle of jewels, inlaid with the shimmering rays of precious gems.
The goddess wears red garments and is adorned with garlands of jewels;
her radiance is intensified by gems, she is blazing with flaming crests, and she is compassionate.
Compassionate, a wish-fulfilling creeper, resembling the fire at the end of an aeon,
Bhairavī, of terrifying roar, with a fearsome face, and the womb.
Kārā, whose form is compassion, adorned with a garland of vulvas (bhaga), the Mistress of the Vulva, residing in the vulva, Kurukullā, and the slender-waisted one. || 8 ||
Kādambarī, most excellent, supreme, the highest sovereign;
she is Satī, Sarasvatī, the truthful, whose nature is both truth and untruth.
She is the lineage, the banner-like one, the trumpet-flower tree, and the radiance of the trumpet-flower;
she is the lotus-lake, the lotus-faced one, the lotus-like goddess, the one with lotus-hands, and the auspicious one.

She who rests in Śiva; she who is tranquil as autumn; Śacī; Rambhā; Vibhāvarī; the jewel of the sky; the one who traverses; Pāṭhā; the Mistress of the Seat; she of full form; she of beautiful form. || 11 ||
Inconceivable, bearing the mace, Mātaṅgī, sweet-voiced,
fond of lute-playing and song, the Gāthā, the Gāruḍī, she whose banner is Garuḍa. (12)
Sundarī, of exceedingly beautiful form and lovely tresses, dwells in the midst of Alakā; she is a celestial nymph honored by the gods.
She is worshipped by the Lord of Pātāla, she moves within the depths of Pātāla; she possesses infinite and endless forms, she is unknown, and she increases wisdom. (100) 14.
For she is immeasurable, indeed unfathomable, and possesses the form of infinite suns;
she is to be worshipped as the twelve suns, and she is Śamī, whose seed is the śyāmāka grain. (15)
She is radiant with a brilliant complexion, the destroyer of all asuras;
she consists of nectar, her very form is nectar, and she is nectar that brings joy to all. || 16 ||
The goddess of the lords of the gods is the giver of happiness; the beloved of Kṛśānu (Fire) is the oblation;
Svāhā is the eye of the lord of Svāhā, and she is indeed Agnivaktrā, satiated by fire. || 17 ||
She whose eyes are the moon, the sun, and fire; who is the very embodiment of the worlds Bhūr, Bhuvas, and Svar;
who is the earth, worthy of worship by the gods of the earth (Brāhmaṇas); who is self-born, and whose worshipper is her own Self. 18.
Richly adorned with garlands of self-manifested flowers, she is fond of self-manifested flowers;
she is the root-stalk of the sprout of bliss, the mother of Skanda, and whose abode is the stone.
She is volition, whose form is the manifestation of consciousness; she is the consort of Bhava and the remover of fear.
She is Vighneśvarī, Gaṇeśānī, the destroyer of obstacles, and the Night.
She was submissive, praised by those under her control, a hymn of praise, and possessed of the power to retain whatever she heard;
she was proficient in the injunctions of the scriptures and an expert in the meaning of the Vedas and the Shastras. || 21 ||
She is the altar, she is composed of the Vedas, she is knowledge, the bestower of boons upon the Creator, and the bride;
she is in the form of a bride, worshipped by the bride, and gratified by the drinking of wine by the bride. || 22 ||

Satisfied by the worship of the bride, adorned with a garland for the bride, she is the Left-hand goddess (Vāmā), the Mistress of the Left (Vāmeśvarī), the one belonging to the Left (Vāmyā), who wanders through both the Kula and Akula paths. || 23 ||
(428) She is the abode of initial and sustained thought, resembling the fire of universal dissolution;
she is the Mistress of Sacrifice, the Mouth of Sacrifice, the Sacrificer, and the sacrificial vessels. 24.
The sovereign of the yakṣas, the nourisher of the yakṣas, Pārvatī who dwells in the mountains, Pilampilā, she who abides in the sacred sites, the bestower of stations, and the ender of hell. || 25 ||

She is the woman who delights in jest, the bestower of fortune, the fortune of Śrīda, the one whose weapon is the arrow, the mistress of desire, delight, invocation, oblation, and the bearer of the sacrificial offering. || 26 ||
Hareśvarī, Harivadhū, adorned with golden armlets, Hapuṣā, Svargati, Vaidyā, Sumukhā (or Svamukhā), and Mahauṣadhi. || 27 ||
She is the remover of all diseases, devoted to the drinking of honey-wine;
she abides in honey, consists of honey, and is skilled in bestowing honey.
Satiated with honey, sweet in form, and possessing the luster of the *madhūka* flower;
she is Mādhavī, the creeper of Mādhava, intoxicated by honey, and languid with passion.
She who is dear to Māra, worshipped by Māra, and who brings delight to the gods of Māra;
she who is the mistress of Māra, the remover of death, beloved by Hari, and the one who transcends the mind.

Beloved by the great physicians, she is a physician herself, follows the conduct of a physician, and is worshipped by the gods; she is a sovereign with a full-bodied form, a pill that is weighty and most efficacious.
Kālāntakā, Kālamukhī, Kaṭhorā, Karuṇāmayī, Nīlā, Nābhī, Vāgīśī, Dūrvā, and Nīlasarasvatī. || 32 ||
She is the shoreless one who reaches the further bank; she is the goal to be attained, delight, and the bearer of breasts.
Her luster is like that of a rain cloud, and she is intent upon the form of mercury.
Policy has its abode in the lotus; fame is the narrator of glorious tales; Kāśī is desirable; the hope for matted locks is like the kāśa flower; and Lakṣmī is comparable to the kāśa blossom. (34)
She is Rāmā, beloved of Rāma, worshipped by the god Rāmabhadra;
she is honored by Rāma, the bestower of success upon Rāma, and the giver of sovereignty to Rāma. (35)
Reva is worshipped by the noble Rāma; she is Devakī, who is affectionate toward the gods;
she is worthy of worship by the gods, worthy of salutation by the gods, and honored by the forest-dwellers of the gods.
Dūtī, Drutagati, Dambhā, Dāminī, Vijayā, and Jayā;
she is worshipped by all the gods and is the destroyer of all the asuras.
The female ascetic (vaṭinī) who dwells at the root of the banyan tree, whose sole delight is in dance and laughter;
she is formless, beyond qualities, the truth, and the eternal increaser of contentment. (38)
Saumyā, Yajurvahā, Yāmyā (300), Yamunā, Yāminī, Yamī, Dākṣā, Dayā, Varadā, Dālbhyasevyā, and Purandarī. || 39 ||

She is Paurandarī, Pulomeśī, Paulomī, and she whose hair bristles with joy (Pulakāṅkurā); she dwells in the city (Purasthā), she is the forest ground (Vanabhūḥ), she is Vanyā, Vānarī, and Vanacāriṇī. || 40 ||
The abode of all castes, worshipped by all castes, enriched by the colors of all castes, and beloved by all gurus. || 41 ||
She is richly adorned with a complete garland of severed heads, wears a wreath, and has the sound of a bee;
she bestows a treasure-trove, dwells within a treasury, is a source of wonder, and is free from the flow of worldly attachment.
She is the giver of laughter, whose nature is both existent and non-existent, the tradition (smṛti) consisting of all castes,
the knowledge (vidyā) consisting of all syllables, and the sovereign of the sovereigns of the root-mantras.
She consists of the sixteen vowels, she is the liberator from the bondage of conditioned existence;
she is pervaded by the consonants beginning with *ka*, and she is the abode of all mantra-syllables. (44)
She is subtle and stainless, yet she is not conquered by the three qualities (guṇas);
she is Ambikā, Ambālikā, and Ambā, with her girdle consisting of infinite virtues.
Aparṇā, Parṇaśālā, Sāṭṭahāsā, Hasantikā,
Adrikanyā, Aṭṭahāsā, Ajārāsyā, and Arundhatī. (46)
The lotus-eyed goddess Abjinī is indeed worshipped by the one seated upon a lotus;
she holds a lotus in her hand, has lotus-like feet, and is gratified by the worship of the lotus. || 47 ||
The Goddess Mātṛkā, whose form is the letter A, is the digit that brings bliss to all;
she is the primordial Ānandasundarī, her eyes rolling and reddened with passion.

The goddess who is the beginning of the gods, the ender of the cruel, the ornament of the Solar dynasty (Āditya-kula), whose decoration is the seed-syllable "Āṃ," and who is the series of mother-letters (Mātṛkā) beginning with the letter "A. || 49 ||
She whose face is like the orb of the full moon, who possesses a radiance equal to ten million suns;
she is Indirā, Mandurā, Śālā, Itihāsā, Kathā, and Smṛti. || 50 ||
Ilā, whose essence is the taste of sugarcane juice, adorned with the syllable *ikāra*;
she who is praised by Indra, worshipped by Indra, auspicious in her power, and the sovereign lady of power. || 51 ||
She whose gait is like that of an elephant, whose song is like that of an elephant, and who is the mother of the syllable *ī*;
she is the Sovereign renowned for her majesty, the Mistress, and the beloved of the Lord.
The Goddess Kāmakalā is the sovereign; she is the Mātṛkā residing in the letter *ī*.
She possesses fierce radiance and a fierce mind, and she dwells upon the left side of the Fierce One. || 53 ||
Uṣā is indeed worthy of worship by the Vaiṣṇavas; she has the face of Ugratārā and a flaming torch;
she is the supreme Mistress of Umā, the Lord, and the Sovereign Goddess of the Waters.
Udakā, Acchodakā, and Ukārodbhāsamātṛkā; Ūṣmā, Pyūṣā, and Ūṣaṇā, likewise Ucīta-varapradā [and Uditādityasuprabhā]. || 55 ||
She who takes away debt, the mistress of the letter Ṛ, possessing the sounds Ṛ and Ḷ, partaking of the sound Ḷ,
with eyebrows shaped like the letter ḹ, the youthful maiden whose radiance is equal to the rising sun.

She who wears a crown marked by the deer, she whose seed-syllable is the letter *E*, she who is fond of the deer, she who dwells in the midst of the deer, and she who is affectionate toward the deer. || 57 ||
Seated in the center of the moon, she is crowned with the radiant syllable *ai*;
the Goddess has the syllable *oṃ* as her crest-ornament and is adorned with the jewels of the appropriate words. (58)
She whose abode is the lotus-seat, whose nature is the syllable *Aḥ*, and who is the path to heaven;
she whose form consists of the sixteen vowels and who sings the sixteen vowels.
She is the Sixteenth, possessing sixteen forms; she is Kamalā, born from the lotus;
she is Kāmeśvarā, skilled in the arts; she is Kumārī, with curly locks of hair.
Kuṭilā is crooked in form, auspiciously joined with her family;
she is the mistress of the family (Kuleśī), Kubjikā, the digit (Kalā) who brings about the states of both Kula and Akula. 61.
She is Kāmā, Kāmapriyā, Kīrā, Kamanīyā, and Kapardinī;
she is Kālikā, Bhadrakālī, and the one who brings an end to the desires of Time (Kāla). || 62 ||
Kapālinī, Kapāleśī, she who is anointed with heaps of camphor;
Kādambarī, she of tender limbs; Kāśmīrī, she with the luster of saffron. || 63 ||
She is enriched with the seed-syllables of the *kūrcas* and *arṇas*, beautiful, belonging to both the *kula* and *akula*;
she has a formidable mouth, formidable eyes, and a most terrifying form.
She is the beautiful Alakā, the cow of plenty, the beloved woman, and the protectress of desires;
she dwells upon the throat, is the creator of compassion, and is the Mother of Letters whose first syllable is "Ka."
She holds a sword in her hand, she is the Mistress of the Skull-bowl, she moves through the sky, and she travels like a bird;
joined with the Khecarī mudrā, she bestows the power of moving through the air.
Seated upon a bird, with tremulous eyes, she is the Mistress of the Planets and the destroyer of the wicked;
holding a shield as her weapon in hand, she resembles the radiance of the sun. (500) 67.
The beloved one whose abode is the void, the Mother who is the radiance of the void;
she is Vaikharī, whose abode is the seed-syllable, situated in the void, the beloved of the Khecarīs.

She is the possessor of qualities, the mother of the elephant-faced one, the bestower of boons upon Gaṇeśa, and Gayā; she is the Godāvarī, the mace-bearer, the bearer of the Gaṅgā, and the bestower of boons upon the Wielder of the Mace (or the beloved of the Wielder of the Mace).
Godhā, mistress of the vehicle of the bull, beloved of the poison-eater,
adorned with profundity, the Gaṅgā, adorned by the ocean of the letter *ga*, Gāyatrī.
[She who has an elephant as her vehicle. || 70 ||
She who is praised by the nose-born (Agni), who makes the *ghurghura* sound, who roars terribly;
who dwells in the jar (*ghaṭa*), who is served by the jar-born (Brahmā), whose form is dense (*ghana*), and who is the Mistress of the Woodworm (*Ghuṇeśvarī*). || 71 ||
She is served by Ghanavāhana, she is the Mother of Letters whose first syllable is the letter *gha*;
she ends with the letter *ṅa*, she is the abode of the letter *ṅa*, she has the form of the atom *ṅa*, and she dwells in the letter *ṅa*.

She is without distress, without fatigue, and beyond all that can be muttered in prayer; she is adorned with letters of no particular color, possessing the luster of refined gold, like the moonlight of the moon, and devoted to the Moon.

Moving, moving, she who moves; clothed, she who is like the moon, she who moves with the rays of the moon; she whose speech is the sound of the *cañcurīka* bird, she whose very nature is wonder. || 74 ||
Agile, flattering, beautiful, like the *campā* flower and resembling the *campaka*, wearing Chinese silk and adorned with the ocean, she performed her flatteries. (75)
She who possesses a parasol, she who holds a parasol, she who is severed, she whose head is severed, she whose complexion is radiant;
she who is fond of the son of Chāyā, she who is the shadow, she whose color is like a flower, and she who is the stainless Mother.
The Mother of the World, the Light of the World, whose form is light, who wears matted locks;
she who bestows victory, who causes victory, who abides in victory, and who smiles with victory. || 77 ||
Beloved of the world, worshipped by the world, the creator of the world, afflicted by old age;
the destroyer of fever, the subduer of Jambha, the life-breath of the world, the bringer of victory. || 78 ||
She is the bestower of boons upon the foremost of the Jambhas, the victorious, the life-giver, and the one who grants the speech of the living;
she is the ever-awake, the sleep of the world, the womb of the universe, and the bearer of the waters.
Jālandharadharā is the consort, the mother-syllable of the letter *ja*;
Jhampā is Jhiṃjheśvarī, ending with *jhā*, the mother-syllable of the letter *jha*. (80)
She whose form is knowledge, whose abode is knowledge, who is the mistress of the letter *ña*, whose weapon is knowledge,
who is enriched by the ornaments of the seed-syllables of the *ña*-group, she is the Mother of Letters (*mātṛkā*) whose syllable is *ña*.
She whose weapon is a chisel (ṭaṅka), who is enriched by the letter Ṭa, whose eyes are like a ṭoṭā, whose hair is beautiful (ṭasu),
whose weapon is a chisel, whose form is that of a ṭalī, she is the Mother of the syllable Ṭa.
She is the noble lady (Ṭhakkurā), the sovereign of the noble ones (Ṭhakkureśānī), the mistress of the triad of the letter Ṭha;
she is the very nature of the syllable Ṭhaḥ, enriched with the letter Ṭha, the Mātṛkā of the syllable Ṭha.
Ḍakkā, Ḍakkeśvarī, Ḍimbhā, the Mother of Letters whose syllable is the letter Ḍa;
Ḍhiṇī, Ḍhehā, Ḍhillahastā, the Mother of Letters whose syllable is the letter Ḍha. || 84 ||
She whose end is *ṇa*, whose end is the *ṇa*-group, adorned with the syllable *ṇa*;
she who is the fourth, the state of the fourth, whose form is the balance, Tripurā, beloved of Tāmasa. (85)
She is the all-pervading Tāriṇī, the Savior Tārā, manifesting in twenty-seven forms;
she is Tripurā, composed of the three qualities (guṇas), the one whose lord is Tryambaka, and the sustainer of the three worlds—thus she is to be meditated upon. 86.
She is the mistress of the three aims of life, the triple Veda, the three-eyed one, and the three-footed embodiment of the Vedas;
she is the mother of the three worlds, the protector, and worshipped by the Lord of Tripura.
She who dwells in the triangle, she who is the mistress of the triangle, she who resides in the three corners;
she who is pleased by the worship of the triangle, she who is devoted to the worship of the triangle. || 88 ||
Attached to the gift of the triangle, she bestows auspicious wealth upon all corners;
the Goddess, residing in the eight corners, proclaims the wealth of the eight corners. (89)
Worshipped by Vasu and Koṇa, she dwells in the sequence of the six cakras;
seated upon the leaf of the serpent, the Śārī bestows the purpose of the threefold worship.
She stands at the forefront of the four gates, dwelling both inside and outside the circle;
she is of the nature of darkness (tāmasī), resembling a javelin, and resounds with the sound of Tumburu.
Tulākoṭisvanā, Tāpī, the increaser of the fruits of austerities;
Taralākṣī, the destroyer of darkness, and the slayer of the demon Tāraka. || 92 ||
She is the boat and the form of the ferry, the Mother of Letters in the form of the syllable *ta*;
she is the dry land and the form of the Elder (the Buddha), the gross, the cooking pot, and the lotus of the earth.
Sthāvareśā, Sthūlamukhī, the Mātṛkā whose syllable is the letter Tha; Dūtikā, Śivadūtī, and Dyuti, who bears a staff as her weapon. || 94 ||
She is compassion, she is pity for the wretched, and she is the beloved of the wielder of the thunderbolt;
she wanders through the lands, she is Drekkā, the sovereign of Draviḍa, and she is most remote.
Dākṣāyaṇī, Drumalatā, Devamātā, Adhidevatā, Dadhijā, Durlabhā, Devī, and Paramākṣarā are the Goddesses. || 96 ||
She is the one highly worshiped by Dāmodara, the bestower of boons upon Dāmodara;
she is the destroyer of the daughter of Danu and is adored by the clan of Danu’s sons. || 97 ||
She holds a staff in her hand, she is worshiped by those who bear staffs, she bestows self-restraint, and she abides in self-restraint;
she possesses the beautiful form of ten cows and is the Mother of Letters whose initial syllable is "Da."
She is the one endowed with righteousness, the source of dharma, the most excellent, the giver of wealth, and the increaser of wealth;
she is fortitude, the clever one, the fortunate wife, and the mother of the syllable *dhak*.
She is not a hollow lotus stalk, nor does she bear iron arrows as weapons;
standing in the midst of a grove of *nīpa* trees, she is the sovereign of the city, the most excellent among men.
She is the sovereign of men, worthy of being propitiated by kings, honored by kings, and the bestower of wealth upon kings;
she is to be served by kings, adored by kings, and the mother of Nara and Nārāyaṇa. 101.
The dancer, the lotus-eyed one, adorned with the nine-syllable mantra;
the Mistress of the Lotus, the lotus-faced one, whose vehicle is the leaf, both transcendent and immanent. (102)
Pārāvārasutā, Pāṭhā, Paravargavimardinī;
Pūḥ, Purārivadhū, Pampā, Patnī, and Patrīśavāhanā. (103)
She has full shoulders, possesses the strength of her husband, and has yellow eyes; she is devoted to her husband.
She is Pīṭhā, established upon the throne (pīṭha), yet not a mere seat (apīṭhā); she is adorned with yellow ornaments. || 104 ||
She is the essence of Purūravas, the vessel, the daughter, the giver of sons, and progeny;
she is adorned with flowers as her crest-ornament, she is the abundance of flowers, and she is decorated with garlands of flowers.
She is richly adorned with the supreme splendor of flower garlands; she is the Mother (Mātṛkā) whose seed-syllable is the letter *pa*;
she is the bestower of fruits, possessed of abundant garments, and terrifying with the howling of jackals.
Phalgunī, residing at Phalgutīrtha, whose mandala has the form of the letter Pha;
the bestower of strength, Bālakhilyā, the youthful one, and the beloved of the enemy of Bala (Kṛṣṇa). || 107 ||
She is the state of childhood, the mistress of the barbarians, the mother whose form is the letter *ba*;
she is auspicious, the wife of Bhīma, the formidable one, the crest-jewel of Bharga, and the fearless. || 108 ||
She is the destroyer of fear, possessing a terrifying roar, with a formidable face and eyes;
she is the sovereign of the Bhillīs, the remover of fear, the bestower of auspiciousness, and the performer of auspicious deeds. || 109 ||
Bhadreśvarī, Bhadradharā, she who is called Bhadrā, the increaser of fortune; Bhagamālā, the abode of fortune, Bhavānī, the savior from worldly existence. (800) 110.
She whose source is the *bhaga*, who has the form of the *bhaga*, who resides in the *bhaga*, and whose nature is the *bhaga*;
she who delights in the nectar of the *bhaga-linga*, and who is the mother of the syllable *bha*. 111.

She is worthy of honor, the bestower of honor, the fish, she who is devoted to the one whose banner is the fish; she is raised up by passion, the one to be honored by the mind, Menā, and she who is affectionate toward Maināka.
Intoxicated by honey, worthy of worship with honey, giver of honey, the honey-like Mādhavī;
she who eats meat, who delights in meat, who consumes meat, and who bestows meat. || 113 ||
Afflicted by Māra, she has the form of a fish, and as a great fisherman, her mouth is as high as the peak of Mount Meru; she is honored with offerings of sweetmeats.
Mātaṅginī, intoxicated by honey, intoxicated with passion, the mistress of intoxication;
she whose marrow is charming, whose face is lovely, and who is adorned with the letter 'Ma'. || 115 ||
The illustrious one, the mistress of ascetics, the performer of effort, the lover of the Yajus;
the sustainer of sacrifice, the fruit of sacrifice, and the fruit of the Ṛks of the Yajurveda. (116)

Yaśodā, she who is to be served by ascetics, the festival itself, she who is affectionate toward pilgrims, the Mistress of Yoga, she who is attainable through yoga, and she who is affectionate toward the people who are lords of yoga. || 117 ||
She is the daughter of Yadu, the slayer of Yama, and the mother of the syllable *ya*;
she is Ratneśvarī, served by the Lord of Ramā, the thoroughfare, and the one who is menstruating.
She who bestows sovereignty, the sovereign queen of the lords of kings, the remover of disease, she who possesses passion;
the daughter of the ocean, the delightful one, night, and she whose splendor is like that of the lord of night. 119.
She is the destroyer of Rākṣasas, the sovereign of the Rākṣasas, and worshipped by the Lord of the Rākṣasas;
she is fond of pleasure, has a face of delight, and her crest is shaped like the letter Ra.
She has a protruding belly, a quivering tongue, and a mind intent on the dance of *lāsya*;
her mouth is like a web of spider-silk; she is Lakṣmī, Modesty, and the destroyer of dissolution.
The Mistress of the World, the Sustainer of the World, residing in Lāṭa, whose form is characterized by auspicious marks;
she who is long, with her flowing hair shimmering, increasing in the form of the letter La.
She is the Mistress of the Linga, she whose very nature is the Linga, she who wears a garland of Lingas, and she of radiant luster;
she is the form of Lakshmi, the delight of aesthetic rasa, the beautiful woman, the river Revā, and she who is full of passion.

Layadā is the one characterized by [the letter] *la* (900); she is the playful one (*lolā*), the mother of the syllable *la*, Vārāhī, the bestower of boons, the mother of heroes, and the giver of heroes. || 124 ||
Vīreśvarī, the mother of heroes, adorned with the chewing of heroes;
possessing excellent weapons, she is both most excellent and short, being of a dwarf-like form. || 125 ||

She who has cast off [worldly bonds], she who is not to be slain by the slayers, she who is the ground for those to be slain, she who is dear to the merchant, she who is the splendor of spring, she who is the young girl, she who is the young boy, she who is the mistress of the young boy. 126.

She who is dear to the student (Vaṭu), the one with beautiful eyes, she who is solely intent upon the left-hand path (vāmācāra), the news, the one belonging to the left, the one of excellent hips, the mother of the Vedas, and the earth. 127.
She whose vehicle is the wind, who is the companion of the wind, and whose alphabet begins with the letter *va*;
she who is dear to Śambhu, who is the autumnal discourse, who is the green meadow, and who is affectionate toward the moon. 128.
She who possesses cool radiance, whose essence is cool, whose lips are crimson, and who bestows refreshing sprays;
she who bears the Śrīvatsa mark, who is identical with Śarva, and who dwells upon the left side of Śarva. || 129 ||
She possesses the stainless splendor of the moon; she has the body of a tiger; she is the daughter of the mountain;
she is the remover of desiccation; she dwells at the root of the Śamī tree; and her crest is fashioned from the letter Śa.
She is the Sixteenth, whose form is the Sixteenth; she is sixfold and sixfold, the six-faced one;
she possesses six peaks, she tastes the six flavors, and her lotus-face has eighty-six petals.

She is the mother of the six-faced one, the neuter, the Mātṛkā of the letter *ṣa*, the progenitor of Sarasvatī, the all, the omnipresent, and the one whose face is turned in every direction. || 132 ||
She is Samā, Sītā, Satīmātā, and the bestower of fearlessness from the ocean; she is the pacifier of all curses, Sālabhañjī, and Sudakṣiṇā.
She is deep sleep, she is the most excellent, she is the virtuous one, she is the singer of the Sāman chants, and she is born from the Sāmaveda;
she is fond of truth, she has the moon as her face, she resides in the aphorisms, and she is beloved by the Sūtas.
Sanakeśī and Sunandā abide in their own group as the eternal one;
she is the bridge for all directions and the beloved of the letter "Sa."
She who is fond of the *hālāhala* poison, whose play is effortless, whose ornament is the cry of "Alas!
Alas!", whose nature is that of Hāhā and Hūhū, who is the supporter of the plow (Balarāma), and who is beloved by Indra.

She has tawny eyes, a formidable form, and is fond of oblations of clarified butter; her essential nature consists of the syllables *haṃ*, *kṣaṃ*, *laṃ*, and *kṣaḥ*, and she is worshipped by all the Mothers.
Oṃ aiṃ sauḥ hrīṃ mahāvidyā āṃ śāṃ phrāṃ hūṃ svarūpiṇī (1000). Thus ends the Thousand Names of the Mantra of the Goddess Śrī Śārikā. 138.
O Goddess, whoever reads this—which is meritorious, praised by the Puṇyajanas, worthy of praise, and honored by the Vaiṣṇavas—and whoever causes it to be heard or listens to it themselves; || 139 ||
That very Lord, the God—truly, truly so, O Mistress of the Gods—is he whom the man who recites [this] once, twice, or thrice a day [attains]. (140)
O Goddess, listen to the fruit of the merit of one who is devoted to the left-hand practice (vāmācāra):
it destroys muteness, deafness, leprosy, and vitiligo.
In that same way, one should destroy [it]. || 141 ||
O Goddess, he who recites this at night with faith immediately pacifies disorders of wind, bile, and phlegm, abdominal tumors, hemorrhaging, and cholera. (142)
He who recites this for even a single month is certainly freed from epilepsy, earache, violent colic, and fistula. (143)
O Maheśānī, if one recites [this] within the center of the wheel on a Tuesday or a Saturday, Śārikā will immediately become a granter of boons to him.
He who recites this at a crossroads for three nights, at the end of each night,
having offered an oblation consisting of liquor, honey, fish, meat, and cooked rice; 145.
O Goddess, a Śārī [plant] covered with the tips of *vabbola* bark will appear for one who recites [this] at Lolā, upon a funeral pyre in the presence of a corpse. 146.
Listen now to the fruit of merit for him who drinks it three times;
[it destroys] the killing of a Brahmin, the killing of a guru, the drinking of liquor, and the slaughter of a cow.
It destroys the accumulation of great sins arising from violating the teacher’s bed, as well as theft or the killing of a fetus; of this there is no doubt. (148)
For he alone, O Goddess, is the son of Ramā, illustrious, honored by the world, capable of granting boons, the Lord of Heroes, and the beloved of all beings. 149.
The practitioner who, endowed with faith, recites this three times during the worship of the wheel in the presence of the Śakti, shall become Bhairaveśvara.
O Goddess Śivā, what is there that the practitioner, the hero-practitioner, does not obtain? He becomes possessed of sons, possessed of wealth, and devoted to truthful conduct.
O Goddess of the gods, having fully worshipped Śakti, one should recite this supreme hymn;
having enjoyed happiness in this world, one shall go to the third heaven in the hereafter. (152)
Thus ends this enchanting thousand-name hymn of Śārikā, which is secret, most secret in the world, and to be guarded like one's own private parts. (153)
Thus ends the Thousand-Name Hymn of Śrī Śārikā, within the *Daśavidyārahasya* of the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*.
Now, the Śrīśārikā Stotra.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim this supreme hymn consisting of mantras;
it comprises five limbs, is my very essence, and bestows the fruit of ten million mantras. (1)

Of this *Śrīśārikābhagavatīstavarāja*, the Seer (*ṛṣi*) is Śrī Mahādeva, the Metre (*chandaḥ*) is Triṣṭubh, the Deity (*devatā*) is Śrī Śārikā Bhagavatī, the Seed-syllable (*bīja*) is ŚĀM, the Power (*śakti*) is ŚRĪM, the Pin (*kīlaka*) is PHRĀM;

its application (*viniyoga*) is in the recitation of this King of Hymns for the sake of attaining the accomplishment of Śrī Vidyā. Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*), one should meditate.

I worship in my heart Śārikeśī, who possesses the brilliance of ten million rising suns, who is crowned with the moon, whose arms hold a supreme sword, a discus, and the gesture of fearlessness, who is seated upon a lion, and who is merged into the left body of Śiva.
One should meditate in the mind upon Your three-eyed [form] within the third eye, which has become the ruby upon the crest of the head of Manu, adorned with the crescent moon and the orb of a dot.
That lord of mantras who recites [the mantra] with his mind becomes worthy of honor by the great, blessed with merits, and like Indra himself, fanned by the Maruts. || 1 ||
He who meditates upon the seed-syllable of Parā, a treasury of splendor situated above the fire-mantra (Ra),

becomes like the rising sun that dispels the dense mass of darkness— the delusion of the world; having become a Lord of the World, he wanders as a great master of mantras upon the earth, in heaven, or in the city of the serpents.
As you desire, throughout the three worlds. || 2 ||
O Goddess, that perfected one who, within the midst of your mantra, recites it without seed-syllables and without the arising of bliss—
[he is] seated upon half the throne of the Lord of Gods, his eyes slightly reddened by wine.
O Śivā, he who, though fickle in the amorous play of love, recites the *kūrca* mantra— which shines with wondrous grace—
shall slay the host of his enemies by a mere utterance of "Huṃ" and become a sovereign emperor of the earth.
He who, situated between the full breasts of a deer-eyed woman, recites for a moment upon hearing the sound of an elephant’s roar,
becomes an expert in Menakā’s amorous arts and performs the playful dalliance of a Līlāvatī.
If a fool, submerged in the ocean of dullness and defeated by enemies, should mutter the seed-syllable *śūnya* in the midst of a mantra,
then eloquent words— flowing with the essence of wine— will issue forth from his lotus-like mouth in both prose and verse.
If the supreme adept recites the auspicious seed-syllable within his mind at the goddess Śivā during midnight,
he shall become a lord of enjoyments, a sovereign king intent on attainment; having reached Bhogavatī, he shall become the Lord of Bhaga.
O Great Goddess, for that crest-jewel of practitioners who recites your name-mantra within the midst of your mantra, O Śrīśārikā,
the fortune of the assembly of kings shall come under his control upon the field of battle.
O Īśānī, she who recites the seed-mantra of Aśmarī at midnight—
the Goddess seated upon the lion-throne— bestows boons and grants her vision.
O Mother, he who meditates upon You— residing within the mandala of the earth consisting of a dot, a triangle, an eight-cornered figure, a perfect circle, a serpent-leaf, and three circles;
whose lotus-face resembles the orb of the rising sun— he shall become a sovereign emperor upon this earth.

That which is the *bindu* is Pītāmaha; that which is *hari* is the Sun, proclaimed as the vowel (*svara*). That which is the letter *repha* is Rudra, who always crushes the flood of evil and is ever-sung.
That which is *prāṇa* is the Supreme; he alone is the Blessed Lord, the Sound (*nāda*), Śiva, and the Goddess is always the digit of the Moon (*candrakalā*).
O Illusion, you who are free from blemish, salutations to you! || 11 ||
Whoever recites this Śrīśārikā-stava at dawn, or at midnight, or at the time of worship, Indra himself,
accompanied by gods and asuras, comes to him and, having performed worship, grants him sovereignty over the three heavens.
Thus, O Goddess, this five-limbed secret of Śārikā is her entire essence, supremely hidden, and capable of uplifting the three worlds. (13)
Meritorious, purifying, life-prolonging, conducive to welfare, and bestowing fame—
this [mantra] consisting of five *m*s is to be worshipped and accomplished by the most excellent of practitioners. (14)
O Goddess, it should be protected like a son and revealed only to beloved friends;
this supreme essence of the Śārikā has been declared as a secret. 15.

It must not be given to one who is not a devotee, nor to one with poor clothing, nor to one who is evil-minded, nor to a slanderer, nor to one who is not a disciple; otherwise, that practitioner of mantra shall go to hell.
The Śrī Devī said:
"O Blessed One, by this exposition of the five limbs, I have indeed been purchased by you; I am your servant. What else shall I say to you? (17)
Śrī Bhairava said:
O Īśānī, this five-limbed reality is the supreme essence of all stones;
it is a secret, most to be guarded, O Goddess, and must be concealed by those seeking liberation.
Thus ends the Śrīśārikā Stotra, the secret of the ten Vidyās, within the Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra. 5.
And thus concludes this *Śrīśārikā-pañcāṅga*.
(p. 443) Now follows the five-limbed ritual manual (pañcāṅga) of the illustrious Mahārājñī.
To the Blessed Lord, the consort of Umā, seated upon the peak of Śrīśaila—
the God who wears the crescent moon as his crown and whose eyes are the sun, the moon, and fire.
Clad in an elephant hide, Virūpākṣa, the lord of the gods, who is saluted by the hosts of Gaṇas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, and by gods and Asuras. || 2 ||
Laughing and muttering prayers while reciting [mantras] again and again,
richly adorned with serpent ornaments, and saluted by Brahmā and Acyuta.
Rising up and bowing down, Bhairavī questioned him.
The Illustrious Goddess said:
"O Blessed One, you are the supreme deity, saluted by gods and asuras alike."
He is possessed of all attributes, a knower of the Vedānta system, transcendent beyond qualities, and the conscious Lord.
O Lord, though I am constantly devoted to the recitation of what mantra, that supreme reality remains unknown to me even today; you ought to explain that reality to me.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
That Goddess who is partless, dark-hued, lusterless, and stainless— she,
the Great Śrīṣoḍaśī-vidyā, is called the Queen.
The Great Goddess, the Queen of Vidyās, who bestows the entire kingdom in this world,
is that very Fifteenth Goddess, the consort of the Supreme Brahman.
She has appeared today in Bhārata for the destruction of the poverty of men—
she whose secret fifteen-fold lore was previously unknown.
p. 444) "I recite that Great Vidyā; I remember its five limbs.
The Illustrious Goddess said:
O Blessed One, ocean of compassion, affectionate toward those who have come for refuge:
that goddess who is known as Lokamātā, the queen who bestows sovereignty. (9)
"O Remover of Poverty, if I am dear to you, then tell me today that five-limbed [mantra] in its true essence, enriched by the Vedas and Tantras."
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Listen attentively to this chapter, which is the very embodiment of mantra;
it is my secret, the essence of all things for the Queen, difficult even for the gods to obtain.
O Great Goddess, having heard this extraction of the mantra spoken from my mouth by the Queen, conceal it with effort, so that success may arise.
*Tāra* (Oṃ), *māyā* (Hrīṃ), *mānalaḥ* (Śrīṃ), and *kāmaśaktī* (Klīṃ) are in the middle; then *ākhyā* (Namo Bhagavatyai) and for the Queen (*rājñyai*).
O Goddess, the extraction of the mantra for the Queen, beginning with the *māyābīja* (Hrīṃ) and ending with two *ṭha*s (Svāhā), has been described; it must be kept secret. || 13 ||
For him there is no obstacle, no affliction, and no fear of error anywhere in the auspicious state;
O Goddess, this mantra bestows all accomplishments and increases one's fortune.
First, one should unfasten the mantra, and then one should restore the mantra to life;
O Goddess, once the mantra is perfected, one should then recite it while performing the *sampuṭita* (encapsulation) rite.
Then, O Īśānī, this mantra shall directly bestow accomplishment.
I shall now describe the construction of the yantra, which fulfills all desires. (16)
It bestows all prosperity and likewise accomplishes all aims; it is the wheel that grants all perfections and is composed of all bliss. || 17 ||
One should worship the All-Enchanting Wheel (Sarvasaṃmohana-cakra) during the ritual adoration of the sacred seats (pīṭha).
[The mandala] consists of a point (bindu), a triangle, a hexagon, and is adorned with circles and eight petals. (18)
The three circles and the abode of the Earth are declared to be the Śrīcakra of the Queen;
O Goddess of Gods, hear now its limb of dissolution (layāṅga), extracted from the Vedas and Āgamas.
By the mere hearing of which one obtains the fruit of ten thousand offerings:
Gaṇeśa, Bhīmarāja, Kumāra, and Jāṅgaleśvara. (20)
Indra and the other guardians of the world (Lokapālas) are to be worshipped in the subterranean chamber (bhūgṛha);
O Śivā, the three lineages of gurus are to be honored within the three circles (vṛtta).
O Dear One, the divine hosts of Siddhas and the hosts of mortals are to be worshipped with perfumes and unbroken grains (akṣata);
likewise Vāsuki, Nīla-nāga, Takṣaka, and Padma-nāga.
O Pārvatī, listen as I describe those to be worshipped in the cardinal directions and the intermediate directions:
Kārkoṭaka, Śaṅkhapāla, Kulika, and Śeṣa, O Īśvarī. (23)
Likewise, the Mothers beginning with Brāhmī should be worshipped according to the sequence starting from the southeast;
and the eight Bhairavas, O Pārvatī, should be worshipped in counter-clockwise order.
Brāhmī, Vaiṣṇavī, Rudrāṇī, Aparājitā, Kaumārī, Cāmuṇḍā, Vārāhī, and Nārasiṃhikā. || 25 ||
Asitāṅga, Ruru, Caṇḍa, Krodheśa, Unmatta, Bhīṣaṇa, Kapālīśa, and Saṃhāra are to be worshipped in their proper order. (26)
Śrī Durgā, Śārikādevī, Vaikharī,
Śivā, Śive, Kālikā, and Tripurā are to be worshipped in the six-cornered [mandala] by moving counter-clockwise.
Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, and Bālā are to be worshipped in the triangle;
in the Bindu are Rājñī, who bestows sovereignty, and the fifteen-syllable Vidyā. (28)
O Goddess, one should worship Bhūteśvara Śiva, as well as the sword and the lotus;
likewise, one should worship the water-pot, the vessel of nectar, and Vaṭuka.
O Maheśānī, the Yoginīs, the Kṣetrapālas, the Bhūtas, Vināyaka there, and Rāmeśvara— this is declared to be the limb of dissolution (layāṅga). (30)
The sage of the root mantra of the illustrious Queen is declared to be Brahmā;
the meter is Gāyatrī, and the deity is the Goddess Queen Īśānī. (31)
O Īśvarī, *māyā* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), *śaracchakti* is the power (*śakti*), and *kāma* is the pin (*kīlaka*);
its application (*viniyoga*) is proclaimed for the sake of attaining both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
O Goddess, I shall now describe her sattvic meditation, which brings about the fulfillment of desires, bestows all perfections, and yields the fruit of ten million mantras. (33)

I worship the Queen, whose lotus-face is in full bloom, who possesses the luster of thousands of rising suns, who has three eyes, who sits upon a lion-throne, who wears a serpent as a sacred thread, and who holds in her hands a sword, a lotus, a jar, and a vessel of nectar. 34.

I worship in my heart the Queen who bestows sovereignty—she who has four arms, whose crest is adorned with a digit of the moon, who sits upon a lion-throne, who wears a serpent as a sacred thread, and who holds a noose, a goad, a lotus, and a sword. (35)
Now, O Goddess, I shall explain the eight applications according to their true nature,
by the mere accomplishment of which a mantra becomes like a wish-fulfilling tree.
O Dear One, [the rites of] immobilization, delusion, killing, and attraction, as well as subjugation, expulsion, pacification, and nourishment; || 37 ||
O Maheśvarī, I shall describe the means for accomplishing these applications:
having bathed during the sun's transit, one should recite the root mantra ten thousand times in a cremation ground.
When the mass of hair from Sarpirmālinī is cast into the fire of Huna,
there occurs a paralyzing immobilization of water, the moon, wind, the sun, and the waters.

Likewise, at night, staying in a cremation ground and wearing the garments of a corpse, the wise one should properly recite the mantra ten thousand times and perform the fire sacrifice (homa) with a tenth part of that amount. || 40 ||
With branches of *vānīra* smeared with ghee and cloves, there shall be enchantment (*mohana*).
Having bathed on a Tuesday, one should go to a cremation ground and recite the mantra before a funeral pyre.
O Pārvatī, by offering clarified butter, fish, thorns, and cow dung in the tenth part of the oblation,
even an enemy equal to Death himself shall meet his demise.
O Goddess of the Gods, at midnight in a cremation ground on a Wednesday, one should recite the mantra ten thousand times;
O Beloved, one should offer oblations of clarified butter in a tenth part of that amount, together with the hair of a Caṇḍāla.
"O Goddess, either Rambhā or Tilottamā will appear in the morning; one should recite the mantra at the cremation ground before the Guru with hair disheveled. (44)
One should offer ten thousand oblations, with a tenth part of that consisting of clarified butter mixed with milk-rice, camphor, and sandalwood; by this, even Indra becomes a servant.
In the cremation ground during the bright fortnight, one should recite the mantra ten thousand times;
naked and with disheveled hair, one should offer clarified butter along with a flaming brand into the fire.
By offering oblations of dūrvā grass and sugar, one will cause an enemy to be driven away.
On a Saturday, at the abode of a cremation ground, the wise man should mutter the mantra of Rājñī.

One should offer ten thousand oblations of clarified butter mixed with *śambūka* (a type of snail), along with the ashes of a porcupine and the alkali of *sameṣa* and *plīha*; this shall pacify danger from all sides.
O Daughter of the Mountain, having performed the recitation of the root mantra ten thousand times on a Sunday in a cremation ground— or indeed on every day—
one should offer oblations of pigeon meat, clarified butter, and buffalo meat.
This ritual practice bestows nourishment upon the ancestors and the deities;
such is this chapter of the Queen, containing the secret of all the Agamas. 50.
It must not be given to another disciple, especially not to a wicked person, nor to one devoid of devotion to the guru, nor to one who is poorly clothed or evil-minded. (51)
Even by giving it to sons who are not devoted, one may fall into hell;
O Pārvatī, it should be given to a disciple who is peaceful and devoted to the guru. (52)

To you, who are initiated, of noble birth, and devoted to the Queen, this supreme secret has been declared by me because of your devotion. It is a mystery, the most hidden thing in the world; it must be guarded like one's own womb.
Thus ends the first chapter, the Śrīmahārājñī-paṭala, within the Daśavidyā-rahasya of the Śrīrudrayāmala Tantra.
Now follows the ritual manual for the worship of Śrī Mahārājñī.
The venerable Bhairava said:

Now, O Goddess, I shall describe the manual (paddhati) conjoined with the worship of the Śrīrājñī; it consists of both prose and verse, is to be kept secret, and is established according to all the Āgamas. I shall speak this manual in the form of prose.
[This is] the Śrīrājñī-nityapūjā, which truly bestows happiness. || 1 ||
If one worships the Goddess with devotion without having performed the morning rites,
that worship is indeed fruitless, like a ritual action devoid of purity.

Therein, the illustrious practitioner, having risen from his bed during the *brāhma-muhūrta* and having washed his hands, feet, and so forth, sits upon his own seat in the bound lotus posture (*baddha-padmāsana*).
He then [visualizes] his own guru within the pericarp of a thousand-petaled downward-facing lotus situated at the crown of his head, according to his own capacity.

Having meditated upon [the deity] together with [the retinue], worshipped with mental offerings, prostrated like a staff, and having meditated there upon the Goddess together with Śiva, one should mutter the root mantra as much as possible, offer the recitation to the Guru, receive his permission, and come outside.

Having performed the purification of impurities and so forth, having gone to a river or similar place, and having performed the cleansing prescribed for one's caste, one should clean the teeth with the mantra: *oṃ klīṃ kāmadevāya sarvajanapriyāya namaḥ*, and then perform the bath for the removal of impurities.
Having prepared three earthen vessels and purified them with the root mantra, one should visualize either the Śrīcakra or the Yonicakra within the water.
Therein, having invoked the sacred waters (*tīrthas*) using the *aṅkuśamudrā* with the mantra beginning "O Gaṅgā,
O Yamunā," [one should worship] the Great Fifteenfold Knowledge (*mahāpañcadaśī-vidyā*) which resides there, resembling ten million rising suns and accompanied by Bhūteśvara.

"O Lord, you who are in the water, please come here. Having thus displayed the mudrās for invocation (*āvāhana*) and the others, having smeared clay upon one’s limbs, and having recited the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*), one should immerse oneself three times in the water while forming the *kumbha-mudrā*. Then, having offered three *arghya* oblations with "Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ, this is your *arghya*, O Sūrya, obeisance," and having recited the root mantra as many times as possible, [one should proceed].
Having put on two garments and performed the Vedic *saṃdhyā*, one should perform the Tantric *saṃdhyā*. Therein,

having performed the primary six-limbed ritual (*mūla-ṣaḍaṅga*) and placed water in the left hand, one should consecrate it seven times with the mantras of the five elements— *yaṃ raṃ vaṃ laṃ haṃ*— and cover it with the *tattvamudrā*.
Uttering the root mantra, one should sprinkle the head seven times with the falling drops of water;

then, holding it in the right hand and drawing it into the interior of the body through the *iḍā* [nāḍī], one should wash away the sin. Having expelled that water through the *piṅgalā* [nāḍī] into the left hand, one should cast that turbid water onto a stone situated in the left direction while uttering "phaṭ."
Having thus performed the *aghamarṣaṇa* and having performed three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with the *praṇava* and the *māyā* [seed-syllable], one should sip water (*ācamana*) while reciting:

"Oṃ hrīṃ, I purify the *ātmatattva*, svāhā! Oṃ hrīṃ, I purify the *vidyātattva*, svāhā! Oṃ hrīṃ, I purify the *śivatattva*, svāhā! Then, one should perform the six-limbed assignment (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) with "Oṃ hrīṃ..."

Having performed [the ritual] with these and other [mantras], one should recite the Gāyatrī: *oṃ rājyapradāyai vidmahe hrīṃ pañcadaśākṣaryai dhīmahi śrīṃ tanno mahārājñī pracodayāt* (3 times). Having recited the Gāyatrī and the root-vidyā, [one offers] this arghya to Śrī Mahārājñī and Bhūteśvara by means of the Gāyatrī.

Having offered three *arghya* oblations with "Svāhā," one should again visualize the *yonicakra* in the water; having recited the root mantra seven times, one should offer libations seven times with the formula: "May the venerable Mahārājñī—along with her limbs (*aṅga*), vehicles (*vāhana*), weapons (*āyudha*), retinue (*paricchada*), and accompanied by Bhūteśvara—be satisfied. Then, one should separately offer libations to Bhūteśvara three times.
Having satiated his attendants by offering them the *praṇava* and *māyā* mantras once each,
and having likewise satiated the Guru, Paramaguru, Parameṣṭhiguru, and the ancestors,
he should offer three *arghya* oblations to the Sun as before, then bring the God and Goddess back into his heart and dismiss the sacred water (*tīrtha*).
"One should come to the sacrificial hall"—this is the rule for the twilight ritual (saṃdhyā).

There, having washed his feet and worshipped the deities of the door— Gaṇeśa, Vaṭuka, Kṣetreśa, Yoginī, Gaṅgā, Sarasvatī, Dehalī, and Dvāraśrī— with the mantra *oṃ hrīṃ*, and having entered the interior of the pavilion while touching the two door-posts with his left shoulder, he should perform the purification of the seat (*viṣṭaraśuddhi*) with the mantra *oṃ āṃ*.
The seer (ṛṣi) of the mantra for purifying the seat is Merupṛṣṭha; the meter (chandaḥ) is Sutala; the deity (devatā) is Kūrma;
its application (viniyoga) is in the purification of the seat. *Prīṃ*, obeisance to Earth (*pṛthivī*). By you, O Great One, the worlds are supported. (p. 450)
O Goddess, you are upheld by Viṣṇu; do you likewise uphold me in this world and make my seat pure.
Oṃ Āṃ, obeisance to the Support-Power (Ādhāraśakti). Obeisance to the Tortoise (Kūrma). Obeisance to Ananta.

Obeisance to the eight-petaled lotus. Obeisance to the thousand-petaled lotus. Having sat there, [one should recite]: "May those beings depart who dwell upon the earth; may those beings who create obstacles perish."

"By the command of Śiva. Having thus struck the three *tāla* gestures and dispelled the terrestrial obstacles, he should display the *nārāca-mudrā* and say: "May all the *bhūtas*, *pretas*, *piśācas*, *rākṣasas*, and reptiles depart, tormented by the weapon of the Goddess! Having thus struck the left heel three times, he should prostrate before the Guru.

Salutation to that venerable Guru who, with the collyrium-stick of knowledge, has opened the eyes of one blinded by the darkness of ignorance. Om, salutation to the Gurus. Om, salutation to the Parama-gurus.
Om, salutation to the Parāpara-gurus. Salutation to the Parameṣṭhi-gurus. Having thus performed worship:

For this mantra of the illustrious Mahārājñī: Brahmā is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandaḥ), the illustrious Bhūteśvarī Mahārājñī is the deity (devatā), Hrīṃ is the seed-syllable (bīja), Sauḥ is the power (śakti), Klīṃ is the bolt (kīlaka); the application (viniyoga) is for the attainment of the fourfold aims of human life. Salutation to Brahmā, the seer, upon the head.

Salutation to the *gāyatrī* meter at the mouth; salutation to the goddess Rājñī at the heart; salutation to the seed-syllable *hrīṃ* at the navel; salutation to the power (*śakti*) *sauḥ* at the secret place; salutation to the *kīlaka* *klīṃ* at the feet; salutation to the application (*viniyoga*) in worship at all limbs. *Oṃ hrāṃ* to the two thumbs, salutation.

Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to the two index fingers. Oṃ hrūṃ, salutation to the two middle fingers. Oṃ hraiṃ, salutation to the two ring fingers. Oṃ hrauṃ, salutation to the two little fingers. Oṃ hraḥ, salutation to the palms and backs of the hands. Thus is the ritual placement on the hands (*karanyāsa*). In the same manner is the ritual placement of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*).

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) in this manner, one should perform the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*). With the mantra *oṃ hrīṃ*, one should lead the Kuṇḍalinī—shaped like the flame of a lamp—from the foundational support (*ādhāra*) through the path of the Suṣumṇā into the interior of the Brahma-path, bring her to Paramaśiva, and effect their state of essential identity (*sāmarasya*). Then, with the stream of the nectar of bliss arising from that union, [one should worship] the ancestral gurus (*kulaguru*).

Having satisfied [the deities] and again pierced the six cakras, one should bring [the vital energy] back to its own place; then, having visualized the personification of sin (pāpapuruṣa) in the left side of the abdomen— measuring the size of a thumb, black in color, and with a red beard— one should perform the drying and other rites through the practice of breath control (prāṇāyāma), beginning first with the seed-syllable of air, *yaṃ*, recited sixteen times.

One should dry it. One should burn it with the fire-seed syllable *raṃ*, recited sixteen times. One should flood it with the water-seed syllable *vaṃ*, recited sixteen times. Having contemplated the body as firm by means of the earth-seed syllable *laṃ* recited sixteen times, one [should contemplate] one's own self by means of the space-seed syllable *haṃ* recited sixteen times.
Having generated the divine body, one should perform the consecration of the vital breaths (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*).
*Oṃ hrīṃ āṃ kroṃ sohaṃ haṃsaḥ mama prāṇā iha prāṇāḥ* (8 times). *Mama jīva iha...* (p.

"Remaining [here], Oṃ! May my speech, mind, eyes, ears, tongue, nose, and vital breaths come here and remain happily for a long time, Svāhā! Having thus performed the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā*, one should perform *prāṇāyāma* as before, sip water (*ācamana*) with the three *tattvas*, and perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*). Oṃ namaḥ at the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*), Hrīṃ on the head.

Śrīṃ on the two eyes; rāṃ on the two ears; klīṃ at the tip of the nose; sauḥ on the mouth; bhaṃ on the throat; gaṃ on the two arms; vaṃ on the chest; tyaiṃ on the belly; rāṃ on the navel; jñyai on the genitals; hrīṃ on the knees; svāṃ on the two shanks; hāṃ namaḥ on all the limbs. Thus is the placement of the root mantra (mūlamantranyāsa).

Oṃ hrāṃ śrāṃ, salutation to the heart. Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, svāhā to the head. Oṃ hrūṃ śrūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock. Oṃ hraiṃ śraiṃ, huṃ to the armor. Oṃ hrauṃ śrauṃ, vauṣaṭ to the two eyes. Oṃ hraḥ śraḥ, phaṭ to the weapon. Oṃ rāṃ, salutation to the heart; [assign] to the two thumbs.

*Namaḥ*. *Oṃ rīṃ*, salutation to the head (*śiras*) with the two index fingers (*tarjanī*). *Oṃ rūṃ*, salutation to the crest-lock (*śikhā*) with the two middle fingers (*madhyamā*). *Oṃ reiṃ*, salutation to the armor (*kavaca*) with the two ring fingers (*anāmikā*). *Oṃ rauṃ*, salutation to the two eyes (*netra*) with the two little fingers (*kaniṣṭhikā*). *Oṃ raḥ*, *astrāya phaṭ*, salutation to the weapon (*astra*) with the palms and backs of the hands (*karatalapṛṣṭha*).
Salutation! Oṃ sauḥ klāṃ to both thumbs; oṃ sauḥ klīṃ to both index fingers;
oṃ sauḥ klūṃ to both middle fingers; oṃ sauḥ klaiṃ to both ring fingers; oṃ sauḥ klauṃ to both little fingers; oṃ sauḥ klaḥ to both palms and backs of the hands. Thus.
The ritual placement of the six limbs, beginning with the heart.

Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Jālandhara-pīṭha at the mūlādhāra. Oṃ śrīṃ, salutation to Uḍḍīyāna-pīṭha at the svādhiṣṭhāna. Oṃ rāṃ, salutation to Kāmarūpa-pīṭha at the anāhata. Oṃ klīṃ, salutation to Madhupurī-pīṭha at the maṇipūra. Oṃ sauḥ, salutation to Vārāṇasī-pīṭha at the viśuddhi. Oṃ hrīṃ...
*Anantapīṭhāya namaḥ* at the *ājñā* [cakra]; *oṃ svāhā śāradāpīṭhāya namaḥ* at the *brahmarandhra*. Thus is the *pīṭhanyāsa*.

Oṃ aṃ kaṃ 5 āṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ | Oṃ hrīṃ iṃ caṃ 5 īṃ śirase svāhā | Oṃ śrīṃ uṃ ṭaṃ 5 ūṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ | Oṃ rāṃ eṃ taṃ 5 aiṃ kavacāya huṃ | Oṃ klīṃ oṃ paṃ 5 auṃ netratrayāya vauṣaṭ | Oṃ sauḥ aṃ yaṃ 10 aḥ astrāya phaṭ | Thus.
The ritual placement on the hands (kara-nyāsa). Thus concludes the ritual placement of the pure alphabet (śuddha-mātṛkā-nyāsa).

Then, having performed the *mātṛkā-nyāsa*, [one should recite]: *oṃ ātmatattvāya hṛdayāya namaḥ*; *hrīṃ vidyātattvāya śirase svāhā*; *śrīṃ śivatattvāya śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*; *rāṃ śaktitattvāya kavacāya huṃ*; *klīṃ śivatattvāya netrebhyo vauṣaṭ*; *sauḥ sarvatattvāya astrāya phaṭ*. Thus.

This is the *karanyāsa*, which is the *tattvanyāsa*. Having performed the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) as before with "Oṃ hrāṃ," one should contemplate one's own self in the form of the *kāmakalā*. Then, having contemplated the venerable Mahārājñī seated upon the lap of Śrī Bhūteśvara within the pericarp of the heart-lotus, [one should worship her] with mental offerings (*mānasopacāra*).

Having worshipped the Śrīcakra outside, which shines with a central point (*bindu*), is resplendent with triangles, adorned with hexagons, embellished with eight petals, and illuminated by three circles.

Having either drawn or installed [the mandala] adorned with four gates, one should prepare the yoga-seat (yogapīṭha) and perform the worship of the yoga-seat: *Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Maṇḍūka*. 2. *To Kālāgnirudra*. 2.
*Obeisance to Mūlaprakṛti*. 2. *To Ādhāraśakti*. 2. *To Varāha*. 2. *To Kūrma*. 2.
To Ananta, 2; to Pṛthivī, 2; to Sudhāmbudhi, 2; in the center, to Suvarṇadvīpa, 2;
to Kalpavana, 2; in the center, to Maṇigeḥa, to Ratnavedikā, in its center, to Cintāmaṇimaṇḍapa, there, to Śmaśāna, 2.

To [the lotus] from *dharma*, *jñāna*, *vairāgya*, and *aiśvarya*—[prostration]. To its left: to [the lotus] from *adharma*, *ajñāna*, *avairāgya*, and *anaiśvarya*—[prostration]. Above that: *raṃ* salutation to the fire-maṇḍala. *aṃ* salutation to the sun-maṇḍala. *soṃ* salutation to the moon-maṇḍala. *taṃ* salutation to darkness (*tamas*). *raṃ*.
To Rajas, svāhā. To Sattva, svāhā. To the root, the thousand-petaled lotus, svāhā.

To the stalk of consciousness, svāhā. To the petals consisting of Prakṛti, svāhā. To the filaments consisting of Vikṛti, svāhā. To the pericarp adorned with the fifty seed-syllables, svāhā. Having uttered the root-mantra and the Mātṛkā, [offer] to the Śrī Yogapīṭha.

Saying "Namaḥ," having worshipped with unbroken rice grains and flowers, and having either placed or visualized the Śrīcakra upon the Śrīyogapīṭha, one should perform the worship of the vessels between oneself and the Śrīcakra. Therein, having drawn a mandala consisting of a circle, a hexagon, and a square on one's left, and having performed the six-limbed worship with the root mantra, [End of segment]
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, salutation to the general arghya-maṇḍala of the Blessed Mahārājñī;

having worshipped thus with unbroken rice grains (akṣata), and having worshipped with akṣata saying, "Raṃ, salutation to the fire-maṇḍala consisting of ten kalās," one should place the support (ādhāra) there, [saying] "Aṃ, to the sun-maṇḍala."

Having worshipped with "Obeisance to the one whose self consists of twelve kalās," and having filled the conch with the reverse-order Mātṛkā, he worships therein with "Oṃ: Obeisance to the lunar maṇḍala, whose self consists of sixteen kalās.
Then, from the solar maṇḍala, he invokes the sacred waters (tīrthas) using the goad mudrā and the mantra beginning with "O Gaṅgā and Yamunā... and so forth.
"One should meditate on the pure"—this is the general procedure for the arghya offering.
To the left of the general *arghya*, having prepared a mandala consisting of a triangle, hexagon, circle, and square,

and having worshipped it with the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), one should recite the root mantra and say, "Salutation to the mandala of the vessel of the venerable Queen (*śrīrājñī*)," and having placed the support (*ādhāra*) there, worship it with: "Oṃ raṃ, salutation to the fire-mandala (*vahnimaṇḍala*) consisting of ten digits (*kalā*)."

There, having placed a flask washed with [the Weapon-mantra] (astra), and having worshipped it with "Oṃ, obeisance to the solar orb consisting of twelve digits" (arkamaṇḍalāya dvādaśakalātmane namaḥ), one should fill the flask there by pouring a stream of nectar using the ring finger and the thumb,
while reciting "Oṃ Soṃ, obeisance to the lunar orb consisting of sixteen digits" (soṃḥ somamaṇḍalāya ṣoḍaśakalātmane namaḥ).

Having worshipped with flowers and unbroken rice grains, [recite]: *oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ rāṃ rīṃ rūṃ raiṃ rauṃ raḥ amṛte amṛtodbhave amṛtavarṣiṇi amṛtaṃ srāvaya 2 śukraśāpaṃ mocaya 2 oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ surādevyai vauṣaṭ*.

Having thus consecrated it three times with the root mantra ten times, one should recite the Ānandabhairava-gāyatrī three times as follows: "We know Ānandeśvara; we meditate upon Surādevī; may Ardhanārīśvara inspire us. (3) Having thus recited the Ānandabhairava-gāyatrī three times...

Having worshipped with the mantra: *hasakṣamalavaraya-ūṃ ānandabhairavāya vauṣaṭ sahakṣamalavaraya-ūṃ ānandabhairavī-surādevī-pādukābhyo namaḥ*, [one should continue]: *oṃ hrīṃ sūryamaṇḍalasaṃbhūte varuṇālayasaṃbhave amābījamaye devi*.

May [she] be released from the curse of Śukra. *Oṃ hrīṃ*. If the *praṇava* is the seed-syllable of the Vedas, consisting of the bliss of Brahman, by that truth, O Goddess of Gods, may the sin of killing a Brahmin (*brahmahatyā*) be destroyed. *Oṃ hrīṃ*. The Supreme Brahman alone is eternal, consisting of both the gross and the subtle; by that [truth], may the sin of killing a Brahmin arising from the hair of your head [be destroyed].
I destroy [it]. Oṃ Hrīṃ! You are the purifying one, supreme bliss; you are the purifying one, supreme essence; you are the purifying one, supreme knowledge. By that, I purify you. Oṃ Hrīṃ!
You are liberated from the curse of Kṛṣṇa, liberated from the curse of Brahmā, and liberated from the curse of Rudra.

"Become pure now! Having thus worshipped and recited the root mantra three times, one should display the Dhenu, Yoni, and Matsya mudrās over the substances; then, saying "The jar is full," and meditating upon it as consisting of nectar, one should cover it with the Tattva-mudrā—this is the purification of the substances.

Oṃ Hrīṃ! Having descended as an incarnation by Hari, for the sake of the welfare of the Kaulikas and because the world was oppressed by Kali and subdued by Bali, the Lord himself became a Fish (Mīna) in order to please Bhavānī.
Reciting the *mūlamantra* three times over the fish, and displaying the three mudrās, one should say: "Oṃ hrīṃ!

Salutations indeed to the one who has assumed forms made from goats and other animals up to cows. For the sake of the offering (*bali*) for the God and Goddess, become pure now. Thus: "Oṃ hrīṃ! At the time of worshiping the Yantra of the Queen, whatever [implements] are here for the sake of success..."

Now, these sacred objects pertaining to the descendants of Surabhi are present here. Reciting the root mantra three times and displaying the three mudrās, one should place the vessels for *pādya*, *arghya*, *madhuparka*, and *ācamanīya* to the north of the *kalaśa*.
Having also placed the vessels for the Guru, Śakti, Vaṭuka, and the Sādhaka, one should worship them as in the case of the *sāmānyārghya*.
"One should worship the Śrīcakra" refers to the placement of the vessels.

There, having brought forth the venerable Queen seated on the lap of Bhūteśvara from the heart-lotus by way of the *suṣumṇā* channel, and having established her upon the seat of the *bindu* of the *Śrīcakra*, one should display there the mudrās of invocation (*āvāhana*) and so forth,
and then display the mudrās of the sword, the lotus, the vase, and the vessel of nectar, while reciting the root mantra.

Having bestowed the vital breaths with the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* mantra, [recite] the root mantra (*mūla*): "I offer water for the feet, the respectful offering (*arghya*), water for sipping (*ācamanīya*), and so forth, to Śrī Bhūteśvara and Bhūteśvarī; obeisance. [Recite] the root mantra: "I offer honey-mixture (*madhuparka*), water for sipping, fragrance, unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), flowers, and so forth, to Bhūteśvara and Bhūteśvarī; obeisance. [Recite] the root mantra.

Having offered the food offering (naivedya), water for sipping (ācamanīya), betel leaves (tāmbūla), and so forth, having performed the six-limbed ritual (ṣaḍaṅga) with the root mantra, having received the command of Bhairava, having praised the God and Goddess, having meditated upon the goddesses of the retinue, and having prostrated like a staff, one should worship the square enclosure (caturaśra).
Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the wheel that fulfills all desires. Having thus offered a handful of flowers, [one recites]:
Oṃ hrīṃ gāṃ, I worship the sandals of the illustrious Gaṇeśvara; obeisance, I offer libations; obeisance. (Twice).

I worship the venerable sandals of Bhairavarāja; salutations, I satiate you, salutations! 2. Hrauṃ, I worship the venerable sandals of Kumāra. 2. Juṃ, I worship the venerable sandals of Jāṅgaleśvara. In that very place, in the cardinal and intermediate directions: 2. Indraśrī. 2. Agniśrī. 2. Dharmarājaśrī. 2. Nirṛtiśrī.
2. Varuṇaśrī; 2. Vāyuśrī; 2. Kuberaśrī; 2. Īśānaśrī.
Above: 2. Brahmaśrī. Below: 2. Anantaśrī. Thus one should worship with perfumes and unbroken rice (akṣata) in counter-clockwise order (vāmāvarta).
Again, in that very place: 2. Vajraśrī; 2. Śaktiśrī; 2. Daṇḍaśrī; 2. Khaḍgaśrī; 2. [Pāśaśrī].
Pāśaśrī (2), Dhvajaśrī (2), Gadāśrī (2), Triśūla (2), Padmaśrī (2), Cakraśrī (2). Thus one should worship with flowers and unbroken rice grains; this is the first enclosure.

Then, in the three verses, having offered a handful of flowers with the mantra *oṃ hrīṃ sarvasaṃpatpradacakrāya namaḥ*, one should worship with scents and unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*) using the following: *oṃ hrīṃ guru-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ* (twice), *paramaguru-śrīpādukāṃ* (twice), *parāparaguru-śrīpādukāṃ* (twice), and *parameṣṭhiguru-śrīpādukāṃ*. This constitutes the second enclosure (*dvitīyāvaraṇa*).

Then, having offered a handful of flowers with the mantra "Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the wheel that accomplishes all aims (Sarvārthasādhakacakra)," [one should worship] in the directions starting from the east: "Oṃ hrīṃ, [obeisance to] the sandals of Vāsuki-Śrī; 2; [obeisance to] Nīlanāga-Śrī; 2; [obeisance to] Takṣaka-Śrī; 2; [obeisance to] Padmanāga-Śrī; 2; [obeisance to] Kārkoṭaka-Śrī; 2; [obeisance to] Śaṅkhapāla-Śrī; 2."
Kulikaśrī0 | 2 | Śeṣanāgaśrī0 | Thus one should worship in the intermediate directions with scents and unbroken grains (akṣata). In that very place:

Oṃ hrīṃ, to Brāhmīśrī accompanied by Asitāṅgabhairava | 2 | To Vaiṣṇavīśrī accompanied by Rurubhairava | 2 | To Rudrāṇīśrī accompanied by Caṇḍabhairava | 2 | To Aparājitāśrī accompanied by Krodhabhairava | 2 |
Śrī Kaumārī accompanied by Unmattabhairava; Śrī Cāmuṇḍā accompanied by Bhīṣaṇabhairava; Śrī Vārāhī accompanied by Kapālibhairava; Śrī Nārasiṃhikā accompanied by Saṃhārabhairava.
Thus, one should worship on the eight-petaled lotus in counter-clockwise order with perfumes, unbroken rice, and flowers; this is the third enclosure.

Then, in the hexagon: having offered a handful of flowers with "Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the Śrīcakra that bestows all siddhis," one should worship with scents and unbroken rice (*akṣata*) by circling counter-clockwise (*vāmāvartena*), reciting: "Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Durgāśrī" (twice); "obeisance to Śārikāśrī" (twice); "obeisance to Vaikharīśrī" (twice); "obeisance to Śivāśrī" (twice); "obeisance to Kālikāśrī" (twice); "obeisance to Tripurāśrī. Thus one should worship.
The fourth veil.

455) Then, in the triangle, at the points of Īśāna and Agni: having offered a handful of flowers with "Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the wheel that completely deludes all (sarvasaṃmohanacakra)," [one recites] "Oṃ hrīṃ, Lakṣmī-Śrī," "Sarasvatī-Śrī," and "Bālā-Śrī."
One should worship with perfumes, flowers, and unbroken grains (akṣata); this is the fifth enclosure.

Then, at the *bindu*: having offered a handful of flowers with "Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the wheel consisting of all bliss (*sarvānandamaya-cakra*"), and having recited the root mantra (*mūlavidyā*) seven times, [one should worship] with: "Oṃ hrīṃ, the venerable sandals (*śrīpādukā*) of Bhūteśvara and Bhūteśvarī;
the root mantra, the venerable Mahārājñī; twice; the venerable Bestower of Royal Power (*rājyapradā*); twice; the venerable Fifteen-Syllabled One (*pañcadaśākṣarī*); twice."
Bhūteśvaraśrī [2], Khaḍgaśrī [2], Padmaśrī [2], Kalaśaśrī [2], Sudhāpātraśrī [2]. Thus one should worship with perfumes, flowers, and unbroken rice; this is the sixth enclosure.

In the Bhairava-cakra, the root [mantra] is offered to Bhūteśvara and Bhūteśvarī with perfumes, unbroken grains, flowers, incense, lamps, water for sipping, food offerings, betel, an umbrella, and chowries—
*oṃ hrīṃ devīputra vaṭukanātha kapilajaṭābhārabhāsvara trinetra jvālāmukha imaṃ*.
"Accept the bali offering, accept it twice; grant me my desired accomplishment, grant it twice"—thus on the south.
"Oṃ yāṃ yī yūṃ, obeisance to the hosts of Yoginīs, svāhā"—thus on the north. "Oṃ hrīṃ kṣāṃ kṣīṃ oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, vauṣaṭ to the Kṣetrapāla Rāmeśvara"—thus on the west.
Having offered the bali with "Oṃ gāṃ glāṃ, obeisance to Gaṇapati" in the east, and having cast the bali with "Oṃ sauḥ, svāhā to all beings who create obstacles" in the direction of Nirṛti,
one should establish [the deity] there, perform the mantra-consecration as before, perform the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) with the root mantra, and meditate upon the Goddess.
Having worshipped the rosary and held it in the right hand, one should recite the root-mantra (*mūlavidyā*) according to one's capacity. Then,

having offered the recitation to the Goddess with the mantra beginning "O you, the protector of the most secret of secrets," and having taken the fruit of the recitation in the form of radiant light, one should perform the recitation of the armor (*kavaca*), the thousand names (*sahasranāma*), and the hymn (*stava*) before the God and the Goddess.

"Having offered even that, O Mother of the World, whatever I do from morning until evening and from evening until morning— let that be your worship. Having thus offered a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*) and prostrated with the *yonimudrā*,
one should bring the God and Goddess [back] by means of the *saṃhāramudrā* using a flower to the tip of the nose, [and then] into the pericarp of the heart-lotus.
Having brought [the deity] forth, one should contemplate, "I am he who has the form of the Goddess," and sport happily with one's own Śakti.

Having performed the offering of the vessel (pātrārpaṇa) and having assumed the physical form of the Queen (Rājñī), one should meditate upon oneself as being composed of bliss; such is the procedure for the daily worship (nityapūjā-vidhi).
Thus, this manual for the daily worship,
composed in prose and embodying the very essence of the Queen [of Tantras], must not be given by those who speak the truth.
The secret manual of the Illustrious Queen, marked by the sequence of daily worship,
is rich with the most secret of secrets; it must be concealed from those seeking liberation.
Thus ends the manual for the daily worship of Śrī Mahārājñī, within the *Daśavidyārahasya* of the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*.
2. Now follows the *Kavaca* (armour) of Śrī Mahārājñī.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the supreme armor (kavaca) of the Queen,
named *Trailokyavijaya*, which is divine and bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
Consisting of the root mantra, it is primary, bestowing the eight supernatural powers (siddhis), granting all sovereignty in the world, and is determined by all the scriptures. || 2 ||
O Goddess, through its recitation and retention, this root-vidyā—which is captivating—is the destroyer of great sins and the pacifier of major portents. (3)
O Goddess, Śiva is Virūpākṣa, the powerful Viṣṇu is Nārāyaṇa,
Brahmā is Pitāmaha in the world, and Jiṣṇu is the leader of the hosts of Gīrvāṇas.
Likewise, he is the great ocean, the sun, the moon which is the lord of the stars,
the ocean that is a mine of jewels, and Śeṣa who has attained infinity.
O Goddess of gods, by the constant recitation and wearing of this armor of Śrīrājñī— what is the use of saying more?— from the wearing of this armor [all blessings are attained].
Even a mortal attains immortality and may obtain the status of a queen;
O Great Goddess, Brahmā is declared to be its seer (ṛṣi), and the meter (chandas) is said to be Samīrita.
Gāyatrī is the queen deity, Māyā is declared to be the seed-syllable (bīja),
Śara is the power (śakti), and Kāmarāja is the pin (kīlaka), O Sovereign of the Gods.
The application (viniyoga) is traditionally taught for the sake of attaining worldly enjoyment (bhoga) and liberation (apavarga).
Of this *Śrīmahārājñītrailokyavijaya-kavaca*, the Seer (ṛṣi) is the venerable Brahmā, the Metre (chandaḥ) is Gāyatrī,
the Deity (devatā) is the venerable Mahārājñī, the Seed-syllable (bīja) is Hrīṃ, the Power (śakti) is Sauḥ, and the Pin (kīlaka) is Klīṃ.

The application (*viniyoga*) is for the sake of attaining worldly enjoyment (*bhoga*) and liberation (*apavarga*). *Namaḥ* to the Brahman-sage (*brahmarṣi*), on the head. *Namaḥ* to the Gāyatrī metre (*chandas*), on the face.

*Namaḥ* to the deity Mahārājñī, on the heart. *Namaḥ* to the seed-syllable *hrīṃ*, on the navel. *Namaḥ* to the power (*śakti*) *sauḥ*, on the private parts. *Namaḥ* to the pin (*kīlaka*) *klīṃ*, on the feet. *Namaḥ* to the application (*viniyoga*).
Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) on the hands and limbs with the *māyābīja* (Hrīṃ) joined with the six long vowels beginning with *oṃ hrāṃ*, one should meditate [on her] as follows:
possessing the brilliance of a thousand rising suns, three-eyed, seated upon a lion throne, and wearing a serpent as a sacred thread.
I worship the Queen, whose lotus-face is in full bloom, and who holds in her hands a sword, a lotus, a jar, and a vessel of nectar. || 1 ||

I worship in my heart the Queen who bestows sovereignty— she who has four arms, is crowned with the crescent moon, sits upon a lion-throne, wears a serpent as her sacred thread, and holds a noose, a goad, a lotus, and a sword.
Oṃ, may Lakṣmī protect my head; Hrīṃ, may Sarasvatī protect my forehead;
Śrīṃ, may Bālā protect my eyes; and may the Triangle protect my ears. || 9 ||
RĀṂ—may Durgā protect my nose; KLĪṂ—may Śārikā protect my face;
SAUḤ—may Vaikharī protect my throat; BHAṂ—may Śivā protect my arms.
May Kālī protect my two hands; may Tripurā protect my chest;
may she protect my hexagonal center; and may she protect my two sides.
May Tyaiṃ protect my back; may Brāhmī, Rāṃ, protect my navel;
may Jñyaiṃ protect my anus; and may Rudrāṇī, Hrīṃ, protect my hips as Aparājitā. (12)
May Svāṃ protect the knees as Kaumārī; may Hāṃ protect the shanks as Caṇḍikā;
may Svāhā protect the ankles as Vārāhī; and may Oṃ protect the feet as Nārasiṃhikā. || 13 ||
May the Supreme Queen, who consists of the root-vidyā, protect all those places that have been forgotten and those places devoid of names. (14)
May Vāsuki protect [me] in the east; may the blue serpent (Nīlanāga) grant protection in the southeast;
may Takṣaka protect in the south; and may Padmanāga protect in the southwest. || 15 ||
May Kārkoṭaka protect in the west, and Śaṅkhapāla in the northwest;
may Kulika protect in the north, and Śeṣa in the northeast quadrant.
May Brāhmī protect me during the hour of Brahmā (brāhmamuhūrta), and may Vaiṣṇavī protect me at the beginning of the day;
may Rudrāṇī protect me at midday, and may Aparājitā protect me in the evening. || 17 ||
May Kaumārī protect at the beginning of the night; may Caṇḍikā protect at midnight;
may Vārāhī protect at the end of the night; and may Nārasiṃhikā protect always. (18)
May Asitāṅga protect me from the earth; may Rurubhairava protect me from water;
may Caṇḍa protect me from wind; and may Krodheśa protect me from fire. (19)
May Unmatta protect from Soma, may Bhīṣaṇa protect from Sūrya;
may Kapālīśa protect from the sacrificer, and may Saṃhāraka protect from the ether.
May my eight-petaled body protect me always on all sides;
may the gurus protect me everywhere, and may the lords of the directions protect me from all quarters. (21)
May the three circles protect me eternally; may the abode of the earth protect me always; may the Śrīcakra protect me from fears, and may the Yoginīs protect me at all times.
May the Lord Śiva, Rāmeśvara, always protect [us] above and below;
may the Lord of Beings, whose form is truth, protect us everywhere and at all times. 23.
May my body, from the feet up to the head, be protected everywhere;
from the head down to the feet, may the fifteen-syllable Queen protect me. (24)
Thus, this armor, containing mantras, brings victory;
named "Conquest of the Three Worlds," it destroys poverty and fear. (25)
It directly removes all diseases, bestows spiritual accomplishments, and destroys sins;
O Goddess, it is the supreme remover of great fears, consisting of the root-vidyā. (26)

O Goddess, he who recites this armor-mantra— which eternally bestows the ultimate truth and is the sole cause of both worldly enjoyment and liberation— will, in an instant, overcome battle or the fear of kings.
Having conquered his enemies in battles, the victor shall return home;
by the recitation of this armor, the king's wrath is pacified.
In gambling, the gambler shall obtain wealth; in the cremation ground, he shall attain siddhi.
