O Maheśvarī, he who recites this three times at night upon the emission of semen [shall achieve these results]. (29)
His queen shall become a Great Vidyā who grants all desires in dreams, through pure *svayambhū* flowers marked with both semen and blood. (30)
O Maheśvarī, one should write the armor-mantra on birch bark with juices at sunrise;
it should be wrapped in Chinese silk threads and likewise encased in lac.
One should worship that which resides within the golden pill as if it were the king of yantras;
this pill is a great vidyā, a queen, like another embodiment of the Goddess herself. (32)
O Goddess, you consist of the root-vidyā and bestow all desired fruits;
stationed at the head, O Goddess, you are the giver of wealth; stationed at the throat, you are the bestower of speech. (33)
O Goddess, when situated on the chest she bestows sons; when situated on the waist she grants enjoyments;
when situated on the back she constantly bestows strength; and when situated on the belly she destroys diseases. || 34 ||
This auspicious pill, which accomplishes all aims in the world and bestows fruits according to one's desire, must not be given by the Queen to just anyone. (35)
O Īśānī, this armor is eternal and consists of the root-vidyā;
it bestows eloquence and increases wealth, sons, and grandsons. (36)
It bestows long life, nourishment, prosperity, and fame;
it has been described by extracting the essence of the sixty-four and other tantras. (37)
O Great Goddess, that practitioner who recites this at night in a cremation ground shall become the son of a queen, a lord of the Mahācīna-krama. || 38 ||
Thus, this is my everything, the armor named Trailokyavijaya, containing mantras within; it must be guarded like one's own private parts. (39)
Thus ends the third [chapter], the armor named Trailokyavijaya, belonging to the illustrious Mahārājñī, within the *Śrīrudrayāmala Tantra*, in the secret doctrine of the ten Vidyās.
Then, regarding the *Mahārājñīsahasranāma*,
the illustrious Bhairava said:
O Blessed One, knower of the truth of the Vedas, expert in mantra and tantra, refuge for all, Lord of all worlds, you who are compassionate toward those who have come for shelter! || 1 ||
O Lord Bhairava, you should tell me how one who suffers the misery of poverty may attain prosperity in this world through the power of mantras.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
That Goddess who is partless, the sovereign queen, the Blessed Mistress of the Immaculate.
She creates and sustains the manifest world, and as the quality of darkness (tāmasī), she shall withdraw it.
O Pārvatī, out of affection I shall declare to you its thousand names,
which are unspeakable and rare in this world, and which destroy suffering and poverty.
It eternally bestows the ultimate truth, is the cause of supreme sovereignty, is rich with the secrets of all scriptures, and illuminates every object of knowledge. || 5 ||
This divine Thousand Names of the Queen pacifies all sorrow, destroys great sins, and consists of all mantras.

For this *Śrīmahārājñīnāmasahasra*, Brahmā is the seer (*ṛṣi*), the Gāyatrī is the meter (*chanda*), the goddess Śrībhūteśvarī Mahārājñī is the deity (*devatā*), *hrīṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), *sauḥ* is the power (*śakti*), *klīṃ* is the pin (*kīlaka*),
and its application (*viniyoga*) is in the recitation of the Thousand Names of the Great Queen. *Namaḥ* to Brahmā the Seer on the head.

Salutation to the Gāyatrī metre at the mouth; salutation to the deity Śrī Bhūteśvarī Mahārājñī at the heart; salutation to the seed-syllable *hrīṃ* at the navel; salutation to the power (*śakti*) *sauḥ* at the secret place; salutation to the pin (*kīlaka*) *klīṃ* at the feet; salutation to the ritual application (*viniyoga*) at all limbs. Having performed the assignment of the six limbs of the hands with *oṃ hrām* and so forth.
One should perform meditation:

I bow to her whose form is adorned by twelve suns, who sits alone upon a lion-throne, who is surrounded by serpents, who is the Goddess beyond the reach of the senses, who has attained supreme lordship, and who possesses the body of Bharga.
To the Queen of Ultimate Reality. || 1 ||

I worship in my heart the Queen who bestows sovereignty— she who has four arms, is crowned with the crescent moon, sits upon a lion-throne, wears a serpent as a sacred thread, and holds a noose, a goad, a lotus, and a sword.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ rāṃ mahārājñī klīṃ sauḥ is the fifteen-syllable mantra;
hrīṃ svāhā is the three-syllable vidyā, the supreme Goddess Vibhā. (1)
Radiant, auspicious, formidable, possessing the form of Bharga, and full of splendor;
worthy of honor, wise, born of the mind, and swift as thought. || 2 ||

She is the giver of honor, the science of mantra, the Great Knowledge (Mahāvidyā), and the six-syllabled one; she is the six-peaked, the three-peaked, the triple Veda, and the auspicious Śivā. (Note: In this context, it should be understood that wherever a name is marked with a line, it is the same single name throughout.)
She is auspicious in form, Virūpākṣī, adorned with a crescent moon;
she is Mahālakṣmī, broad-chested, possessed of great luster, and of great prosperity.
Mātaṅgī, who feeds on sweetmeats, whose eyes are reddened by wine,
is virtuous, possessed of good character, a beautiful hall, and a bearer of the nectar-jar.
She who possesses a sword, she who is like a lotus-pond, she who is the lotus itself, she who is colored by the filaments of the lotus;
she who dwells in the heart-lotus, she who is dear to the heart, she who holds a drinking vessel, and she who is the Earth.
The daughter of the lord of mountains, Dakṣiṇā, the daughter of Dakṣa,
Compassion, the Merciful One, Great Intelligence, the Joyful One, the Awakener, and the Mace.
Worshipped by Gadādhara, she is Godhā, Gaṅgā, Godāvarī, and Gayā;
she is endowed with great power and adorned by the great serpents.

She who provides hospitality for the Great Sage; she who is sweet as honey; she who possesses human-like pride; she who is Maghā; she who is a young girl; she who is Sarasvatī; she who is Lakṣmī; she who is Durgā; and she who destroys misfortune. || 9 ||
Śārī resides within the body; Vaikharī is the sovereign of the sky-farers (khecarīs);
Śivadā dwells upon the chest of Śiva; and Kālikā is the city of Tripura.
She who dwells within the belly of the Enemy of Tripura, the Mistress of the heart of Murāri,
the fierce Caṇḍī who bestows the kingdom upon the enemy of Bala, Cāmuṇḍā, the bearer of severed heads.
Adorned with a garland of severed heads, the Mudrā is capable of both agitating and attracting;
she is the goddess Brāhmī, Nārāyaṇī, Kaumārī, and Aparājitā. (12)
Rudrāṇī, Śacī, Indrāṇī, Vārāhī, Vīrasundarī, Nārasiṃhī, and Bhairaveśī, who is terrifying with her fearsome form. (13)
The sovereign of the gods is enriched by the splendor of serpent-ornaments, wears a sacred thread of serpents, possesses serpent-bracelets and armlets, and has a necklace of serpents. (100) 14.
Surārighātinī, Pūtā, Pūtanā, Ḍākinīkriyā, Kriyāvatī, Kurī, Kṛtyā, Ḍākinī, Lākinī, and Layā. (15)
Līlāvatī is overflowing with aesthetic flavor, enchanting like a daughter of the Nāgas;
she is enriched by the splendor of necklaces and bracelets, eternally blissful, and the bringer of auspiciousness. (16)
She is the one who causes laughter, the honeyed one, the lake, the enchantress of Smara;
she possesses a most formidable form, she is the news, she is fond of the left-hand path, and she is the vital channel.
The beautiful heroine, the slayer of enemies, holds a bamboo flute made of nectar;
she stands in the midst of the waters, lovely, with beautiful eyes and the luster of the moon.
Bestower of refuge, the benefactress Śaṅkarī, Sītā, whose eyes are the sun, moon, and fire;
she is Madirā, Vāruṇī, the knower of lute-playing and song, and Madirāvatī.

The power Vāruṇī resides in the banyan tree; she is born of the banyan, dwells in the banyan, is the daughter of the banyan, the mother of heroes, worthy of worship, the paralyzer, the deluder, and the joy (or army). 20.
Kuṭī holds a mallet and a goad in her hands and displays the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness;
Pāṭīradrumavallī, Vaṭikā, and Vaṭukeśvarī likewise [bear these emblems]. (21)
She is the bestower of desires, the soil for cultivation, the wearer of a crown, the beloved of the Lover of Revatī;
she is Rohiṇī, Revatī, the delightful one, the source of delight, and the one who causes the hair to stand on end.
She is the delight of aesthetic flavor, the essence of flavors, the flowing river, the savior, and the lightning;
she holds a boat and oars in her hands, she is the goddess Totilā, and she possesses the splendor of the sun.
Ratnākarapriyā, Rambhā, adorned with jewel ornaments, wearing golden armlets, holding a mace in her hand, she is the bestower of boons upon the wielder of the mace (Viṣṇu). || 24 ||
She possesses six flavors and two flavors; she is a garland adorned with garland-ornaments;
she has the fragrance of jasmine and *mallikā*; she is fond of sweetmeat as food. (25)
Vallabhī, Mathurā, Māyā, Kāśī, Kāñcī, Lalantikā, Hasantikā, Hasantī, Bhramantī, and Vasantikā. || 26 ||

Kṣemā, Kṣemaṅkarī, Kṣāmā, she who wears linen garments (Kṣaumavastrā), the Mistress of the Moment (Kṣaṇeśvarī), the Giver of the Moment (Kṣaṇadā), the Giver of Security (Kṣemadā), Sīrā, and she who is worshipped by the wielder of the plow (Sīrapāṇi). || 27 ||
She who is purchased, she whose heat is purchased, the cruel one, the desirable one, the sovereign of the lineage;
she whose seed-syllable is *kūrca*, she who is rich in the axe, the tortoise-like one, and the beautiful tortoise. || 28 ||
Kāruṇyā, Kāśmīrī, Dūtī, Dhruvā of Dvāravatī, Dhruvastutā, Dhruvagati, Pīṭheśī, and Bagalāmukhī. (29)
Sumukhī, Śobhanānīti, Ratnajvālāmukhī, Nati, Alakojjayinī, Bhogyā, Bhaṅgī, Bhogāvatī, and Balā. (30)
Dharmarājapurī is pure; Pūrṇasattvā is Amarāvatī;
Ayodhyā is Yodhanīyā; and Yugamātā is Yakṣiṇī. || 31 ||
The mistress of sacrifice, attainable through yoga, the object of meditation for yogis, the illustrious one;
she who possesses fame, the one with beautiful limbs, the sweet-smiling one, and the immovable one.
Harīśvarī, the illusory power (māyā) of Hari, the enchantress, she who possesses the speed of the wind;
Ambālikā, the Mother, Bhargeśī, Bhṛgukūṭā, and Mahāmati. || 33 ||
She is the mistress of the treasury, the lotus-born Lakṣmī, the giver of fame, and the increaser of renown;
she is the embodiment of the harsh voice of the new moon, with a face like the orb of the moon.
Her limbs are smeared with moon-like saffron, she dwells upon the Golden Mountain;
she stands on the peak of the Malaya mountain, her body being that of the Daughter of the Himālaya.
Kubjikā, the sovereign lady of Kosala, resides in a region within the lap of the Himālaya mountains;
she is bound by the single fetter of *kāra*, hidden, with concealed ankles, and most profoundly secreted.
Tanujā, Tanurūpā, Bāṇacāpadharā,
Nuti, Dhurīṇā, Dhūmravāsas, Dhūmrakeśā, and Aruṇānanā. (37)
Aruṇeśī, Rati, Svāti, Gariṣṭhā, Garīyasī, Mahānasī, Mahākārā, and she who causes terror to both gods and demons. || 38 ||
She is the subtle, great light, the unceasing Sarasvatī;
she is dark-hued with a dark face, peaceful, and the remover of the exhaustion of suffering.
She is the cow, she is to be counted, she is made of cow-dung, she is the secret one, she is the possessor of cows, she is the speech of the Guru, she is the one who goes to the Guru;
(300) she is intent on satisfaction through song, she is the seizer, she is the grasper, she is the planet.
She is beloved by the Gaṇas, possesses the gait of an elephant, is Gāndhārī, and delights in fragrances;
she dwells upon the ridges of Mount Gandhamādana and has made her abode on the Sahya mountain.
She is beloved by the elephant-faced one, the possessor of cows, the seizer, she whose vehicle is the crocodile;
she is born from the cave, dwells in the cave, and is adorned with a garland of planets.
Kauberī, Kuhakā, Bhrānti, Tarkavidyā, Priyaṅkarī, Pītāmbarā, Paṭākārā, Patākā, Sṛṣṭijā, and Sudhā. (43)
Dākṣāyaṇī, daughter of Dakṣa, destroyer of Dakṣa’s sacrifice;
Tārā stationed in the circle of stars, Tārā, Turī, Turyā, Tuṭi, and Tulā. 44.
She is the three junctions of the day, the aging at the junctures, and she who is cherished by the dawn of youth;
she is Lalitā, Lohitā, Lampā, Campā, and Kampākulā, as well as the goad.
She is the path, the truthful one, established in her own state, equanimous, and the increaser of humanity;
she consists of light, the satisfaction of the mind, the eternal wish-fulfilling cow.
Sūkṣmarūpā, Sūkṣmamukhā, Sthūlarūpā, Kalāvatī, Talātalāśrayā, Sindhu, Tryambikā, Lampikā, and Jayā. (47)
Saudāminī, Sudhādevī, she who is worshipped by the Sanaka-sages, Mandākinī, Yamunā, Vipāśā, and the river Narmadā; (48)
The Gaṇḍakī, Airāvatī, Siprā, Vitastā, and Sarasvatī; the Revā, Airāvatī, Ikṣumatī, and Sāgaravāsinī. (49)
Devakī, mother of the gods, queen of the gods, beautiful as a goddess; slayer of the Daityas, subduer, giver, Diti, and the beautiful daughter of Diti. || 50 ||
Vidyādharī, Vidyeśī, Vidyādharajasundarī, Menakā, Citralekhā, Citriṇī, and Tilottamā. || 51 ||
Urvaśī, Mohinī, and Rambhā, the most beautiful among the hosts of Apsaras;
Yakṣiṇī, the sovereign of the world of Yakṣas, who is worshipped by Naravāhana.
The daughter of the lord of yakṣas, the beautiful consort of the leader of yakṣas, Gandhavatī—whose body is fragrant, who is sweet-smelling, and who is devoted to song. (53)
The daughter of the Gandharva, Namrā; Gīti, Gandharvasundarī; Mandodarī, Karālākṣī, and Meghanādavarapradā. || 54 ||
Meghavāhanasantuṣṭā, Meghamūrti, the Rākṣasī Rakṣohantrī, Kekasī, and Sundarī, the leader of the Rākṣasas. || 55 ||
Kiṃnarī, Kambukaṇṭhī, Kalakaṇṭhasvanā, Sudhā, Kimukhī, Hayavaktrā, Kelā, and Kinnarasundarī. (56)
Piśācī, Rājamātaṅgī, she who abides in the state of the remnants (ucchiṣṭa), Mahāpiśācinī, Cāndrī, and Piśācakulasundarī. || 57 ||

The Mistress of Secrets, whose form is secret, the venerable one, the beautiful lady of the Guhyakas; the bestower of accomplishments, the wife of the Siddhas, the Queen of the Siddhas, the beautiful lady of the Siddhas. || 58 ||
The mistress of beings, the abode of beings, the sustainer of beings, the remover of fear;
the dispeller of the terror of beings, the auspicious one, born of beings, and beautiful as all beings. || 59 ||
Pṛthvī, the sovereign of the world of kings, Pṛthā, worshipped by Viṣṇu; Vasundharā, bowed down to by the Vasus, Pṛthivī, the beauty of the earth. (60)
The daughter of the ocean, the one whose lotus-eyes are never obscured, the mistress of the waters;
she who is formless yet composed of water, the destroyer of Māra, dwelling in the water, the beauty of the water.
She is radiant, the great sustainer, composed of light, and abiding within the solar orb;
she is the splendor of the sun, possessing the brilliance of the sun, whose singular beauty is the very form of radiance.
She is borne by the wind, has the wind as her mouth, and is the sole beauty of the world of wind;
she dwells in the sky, is the sovereign of sky-goers, and is formless, having the nature of the void.
She is the radiance that appears yet is without appearance, beautiful as the sky;
she assumes the form of the earth, infinite, and the beauty of the world of mountains.
She travels by sea, possesses the splendor of jewels, is the mistress of Varuṇa, and wields excellent weapons;
she holds a noose in her hand, nourishes all beings, and is the beautiful consort of the Lord of Varuṇa.
She is the light whose delight is the fire of digestion, who abides in the movement of the five vital winds;
she is the nature of the prāṇa, apāna, samāna, udāna, and vyāna breaths.
She who moves through the five winds, whose form is the channels, is Vātasundarī;
she whose form is fire is Vahniśikhā, resembling the submarine fire (vaḍavānala). || 67 ||
She is the weapon, the oblation, the light offered in sacrifice, born of fire, and beautiful as fire;
she is the Mistress of the Moon, a digit of the moon, and devoted to the drinking of soma.
She has a gentle face and a gentle form; she dwells in the moon and is as beautiful as the moon.
She possesses the radiance of the sun, a sun-like countenance, is born of the sun, and is as beautiful as the sun.
She is the sacrificial rite, the desire for a share in the sacrifice, and the bestower of boons upon the sacrificer;
she is the priestly knowledge and the singular beauty of the sacrificer. (500) || 70 ||
She who moves through space, she who is worthy of worship, she who is born of sound, she who is beautiful as the sky;
she who is fond of fish, she whose eyes are like fish, she whose hope is fish, she who is beautiful as a fish.
She who rests upon the back of a tortoise, the female tortoise, born of the tortoise, having the form of a tortoise;
she who is Vārāhī, the mother of heroes, worthy of praise, possessed of excellent hips, and having eyes like a deer’s. (72)
The goddess Varāhasundarī has the form of a boar, is eloquent, and possesses formidable tusks;
she has the appearance of Narasiṃha and is the slayer of wicked Daityas.
The woman who grants boons to Pradyumna, the uniquely beautiful one for Narasiṃha, born from his left side, of short stature, and solely devoted to Nārāyaṇa. (74)

The destroyer of Bali and Dānava's pride, the one who is contrary, the beautiful dwarf, the beloved of Rāma, the playmate of Rāma, the one who brought about the destruction of the Kṣatriya lineage. || 75 ||
The daughter of Danu [Kh: the daughter of Bhṛgu], the princess Rāmā, who wields the battle-axe;
she is the descendant of Bhṛgu, beloved by those of Bhṛgu’s lineage, and the bestower of boons upon Jamadagni’s son.
Night holds an axe and is the sole beauty of Jamadagni’s son;
she is served by Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, and she is the destroyer of the race of Rākṣasas. || 77 ||
She is the beloved of Rāma, the destroyer of enemies, the bestower of desires upon Śatrughna and Bharata;
she is enriched by streams of the nectar of beauty and is the slayer of the demon Lavaṇa.
Red-faced, with a serene countenance, delighting in her own self, beautiful as Rāma;
black-haired, black-faced, she is the destroyer of the Yādavas and the dissolution.
Rādhā, the beautiful Śrī-Kṛṣṇa, who is worshipped by the hosts of aquatic beings, is the mother of Buddha, the goddess of the Buddhas, and devoted to the path of the Jinas. (80)

Having conquered anger, having conquered sloth, she is to be served by the Victors; she has conquered her senses, she is fierce as the upholder of the lineage of the Victors, she is blue-edged, and she is beautiful as a Buddha. 81.
Kālī, who delights in tumultuous noise, whose vehicle is a ghost, the sovereign of the gods;
beloved of Kalki, bearer of the conch, the uniquely beautiful one of the Kali age. 82.
She is the illusion of Viṣṇu, the illusion of Brahmā, the power of Śambhu, and she whose vehicle is a corpse;
she dwells upon the chest of Indra’s younger brother, she is the consort of Sthāṇu, and she who scatters the grain. (83)
Jṛmbhiṇī, the remover of yawning, she whose hair is disheveled as she yawns; she who is designated by the station of Kulākula, the bestower of the fruit of granting boons. || 84 ||
The mistress of the family speech, born of noble lineage, born of the Kula, beautiful of form;
beloved by Indra, auspicious, the abode of youth, and the sovereign of the merit-born ones.
She is the one who inspires merit, the destroyer of evil, and the beautiful consort of Indra;
she resembles ten million suns, consists of solar splendor, and is the primordial ink.
Likhinī is radiant, Sūryasundarī has the form of a rope, Candrikā is a stream of nectar, and Jyotsnā is as beautiful as the cool-rayed moon. (600) 87.
She of the tremulous eyes, she of the hundred eyes, she of the thousand eyes, and she of the thousand feet;
she of the thousand heads, she with Indra-like eyes, and she whose creeper-like arms are a thousand in number.
She is radiant with the splendor of ten million jewels, clothed in white garments, and possesses a hundred faces;
she is the joy of hundreds, the upholder of sacred revelation, tawny-hued, and of fierce roar.
Suṣumnā is crowded with the sounds of necklaces, armlets, and anklets;
she has a terrible roar, a terrifying face, is ever-facing forward, and has flaming torches as her weapons.
She is the hidden one, the Gūrjarī song, the Gāyatrī, the beloved of the Vedas; she is the resonance of the lute’s sound, the science of sound, and the riverbank.
She whose form is the *bindu*, the womb of the *cakra*, whose nature is the *bindu* and *nāda*;
she is the Mistress of the *cakra*, the Sovereign of Bhairava, the beloved of Mahābhairava. 92.
She is the wife of Kālabhairava, a dancer upon the stage of the end of the aeon;
possessing the smoky luster of the fire of universal destruction, she has made her abode within the center of the womb.
She is the Bhūcarī and Khecarī Mudrā, sporting with the nine mudrās;
she is the Viyoginī who dwells in the cremation ground and is gratified by worship in the cremation ground.
She whose limbs are radiant, the crest of the flame of destruction, she who dwells upon the left side of the body of Bharga;
she is Bhadrakālī, Viśvakālī, Śrīkālī, and Meghakālikā. (95)
Nīrakālī, Kālarātri, Kālī, Kāmeśakālikā, Indrakālī, Pūrvakālī, and Paścimāmnāyakālikā. || 96 ||
Śmaśānakālikā, Bhadrakālī, Śrīkṛṣṇakālikā; Kālī of the syllable Krīṃ, and Dakṣiṇakālikā of Śrīṃ Hūṃ Hrīṃ. || 97 ||
Sundarī, Tripureśānī, Trikūṭā, Tripurārcitā, Trinetrā, Tripurādhyakṣā, Tripuṭā, and Puṭabhairavī. || 98 ||
The mother of the three worlds, she who is Tretā, the Great Tripurasundarī;
Kāmeśvarī, the digit of desire (Kāmakalā), beautiful as the very embodiment of time and passion. 99.
She is the three-syllabled one, the goddess of the three syllables, the meditative realization, and the sovereign of the worlds;
she is the single-syllabled one, the four-peak one, the mistress of the three peaks, and the sovereign of dissolution.
She who consists of the four castes, the mistress of the castes, enriched by the castes;
she who has four syllables, five syllables, six faces, six peaks, and six syllables. || 101 ||
She is the seven-syllabled one, the nine-faced one, the supreme mistress of the eight syllables;
she is the ninth, the fifth, the sixth, the mistress of the serpents, and the nine-syllabled one.
She who possesses ten syllables is the mistress of the ten-faced one; she who possesses eleven syllables is the goddess;
she who resembles the twelve Ādityas is the twelfth, possessing twelve syllables. (103)
The thirteenth is Vedagarbhā, the first being the fourteen-syllabled mantra;
there is the fourteen-syllabled Vidyā and the fifteen-syllabled Vidyā. || 104 ||
She is the sixteenth, the sovereign of all vidyās, the Great Śrī of sixteen syllables;
she is the Mahāśrī-Ṣoḍaśī-vidyā, dear to the Cintāmaṇi-mantra.
The twenty-two-syllable Śyāmā, the consort of Mahākāla, Vajratārā, Kālatārā, Nārī, Tārā, and Ugratāriṇī. (106)
Tārā of Desire, Tārā of Sound, Tārā of Touch, the Abode of Taste,
Tārā of Form, Tārā of Fragrance, and Mahānīla Sarasvatī. (107)
Kālajvālā, Vahnijvālā, Brahmajvālā, who is garlanded with matted locks;
Viṣṇujvālā, Jiṣṇuśikhā, Bhadrajvālā, and Karālinī. || 108 ||
The goddess Vikarālamukhī is Karālī, adorned with ashes;
she reclines upon a funeral pyre as her seat, is the very embodiment of contemplation, and dwells in the center of the circle of the funeral pyre.
She is served by the Bhairavas of the elements and is the protectress of the Bhairavas of the elements;
she is the unchaste woman, she is the seal bound [upon] all, and she is the destroyer of the bonds of worldly existence. || 110 ||

Bhavānī is the sovereign goddess of the gods, worshipped by those initiated through initiation; she is the mistress of practitioners, the bestower of success, and the increaser of the joy of practitioners.
She is the locus of the practitioner and the bestower of the desired fruits upon practitioners;
she is Rajovatī, Rājasī, Rajakī, and Rajasvalā. || 112 ||
She who loves flowers, who possesses flowers, who wears a garland of self-arisen flowers, who is rich with the fragrance of self-arisen flowers, and who is the slayer of Pulastya’s son. 113.
She holds a vessel in her hand; she is a daughter and a granddaughter; she has a yellow face and yellow ornaments;
she has a tawny face, tawny hair, is tawny-colored, and is the sovereign of the tawny ones.
She is auspiciousness itself, the sovereign of all that is auspicious, and the source of auspiciousness for all that is auspicious;
she is the mistress of Purūravas, the bearer of the noose, the bearer of the bow, and the one who is never burdened.
She is the nurse of merit, composed of merit, and dwells in the world of merit;
she is to be served by the officiating priests, resides in the letter *ha*, and as the letter *sa*, she is the realm of Sukhāvatī.
She is a friend, beautiful, truthful, and devoted to the practice of truth; she is the power of Śiva, the Lord of the virtuous, and rests upon a portion of Vāmadeva.
The goddess Sadyojātakalā is auspicious and possesses the form of the Aghora-kalā;
she is like the night, resembling milk, and is the one who distinguishes milk from water. (800) || 118 ||
The abode of discursive thought, eternal, perpetually moist, the supreme Mother; beloved by the Destroyer of Cities, long-limbed, long-nosed, and soft-spoken. (119)
Kāśikā, Kauśikī, Kośyā, Kośadā, Rūpavardhinī,
Tuṣṭi, Puṣṭi, Prajāprītā, Prājikā, and Pūjakapriyā. || 120 ||
She is the mother of progeny, the bearer of the embryo, and the nourisher of the fetus;
clad in white garments, possessing a white form, dressed in pure raiment, she brings victory.
Jānakī is the mother of progeny, intent on pleasing her parents,
fond of discourse, devoted to musical instruments, skilled at playing them, and beautiful in debate.

She who paralyzes speech, whose voice is like that of a parrot, who is both steadfast and unsteady, who bears the burden, who is a suckling infant, who kindles the sacred fire, who is devoid of joy, and who is homeless. || 123 ||
She bestows all happiness, she is the essence, the giver of boons from the ocean of waters;
she is Vālukī, beloved by heroes in their drinking bouts, the supporter of the earth, and dear to the Vasus. 124.

She who delights in the parrot, whose essence is the parrot, who is worshipped by the parrot, who is dear to the parrot, who is the female parrot, who holds a parrot in her hand, and who is the destroyer of all hells. 125.
She is the abode of all principles, whose form is the *bhaga*, the Mistress of the *bhaga*,
the embodiment of the *bhaga*, beloved by the *bhaga*, and whose essential nature is the *bhaga-linga*.
She is the Mistress of the Bhaga and Liṅga, the bestower of fortune, the one from whom the nectar of the Bhaga and Liṅga flows;
she subsists on milk, delights in milk, and is devoted to drinking clarified butter.
Devoted to drinking wine, mature, with full shoulders, in continuous succession, swaying, resembling a gourd, and with eyes as red as the pāṭala flower. || 128 ||

She who loves the ocean of milk, the intoxicated one, the straightforward one, she whose weapon is the straight shaft; she who is the battle, the good policy, the fallen, the cycle of existence, and the primordial mistress.
The maiden Kanakarekhā, a resident of Kānyakubja, whose body is adorned with gold, is the very quarter of the horizon who destroys the disease of leprosy. || 130 ||
Kuntī has thick hair; she is the fortitude that wields the spear as her weapon.
She is clad in skins, possesses cruel claws, eyes like those of the *cakora* bird, and has four arms. (131)
She who is dear to the four Vedas, the eloquent one, the bestower of the fruits of the four aims of life;
she who moves through the cosmic egg, the manifestation, the consort of Brahmā, and she who is honored by Brahmā. 132.
She is the one who brings about honor, the mother, the creeper, and the great vine;
she is the wish-fulfilling plant, the slender-limbed one, and the dweller in the celestial tree of plenty.
The great vidyā Kalpapāśā (or Kalpaśākhā), the queen of vidyās, the refuge of happiness;
the queen of prosperity, the queen of the universe, the queen of the world, the refuge of auspiciousness. || 134 ||
Brahmarājñī, Viṣṇurājñī, Rudrarājñī, Jaṭāśrayā, Nāgarājñī, Vaṃśarājñī, Vīrarājñī, and Rajapriyā. || 135 ||
Sattvarājñī, Tamorājñī, Guṇarājñī, Calācalā, Vasurājñī, Satyarājñī, Taporājñī, and Japapriyā (or Rajapriyā). || 136 ||
Queen of Mantras, Queen of the Vedas, Queen of Tantras, lover of the sacred revelation;
Queen of the Vedas, Queen of the Gods, Queen of Mortals, Queen of Ministers, Queen of the Daityas, the source of compassion. || 137 ||
Kālarājñī, Prajārājñī, Tejorājñī, Harāśrayā, Pṛthvīrājñī, Payorājñī, Vāyurājñī, and Madālasā. || 138 ||
The Queen of Nectar, the Queen of Wine, the Queen of Terror who is free from fear,
the Queen of Truth, the Queen of Victory, the Great Queen whose form is the lineage (or whose form is stone).
Vāmarājñī, Cīnarājñī, Harirājñī, Halīśvarī, Parārājñī, Yakṣarājñī, Bhūtarājñī, and Śivāsanā. || 140 ||
Vaṭurājñī, Pretarājñī, Śeṣarājñī, the bestower of peace;
Ākāśarājñī, Rājeśī, Rājarājñī, and she who is fond of Rati. || 141 ||
The Queen of the Netherworld, the Queen of the Earth, the Queen of the Departed, the Dispeller of Poison;
the Queen of Accomplishment, the Queen of Radiance, the Queen of Splendor, she who consists of light. (142)
The radiant queen, the moon-queen, the star-queen, the dweller in the sky;
the queen of the planets, the vine-queen, the tree-queen, the bestower of intelligence. 143.
Dhīrarājñī, Manorājñī, Manurājñī, and Kāśyapī;
Munirājñī, Ratnarājñī, Yugarājñī, and Maṇiprabhā. (144)
The Queen of the Sindhu, the Queen of the rivers, the Queen of the streams, residing in the caves;
the Queen of the Bindu, the Queen of Sound, and the Queen of the Self, who is the true goal. || 145 ||
Putrarājñī, Dhyānarājñī, Layarājñī, Sadīśvarī, Īśānarājñī, Rājeśī, Svāhārājñī, and Mahattarā. || 146 ||
The Queen of Fire, the Queen of Yoga, the Queen of Sacrifice, whose form is consciousness;
the Queen of the World, the Queen of Reality, the Queen of Speech, who possesses the universal form. || 147 ||
The fifteen-syllable queen-mantra is *oṃ hrīṃ bhūteśvareśvarī*.
This is the essence of all mantras, the thousand names of the Queen. (148)
The reality of the fifteen-syllable mantra is the essence of all mantras, beloved by Manu;
it consists of all principles, is meritorious, and destroys even the greatest sins. (149)
It bestows all accomplishments in the world, eradicates all diseases, pacifies all calamities, and is supreme for bringing peace to the planetary spirits. 150.
Beloved by all the gods, abundant, dispelling the fear of all enemies, pacifying the flood of all sufferings, and destroying all sorrows. || 151 ||
Whether one recites or causes others to recite this Thousand Names in the presence of Śakti, calamities and the fears of enemies flee far away. (152)
Rākṣasas, bhūtas, vetālas, serpents, and lions flee swiftly upon its recitation, just as living beings flee from Mahākāla. (153)

By hearing this, sin shall be destroyed; he who causes it to be heard is fortunate. Having enjoyed various kinds of pleasures upon the surface of the earth, he will swiftly go to the supreme state—of this there is no doubt.
It is equal to a thousand horse-sacrifices, ten million Vājapeya sacrifices, a thousand baths in the Gaṅgā, and ten thousand Cāndrāyaṇa penances. || 155 ||

Ten million performances of the Rājasūya sacrifice, each accompanied by one hundred thousand *taptakṛcchra* penances, do not equal even a sixteenth part of the merit of reciting the Thousand Names. (156)
O Maheśvarī, he who desires sovereignty should recite this thousand names of the Queens, which grants all perfections as its goal and contains the essence of the mantra. 157.
O Īśvarī, he who is intent on the worship of Śakti, performing the *śatāvarta* [mantra] for one year while immersed in the great *Cīna-krama*, shall obtain a kingdom at night.
O Maheśvarī, one who desires a son should, at evening, smeared with the ashes of a funeral pyre, naked and with disheveled hair, recite this one hundred times.
In a cremation ground, however, one shall obtain a son who is truly like Vaiśravaṇa himself;
the wise man, intent on worshipping the wives of others, should meditate upon the form of Bhaga.
One who desires wealth shall obtain riches by reciting the Thousand Names;
O Goddess, on a Sunday one should recite the Thousand Names three times.
Reclining on a soft seat and intent on drinking milk,
he beholds in a dream the Queen, the bestower of boons, upon her throne on the earth.
Satiated by the chewing of milk, filled with the essence of the drink of heroes,
whoever recites the Thousand Names of the Queens with supreme devotion— 163.
That practitioner who, with devotion, recites this while seated upon the breast of Śakti, is immediately liberated from the terrible fear born of great sins. 164.
At the time of the moon's rising, the eight supernatural powers (aṣṭasiddhi) reside in his hand—
he who recites [this] at night before the circle (cakra), intent on meditating upon the wife of another. (165)
Delighting in the taste of wine and spirits, he shall obtain victory in battle;
for this thousand names, O Śivā, consists of all mantras.
At night, during the assembly for the worship of the wheel,
one should draw [the design] upon the bark of a banyan tree with pure eight-fold fragrance, and then enclose it within a golden leaf.
One should wear it around the neck, for then all accomplishments arise;
whoever wears this great protection, which is exceedingly difficult even for all the gods to obtain. (168)
In battle, in the royal court, in gambling, or in calamities such as thieves and disease, that practitioner who is a leader of heroes immediately attains victory. (169)
He who worships the Śrīcakra, wears the armor upon his head,
and likewise recites the Thousand Names as well as the hymn consisting of mantras— 170.
What desire does one not obtain, even that which is difficult for the gods to attain? From that [practice], one gains the drinking of wine, the chewing of meat, and the eating of fish. (171)
O Dear One, the union with a young maiden is the mudrā; the sound of the lute is the [mantra];
association with the virtuous and the presence of the Guru are present; and the Śrīcakra of the Queen is before one. (172)
O Goddess, he alone shall be a yogi, a knower of Brahman, and a lord;
this supreme secret has been declared by me to you out of devotion. (173)
It must not be made public, it must not be given, and it should not be imparted to just anyone—to another disciple, to the wicked, to the base, or to one of evil nature. (174)
It should not be given by those who perceive the truth to one devoid of devotion to the guru, to one who reviles divine women [or the wives of others], to an atheist, or to one of evil conduct. 175.
It should be given to a disciple who is tranquil, devoted, and a proponent of non-duality;
to one who has been initiated, of noble birth, and who delights in devotion to the Queen.
Having given [this], the best of practitioners shall obtain both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
Thus ends the thousand names of the Queen, uttered from the mouth of Śiva.
It is extremely difficult to obtain, and it must be guarded and concealed like one's own private parts.
Thus ends the Thousand Names of the Glorious Mahārājñī, within the *Śrīrudrayāmala Tantra*, in the secret doctrine of the Ten Vidyās. 4.
Now, the Hymn to the Illustrious Mahārājñī.
The Illustrious Bhairava said:
Now I shall proclaim the King of Hymns, which is supreme in nature, consisting of the root mantra, divine, the very essence of reality, and captivating to the mind. (1)
O beloved, this hymn is dear to the Queen, it removes sins, bestows the fruit of a hundred thousandfold worship, is equal to a hundred thousand recitations, and is equal to ten million meditations.
O Goddess of the gods, for this hymn to Rājñī, Brahmā is declared to be the seer (ṛṣi);
Gāyatrī is said to be the meter (chanda), and the deity is proclaimed to be Śrīrājñī. (3)
Māyā is the seed-syllable, Parā is the power, and Kāma is the pin, O Īśvarī; the application (viniyoga) is proclaimed for the sake of attaining both worldly enjoyment and liberation. || 4 ||

Of this mantra of the King of Hymns to the Illustrious Mahārājñī: Brahmā is the seer (ṛṣi), the Gāyatrī is the meter (chandaḥ), the Illustrious Bhūteśvarī Mahārājñī is the deity (devatā), Hrīṃ is the seed-syllable (bīja), Sauḥ is the power (śakti), Klīṃ is the bolt (kīlaka); the application (viniyoga) is for the attainment of enjoyment and liberation. Salutation to Brahmā, the seer, on the head; to the Gāyatrī meter...

Salutation to the deity Śrīrājñībhūteśvarī in the mouth; salutation to the seed-syllable *hrīṃ* in the heart; salutation to the power (*śakti*) *sauḥ* at the navel; salutation to the *kīlaka* *klīṃ* in the secret place; salutation to the ritual application (*viniyoga*) in the feet; salutation to all the limbs.
Meditation:
[One should visualize the Goddess] possessing the splendor of a thousand rising suns, three-eyed, seated upon a lion throne, with a serpent serving as her sacred thread.
I worship the Queen, whose lotus-face is in full bloom, and who holds in her hands a sword, a lotus, a jar, and a vessel of nectar. || 1 ||
That practitioner who recites at dawn this captivating jewel of the ocean of the Vedas— tāram, adorned with the digit of the moon (indukalikā)— using a rosary of gems, quickly attains sovereignty.
Whoever recites even once this mantra— which is adorned with the digit of the new moon and graced by the *nāda* and *bindu*—
while standing upon a great elephant, shall conquer in battle the enemies who are arrogant and intoxicated with pride.
O Mistress of the World, the practitioner who, tormented by passion, recites the *ramā* mantra within your own mantra,
shall embrace Rambhā, travel in celestial chariots, and enjoy playful delights in the groves of Nandana.

He who, desiring wealth, recites at night this seed-mantra of Fire—bestowed with the powers of atomization (*aṇimā*) and the rest, adorned with the Bindu, the lunar orb, and the crescent moon—he becomes like the god of wealth in an instant. (5)

If one who is saluted by the immortals recites the Kāmarāja mantra with a rosary of *akṣa* seeds during sexual union, even the celestial maidens come under his control; how much more so, then, the women of the earth in this world? (6)
If one recites the Śakti mantra with devotion at the time of the worship of Śakti, offering it into the lotus-feet of Kālī,
then at night either the celestial nymph Ghṛtācī with her smiling face or even Śacī from heaven shall become submissive to him.
One should likewise remember the name-mantra for the Blessed Goddess and the Queen;
O Goddess, for such a person, the eight siddhis of Bhairava shall come under his control.
O Maheśānī, if the supreme practitioner, staying in a cemetery, should recite [the mantra] at the end of the ocean of illusion,
he shall immediately behold the Goddess Paramārtharājñī right there, the bestower of excellent accomplishments.
If one recites the two *ṭha* syllables at the end of the night while subsisting on milk and staying on the bank of a river, then,
O Goddess, Indra, Viṣṇu, Brahmā, and Īśvara come under one's control in an instant.

I worship the Queen, the crest-jewel of the royal family, who sits within the mandala consisting of the earth-house, three circles, serpent-leaves, a hexagon, another triangle, and a circle of dots— the presiding deity of the royal lineage.

O Goddess, Śrī Bhūtadhātrī, composed of preeminent qualities, partless and devoid of attributes; O Māyā, my Mother, refuge, daughter of the mountain king, consisting of pure consciousness, whose nature is reality; O Durgā, Caṇḍī, Pramattā, conqueror of Tripura, with a smiling face, most excellent, rich in compassion, and most praiseworthy!
O Queen, born from the gods and the earth, please be gracious!

O Daughter of the Mountain, whoever recites this hymn with devotion in the morning— this praise which is the abode of bliss and compassion arising from the radiance of the mantra— without indolence; [he shall attain his desires].
O Giver of Boons, a mortal whose feet are instantly honored by the crowns of kings upon the earth shall, upon death, attain liberation and reach your abode.
Thus, O Śivā, this entire five-limbed supreme truth of the queen is my whole being and secret, which bestows all eloquence.
This secret [teaching] increases bliss, is the cause of supreme sovereignty, bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation, is meritorious, and destroys the fear of poverty. (15)
Bestowing sovereignty, inspiring devotion, and destroying all enemies—this entire five-limbed [mantra] of the Goddess must not be told to the wicked-minded.
Out of devotion for you, I have revealed it; it must be guarded with great effort.
The Goddess said:
O Blessed One, ocean of compassion, I have now been purchased by you;
I am your servant, I am your devotee, and I have attained my life's purpose, O Lord of the World. (17)
O Maheśvara, by your grace, this queen, the goddess, has been described with her five limbs; what else shall I tell you? 18.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
This five-limbed secret of the Goddess Rājñī has been proclaimed by me; it bestows success upon the Kaulas and, originating from the Left-hand path (vāmamārga), must be guarded like one's own womb.
Thus ends the "Hymn to the Great Queen" (*Śrīmahārājñīstotra*) within the *Daśavidyārahasya* of the *Śrīrudrayāmala Tantra*. (5)
This *Śrīmahārājñī-pañcāṅga* is completed.
Now, (p. 481) [the next section begins].
The Five-Limbed Ritual of Bālātripurā; the Chapter on Bālā.
To the Blessed Lord, the Consort of Umā, seated upon the peak of Kailāsa.
The god who has the crescent moon as his crown and whose eyes are the moon, the sun, and fire.
Clad in an elephant hide, Virūpākṣa is worshipped by the gods;
he is saluted by the lords of the Gaṇas, Gandharvas, and Yakṣas, as well as by the Devas and Asuras. || 2 ||
Seeing him laughing, muttering prayers, and reciting repeatedly, Bhairavī rose, bowed down, and asked this: || 3 ||
Śrī Bhairavī said: O Blessed One, ocean of compassion, expert in all the Agamas!
By your grace, O Lord of the Gods, I have heard all the Vidyās.
Now I wish to hear about the young Tripurasundarī;
if she is to be granted to me, O God, then tell me the Vidyā, O Maheśvara. Śrī Bhairava said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the five-limbed [rite] which grants the desires of practitioners:
the chapter (paṭala), the manual (paddhati), the armor (varma), and likewise the thousand names (nāmnāṃ sahasrakam).
O Great Goddess, listen with a one-pointed mind to this king of hymns;
it is the Śrī Bālā Parameśānī, the bestower of both worldly enjoyment and liberation. (7)
(482) The kingdom may be given, the head may be given, and likewise the home together with its fortune;
O Great Goddess, everything may be given, but this supreme [teaching] must not be given.
In the Kali age, there is no other knowledge equal to this knowledge;
the Śrī Bālā Tripurā Vidyā is remembered as the bestower of swift accomplishment.
O Supreme Goddess, this knowledge should be given to a disciple who is tranquil and devoted to the guru; it must not be bestowed upon one who is not a devotee.
O Maheśvarī, I shall fully explain the extraction of the mantra, as well as the yantra, the prastāra, the meditation, and the ritual applications of the Goddess of gods.
First, O Goddess of gods, hear the extraction of the mantra which bestows fruit;
it must be guarded with effort, by means of which success is produced. (12)
One should place the Vāgbhava, the Kāmarāja, and the Śakti in the middle;
ending with "namas," O Goddess, this is the eight-syllabled mantra of Bālā. (13)
O Great Goddess, in the Kali age, this king of mantras is spontaneously effective; there is neither obstacle, nor impurity, nor likewise any restriction.
The sage and the meter for the two rows of Dakṣiṇāmūrti are remembered in their respective order;
the deity is Tripurā-Bālā, with the seed-syllable and the power-syllable at the beginning and the end. 15.
*Klīṃ* is prescribed as the *kīlaka* for the sake of dharma, kāma, artha, and liberation;
[it is placed] on the head, the face, O Goddess, the heart, and the secret region. (16)

O Great Goddess, one should likewise place [the mantras] on the feet, the navel-lotus, and all the limbs; one should perform the ritual arrangement of the placement (nyāsa), beginning with the seer (ṛṣi) and so forth.
O Maheśvarī, one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) on the hands and the six-limbed ritual (ṣaḍaṅga) using the seed-syllables (bījas).
I shall now describe her meditation (dhyāna), which bestows benefit upon practitioners. 18.

I meditate upon the Youthful Goddess, clad in red garments, adorned with a crescent moon, resembling the rising sun, and possessing three eyes; she holds a book, a rosary, and displays the gesture of granting fearlessness in her hands, seated upon a reddish lotus. (19)

Having meditated thus upon the Great Goddess, the best of practitioners should recite the mantra that grants perfect success three hundred thousand times during the rite of preliminary service (puraścaryā).

Now, O Goddess of gods, I shall describe the extraction of the yantra, which is very difficult to obtain, and which bestows the fruits of worldly enjoyment and liberation upon the practitioner of the Great Goddess. (21)
And [the mandala] adorned with a dot, a triangle, an eight-cornered figure, an eight-petaled lotus, three circles, and three enclosures of the earth; [Kh: six].
O Girīśa, this wheel of Bālā and others, which removes all suffering and is saluted by Brahmā, Indra, and Viṣṇu, has been described by me to you.
When the yantra has been drawn in this manner, one should worship the powers of the pedestal (pīṭhaśaktis):
namely, Icchā, Jñānā, Kriyā, Kāminī, and Kāmadāyinī.
Rati, Ratipriyānandā, and Manonmanī as the last—having worshipped these Śaktis of the Pīṭhas, one should assign the Pīṭha with their respective mantras. || 24 ||
The third [mantra] consists of "vyomaparvata," followed by "sadāśivamahāpada," ending with "namaḥ" after "pīṭhapadmāsanāya"; this is the seat-mantra (pīṭhamaṃtra). || 25 ||
Then, once the form has been fashioned, one should invoke the Goddess with the sixteen-syllable root mantra and worship her with various kinds of ritual offerings.
Having worshipped the Goddess with discernment in the central womb, the triangle,
he should worship Rati in the left corner, Prīti in the right, and Manobhavā in front.
One should worship the limbs (aṅgas) starting from the southeast corner of the yoni;
in the central yoni, one should worship the arrows (smaras) externally in the eastern directions and at the front.
In the same manner, one should place the Vāṇadevis as Śaktis in the eight wombs:
first Subhagā, then Bhagā, and thirdly Bhagasarpiṇī.
Bhagamālā, Anaṅgā, and next Anaṅgakusumā;
Anaṅgamekhalā and Anaṅgamadanā—these are the eight Śaktis. (30)
The Bhairavas, whose faces are like Brahmā and who dwell within the filaments of the lotus, reside upon the petals;
furthermore, there are eight sacred seats (pīṭhas) at the tips of the petals, the first of which is named Kāmarūpa.
Malaya, known as Kaulagiri, and that called Chauhāra, which is Kulāntaka;
likewise Jālandhara, Oḍyāṇa, and Devakūṭa as the eighth.
And in the underground chamber (bhūgṛha), in the directions starting from the earth [quarter], are Heruka, Tripurāntaka, Vetāla, Agnijihva, Kālāntaka, and Kapālī. || 33 ||
One should worship Ekapāda, Bhīmarūpa, Malaya, and Hāṭakeśvara with all their respective weapons, each in its own direction, beginning with Śakra.
Outside of that, in the cardinal directions, one should worship Vaṭuka, the Yoginīs, and Kṣetrapālaka;
in the intermediate directions, Gaṇeśa, the Vasus, Sūrya, and likewise Śiva.
Having worshipped all the spirits, one should likewise worship the weapons; first, having visualized the young girl in the center, situated in the middle of the lap of Kāmeśvara.
O Great Goddess, the Kaula practitioner, devoted to the Kaula conduct and seeking to accomplish the mantra, should perform worship with the five *makāras*.

With perfumes, unbroken grains, flowers, incense, lamps, and other offerings at the bindu, this is declared to be the limb of dissolution (layāṅga). O Pārvatī, hear now the practical applications (prayoga).
By performing these rites, one certainly and swiftly attains success:
namely, paralyzing (stambhana), bewildering (mohana), as well as killing (māraṇa) and summoning (ākarṣaṇa). (39)
Subjugation, as well as eradication, pacification, and nourishment—O Dear One, I shall describe this essential practice of the mantra. (40)
O Goddess, this is not to be given to one who is not a devotee; it is to be kept secret from the lowest of creatures, being the most profound mystery.
O Goddess, on the first day of the lunar fortnight, having bathed and performed the daily rites, [one should practice this].

At midday, having gone to a secluded place, one should perform the fire sacrifice (homa) according to the rules for up to ten thousand repetitions, using ghee, milk-rice (pāyasa), and peacock feathers, with the oblation consisting of one-tenth of the total number.
Having immediately satisfied the deities, immobilization certainly occurs regarding kings, the sun, the moon, the wind, and the mouths of robbers and others. (43)
On the new moon day, one who sits upon an owl's nest should recite [the mantra] at night in a cremation ground;
ten thousand times, and as its tenth part, one should perform a fire-oblation with ghee and liquor.

O Goddess, by means of *kaṇa*, *kesara*, and *padmākṣa* [or *nāgakesara*], one shall bring about the enchantment of the worlds. On the day known as Bhūta, O Goddess, having gone to a cemetery at night— || 45 ||
At the edge of the funeral pyre, the lord of heroes should mutter the sixteen-syllable vidyā;
and the mantra-practitioner should offer ten thousand oblations of ghee and guggulu into the fire of the pyre.
The fierce enemy dies together with the hair of a Caṇḍāla;
on the eighth day of the bright fortnight, the practitioner should recite [the mantra] in secret.
Having meditated ten thousand times upon the root-mantra, one's beloved who dwells in the mind,
there should be a fire-oblation (homa) consisting of clarified butter, lac, flowers, and cow-dung ashes, performed in a tenth part [of the recitation].
Attraction of women occurs by means of *karīra* stalks and wheat.
On the ninth day, O beloved, the practitioner, having bathed and performed his daily rites, [should proceed].
If an oblation of ten thousand offerings is performed with ghee, sugar, lotuses, pearls, and deer-hair,
using excellent vessels, Vāsava shall become a servant.
On the fourth day of the dark fortnight, O auspicious one,
at moonrise, the hero, seated on a head-rest (śīrṣāsana) on the bank of a river, should mutter the mantra ten thousand times.

There, one should offer oblations with clarified butter, blue lotus stalks, cloves, black pepper, sour substances, and so forth, using a tenth part [of the total]; thus, the eradication of the enemy will occur.
On the fifth night, O Goddess of gods, one should recite [the mantra] ten thousand times;
one should offer oblations consisting of ghee, fish, sugar, and potsherds in a quantity equal to one-tenth [of the recitations].
For the pacification of great illusion, great fear, and great calamity, a man,
having bathed on the Great Eighth (Mahāṣṭamī), [should worship] ten more [times] at the most excellent sacred seat (pīṭha). (54)
There, the hero should offer ten thousand oblations of ghee, dates, grapes, betel leaves, and garlands, according to the one-tenth portion.
The meat of a goat, when accompanied by blood, produces great nourishment;
this secret has been declared, which is the definitive exposition of all principles.
O Goddess of gods, one should guard this secret, my very self, during the Kali age;
by means of recitations numbering ten thousand on the days of the sun and other planets. (57)
One attains all accomplishments; there is no need for deliberation on this point.
Thus, this divine chapter has been revealed to you out of affection. It is more secret than the secret, a greater secret, to be guarded like one's own womb.
Thus ends the chapter on Śrī Bālā Tripurasundarī in the Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra, within the dialogue between Bhairava and Bhairavī.
Now follows the ritual manual (paddhati) of Śrī Bālā.
Now I shall describe the manual in prose form,
which truly bestows happiness upon the venerable Bālā Tripureśvarī.
If one worships the Goddess with devotion without having performed the morning duties,
that worship is fruitless, just like a ritual action devoid of purity. (2)
The illustrious practitioner, having risen from his bed during the *brāhmī* hour, having washed his hands, feet, face, and so forth, and having sat down firmly in the *padmāsana* posture,
[should meditate] upon his own Guru seated within the pericarp of a thousand-petaled lotus facing downwards located at the crown of his head, according to his own capacity.
Having meditated upon [the deity] together with mental offerings and worshipped them, having prostrated like a staff according to the procedure taught by the Guru,

and having performed the morning rites and the *ajapājapa*, one should pray to the earth for permission to carry out one’s duties; then, placing the feet upon it in accordance with the movement of the breath, one should exit from the house through the northwestern direction (*naiṛtya*).

Having performed [the preliminary rites] and gone to a river or similar location, one should complete the Vedic ritual and then begin the Tantric one. Therein, first, having sipped water (ācamana) with the three principles joined with the root mantra, or having sipped water with "hrīṃ svāhā," and having performed the bath for the removal of impurities while recollecting the root mantra, one should sip water again and perform the proclamation of the month and other details beginning with "Today... (adya).

Having made the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*) thus: "For the pleasure of the venerable family deity (*kuladevatā*), I shall perform the ritual bath according to the Tantric method," one should visualize a triangular wheel (*trikoṇacakra*) in the water.

Then, by means of the *aṅkuśamudrā* (the hook-gesture) and reciting "O Gaṅgā, O Yamunā, and so forth," one should invoke the sacred waters (*tīrtha*) from the solar orb and unite them with the water previously prepared before oneself; then, having performed the ritual sipping of water (*ācamana*).

Having sprinkled oneself with water while reciting the root mantra and performed a bath with clay, one should bathe the invoked deity within oneself three times while reciting the root mantra; then, having closed the seven apertures beginning with the ears, one should submerge and emerge from the water three times—
this is the procedure for bathing.

Now, the twilight ritual (*saṃdhyā*). Therein, having performed the ritual sipping of water (*ācamana*) as before, and having performed the root-prāṇāyāma, the *ṛṣi*-assignment, and so forth, as well as the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) upon the hands; having invoked the sacred waters (*tīrtha*) as before, and having placed that water in the left hand and covered it with the right hand, one consecrates it seven times with the five elemental mantras: *yaṃ raṃ vaṃ laṃ haṃ*.

Having consecrated it three times with the root-vidyā, one should sprinkle one’s own head three times with drops of that water using the left thumb and ring finger while reciting the root-vidyā; then, placing the remaining water in the left hand,
consecrating it three times, and uttering the root-mantra, one should [sprinkle it] seven times on the crown of the head with the *tattvamudrā* while reciting the root-mantra.

Having sprinkled [the water] three times, take the remaining water in the right hand, meditate upon it as having the form of light (*tejas*), and wash away the evil within the body through the *iḍā* [nāḍī]. Then, having expelled that black-colored water—which is the very form of sin—through the *piṅgalā* [nāḍī], one should cast it out with the syllable *phaṭ* onto the imagined diamond-stone (*vajraśilā*) on the left. Thereafter, perform the *arghya* offering.

Having offered the arghya three times to the Kula-sūrya with the mantra: *oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ śrīmārtaṇḍabhairavāya prakāśaśaktisahitāya idam arghyaṃ parikalpayāmi svāhā*, one should lead the Root Goddess from the heart-lotus to the solar orb (*sūryamaṇḍala*), meditate upon her there according to the prescribed rule, and [recite]: *aiṃ vāgīśvaryai vidmahe klīṃ*.
"Let us meditate upon Kāmeśvarī; may that Śakti, *sauḥ*, inspire us"—with this root *gāyatrī*, during the four twilights, [one should worship] in the solar orb.

Having offered the *arghya* to the Root Goddess (*mūladevī*), one should recite the mantra according to one’s capacity. Then, during the four junctions of the day (*saṃdhyā*), one should sequentially draw forth the splendor of the Goddess from the *mūlādhāra*, the heart-lotus, the space between the eyebrows, and the aperture of Brahma (*brahmarandhra*). Expelling it through the *iḍā* [nāḍī], one should deposit it there into the imagined circles of fire, sun, moon, and stars.

Having meditated upon the Goddess whose conscious form is [successively] that of a child, a youth, and a mature woman, one should then recite at dawn: "Aiṃ! We know the Goddess Tripurā; we meditate upon Vāgīśvarī; may She who is Liberation impel us. At midday: "Klīṃ! We know the Goddess Tripurā; we meditate upon Kāmeśvarī; may She who is Klinnā impel us. At evening: "Sauḥ..."

In the evening: "We know the Goddess Tripurā; we meditate upon the Mistress of Power (Śaktīśvarī); may She impel us toward immortality. At midnight: "Aiṃ! We know Vāgīśvarī; Klīṃ! We meditate upon Kāmeśvarī; Sauḥ! May Śakti impel us. Having thus offered the *arghya* with their respective *gāyatrīs*, [one should worship] according to one's capacity.

Having recited one's own *gāyatrī* and again the root *gāyatrī*, and having recited all of one's respective seed-syllables (*bījākṣara*) as well as the root mantra, one should offer the recitation through *prāṇāyāma* and other means. Then, having brought the splendor of the Goddess from the mandalas back to her own place and the Goddess herself into the heart, one should meditate upon her; such is the procedure for the twilight worship (*saṃdhyā-vidhi*).

Then follows the libation (*tarpaṇa*). There, having performed the ritual sipping of water (*ācamana*) as before, and having performed breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) and so forth, one should invoke the sacred site (*tīrtha*).
Having rendered the water nectar by means of the root mantra and the nectar-gesture (*amṛtamudrā*), one should meditate upon the Yantra within that water.

Then, having invited the Goddess together with her retinue from the heart, one should effect the ritual integration (*sakalīkaraṇa*) through the yoga of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), starting from the Kuṇḍalinī.

Having consecrated [the disciple] with the nectar of the ritual application (*prayoga*) and having worshipped him according to the rules, one should satisfy [the deities] three times in the northeast, saying: "May Śrī Kaulānandanātha Bhairava be satisfied. Then, in the fire, [one satisfies] the *paramaguru* in the southwest, the *paramācārya* in the northwest, and the *parameṣṭhiguru* either three times or once.

Having satisfied the gurus of the divine, siddha, and human lineages, and having likewise satisfied them in the water while visualizing the *yantra*, one should satisfy the Root Mantra three times with the words, "May Bālā Tripurā Vāgīśvarī, together with Kāmeśvara,
be satisfied," and having also satisfied the retinue, one should perform *prāṇāyāma* and other rites, and then dismiss the Goddess into one's own heart.
And one should dismiss the sacred ford (tīrtha) to its own place; this is the libation (tarpaṇa).

Then, having entered the sacrificial hall, one should worship the deities of the door with water and other offerings: *oṃ dhātre namaḥ* (obeisance to Dhātṛ) and *oṃ vidhātre namaḥ* (obeisance to Vidhātṛ) on the right; *gaṃ gaṅgāyai namaḥ* (obeisance to Gaṅgā) and *yaṃ yamunāyai namaḥ* (obeisance to Yamunā) on the left;
*dvāraśriyai namaḥ* (obeisance to Dvāraśrī) and *vāstupuruṣāya namaḥ* (obeisance to Vāstupuruṣa) above; and *dehalyai namaḥ* (obeisance to Dehalī) below.

Having performed worship and spread out one's own seat, and having worshipped it with "Hrīṃ, obeisance to the lotus-seat of the foundational power (ādhāraśakti)," one should sit upon the Vīrāsana or other appropriate posture. Then, having prayed to the Earth with the mantra beginning "O Earth, by you the worlds are supported," one should worship the deities:
"Obeisance to Maṇḍūka," "Obeisance to Kālāgnirudra," and "Hrīṃ, obeisance to the lotus-seat of the foundational power."

"Oṃ hrīṃ, to the seat of the sacred pedestal (pīṭhāsana). Having thus worshipped the seat and sat upon it, one should internalize the consciousness (saṃvit) according to the mantra. The procedure for this is as follows:

O Consciousness, born of Brahman, daughter of Brahman, ever sinless! For the sake of the satisfaction of the Brāhmaṇas, be forever pure. *Oṃ*, obeisance to Brāhmaṇī, *svāhā*. *Oṃ*, O Goddess who possesses the price of perfection (*siddhamūlya*), who is imperishable, who awakens those of deficient understanding!

O you who bring under control kings and subjects, O destroyer of the faction of enemies! Aiṃ, obeisance to the Kṣatriyā, Svāhā! O you whose fire blazes with the fuel of ignorance, O you whose form is the Brahman-fire of knowledge, [accept] this oblation of bliss and joy.

Grant me right knowledge! Hrīṃ, obeisance to Vaiśyā, svāhā! I bow, I bow to you, O revealer of the path of Yoga! O Mother Trailokyavijayā, be victorious through meditative absorption (samādhi) and grant the fruit [of success]. Klīṃ, obeisance to Śūdrā, svāhā!

Having consecrated [it] thus with the mantra: *Oṃ amṛte amṛtodbhave amṛtavarṣiṇi amṛtam ākarṣaya 2 siddhiṃ dehi dehi tripurasundari padaṃ me vaśam ānaya 2 svāhā*, and having recited the root mantra seven times over it, one should transform it into nectar using the *dhenu* and *yoni* mudrās, and display the *āvāhana* and other mudrās.

Having performed the binding of the directions with finger-snaps (*choṭikā*), and having satiated the venerable Guru and the deity seven or three times, one should offer into the mouth [of the deity] while reciting: *aiṃ vada vada vāgvādini mama jihvāgre sthirībhava sarvasattvavaśaṅkari svāhā*. Thereafter, becoming filled with bliss (*ānandamaya*).

May those beings depart who dwell upon the earth; may those beings who create obstacles vanish by the command of Śiva. May those beings who cause heresy, whether they move on the earth, in the intermediate space, or reside in the heavenly world, vanish by the command of Śiva. Thus.

Having dispelled the three kinds of obstacles by clapping the hands three times with the index and middle fingers raised upward, by striking the left heel three times, and by means of the divine gaze; having performed the binding of the ten directions with snapping sounds (*choṭikā*) and visualized a wall of fire in the four directions, one should perform *prāṇāyāma*. Therein, [one recites] the *praṇava*...
Reciting [the mantra] sixteen times, one should block the right nostril with the right thumb and fill [the lungs] with air through the left. Then, reciting that same [mantra] sixty-four times,
one should block the left nostril with the right ring finger and little finger and [retain] the air with both hands.

One should perform *kumbhaka*. Then, while reciting that same [mantra] thirty-two times, having likewise blocked the left channel (*puṭa*), one should exhale the breath through the right; this is the first *prāṇāyāma*. This same process performed in reverse is the second.
The third is like the first. By means of these three *prāṇāyāmas*, one's own body is cleansed of all impurities.

Having contemplated that one is fit for the propitiation of the deity, one should perform the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*). Then, with the mantra "Haṃsa," one should bring Kuṇḍalinī from the *mūlādhāra* to the *svādhiṣṭhāna* along with the earth element; there, one should contemplate the earth dissolved in the water, and from that [water], together with the water...
Having brought [the water] to the Maṇipūraka, one should contemplate the water dissolved there in the fire; then,
having brought it from there along with the fire to the Anāhata, one should meditate on the fire dissolved there in the air, and from that, together with the air...
Having brought the pure [element] there, one should contemplate the wind dissolved in the space situated therein; then,

having brought the wheel of command (ājñācakra) together with that space, one should contemplate the space dissolved in the mind (manas) there, and having visualized the mind dissolved in sound (nāda), one should offer the sound into the resonance (dhvani).

Reciting sixteen times the mantra consisting of light located within the triangle situated in the middle of the lunar disc at the pericarp of the thousand-petaled lotus, one [should visualize] the embodied personification of sin (pāpapuruṣa) residing in the left side of the abdomen— smoky-colored, with the murder of a Brahmin as its head and the theft of gold as its two arms.

One should visualize the sinner within one's belly as being joined with a heart of liquor-drinking, having both hips for violating the teacher’s bed, and a pair of feet for associating with such persons;

his limbs and minor members are the great sins, his body hairs are the secondary sins (upapātaka), and he has red beard and eyes. Enraged and bearing a sword and shield, one should contemplate this wicked man in the stomach.
Having thus dried [the body], while reciting the fire-seed syllable *raṃ*, red in color, sixty-four times, one should burn that very [body]; then,
having visualized the nectar-seed syllable *vaṃ*, white in color, within the thousand-petaled lotus (*sahasrāra*), and reciting it thirty-two times,
one should produce a sinless body by means of the rain of nectar arising from that, [and finally contemplate] the syllable *laṃ* located at the forehead.

Having made [the body] very firm with the yellow-colored seed-syllable *pṛthvī* (laṃ), and having established sovereignty by means of the root seed-syllable *hrīṃ* located at the base, one should, by means of the mantra *so'haṃ*, unite the five elements and the individual soul (*jīvātman*)— which have become merged with the nectar of Kuṇḍalinī— into their respective places via the path of Brahman (*brahmamārga*). Then, [one should contemplate] oneself in the form of the Goddess.
Having reflected thus, one should place the hand upon the heart and perform the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* (consecration of the vital breaths):

*Oṃ āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ haṃsaḥ | The vital breaths (*prāṇāḥ*) of the illustrious Bālā Tripurā are here as vital breaths; 13 times. The life-force (*jīva*) is stationed here; 13 times. All the senses (*sarvendriyāṇi*) are stationed here; 13 times. Speech, mind, sight, hearing, and smell...*

Having performed the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* (consecration of the vital breaths) with the mantra: "Having come here, may they remain happily for a long time, svāhā," one should perform the contemplation of the *ṛṣi*, *chandas*, and other attributes of one's own root-mantra (*mūlamantra*). For example:
"Of this Śrī Bālātripurā mantra, Dakṣiṇāmūrti is the *ṛṣi* and Paṅkti is the *chandas*."
The deity is Śrī Bālā Tripurā; Aiṃ is the seed-syllable (bīja), Sauḥ is the power (śakti), and Klīṃ is the peg (kīlaka).

Having remembered that the application (viniyoga) is at the beginning of the worship, one should perform the placement (nyāsa) according to the rules with palms joined in reverence: "Salutation to Dakṣiṇāmūrti the Seer (ṛṣi) on the head;
salutation to the Paṅkti metre (chandas) on the mouth; salutation to the deity Śrī Bālā Tripurā on the heart; [salutation] to the seed-syllable Aiṃ."

*Namo* to *guhya* (the secret place), *sauḥ* to *śakti*, *namaḥ* to the feet, *klīṃ* to the *kīlaka*, *namaḥ* to the navel for the *viniyoga*, and *namaḥ* to all limbs. *Aiṃ* *namaḥ* from the navel to the end of the feet; *klīṃ* *namaḥ* from the throat to the navel; *sauḥ* *namaḥ* from the head to the throat. *Aiṃ* *namaḥ* on the palm of the left hand.
Klīṃ, salutation to the right; Sauḥ, salutation to both.
p.
491) *Drāṃ*, salutation to the arrow of agitation, on the two thumbs; *Drīṃ*, salutation to the arrow of melting, on the two index fingers;
*Klīṃ*, salutation to the arrow of attraction, on the two middle fingers; *Blūṃ*, [salutation] to the arrow of subjugation...
"Namaḥ" is for the two ring fingers; thus is the ritual placement of the arrows (bāṇanyāsa).

*Sauḥ* to Kāma, *namaḥ* on the two thumbs; *klīṃ* to Manmatha, *namaḥ* on the two index fingers; *aiṃ* to Kandarpa, *namaḥ* on the two middle fingers; *blūṃ* to Makaradhvaja, *namaḥ* on the two ring fingers; *strīṃ* to Menaketa, *namaḥ* on the two little fingers—this is the *Kāmakara-nyāsa*.

Now follows the *nyāsa* of one's own root-mantra (*svamūlaka-nyāsa*). Aiṃ to the two thumbs, namaḥ; Klīṃ to the two index fingers; Sauḥ to the two middle fingers; Aiṃ to the two ring fingers; Klīṃ to the two little fingers;
Sauḥ to the palms and backs of the hands. In this same manner, perform the *nyāsa* on the heart and other limbs.

Then, having performed the internal placement of the Mātṛkās (antarmātṛkānyāsa) and the external placement of the Mātṛkās (barhirmātṛkānyāsa), one should perform the placement of the Mātṛkā-vidyā. As follows: *aiṃ* namaḥ on the wrist (*maṇibandha*), *klīṃ* namaḥ on the palm (*tala*), and *sauḥ* on the tip (*agra*)—thus on the right hand. Likewise on the left hand: *aiṃ* namaḥ on the armpit (*kakṣa*), *klīṃ* on the elbow (*kurpara*), and *sauḥ*...

*Aiṃ* at the right hand; likewise on the left. *Namaḥ* at the lower armpit; *klīṃ* at the knee; *sauḥ* at the tip of the foot—thus on the right; likewise on the left. *Aiṃ namaḥ* at the *liṅga*; *klīṃ* at the heart; *sauḥ* at the end of the *nāda*—this is the placement of the Vidyā (*vidyānyāsa*).
Now follows the placement of the nine wombs (*navayoninyāsa*): *aiṃ namaḥ* at the right ear; *klīṃ* at the left; *sauḥ* at the chin; *aiṃ*.

*klīṃ* in the right conch-shell, *sauḥ* in the left; *aiṃ* in the mouth, *klīṃ* in the right eye, *sauḥ* in the left; *aiṃ* in the nose, *klīṃ* in the right arm, *sauḥ* in the left; *aiṃ* in the belly, *klīṃ* in the right knee, *sauḥ* in the left;
*aiṃ* in the navel, *klīṃ* in the right foot, *sauḥ* in the left; *aiṃ* in the private parts, *klīṃ* in the right side, *sauḥ* in the left; and *aiṃ* in the heart.
Aiṃ on the right breast, Klīṃ on the left, and Sauḥ on the throat; thus is the Navayoni-nyāsa.

Now, the ritual placement (nyāsa) of Rati and the others: at the *mūlādhāra*, "Aiṃ, obeisance to Rati"; in the heart, "Klīṃ, obeisance to Prīti"; between the eyebrows, "Sauḥ, obeisance to Manobhavā. Furthermore, one should place these [mantras] again in these same locations: "Sauḥ, obeisance to Amṛteśī"; "Klīṃ, obeisance to Yogeśī"; "Aiṃ, obeisance to Viśvayoni. Then, once again, the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*).

According to the tradition: *Aiṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*; *klīṃ* to the head; *sauḥ* to the tuft of hair; *aiṃ* to the armor; *klīṃ* to the two eyes; *sauḥ* to the weapon, *phaṭ*. Having thus armored the body with these *nyāsa*s, one should [visualize] the Root-Mantra at the *mūlādhāra*, possessing a radiance equal to ten million flashes of lightning and resembling ten million suns.

O Dear One, O lady of beautiful countenance, one should contemplate that Supreme Reality— which is as cool as millions of moons, whose nature is like a lotus fiber, and which possesses a central point surrounded by three circles— through the descent of the upward-pointing power (*ūrdhva-śakti*) which is innate, by means of the firmness of the root power (*mūla-śakti*) and the awakening of the middle power (*madhya-śakti*), and which is filled with bliss through the mass of supreme bliss.
Having thus performed the internal sacrifice (*antaryajana*), one should perform the worship of the seat (*pīṭhapūjā*) within one's own body by means of ritual placement (*nyāsa*).
(p. 492) At the *mūlādhāra*: "Obeisance to Ādhāraśakti; obeisance to Prakṛti. At the *svādhiṣṭhāna*: "Obeisance to Kamaṭha."

To Śeṣa in Maṇipūra; to Earth in Anāhata; there likewise, to the Ocean of Nectar, to Maṇidvīpa, to the House of the Cintāmaṇi, to the Jewel Altar, and to the Jewel Throne. To the various hosts of sages in the cardinal directions;
to the various gods; to Dharma, salutation, on the right shoulder; to Jñāna, on the left shoulder; to Vairāgya.

To Bāma (Vāyu) on the right shoulder; to Aiśvarya (Sovereignty) on the right thigh; to Adharma (Unrighteousness) in the right side of the abdomen; to Ajñāna (Ignorance) on the right back; to Avairāgya (Non-detachment) on the left back; to Anaiśvarya (Lack of Sovereignty) in the left side of the abdomen;
to Śeṣa; to Padma; to the petals consisting of Prakṛti; to the filaments consisting of Vikṛti.
To the pericarp adorned with fifty letters; to the solar maṇḍala; to the lunar maṇḍala;
to the fiery maṇḍala; *saṃ* to Sattva; *raṃ* to Rajas; *taṃ* to Tamas; *āṃ* to Ātman;
*aṃ* to Antarātman; *paṃ* to Paramātman; *hrīṃ* to Jñānātman; on the petals, to Vāmā.
To Jyeṣṭhā; to Raudrī; to Ambikā; to Icchā; to Jñānā; to Kriyā; to Kubjikā; to Citrā; to Viṣaghnikā; to Dūtī; to Ānandā; in the center, to Manonmanī; Aiṃ, to Parā; to Aparā; to Parāparā; Hsauṃ.

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the seat with the words, "Salutation to Sadāśiva, the great ghost, upon his lotus-seat; salutation to the couch of Paramaśiva," one should meditate upon the venerable Bālā right there in the heart:
[as she who is] thinner than a lotus fiber, extending from the *mūlādhāra* to the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*).
Her braided hair, adorned with pure flowers, possessed the dark luster of wandering bees. || 1 ||
She was resplendent with a parted line of hair shimmering at the aperture of Brahma (brahmarandhra),
adorned with a jewel-tilaka fixed upon that parting, and radiant with a crown.
She is adorned with pure pearls and diamonds, wears a crown marked by a crescent moon,
and is resplendent with three eyes that have the dark luster of wandering bees.
She is supreme, adorned with great jewel earrings as radiant as the sun,
and decorated with necklaces of pearls shimmering like the color of Venus.
She is adorned with necklaces, armlets, and rows of leaf-patterned ornaments, surpassing even nectar with her shimmering luster;
she is resplendent in white garments as bright as the camphor-like waves of the Ganges.
She was adorned with creeper-like arms resembling sandalwood trees,
graced with shining ornaments such as bracelets, and radiant with the luster emanating from her wrists.
Adorned with sprout-like feet shaped like the petals of a red lotus,
she is decorated with pearl anklets that resemble stars. (7)
With one left hand she holds a book, and with the other,
O fair-faced one, she bestows the gesture of fearlessness upon the practitioners.

O Beloved, one should meditate upon the Goddess, who bestows subjugation, good fortune, and eloquence; she holds a rosary and the gesture of granting boons with her two right hands, and one should remember her as serene and white as milk, a kunda flower, and the moon. (9)

Thus, having meditated upon the illustrious Bālā Tripurā and worshipped her with mental offerings (*mānasopacāra*), and having performed mentally, according to one's capacity, the recitation of mantras (*japa*), fire-oblations (*homa*), and so forth, [one should offer]: "In the fire of my own self, kindled by the oblation of merit and demerit, I constantly offer the fluctuations of the senses through the channel of the *suṣumṇā* with the mind as the sacrificial ladle; Svāhā! Having thus contemplated the *kāmakalā*.
Meditating upon the venerable Bālā as previously described above that,
one should draw on the ground to one's left a hexagon containing two triangles, with a circle and a square outside the points;
then, having fashioned a triangle, a circular disc, and a mandala to one's right, one should worship the Support-Energy (Ādhāraśakti) therein.

There, having placed a support and set down a vessel such as a conch— purified over it with the Astra-mantra and filled with water using the Hrdaya-mantra— one should invoke the sacred waters (tīrtha) therein with the mantra beginning "O Gaṅgā and Yamunā," and having offered scents and other articles with the Praṇava, one should worship [the vessel] with the digits (kalā) of Fire, Sun, and Moon.
Having displayed the *dhenumudrā* and worshipped with one's own mantra,
one should sprinkle the maṇḍala made on one's left with the water of the general *arghya* prepared according to the prescribed rite; there,

having worshipped according to the sequence of the pedestal worship (*pīṭhapūjā*) beginning with "Obeisance to the Support-Energies" (*ādhāraśaktibhyaḥ*), one should [worship] the support (*ādhāra*) with "Obeisance."
Having washed it and placed it upon the mandala, one should worship it with the mantra: *raṃ vahnimaṇḍalāya daśakalātmane namaḥ*.

Then, having cleansed the water-pot (*kalaśa*) with *phaṭ*, filled it with the causal substance (*kāraṇa*), adorned it with red cloth, garlands, and so forth, and established it while regarding it as the Goddess, one worships it with: *aṃ arkamaṇḍalāya dvādaśakalātmane*.

Having worshipped with "Namaḥ" in the pitcher, having worshipped the substance with "Oṃ candramaṇḍalāya ṣoḍaśakalātmane namaḥ," having protected it with "Phaṭ," having veiled it with "Hūṃ," having gazed upon it with the root mantra, having sprinkled it with "Namaḥ," and having smelled the fragrance with the root mantra, one should place a flower in the pitcher and perform the rite of liberation from the curse (*śāpamocana*).
One should perform [this]:

"The Supreme Brahman alone is eternal, consisting of both the gross and the subtle; by that, I destroy for you the sin of killing a Brahmin born from a mere flash [of thought]. O you who are born from the solar disc, born from the abode of Varuṇa!"

O Goddess, who consists of the seed-syllable *amā*, may [this one] be liberated from the curse of Śukra. If the *praṇava* is the seed of the Vedas and consists of the bliss of Brahman, by that truth, O Queen of the Gods, may the sin of killing a Brahmin be removed. The purifier is supreme bliss; the purifier is the supreme essence.
Pavamāna is supreme knowledge; by means of that, I purify you. Released from the curse of Kṛṣṇa, released from the curse of Brahmā, and released from the curse of Rudra, become pure now.

Having recited this three times, then also three times: *oṃ vāṃ vīṃ vūṃ vaiṃ vauṃ vaḥ, obeisance to Surādevī, who has been liberated from the curse of Brahmā*. Then three times: *hrīṃ śrīṃ krāṃ krīṃ krūṃ kraiṃ krauṃ kraḥ, release [her] from the curse of Kṛṣṇa, release! cause nectar to flow, cause to flow! svāhā*. Haṃsaḥ.
