and these are the seed-syllables *krīṃ*, as well as others that are artificial. (2)
*Krīṃ* is the seed-syllable of the tongue. Now, the names of the seed-syllables of the snare (*vāgurā*): *Vāgurā*, *Vāyupūjyā*, and *Vātudāsya*—these three constitute the triad of seeds.
*Prīṃ* is said to be the seeds, while others are indeed false.
*Prīṃ* is the seed-syllable of Vāgurā. Now, regarding the names of the seed-syllables of Cāruka, they are stated in the *Muṇḍamālātantra*:
"Cāruka, Cārvaṅgī, Cārutā, and Ucchūnabījaka—these four are the *chrīṃ* seed-syllables; others are not true. (1)
The two seed-syllables of Cārvaṅgī are *cchrīṃ* and *aiṃ*. Next are the names of the lotus seeds, as stated in the Vāmakeśvara: "Padma, paṅkaja, payoja, nīraja, and likewise ambuja."
Indeed, the five seed-syllables beginning with the letter *ṭha*, as well as others, are unreal. || 1 ||

*Ṭhaḥ* is the seed-syllable of the lotus. The manifest [mantra] is: *Oṃ krīṃ śrīṃ prīṃ prīṃ cchrīṃ ucchiṣṭhacaṇḍālini devi mahāpiśācini mātaṅgīdevi krīṃ ṭhaḥ hrīṃ ṭhaḥ aiṃ ṭhaḥ svāhā*. This is the root mantra of Mātaṅgī. Now, the extraction of the Śārikā mantra is stated:
In his own work, the *Tripurāśiromaṇi*:
"The Tāraka, Māyā, Śrī, Kūrca, Sindhu, Śūnya, and Kalyāṇa—this is remembered as the seven-syllable seed-mantra (bīja) of the goddess Śārikā. (1)
And before the pillar, one should know the supreme mantra of Śārikā.
In that regard, the names of the seed-syllables of Sindhu are stated in the Vāmakeśvara:
"Sindhura, Gaṇa, Ghoṇā, and Hastina."
Likewise, the elephant;
and the four artificial *phrāṃ* seed-syllables, as well as others. || 1 ||

*Phrāṃ* is the seed-syllable of the Sindhu. Next are the names of the void-seeds (*śūnyabīja*), as stated in the *Bhairavatantra*: "The void (*śūnya*), the sky (*kha*), the ether (*ambara*), and the firmament (*vyoma*)—these four are in the seed-syllable *Ām*.
And the letter *ha* should also be understood as having been spoken [therein], as stated in the Rudrayāmala. || 1 ||
Another thing to be known, O you who are endowed with devotion to Tārā, is the unreal (*asatya*).

*Ām* (and *Haṃ*) is the seed-syllable of emptiness (*śūnya*). Following that are the names of the auspicious seeds; therein: "Auspiciousness" (*kalyāṇa*), "Bliss" (*śarma*), "Welfare" (*śam*), and "Purity" (*śubha*)—these four.
Another falsehood is to be known, O daughter of Parvateśvara. (1)

The two seed-syllables of *śarma* are *sauḥ* and *śa*. The *prakāśa* is: *oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hūṃ phrāṃ āṃ śāṃ śārikāyai namaḥ*. Thus it is said. Then, the extraction of the Queen’s mantra from the *Śyāmātantra*:
"The *tāra* (oṃ), *lajjā* (hrīṃ), *śrī* (śrīṃ), fire (raṃ), desire (kṛm), and power (hrīṃ) constitute the six syllables."
The seed-syllable should be known as the six-headed one; from that, one should extract the sprout.
Likewise, for the Blessed Queen, the word *māyā* and the two *ṭha*s are placed at the end;
together with these, the mantra of the Queen is said to consist of fifteen syllables.
Thus it is said. Regarding that, the names of the seed-syllable of fire (agnibīja) are given in the Śyāmātantra:
"Agni, Repha, Vahni, Hutabhuj, and Havyavāhana—this is the extraction of the seed-syllable 'Raṃ'; indeed, this is remembered as the artificial [form], while the other is different. (1)
*Raṃ* is the seed-syllable of Agni. *Prakāśa*: *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ rāṃ klīṃ sauḥ bhagavatyai rājñyai hrīṃ svāhā*. Thus [ends the mantra]. Now, the extraction of the Bhīḍā-mantra from the *Kulacūḍāmaṇi*:
"The *praṇava* (oṃ), *vibhūti* (hrīṃ), and likewise *harikāntā* (śrīṃ)."
Having joined the seed-syllables of Viyat, Śakti, and Agni, as well as Vāgbhava.
One should utter "Madana" and likewise the seed-syllable of doubt (Śaṅkābīja), which consists of seven syllables;
when joined with two "Ṭha"s, it is declared as the twenty-syllabled mantra.
(Tāra, Parā, Ramā, Vedī, Candramanmatha, Śakti, Bhīḍābhagavatī—thus [is the mantra], ending with "O you who have the form of a swan" and the two syllables *ṭha*.
3. [The revealed mantra: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsrāṃ aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ bhīḍābhagavati haṃsarūpiṇi.

Svāhā. Thus. Now, the extraction of the Jvālāmukhī mantra from the *Śāradātilaka-ṭīkā*: "The *tāra* (oṃ), the *lajjā* (hrīṃ), and the *śrī* (śrīṃ), and likewise at the end the *kūrca* (hūṃ), *hara* (huṃ), and *payaḥ* (phaṭ).
And the three-syllable seed-mantra of the goddess Jvālāmukhī, O Sovereign of the Gods, is as follows: [kh: the six-syllable mantra].
(Tāraṃ, lajjā, śriyaṃ, and likewise "jvālāmukhi mama," then "sarvaśatrūn bhakṣaya" twice at the end, followed by the *kūrca* [hūṃ] and the *harapayaḥ* [phaṭ].
Explicitly: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ jvālāmukhi mama sarvaśatrūn bhakṣaya 2 hūṃ phaṭ.
phaṭ svāhā. Thus.
The ten sciences have been declared by me as they are determined in the scriptures;
these goddesses, adorned with various jewels, bestow the desired objects upon practitioners. (1)
I shall describe the qualities of these ten sciences; listen, O Dakṣiṇāmūrti! Tripurā bestows liberation, and Lakṣmī bestows prosperity.
The Goddess of Speech bestows stable knowledge in every birth.
Tārā bestows knowledge as well as liberation, while Bhuvaneśvarī grants sovereignty; Mātaṅgī constantly removes the fear of enemies and Rākṣasas.
Śārikā indeed bestows auspiciousness; Rājñī grants a kingdom; and Bhīḍādevī surely bestows offspring that pervade the universe.
The goddess Jvālāmukhī bestows wealth upon her devotees;
just as these ten Vidyās grant their desired fruits to devotees through worship, fire-oblations, recitation, and other rites, so do these great goddesses. || 5 ||

Thus ends the first ritual manual (kalpa), titled "The Exposition of the Treasury for Extracting the Mantras of the Ten Vidyās," within the *Uddhārakośa*, the essence of all Āgamas, composed by the venerable sage Dakṣiṇāmūrti. || 1 ||
p.
532) Now follows the second alternative.
Śrī Īśvara said: Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim Tripurā surrounded by her retinue;
I shall tell you the extraction of the mantras for those six companions. 1.
Akṣobhya said:
O Guru, born of the Creator, you who are proficient in various scriptures, I desire to hear all the mantras for the sake of complete liberation. || 2 ||
Dakṣiṇāmūrti said:
"Listen, O noble Akṣobhya; I shall explain everything according to its true nature.
The ten Vidyās are Bhadrakālī, Turī, and Chinnamastakā. (3)
O handsome one, Dakṣiṇākālikā, Śyāmā, and Kālarātrī—
of those six companions, I shall tell you the extraction of their mantras.
First, therein is the extraction of the mantra of Bhadrakālī. In the Śyāmātantra:
"Three Kālīs, a pair of Kūrca-syllables, a pair of Lañjās, and the word 'Bhadrikā'; one should utter the word 'Bhadrakālī' [and then] the seed-syllables in reverse order. (1)
The great mantra of Bhadrakālī is joined with two *ṭha* syllables.
Regarding the names of the seed-syllable (*bīja*) of Bhadrikā therein, the *Muṇḍamālā-tantra* states:
"Bhadrikā, Bhāsvatī, and Bhīmā—this triad is remembered within the *bhaiṃ* seed-syllable."
O one born of the lineage of Brahmā, another falsehood is to be known. || 1 ||
Aloud: *krīṃ 3 hūṃ 2 hrīṃ 2 bhaiṃ bhadrakāli bhaiṃ hrīṃ 2 hūṃ 2 krīṃ 3 svāhā*. Thus.
(p. 533) Now follows the extraction of the mantra of the Fourth (Turya). In the *Svatantra*:
"The Praṇava, the Savior, the Light, the Star—indeed, at the end, the word 'Namaḥ'."
This is declared by Śambhu himself in the Svatantra to be the root of Turyā.
Now, regarding the extraction of the seed-syllables (bīja) of the Star-Light (Tārakājyotis) from the *Kāmeśvara Tantra*: "Ṛṃ, kṣaṃ, bhaṃ—these are the five seed-syllables of the Star-Light.
Oṃ truṃ trauṃ troṃ, salutation to the Great Fourth (Mahāturya). Thus it is revealed.
Now follows the extraction of the mantra of Chinnamastā. In the *Chinnāśiromaṇi*:
"O Goddess of the Suras, [the mantra consists of] Tryambaka, Sakalā, Padmā, and Cāruka;
at the end is the Ucchūna seed-syllable, joined with two *phaṭ*s and two *ṭha*s. (1)
Aloud: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ cchrīṃ Chinnamastake cchrīṃ phaṭ svāhā. Thus.
The second division in the *Āgamalaharī*:
"Lakṣmī, Lañjā, Māyā, and then the twelve-syllable Mātrā;
the two Māyās of Vajravairocanī, conjoined with Phaṭ and Svāhā. (1)
*Prakāśam*: Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ Vajravairocanīye Hrīṃ Hrīṃ Phaṭ Svāhā. Thus [ends the section]. Now, the extraction of the mantra of Dakṣiṇākālī from the *Śyāmārahasya*:
"The triad of *kuntī*, the pair of *tīra*, the pair of *kṣāmā*, and then the name."
On the right is Kālikā; thus, at the end, there is again a triad of Kālīs.
O Goddess of the Suras, there is a pair of *kūrca*s, a pair of *parā*s, and water;
this is the twenty-two-syllable mantra of Dakṣiṇā Kālikā.
The public recitation: *krīṃ 3 hūṃ 2 hrīṃ 2 dakṣiṇe kālike krīṃ 3 hūṃ 2 hrīṃ 2 svāhā*. Thus. Now follows the extraction of the mantra of Śyāmā. In that regard, the *Śyāmātantra* states:
"The deer-eyed one (*hariṇākṣī*), the modest one (*lajjā*), Kālī, and the four tongues."
Then, O Śyāma, who are the essence of nectar, release me from Kṛṣṇa’s curse.
"O Śyāmā, cause the nectar to flow, svāhā!"—this is declared to be the mantra of Śyāmā.
[The revealed mantra is: *Śrīṃ hrīṃ krīṃ krīṃ krīṃ krīṃ krīṃ*, O Śyāmā, essence of nectar, release [me] from the curse of Kṛṣṇa; cause the nectar to flow, svāhā! Thus. Now...
The extraction of the mantra of Kālarātrī. And it is said in the *Kālarātrīkalpa* (p. 534):
The Praṇava, Vāsanā, Māyā, Manmatha, and Kamalodbhava—this is to be known as the five-headed seed-syllable; from that, one should extract the sprout.
Then, having omitted the name in the middle, say "bring all under control" at the end;
O passionate one, omitting the name in the middle, say "give vigor" twice.
Likewise, at the end, "Gaṇeśvaryai" and "Viśvam" are proclaimed.
[The mantra] begins with *prakāśam*: *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ kāhneśvari sarvajanamanohari sarvamukhastambhini sarvarājavaśaṅkari sarvaduṣṭanirdalini sarvastrīpuruṣakarṣiṇi*.
Break the shackles of the captives! Shatter all enemies! Crush those who hate us! Paralyze everyone!
With the weapon of delusion, drive away the hater! Bring everything under control! Svāhā! Bestow [blessings] twice!
O Sarvakālarātri, O Kāminī, obeisance to Gaṇeśvarī! Now, the divisions:
O Queen of the Gods, the child-form of Tripurā should be known as consisting of twelve aspects. || 3 ||
And it is said in the Muṇḍamālā Tantra:
"O Goddess, that Tripurā-hṛdaya should be known as consisting of twelve parts;
O Goddess, that which is proclaimed for the sake of liberation alone is remembered as auspicious. (1)
In the Uḍḍāmara [Tantra], the sixteen-syllable Vidyā of Śrī is to be known as eightfold;
O Goddess, that which has been indicated is remembered as granting immediate liberation. (1)
Likewise, in his own work, the *Tripurāśiromaṇi*, [it is said]: "This seed-mantra of Tripurā is likewise remembered as being eightfold;
it may be mastered in eight years or even in eight months. (1)
Or else, within eight days, one may recognize the signs of liberation;
the two-fold classification of Lakṣmī has been declared by the one clad in animal hide (Śiva).
One shall obtain the fruit [of worshiping] Lakṣmī and Rukmiṇī in three years.
Now, the varieties of Sarasvatī according to the *Kāminīkalpa* (p.
Vāgdevī, Vāṇī, Sarasvatī, and Analapriyā—these are the renowned varieties; their fruit is obtained within four years.
Then, regarding the divisions of Tārā, it is stated in the Bhairavatantra:
"Tārā, Tāriṇī, likewise Ekajaṭā, Nīlasarasvatī, and Ugratārā are thus proclaimed. (1)
The five varieties of Tārā have thus been revealed by Akṣobhya.
Now, regarding the varieties of Bhuvaneśvarī, it is said in the Bhairava-tantra:
"Bhairavī, Bhīmarūpā, and Bhīmā are also Bhuvaneśvarī."
The Goddess, through devotion, bestows her fruit eternally during every cycle of four years.
Now, regarding the divisions of Mātaṅgī, it is stated in the Rudrayāmala: "The identity of Mātaṅgī and Sumukhī was taught by the sage Mataṅga.
Likewise, there are Mātaṅgī, Cakriṇī, the goddess Kubjikā, and Śāmbarī. (1)
There are four varieties of Devī, and their fruit is obtained within four years.
Now, regarding the two varieties of Śārikā:
Śārikā, likewise Aparṇā, and Phaladā [grant results] within two years.
Now, the classifications of the Rājñīs:
two types of Rājñīs have been declared—the Rājñī and the Khagagāminī.
Through devotion, the Rājñī bestows a kingdom within two years. (1)
In the *Kulikārṇava*:
"She is free from fear and devoid of duality, increasing the fortune of all beings.
Now, regarding Jvālāmukhī, in the *Jvālāśiromaṇi*:
Then Tārā, Jvālāmukhī, and likewise Ambikā in the form of Bhagā—these three varieties of Jvālā are said to bestow fruits according to one's desire. || 1 ||
The various divisions of these ten vidyās have been illustrated;
among them, first are the divisions of Tripurā, as stated in the *Tripurātilaka* and the *Muṇḍamālātantra*:
Tripurā, Bhairavī-vidyā, Hiṅgulā, Caṇḍikā, as well as Cāmuṇḍā, Nārasiṃhī, Aindrī, and Haimavatīśvarī. (1)
Mṛḍānī, Vāruṇī, Durgā, and Mahātripurasundarī—these twelve varieties of the Goddess have indeed been proclaimed by the wielder of the trident. (2)
Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Sauḥ! O Tripurā, you who wear the moon as your garment; Kāma! O Śaradbhairavī! Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! Likewise, Kamalā in Hiṅgula; Kṣāma! And Tryakṣa, O Caṇḍikā!
O Cāmuṇḍā, Hasakalahrīṃ and Sakalahrīṃ! Likewise, O Śrīnārasiṃhī! And indeed, O Aindrī, the wandering one!
Hrīṃ is Madana, Kāma; Parā is Rukmiṇī. || 3 ||
O Durgā, you are remembered by Śambhu as the Goddess, the Sovereign of Himavat, Kamalā, Lañjā, as well as Manmatha,
Candra, Vāruṇī, Kaeīlaparā, Śrīṃ, Hrīṃ, Klīṃ, Cāraṇa, Śarad, Tryakṣa, Parā, and Rukmiṇī.
The sixteen-fold ritual procedure for Vidyāśrī should be performed together with the reverse state. || 4 ||
Thus end the variations of the sixteen-syllable [mantras]. [In public: Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Sauḥ Tripure; Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ Bhairavi;
Oṃ Hrīṃ Sauḥ Hiṅgule; Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Oṃ Caṇḍike; Hasakalahrīṃ Cāmuṇḍe; Sakalahrīṃ Śrī Nārasiṃhi; Oṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Aindri; Klīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Devī.
O Sovereign Lady of the Himavat! Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Mṛḍāni! Aiṃ Vāruṇi! Kaeīlahrīṃ Durge!
Śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ aiṃ sauḥ oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kaeīlahrīṃ hasakahalahrīṃ sakalahrīṃ sauḥ aiṃ klīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ Mahātripurasundarī! Thus [it is said].
The Goddess said:
O Maheśvara, knower of the three times, you who are compassionate toward those who have come for refuge,
you ought to speak the mantras of the goddesses who are endowed with various divisions.
Īśvara said:
O Goddess of gods, out of compassion for you, I shall explain that in brief.
Now, regarding the extraction of the mantra of Śrī, as it was stated in the Bhairavatantra:
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ—the two seeds of Hariṇākṣī grant immediate fruit;
then the three-eyed one (tryakṣa), followed by hrīṃ and the water of Śakti at the end—thus it was declared by Dhūrjaṭi. (1)
Now follows the extraction of the mantra of Rukmiṇī:
Oṃ Hrīṃ; likewise, for Rukmiṇī, there is the Tāra (Oṃ), Lakṣmī (Śrīṃ), and Apas (Hrīṃ);
at the end, O Maheśānī, these two are said to be the varieties of Lakṣmī. (1)

[Aloud: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ Lakṣmī oṃ hrīṃ saḥ svāhā | Oṃ hrīṃ Rukmiṇī oṃ śrīṃ svāhā || Now, the varieties of Sarasvatī: "To" (t), "Mā" (m), and "Parā" (p)—these are the Vāgbhava [seed-syllable]; "Kṣāmā" (kṣām) and "Tāra" (oṃ) are also declared by the Supreme Lord.
For this child bestows the fruit of the Goddess of Speech upon men, and is the supreme refuge for those intent on liberation. || 4 ||
[Aloud: Oṃ hrīṃ aiṃ hrīṃ oṃ, obeisance to Vāgdevatā. Now, the mantra of the Goddess Vāṇī:
The syllable Om (tāra), the seed-syllable above Lañjā (aiṃ), and at the end [the word] stambha is declared [as the mantra].
[Aloud: Oṃ hrīṃ aiṃ, obeisance to Vāṇī Bhagavatī. Now, the mantra of Sarasvatī:

"O Goddess with beautiful limbs, O Goddess of Prosperity, [the syllable] tryakṣa, then 'to Sarasvatī,' and at the end 'obeisance'—thus it has been declared by me, O Parameśānī, O Daughter of the Mountain. (5)

[In] public: *aiṃ hrīṃ oṃ sarasvatyai namaḥ*. Now, the mantra of Analapriyā: *Tāraṃ* (Oṃ), *lajjā* (Hrīṃ), and *vāgbhavaṃ* (Aiṃ) [are placed] in the middle of "Analapriye"; then the *tryakṣaṃ* (Tryambaka), the *viśvaṃ* (Viśvamaya), and likewise at the end, "Parvateśvaranandini. (6)
O fair-faced one, there are four divisions of the goddess Sarasvatī.
The first is *prakāśa*: Oṃ hrīṃ aiṃ analapriye oṃ namaḥ.

Now, the varieties of Tārā are revealed: Oṃ aiṃ hūṃ hrīṃ aiṃ hūṃ tāre phaṭ svāhā | Oṃ hrīṃ aiṃ hūṃ ugratāre phaṭ svāhā | Oṃ strīṃ aiṃ hūṃ ekajaṭe phaṭ svāhā | Oṃ hrīṃ aiṃ hūṃ nīlasarasvatī phaṭ svāhā |
Oṃ hrāṃ strīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ hūṃ Ugratāre phaṭ svāhā. Thus end the varieties of Tārā.
Now, the variations of Bhuvaneśvarī: Oṃ bhairavyai namaḥ | Oṃ hrīṃ bhīmarūpāyai namaḥ | Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ bhīmāyai namaḥ | Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ bhuvaneśvaryai namaḥ | Thus [it is said].

Now, the varieties of Mātaṅgī are revealed: Oṃ krīṃ śrīṃ prīṃ prīṃ chrīṃ ucchiṣṭacaṇḍālini devi mahāpiśācini mātaṅgi devi krīṃ ṭhaḥ hrīṃ ṭhaḥ aiṃ ṭhaḥ svāhā. This is the twenty-two-syllable mantra of Sumukhī, ending with svāhā. Oṃ.
O Ucchiṣṭacaṇḍālinī,
O fair-faced Goddess Mahāpiśācinī, hrīṃ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ (22). Now, [the mantra] of Cakriṇī:
Oṃ krīṃ śrīṃ mahācakriṇi aiṃ ṭhaḥ svāhā. Now, for Kubjikā:
Oṃ śrīṃ prīṃ kubjike devi hrīṃ ṭhaḥ svāhā. Now, for Śāmbarī: Oṃ prīṃ devi śāmbari krīṃ ṭhaḥ svāhā.
Now, the two varieties of Śārikā: therein, the root-mantra of Aparṇā is *oṃ hūṃ śrīṃ āṃ śāṃ devyai aparṇāyai namaḥ*. [Next, the root-mantra of Haimavatīśvarī:
The varieties of Jvālāmukhī: therein, the root-mantra of Ambikā is *oṃ hrīṃ mātarambike hūṃ phaṭ*.
Svāhā! Now, for the one whose form is the vulva (bhagarūpiṇī): Oṃ śrīṃ devi bhagarūpiṇi hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
O Pārvatī, these seed-mantras (bījamantras) have been proclaimed by me;
now listen as I speak of other [mantras] for these ten Vidyās.
Just as the goddess Bhadrakālī is Dakṣiṇā Kālikā,
so too is Turi devoid of differentiation and the bestower of desired fruits.
[Aloud: Krīṃ 3 Hūṃ 2 Hrīṃ 2 Bhaiṃ Bhadrakāli Bhaiṃ Hrīṃ 2 Hūṃ 2 Krīṃ 3 Svāhā!
Krīṃ 3 Hūṃ 2 Hrīṃ 2 Dakṣiṇe Kālike Krīṃ 3 Hūṃ 2 Hrīṃ 2 Svāhā. (22)
Now, Chinnamastā is of two kinds: First: *oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ śrīṃ śrīṃ chinnamastake śrīṃ phaṭ svāhā*.
Second: *oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aiṃ vajravairocani hrīṃ hrīṃ phaṭ svāhā*.
Dakṣiṇā, Kālikā, Śyāmā, Kālarātrī, and Sureśvarī—these are devoid of distinction and bestow the fruits of one's desires according to wish. || 9 ||

Thus ends the second ritual manual (*kalpa*), which indicates the divisions of the treasury for extracting the mantras of the six goddesses, within the *Uddhārakośa*, the essence of all Agamas, composed by the venerable sage Dakṣiṇāmūrti. || 2 ||
p. 539) Now begins the third ritual procedure (kalpa).
Īśvara said:
Now, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the supreme mantra of the goddesses;
listen with a one-pointed mind, for I speak out of my regard for your curiosity. 1.
At that time, Dakṣiṇāmūrti likewise spoke the Ṣoḍaśī-vidyā to his disciple; the sage Akṣobhya rejoiced.
At that time, all the sages, eager and desiring the mantra, arrived at the hermitage of that sage, which was frequented by other munis.
Lohitoddālaka, Śaṅkha, Mātaṅga, Puṇḍarīka, and Jau,
as well as Śāṇḍilya and Gālava— these went to his hermitage.
Having all assembled together, they spoke thus to that Śrī Dakṣiṇāmūrti, the bull among sages;
they indeed inquired of one another regarding the mantras of their respective family deities (kuladevatās), which are worthy of worship and bestowers of auspiciousness. || 5 ||
The illustrious Dakṣiṇāmūrti said:
"Listen, all you sages; I shall declare a most wonderful and supreme truth.
In this world of moving and unmoving beings, the Goddess Tripurasundarī [is the sovereign]."
Nowhere else is there anyone like her, who is the crest-jewel upon the head of the Goddess;
and from her lotus-face, seven goddesses have been heard by me.
Bestowing desired fruits and removing all diseases and fears,
those [mantras] heard from his mouth grant their results in a very short time. (8)
The sages said:
Who are the goddesses? What are their names? And what indeed are their mantras?
O brahmin-sage, show us favor if you have compassion for us.
The Sage said:
Out of supreme affection for the goddesses, listen now to the mantras,
by the mere hearing of which one obtains the fruit of a horse-sacrifice.
Īśvara said: The Lord Dakṣiṇāmūrti spoke again to the lords of sages (or Manus).
The seven sciences were previously proclaimed as the deities, beginning with Vajrayoginī. || 11 ||
O daughter of Parvateśvara, I shall declare their names,
which were revealed in truth by Dakṣiṇāmūrti.
The goddess Śrī Vajrayoginī, Vārāhī, and likewise Śāradā;
Kāmeśvarī, Gaurī, and likewise Annapūrṇā as well. (13)
Indeed, these seven goddesses, the mistresses of the family speech, have been heard by me;
for them, the seven sciences were proclaimed by Dakṣiṇāmūrti. (14)
Relying upon the power of these [energies], O Goddess, Mistress of the Gods, Tripurasundarī created this universe and it is sustained by her. (15)
"In her hand as well, there is likewise the entire universe, including all that is mobile and immobile.
The sage said:
"I have heard this nectar of speech from the lotus-face of her mouth."
I shall declare their mantras; listen, O best of sages! || 16 ||
Now, the extraction of mantras: first, the extraction of the mantra of Vajrayoginī. And it is said in the *Svatantro*:
"The *praṇava* (oṃ), the *sakalā* (hrīḥ), and two seed-syllables that bestow fruit.
In the middle, it is for Vajrayoginī; indeed, at the end, water is prescribed. || 1 ||
Aloud: Oṃ hrīṃ vajrayoginyai svāhā.
Whoever enters into battle after having fully recited her mantra shall conquer all enemies and return home in well-being. || 17 ||
O Goddess, if a person recites these two seed-syllables for twelve days, his desired accomplishment will surely come to pass. (18)
Having imparted its seed-mantra to her, a man should mutter it in a secluded place;
then, when his wife has bathed after her menses, the man should engage in sexual union with her. (19)
O Goddess of the gods, one should draw [this] together with Śukra and seven medicinal herbs. Having drawn this mantra-empowered yantra of hers, he shall become a king.
Having written it, one should wear it upon the head; one will become a conqueror of the three worlds.
O Goddess of the Gods, at the time of its enjoyment, one should recite the mantra.
A man should have sexual intercourse with this beloved woman; he shall be endowed with many sons.
That man who wears her yantra along with its mantra upon his arm [shall attain these results]. || 22 ||
As long as he lives, his enemy shall not survive, provided that man who wears this yantra along with its mantra upon his heart. (23)
As long as he lives, so long shall he possess prosperity—that man who wears her yantra along with the mantra upon his belly. || 24 ||
In debate, he who knows the nature of speech will suddenly overcome his enemies;
this was heard by me from the lotus-face of that Tripurasundarī. (25)
"O best of sages, this fruit is most wondrous," so says the *Vajrayoginī*. Now, regarding the extraction of the mantra of Vārāhī, it is stated in her own work, the *Tripurātilaka*:
"The *vāsanā*, the *vālhīka*, and combined with the seed-syllable of *tamas*..."
One should extract the Vāgbhava, the Sauśmaka, and then the Pallava. || 1 ||
And likewise to the Blessed One Vārtālī, and to the deity Vārāhī; to Varāhamukhī as well, and to Vāsanā and Maṭha. (2)
Then, O Maheśvarī, there are Paṅkaja, Payoja, Hara, and Nīra;
and for the Blessed Vārāhī, there is the mantra consisting of thirty-one syllables.
Regarding the names of the *vālhīka* seeds, the *Muṇḍamālātantra* states:
"O lords of sages, *vālhīka*, *maṭhasaṃjña*, and *hiṅgubīja*."
Having extracted the seed-syllable *glauṃ*, one should speak another [mantra], which is otherwise false.
Now, the names of the seed-syllable of darkness (*tamobīja*) are given in the *Svatantrotantra*:
"The seed-syllable of darkness, likewise *dvānta*, *moha*, and *timira*;
these are the extractions of the seed-syllable *laṃ*, while others are artificial. (1)

The public [mantra]: *Aiṃ glauṃ laṃ aiṃ namo bhagavati vārtāli vārāhi devate varāhamukhi aiṃ glauṃ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ phaṭ svāhā*. This is Vārāhī. Now follows the extraction of the mantra of Śāradā, as stated in the Śāradā-paṭala:
One should know that *tāra* (oṃ), *māyā* (hrīṃ), and *madana* (klīṃ) constitute the *auśmaka*;
the six-syllable mantra is to be known as the *śiras*, and from that, one should extract the *pallava*. || 1 ||
To the Goddess Śāradā, at the end [of the mantra], there is Lañjā and two *ṭha*s.
The revealed [mantra] is: *oṃ hrīṃ klīṃ sauḥ namo bhagavatyai śāradāyai hrīṃ svāhā*. Now follows the extraction of the Kāmeśvarī mantra from the Bhairavapaṭala:

Having joined together Māyā and the deer-eyed woman (hariṇākṣī), the moon (candra) and the cool-rayed one (śītāṃśu), as well as the two—the god of love (madana) and the darkness (dhvānta)—one obtains the seed-syllable of the breasts (stanabījakam). || 1 ||
Manu is to be known as having seven heads; from that, one should extract the sprout.
Then, O Goddess, there is the one called Jṛmbhaṇā, and likewise Kāmeśvarī. (2)
Then, at the end, water is indeed mentioned for Bāṇadevatā;
the mantra of the Great Goddess Kāmeśvarī consists of twenty-two syllables. (3)
Regarding the names of the seed-syllable of the Moon, they are stated in the *Kālīsarvasva*:
"The Moon (*candra*), the Cool-rayed One (*śītāṃśu*), the Indu, and also the Lord of the Night (*śarvarīpati*).
The moon, the lord of stars, possesses rays of nectar, as do other artificial [lamps]. || 1 ||

The two lunar seeds are *aiṃ* and *drāṃ*. Now, regarding the names of the wave-seeds (*ūrmibīja*), it is said in that same [text]: "Wave (*ūrmi*), ripple (*vīci*), and likewise surge (*taraṅga*)—this triad is remembered [as such].
*Blūṃ* is the extraction of the seed-syllables; there are others as well which are artificial."

Now, the names for the breasts are stated in the *Āgamālaṅkāra*: "Stana-bīja, kuca, uroja, hṛd-ja, and jaṃ—these are the names for the seeds (origins) of the breasts; there are also others that are artificial. (1)

The public [mantra]: *hrīṃ śrīṃ drāṃ drīṃ klīṃ blūṃ jaṃ*, O Kāmeśvarī, goddess of the arrow named Jṛmbhaṇā, *svāhā*. Thus it is stated in the Bhairavapaṭala. Now follows the extraction of the Gaurī-mantra from the Tripurāśiromaṇi:
The Praṇava, Kamalā, Māyā, and Vālhīka;
likewise, O Goddess Gaurī, the seed-syllable of Śiva, and Śarva with the two Ṭhas. (1)
"The twelve-syllable mantra of the goddess Mahāgaurī is for the child [initiate].
Regarding that, the names of the seed-syllables of Śiva are stated in the *Kulacūḍāmaṇi*:
"The seed-syllable of Śiva is Śambhu, Śarva, and indeed Śaṅkara."
And the four seeds, both natural and artificial. || 1 ||
Aloud: Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ glauṃ gaṃ devi gauri gīṃ svāhā (12).
Now, the extraction of the mantra of Annapūrṇā from the Kāmeśvarī Tantra: "Tāra (Oṃ), Parā, Kamalā, and Mīnaketana;
then Viśva, followed by Bhagavati, and then Māheśvari. (1)
In the *Annadāpūrṇā*, a pair of *ṭha* syllables is recorded as the twenty-syllable mantra;
"Mīnaketana" is the name of the *doṣa*. And it is stated in the author’s own work, the *Tripurasundarīsarvasva*:
"The three-eyed one (*tryakṣa*), *māyā*, *padmā*, and *kāma* are declared to be the *viśva*."
O beautiful lady, the seed-syllable should be known as having six heads, together with Viśva.

Thus is the extraction [of the mantra]. [Now] openly: *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ namo bhagavati māheśvari annapūrṇe svāhā*. Now follows the extraction of the *Kulavāgīśvarī* mantra, as stated in the *Muṇḍamālā Tantra*:
One should extract the Praṇava, Madana, Skanda, and Nārāyaṇapriyā; likewise the Taṭa and the Icchā-bīja, and thereafter the Pallava. (1)
After that, [the syllable] *jhaṣa* is in the hand; likewise, *kulavāgīśvarī* follows.
At the end is the seed-syllable of latent desire (*vāsanā*), as well as the lotus (*padma*) and the water-born flower (*nīraja*).
O Goddess of the Suras, the seed-syllable of Nartakī is the lotus and water;
this is the twenty-four-syllable mantra of the goddess Kulavāgīśvarī. (3)
Regarding the names of the seed-syllable of Will (*icchā-bīja*) in the *Vāmakeśvara*:
"The seed-syllable of Will, longing, desire, and craving—these are the four names of the seed-syllable. Furthermore, there are other artificial names for the seed-syllable *jhaṃ*. (1)

Now, regarding the names of the seed-syllable (bīja) of the dancer, it is stated in the *Chinnārahasya*: "The dancer's seed-syllable is extremely fierce; likewise, 'veśyā', 'gaṇikā', 'paṇyastrī'—these are the five names. 'Phrīṃ' is the supreme untruth of the seed-syllable. (1)
The fault [in the previous example] is the identity of *ambuja* and *ambhoja*. [The mantra is as follows: *oṃ klīṃ hrāṃ śrīṃ hūṃ jhaṃ jhaṣahaste kulavāgīśvari aiṃṭhaḥ jhaṃṭhaḥ phrīṃṭhaḥ svāhā* (24).
O Great Goddess, these seven sciences have been proclaimed by me;
today, out of devotion to you, I shall grant whatever is dear to your heart that pleases you.
"Tell me quickly, O Goddess; I shall explain that to you in great detail.
The Illustrious Goddess said:
"What are those supreme Manus like for the five who are called 'Bālakas'?"
Out of compassion, they were previously indicated to me, but not fully revealed.
The sages said:
"O Brahmarṣi, knower of all scriptures, we have heard everything from your mouth;
you should now speak to us, the five Kumāras, regarding the Manus. (28)
Dakṣiṇāmūrti, the Lord, speaks to the sages and to Pārvatī.
The venerable Lord said: "Listen, O Pārvatī, Queen of the Gods, O Śivā, regarding the great seers of old."
I shall explain to you in accordance with reality that which was spoken by Dakṣiṇāmūrti.
Heramba, Śarajanman, Kārtavīryārjuna, Hanumat, and Bhairava— these are declared to be the five Bālakas. (30)
Thus it is stated in the Bhairavītantra and the Vāmakeśvara:
"Heramba, Śarajanman, as well as Mahāmṛtyuñjaya, Kārtavīryārjuna, Hanumat, and likewise Bhairava. (1)
The six Kumāras mentioned in the Tantra have been spoken of by me myself. Also in the Rudrayāmala:
"Gaṇeśa, Vaṭuka, Skanda, and likewise Mṛtyuñjaya..."
Kārtavīryārjuna was likewise, as were Sugrīva and Hanumān. || 1 ||
In the *Yāmala*, seven children (*bālaka*) are spoken of beginning with the word "Rudra.

Among them, first is the extraction of the mantra of Gaṇeśa from the *Rudrayāmala*: [The syllables] *praṇava* (oṃ), *kamalā* (śrīṃ), *lajjā* (hrīṃ), *kandarpa* (klīṃ), and the seed-syllable of *maṭha* (gaṃ).
Then one should extract the pallava-mantra of Śaṅkara, which consists of six syllables.
"Obeisance to Gaṇapati," [he says] in the west; then "the bestower of boons";
and thereafter, "bring all people under my control. (2)
It should be known that there are two *ṭha*s at the beginning; thus, the mantra consists of twenty-eight syllables.
As stated in the *Prakāśa*: *oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ glauṃ gaṃ gaṇapataye varavarada sarvajanaṃ me vaśamānaya svāhā*. Now, the extraction of the mantra of Kumāra from the *Kulacūḍāmaṇi*:
The Praṇava and the seed-syllable of the skin (chavi) are known as the two-headed mantra;
"namo kumārāya" is placed in the middle, and "nīra" is declared to be at the end. || 1 ||
Regarding that, the names for the seeds of complexion are given in the *Siddhasārasvata*:

"The seed of complexion (*chavibīja*), the seed of luster (*kāntibīja*), as well as beauty (*śobhā*) and exquisite beauty (*suṣamā*); furthermore, there are four artificial seeds beginning with *hrāṃ*. (1)
[Recite] aloud: *oṃ hrāṃ kumārāya namaḥ svāhā*. Now follows the extraction of the mantra of Kārtavīryārjuna, as stated in the Uḍḍāmaratantra:
"The Praṇava, Vāyu, Pūjya, Cāruka, and likewise Manmatha."
Likewise, the seed of semen is emptiness, and the lotus is the tongue. || 1 ||
O Goddess of the Suras, one should know that the name of Kārtavīryārjuna is to be understood as being in the middle of "candram," "ḍimbam," "kūrcam," and "turagam. || 2 ||
O Śivā, the *ante-paya* mantra is said to consist of twenty-one syllables. Regarding the names of the seed-syllable of Śukra, it is stated in the *Chinnāśiromaṇi*:
"The seed-syllable of Śukra, as well as Kāvya, Bhārgava, and the seed-syllable of the poet (*kavi*)."
O Maheśānī, honored by the Daityas, you who are saluted by both gods and asuras! || 1 ||

The five seed-syllables (*bīja*) are *brauṃ*, along with the other artificial ones: the two seed-syllables of semen (*śukra-bīja*) are *brauṃ* and *ḷṃ*. [The mantra] is as follows: *oṃ prīṃ cchrīṃ klīṃ brauṃ āṃ śrīṃ krīṃ aiṃ hrauṃ hūṃ phaṭ kārtavīryārjunāya svāhā*. Now, [the mantra] of Hanumān:
The extraction of the mantra is found in the *Kulacūḍāmaṇi*:
"The Praṇava, then the upper seed-syllable, and after that Vibhūti;
then Hanumate, and again Rāmadūtāya. (1)
Then, for the very purpose of destroying Laṅkā, Bhūtā emerged from the womb of Añjanī,
and immediately after her, Śākinī and Ḍākinī.
Then, for the sake of destruction, [he uttered] "kili" twice along with the sound "bubuka";
immediately after that, [he addressed] the terrifying Lord Hanuman.
Tryakṣa, Māyā, Hariṇākṣī, Vyoṣa, Skanda, likewise Hara, and Āpaḥ at the end; this mantra consists of sixty-seven syllables.

Aloud: Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ, to Hanumān, the messenger of Rāma, for the destruction of Laṅkā, born from the womb of Añjanī, for the destruction of Śākinīs and Ḍākinīs, Kili 2, by means of the *bubukāra* sound, to Vibhīṣaṇa, to the god Hanumān, Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrauṃ hrāṃ phaṭ svāhā. Now...
The extraction of the mantra of Vaṭukabhairava from the Rudrayāmala:
"Oṃ (the Praṇava), Kāma (the Manmatha), joined with the seed-syllable of the cloud (Ya);
the seed-syllable of the ocean (Va), the seed-syllable of the Kalpa (Ra), combined with the seed-syllable of the Śataghnī (Pha). (1)
By me, for Vaṭuka Bhairava, the stone-disease [mantra] was likewise placed in the middle;
at the end is the water [mantra] of Bhairava—this mantra consists of eighteen syllables. (2)

Regarding the names for "cloud-seed" (*abhrabīja*) in the *Vāmakeśvara*: "Cloud-seed," "jīmūta," "ambuda," "jalada," and "ghana"—these five are the seeds (*bīja*), as well as the supreme [seeds] beginning with *anṛ*. (1)
Now, regarding the names of the ocean-seeds (*abdhibīja*), it is stated in the *Tripurātilaka*:
"The ocean-seed (*abdhibīja*), as well as *sindhu*, *sāṃbara*, and *sāgara*;
and the four seed-syllables *ruṃ*—these are both [natural] and other [artificial ones]. (1)

Through the distinction between the syllables *raṃ* and *ruṃ*, *ram* is the seed-syllable of fire (*agni*), and *rum* is the seed-syllable of the ocean (*abdhi*). Because it is "the innermost within the interval between fire and ocean," it is faultless.
Now, the names of the kalpa-seeds are given in the *Āgamālaṅkāra*:

The seed of the eon (*kalpabīja*), the dissolution (*saṃvarta*), the destruction (*pralaya*), the seed of decay (*kṣayabījaka*), the emaciated (*kṣāmika*), the razor-edged (*kṣuraka*), the honey-like (*kṣaudra*), and likewise the seed of the end of the eon (*kalpāntabījaka*). || 1 ||
Thus, there are eight *dhruṃ*-seeds, both natural and artificial.
Now, the names of the *śataghnī* seeds are given in the *Āgamalaharī*:
*śataghnī*, *śyālikā*, *śyāmā*, *śādvalā*, and likewise *śuṣkalā*.
Thus, there are exactly five seed-syllables beginning with GHNĪM, while others are unreal. || 1 ||
[Aloud: Oṃ klīṃ vīṃ ruṃ dhruṃ ghnīṃ hrīṃ vaṭukabhairavāya namaḥ svāhā. Now, the extraction of the mantra of Mahāmṛtyuñjaya, as stated in the Ānamalaharī:
"The three-eyed one (tryakṣa), born from the heart (hṛjja), and also the splendor of power (śaktiśobha)—O Śaṅkara, protect me from that [danger], and likewise two."
Therefore, O Goddess, the extraction of the mantra of Mṛtyuñjaya is as follows: the power (Śakti), the void (Kha), autumn (Śarat), the heart (Hṛt), and the conqueror of the enemy (Jatāri). || 1 ||
[In] the *Prakāśa*: *oṃ juṃ saḥ haṃsaḥ māṃ pālaya 2 sohaṃ saḥ juṃ oṃ*. Now, the extraction of the mantra of Sugrīva from the *Āgamaśiromaṇi*:
[The syllables] Tāra (*oṃ*), Māyā (*hrīṃ*), Vāgbhava (*aiṃ*), Manmatha (*klīṃ*), and Śakti (*sauḥ*)—having placed the name in the middle, and likewise at the end.
The *kālī* lotuses, the *kūrca* lotuses, and all the lotuses—this is the *nīrameṣa-sugrīva* mantra. || 1 ||
Aloud: Oṃ hrīṃ aiṃ klīṃ saḥ sugrīvāya krīṃṭhaḥ hūṃṭhaḥ hrīṃṭhaḥ svāhā.
"O Maheśānī, these seven boys have indeed been described by me.
Dakṣiṇāmūrti said:
"Listen, O sages, if there is anything in your hearts that you wish to ask."
I speak out of affection for you; please grant me your command.
Thus ends the third kalpa, titled "The Narrative of the Seven Goddesses and Seven Kumāras," in the *Uddhārakośa*, the essence of all Āgamas, composed by the venerable sage Dakṣiṇāmūrti. || 3 ||
Now begins the fourth section.
The sages said:
"O Brahman-sage, knower of all truths, you who have reached the further shore of the ocean of scriptures,
you ought to tell us the mantras of the nine planets.
Īśvara said:
At that time, I shall briefly state those mantras of the nine planets which were spoken by the son of Dhātṛ to the great sages.
O Supreme Goddess, O Great Mistress, Āditya, Induja, Śukra, Guru,
and Indu— these five, O Maheśānī, are the presiding deities of the arrows of the Five-Arrowed One (Kāmadeva). || 3 ||
Bhauma, Arki, and Rāhu— these three lords of sages are the presiding deities of the three eyes of the god Khaṇḍaparaśu.
And Ketu, O Supreme Goddess, is proclaimed as the deity of the earth;
these nine planets have been declared by Śambhu in the Rudrayāmala. (5)
Now, first, the extraction of the mantras for the five planets. Among those, first is the extraction of the mantra for the Sun, as stated in the *Viśvanāthasāroddhāra*:
"The Praṇava, the sky, Lakṣmī, and likewise the seed-syllable of the three pungents (vyoṣa)."
The seed-syllable is to be known as the head of the fourth [vowel]; from that, one should extract the sprout. || 1 ||
Then [the mantra] for the King of Planets, and likewise for Āditya; at the end, milk (payas) is to be known [as the seed-syllable]; this is remembered as the eighteen-syllable Manu-mantra. || 2 ||
Regarding the names of the seed-syllables (bīja) for "space" (āmbara), it is stated in the Bhairavatantra: "Space, the seed of clothing, the void, and power—these two;
green, the seed of the doe, and likewise the seed of turmeric. (1)
The seven artificial seed-syllables (*bīja*) are as follows, along with others:
two *ambarabījas* are *hsauḥ* and *āṃ*. The manifestation is: *oṃ hsauḥ śrīṃ āṃ grahādhirājāya ādityāya svāhā*. Now, the extraction of the mantra for Mercury (*budha*) from the *Svatantre*:
The Praṇava, then Skanda, Rasajñā, and Ṣaḍānana;
in the middle, [the mantra] for Grahanātha, Budha, and at the end, the two Ṭhas. (1)
The fourteen-syllable mantra of Budha, the lord of the planets, is as follows;
therein, the names of the seed-syllables of Ṣaḍānana are given in the *Kubjikāsarvasva*:
"Ṣaḍānana, Śarajanmā, Skanda, and Kumāra-bījaka."
The seed-syllable of Śambhu, the seed-syllable of Śālinī, and likewise the seed-syllable of Ṣaṇmukha. || 1 ||
The seed-syllables are "Ṭaṃ" and likewise seven others which are untruths.
[The mantra] is: Oṃ hrāṃ krīṃ ṭaṃ, svāhā to Budha, the lord of the planets. Now, for Śukra...
The extraction of the mantra is found in the *Āgamaśiromaṇi*:
"The Praṇava, the upper seed-syllable, joined with the breast-seed, then the Śiva-seed in the middle, and again for Graheśvara. (1)
At the end of Śukra is Aśmarī; the mantra for Bāla consists of fourteen syllables.
The revealed [mantra] is: *oṃ aiṃ jaṃ gaṃ graheśvarāya śukrāya namaḥ*. Now, the extraction of the mantra of Bṛhaspati from the Tripurātilaka:

O Goddess who possesses three eyes, O Illusion, O Lady of good fortune, you who are saluted by gods and asuras, O beautiful-limbed one, having joined the seed of asafoetida with the courtesan of the waves; || 1 ||
Above that, one should extract the seed-syllable of the six-headed one (Hūṃ), and from that, the sprout (Aiṃ);
then [the mantra] for Bṛhaspati, the lord of the planets.
Furthermore, O Śivā, Vārivaha, Padma, Lakṣmī, Nīraja, Vāsanā, Paṅkaja, and finally Vana are thus declared.

Thus is the extraction [of the mantra]. Regarding the word "saubhāgya," there is a fault. Dakṣiṇāmūrti, however, says: "Fie upon him, O sages, whose own intellect does not understand this! Where is Rukmiṇī, and where is worldly fortune? The distance between heaven and earth is vast."

Such is the fault. And it has been stated in the author’s own work, the *Sundarīsarvasva*: "O Goddess, one should likewise employ the *praṇava*, *sakalā*, and *rukmiṇī*; thereafter, [the term] *vārivaha*—this is the fault. In the *Vāmakeśvara*: "One should also join the *praṇava*, *parā*, and *lakṣmī* to the *vīciveśyā*."
Then, after the moon, [one should worship] the monastery with the words: "Obeisance to the Lord of Planets. || 1 ||
Then for Bṛhaspati, then Jīmūtabījaka;
Padma, Lakṣmī, Nīraja, and likewise Vāsanā-paṅkaja;
at the end, water (nīra) is declared—this is the twenty-five-syllable mantra.
[Aloud: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ khrīṃ aiṃ glauṃ, to Bṛhaspati, the lord of the planets, brīṃṭhaḥ aiṃṭhaḥ śrīṃṭhaḥ svāhā. Now, the extraction of the mantra of the Moon from the Kālīpaṭala:
The three-eyed [syllable] (tryakṣa), the deer-eyed one (hariṇākṣī), joined with the seed-syllable of Kuntī (bīja),
and having combined the word "hare," it is conjoined with the nasal dot (anusvāra) representing the void.
The seed-syllable of the dance (nāṭyabīja) is [placed] there; in the middle, at the end of the moon, aśmarī is traditionally taught.
Regarding that, the names of the seed-syllables of the dance are found in the Bhairavatantra.
Nāṭyabīja, naṭana, tāṇḍava, and nṛttabījaka—these are the four seeds, as well as other artificial ones. (1)
Aloud: Oṃ śrīṃ krīṃ hrāṃ caṃ, salutation to the Moon (Candra).

These five are indeed proclaimed as the planets of the five arrows. Now follows the extraction of the mantras for the three planets. First, the extraction of the mantra for Mars (Bhauma) is given in the *Śāradāṭīkā*:
"The movement, the seed-syllable of the deer, Rukmiṇī, and the Lord of the Night."
Then, in the center, the seed-syllable of Brahmā (Vedhas), followed by "to the Lord of Planets" (grahādhipataye). || 1 ||
At the end of *Bhaumāya*, the fifteen-syllable mantra was declared by me (*mayā*);
therein, the names of the seed-syllables of Brahmā are given in the *Chinnārahasya*: "The seed-syllable of Brahmā, Vidhi, Brahmā, and also the seed-syllable of Svayambhū."
There are also four other artificial seed-syllables (bīja). || 1 ||
Aloud: Aiṃ Hsauḥ Śrīṃ Drāṃ Kaṃ, svāhā to Bhauma, the lord of the planets.
Now, the extraction of the mantra for Śanaiścara is given in the Āgama-laharī:
The Tāra (Oṃ), the Lajjā (Hrīṃ), and the Śrī (Śrīṃ) seeds, followed by the three-headed [triśira] [or trident, according to manuscripts k and kh] pointing upwards;
then "to Śanaiścara, the emperor of the planets" (grahacakravartine). || 1 ||
Madana, Vāsana, Śakti, and finally Nīra are declared [as the components];
the twenty-syllable mantra of the god Śanaiścara is thus remembered. || 2 ||
[Aloud: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ grahacakravartine śanaiścarāya klīṃ aiṃ saḥ svāhā. Now, the extraction of the mantra of Rāhu is as follows—in that same [work]:
"The Praṇava, the pair of tongues, the pair of banks, and the thunder."
Then the fire-god [spoke] to Rāhu, the wielder of the chisel: || 1 ||
Lajjā, Lakṣmī, and Bhīmā are likewise mentioned at the end; the forest [mantra] is proclaimed as having twenty syllables for Rāhu, which bestows desired fruits just like a child. || 2 ||
In that regard, the names of the seed-syllables of thunder are stated in the *Svatantre*:
"Thunder (*garjita*), the seed of sound (*svanabīja*), as well as rumbling (*stanita*) and roaring (*rasita*)."
And there are four seed-syllables (bījas), both artificial and others. || 1 ||
[Aloud: Oṃ krīṃ krīṃ hūṃ hūṃ ṭaṃ ṭaṅkadhāriṇe rāhave raṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ bhaiṃ svāhā. Thus have I declared the deities of the three eyes of Śambhu.
On an auspicious day, O Śivā, the practitioner should accomplish the mantras of the planets.
Now, the extraction of the mantra for Ketu from the *Mantramuktāvalī*:
"The Praṇava, then the entire *vṛṣṭi*, then *krūrarūpiṇe*, then *ketave*, and after that, *candraḥ śaṅkā payaḥ*. (1)
O Goddess, this fifteen-syllable mantra of Ketu is proclaimed as a great mantra (*mahāmantra*). Regarding the names for the seed-syllables of rain, they are stated in the *Muṇḍamālātantra*:
"The seed-syllable of rain is *karaka*; the hailstone is *vārṣika* (or *kārṣika*)."
Furthermore, there are four other artificial seed-syllables (bījas), beginning with *krūṃ*. || 1 ||
Aloud: Oṃ hrīṃ krūṃ, to the comet of fierce form, aiṃ sauḥ svāhā.
Thus, these mantras of the nine planets have been declared by me.
Now, O Goddess of the Gods, I shall indeed tell you the mantras of the letters. || 1 ||
For the benefit of the world, make this treasury more secret than the most secret;
by the mere knowledge of which, a practitioner becomes a master of mantras.

Thus ends the fourth chapter, titled "The Exposition of the Extraction of Mantras for the Nine Planets," in the *Uddhārakośa*, the essence of all Āgamas, composed by the venerable sage Dakṣiṇāmūrti. || 4 ||
p. 553) Now begins the fifth chapter.
The sages said:
O Brahmarṣi, son of Brahmā, you who have reached the further shore of the Vedas and Āgamas;
O illustrious Lord, you are gracious toward us out of compassion. (1)
Indeed, various scriptures have been heard by us from the lotus of your mouth;
now we wish to hear the treasuries of mantras for the castes as well.
Śrī Dakṣiṇāmūrti said:
Listen, O Goddess; I shall proclaim to you from myself the extensive collection of mantras according to the prescribed rule.
And the treasury of mantras of the phonemes issued forth from the mouth of Tripurā.
Listen, all you sages, to this very extensive treasury of mantras,
which was previously indicated by Dakṣiṇāmūrti to the munis.
In the *Tripurātilaka*:
"The seed-syllable of the Self (*ātma-bīja*) is the letter *a*; the end of the self (*svānta*) is the seed-syllable of the heart (*hṛd-bīja*).
The mind (*mānasa*) is the seed-syllable of the mind (*manas-bīja*); this is remembered as belonging to Pitāmaha (Brahmā). (5)
O Goddess of the gods, another meaning of the letter *a* should be known:
it is spoken of as the void (*śūnya*), space (*kha*), the sky (*ambara*), the firmament (*vyoma*), and that which belongs to Viṣṇu (*vaiṣṇava*).
Another [set of] false forms for the letter *ā* is stated in the Bhairava-tantra:
Indrabīja, Jiṣṇu, Marutvān, Maghavā, and Hari. (7)
(554) O Sovereign of the Gods, one should declare that the phoneme *i* of Śiva is another, artificial [form].
This was taught by me in the Bhairava Tantra, my dear. 8.
Likewise, *buddhi*, *bīja*, *medhā*, *dhībīja*, and *mati* are to be known as belonging to Indra; the supreme *anṛta* belongs to the vowel *ī*.
O Śivā, Mistress of the Gods, I have declared in the *Tripurātilaka*:
"The two seed-syllables of Indra are *iṃ* and *īṃ*;
likewise, the seed-syllable of Ruti, Nandā, Vāmana, and the seed-syllable of Vītu. (10)
O Goddess of the Suras, I have explained within this entire essence [of the Kubjikāmata] the solar syllables, the seed-syllable *u*, and other artificial ones belonging to Kubjikā. 11.
O Goddess of the gods, *kaca-bīja*, as well as *keśa*, *śiroruha*, and *mūrdhaja* are synonyms for hair;
any other [term] is untruth, O Mistress of the Gods, regarding the syllable *ū*.
O Supreme Goddess, I have declared in the Śiromaṇi the seed-syllables of Sundarī:
namely, *pāpmabīja*, as well as *pāpa*, *kilbiṣa*, and *kalmaṣa*;
likewise the seed-syllable of Kiṅkarī, and *maṅgala* and *anṛta*.
O Śivā, I have proclaimed this secret of the syllable *ṛ* pertaining to Kālī.

In the Viṣṇuyāmala, it is stated that the seed-syllable *kṛ* is the seed of grace (*kṛpā*), the seed of compassion (*dayā*), and likewise the field for mercy (*karuṇā*); whereas the other [seed-syllable], *ṛ*, is said to be falsehood. (15)
The two universal seeds should be known as the syllable *ḷ* and *namaḥ*.
O Śivā, I have declared that *gaurvaṃ* is the manifest seed and the seed of the universe. (16)
Regarding the syllable *ḷ*, another falsehood has been stated in the Rudrayāmala:
"The seed-syllable of Gaṅgā is *suḥ*, as well as *nadī*, *nākavāpī*, and *svardhunī*. (17)
O Goddess, another Śākramantra and the syllable *ḷ* have been remembered by me in my own composition, the *Mantrasāgara-tantra*. (18)
"Ekādaśī, Mātrikā, likewise Latābīja,
Vallībīja, Vārākī, and whatever else— she would speak what is untrue. (19)
Furthermore, O Sovereign of the Gods, I have explained the significance of the letter *e* in the work *Kulacūḍāmaṇi*, which was composed by the most excellent of mantra-experts. (20)
The Vāgbhava-bīja, the Ūrdhva-bīja, Cāraṇa, Caṇḍikeśvara, Caṇḍa, as well as Carma, Vasana, and likewise Vāsanā.
O Goddess, I have also described to you the beautiful-limbed Carmāṇa, the measure consisting of twelve syllables, which is known as Rāhu and is the supreme falsehood of the vowel Ai.
In the Tripurāsārasarvasva composed by Dakṣiṇāmūrti, there is the Praṇava, then the Tāra, the three-eyed one, and also Tryambaka. (23)
O Goddess of gods, Trāsa and Tāraka, as well as Kaitava, have been remembered by me;
indeed, when the Chinnāśiromaṇi was composed, it was fashioned by me myself. (24)
Likewise, the seed of liberation, liberation itself, knowledge, and the seed of nirvāṇa—this Āgastya has been proclaimed by me in the Bhairavatantra treatise. (25)

The seed of the mango, the seed of a tree, a footed plant, one that grows from the earth, and one that sprouts from the ground—these have been declared by me; anyone who would speak otherwise would be telling a lie. (26)
In the Siddhasārasvata treatise, it was revealed by Brahmā himself:
the Nāgabīja, the Bhūdhara, the Bhargyabīja, and the Bhānava. (27)

O Goddess, I have declared to you the supreme, eternal, and unmanifest meaning of the syllable *Aḥ*, which is difficult for the whole world to attain within this *Tripurasundarī-Grantha*, the essence of all things. (28)
The syllable *ka* is the seed of the head, and the seed of the crown is beautiful (*cāruṇa*).
The seed of the Creator is the Ordainer (*vidhi*), Brahmā, and indeed the seed of the Self-born (*svayambhū*).
I have declared that the letter *ka* signifies falsehood; one should speak another [truth] in this *Chinnārahasya* treatise, O daughter of Parvateśvara. (30)
The seed-syllable of Nabhā, the Puṣkara, the seed-syllable of Dyu,
and the seed-syllable of Vaiṣṭaraśrava were proclaimed by Tripurā herself. (31)
And even by me, in this *Āgamāmṛtamañjarī* which is difficult to obtain, [the names] Śivabīja, Śambhu, Śarva, and Śaṅkara have been [expounded]. (32)
O Śivā, O beloved, in the *Kulacūḍāmaṇi*—a text difficult to obtain even in heaven—I have spoken something else that is untrue regarding the syllable *ga*. (33)
Jinabīja, Ṣaḍabhijña, and likewise Mārajidbīja; Māyātmaja, Arkabandhu, Gautama, and Anṛta are the supreme [names]. (34)
Regarding the letter *va*, it has been declared by me in the Rudrayāmala Tantra that the six-faced one, born of the arrow, Skanda, is the seed-syllable of Kumāra. (35)
Śāmbhava is the seed-syllable of Śālinī; the other is known as Anṛta.
This has been declared by me in the *Kubjikāsarvasva*, O you who are worshipped by the three worlds. (36)
The seed of drama is *naṭana*, and the seed of dance is *tāṇḍava*;
this has been declared by me regarding the letter *ca* in the *Bhairavatantra* treatise. (37)
The seed-syllable of Śani, that of Arkaja, likewise the seed-syllable of Paṅgu, Kāla, the seed-syllable of Saura, and the birth-seed of Sundara. (38)
Regarding the letter *cha*, I have declared in the *Kāmeśvara* treatise, O Śivā:
the two seed-syllables of Saturn are *chaṃ* and *ñaṃ*;
likewise, the seed-syllable of the breast is *kuca*, and similarly *uroja* and *hṛjja*. (39)
"I have explained the letter *ja*; one should speak of another untruth in the work titled *Āgamālaṃkāra* composed by Bhairava. (40)
The seed of desire is longing, yearning, and greed; this fourfold set is declared by me to be the seed of the letter Jha, while the other is remembered as untruth.
In the *Vāmakeśvara*, the scripture renowned throughout the three worlds, O Goddess,
there are the seed-syllable of Yama and the seed-syllable of Kāla, which both abide as the ender of all things.
O beloved, in the *Tripurāsarvasva* treatise— which is difficult to obtain in the three worlds— I have remembered that the syllable *ña* is the destroyer and the seed of death. (43)

The two seeds of time are *ñaṃ* and *chaṃ*. O Goddess worshipped by the gods, I have declared in my own tantra that the thundering is the seed-syllable of sound (*svana*) and the rumbling is likewise the seed-syllable of resonance (*rasita*), both belonging to the letter *ṭa*.
Padma, paṅkaja, payoja, nīraja, and ambuja—these five, as well as others, have *ṭhaka* as their seed-syllables (*bīja*). (45)
O Goddess of the gods, I have declared these in the Vāmakeśvara Tantra:
Siṃhikā, the seed-syllable of Sarasī, and likewise the seed-syllable of Reṇukā. (46)
O Goddess, in the Rudrayāmala treatise, I have declared that *añjanībījaka* is one [seed-syllable] and *anṛta* is another, both beginning with the letter *ḍa*. 47.
The seed-syllable of Vāyu is to be known as Anila, Samīraṇa, Marut, Samīra, Āśuga, Vāta, and Śvasana. || 48 ||
I have declared the letter *ḍha*; one should speak of another as being false.
The two seed-syllables of Vāyu are *ḍhaṃ* and *yaṃ*.
Likewise, the seed-syllable of the arrow is *mārgaṇa*, *pattriṇa*, and *āśuga*. (49)
In the Bhairava Tantra, the syllable *ṇa* is other than untruth (*anṛta*).
The two seeds of swift motion are *ḍhaṃ* and *ṇaṃ*.
The seed of night, the seed of darkness, and indeed the seed of the quality of *tamas*—[it is said: "and Night is mine, the one characterized by *tamas*"]. (50)
One might speak of something else as the seed-syllable (bīja) of the night-giver (kṣaṇadā), but that would be false;
for in the *Kubjikāsarvasva* treatise, that [specific] seed-syllable has been remembered by me. (51)
The seed-syllable *bilabīja*, the aperture, and the hollow of the world of the Nāgas—
these have been declared by me in the *Kulikārṇava-tantra* (the *Kubjikā-tantra*) for the sake of the letter *tha*.
The seed-mantra of the wheel (cakri-bīja), the seed-mantra of the serpent (vyāla-bīja), sarpa, kākodara, uraga, bhogin-bīja, bhujaṅga, and bhujaṅgama are thus remembered. (53)
p.
558) Regarding the letter *da*, another falsehood has been proclaimed by me;
it was composed by Dakṣiṇāmūrti in the *Svatantra* [tantra], O Goddess of the Lord of Gods. (54)

The letter *dha* is traditionally held to signify a flower-seed, a blossom, procreation, and likewise excellent offspring; anything other than these is considered falsehood in the *Tripurātilaka*. (55)
Alkaline seed, salt, rock salt, the boar, and the wolf—O Goddess of the Gods, I have declared these to be falsehoods concerning the boar and other such things. (56)
O Dear One, in this treatise renowned throughout the three worlds, which is the crest-jewel of Tripurā,
the seed-syllable is similar to the path traversed by the Tortoise and the Fish.
There is no mutual difference between the letter *pha* and the letter *pa*;
however, regarding their pronunciation, extraction, and writing, their fundamental forms are distinct.
The seed-mantra of Matsya, the seed-mantra of Mīna, and likewise the seed-mantra of Śapharī—
the seed-mantra of Jhaṣa has been declared by me in the work *Chinnāśiromaṇi*.
O beautiful lady, I have also described the tortoise as *kūrmabīja* and *kamaṭha*, the crab as *karkaṭa* and *kulīraka*, and the turtle as *kacchapa*; these other names have likewise been told by me.
In the auspicious Śāradā-paṭala chapter of the text renowned throughout the three worlds, it is taught that there is a triad consisting of *ūrmi*, *vīci*, and likewise *taraṅga*. (61)
O Goddess of the Gods, another object of knowledge, which is unreal, has been declared by me in this *Kālikākulasarvasva*, revealed by Brahmā himself. (62)
"Bhadrikā, Bhāsvatī, and Bhīmā—these are the supreme [forms] beginning with the letter Bha;
O Goddess of the Gods, this has been declared by me in the Muṇḍamālā Tantra. (63)
The seed of a lizard, the seed of a chameleon, a frog, and likewise a toad, as well as the seed of a female frog—these have been declared by me; any other is considered false. (64)
In the *Āgamāmṛtamañjarī*, O daughter of Parvateśvara, [are taught] the seed-syllable of Vāyu, as well as the eloquent, the talkative, and the seed-syllable for subjugation. (65)
The seed-syllable of the Hero (vīra-bīja), as well as the Vāpī, has been explained by me in the *Svatantra*.
On the southeast [corner], there is the letter *ra*, which is Fire, the consumer of oblations, and the bearer of sacrificial offerings. (66)
O Goddess of the gods, I have explained the syllable *ra* in the Śyāmātantra;
it is the seed-syllable of darkness (*tamas*), as well as obscurity, delusion, and gloom. (67)
The letter *la* has been explained by me in the *Svatantra*, which is praised by the sages;
the seed-syllable of the earth, the seed-syllable of the ground, the letter *la*, has been spoken of by me. (68)
"Abhra, megha, jīmūta, ambubhṛt, ambuda, ghana—these are the synonyms for the letter 'va' as declared by me in the Vāmakeśvara Tantra. (69)
"Auspiciousness (kalyāṇa), well-being (śarma), peace (śam), and the auspicious (śubha)—this tetrad of the letter Śa has been declared by me in the Bhairavatantra treatise. (70)
The seed-syllable of Śampā, the seed-syllable of Taḍit, likewise Vidyut, Śatahradā, and the seed-syllable of Hrādinī— these others are remembered as being unreal.
O Goddess of the Suras, I have indeed explained this in the Rudrayāmala Tantra;
Śakti and Śarma are to be understood as such, and likewise Śaracchaṅka. (72)
I have explained the letter *sa* in the work titled *Chinnāśiromaṇi*:
it is the seed-syllable of luster, the seed-syllable of splendor, as well as beauty, radiance, and supreme loveliness. (73)
And space is the [nature] of the letter *ha*; that which is other than these has been declared by me in the *Siddhasārasvata* treatise, which is eternally worshipped by practitioners of mantra. (74)
Devabīja, nirjara, tridaśa, tridiveśaka, surabīja, gīrbāṇa, lekha, and amarabījaka. (75)

O beloved, O Goddess of the lords of gods, I have proclaimed the treasury of letters in the *Kulacūḍāmaṇi*; O Śivā, O Goddess, it is joined with various mantras and is determined according to all the Āgamas. (76)
Thus ends the fifth chapter, titled "The Exposition of the Treasury of All Phonemes," in the *Uddhārakośa*, the essence of all Āgamas, composed by the venerable sage Dakṣiṇāmūrti. || 5 ||
(p. 560) Now begins the sixth ritual procedure (kalpa).
Śrī Īśvara said: O Sureśānī, for the two-syllable [mantras], there are separate names—krīṃ, prīṃ, śrīṃ, hrīṃ, hsrauḥ—as well as separate names;
this is determined by all the Āgamas.
Today, O Goddess, I shall declare to you the three deities of the worlds,
which were formerly spoken by Dakṣiṇāmūrti himself to the sages.
Bhavānī, O Goddess of the lords of gods, is the second Bagalāmukhī;
Indrākṣī is the third; these three are the deities of the worlds.
I shall declare these mantras to you; listen, O Pārvatī!
They must not be told to just anyone; they must not be told, O fair-faced one.
In that regard, first is the extraction of the mantra of Bhavānī from the Muṇḍamālā Tantra:
The Praṇava (Oṃ), two lotuses (Padma), a pair of three-eyed ones (Tryakṣa), Parā again; two Hariṇākṣīs, the Kūrca, Hara, joined with two Ṭhas (Ṣṭh). || 1 ||
Aloud: Oṃ śrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ śrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.
Now, regarding the extraction of the mantra of Bagalāmukhī, it is stated in the Āgama-laharī:

"The *tāraka* (om) and the seed-syllable of the earth (laṃ), which are declared to be two syllables, constitute the mantra known as 'Two Heads' (*dviśira*). After that, one should extract the 'Sprout' (*pallava*). (1)
O Bhagavatī Bagalāmukhī Devī, then again,
[seize] the speech, the mouth, and likewise the feet of all the wicked.
Paralyze the tongue twice, likewise pin the intellect twice,
and destroy the seed-syllable of clay (mṛttikā-bījaka) two times.
p.
561) At the end of the three eyes (*tryakṣa*), milk (*payas*) is to be known; this is the mantra consisting of fifty-two syllables.
In that regard, the seed-syllables (*bīja*) and names are stated in the *Bhairavatantra*:
O daughter of Parvateśvara, "mṛd-bījam," "mṛttikā-bījam," "mṛtsnā-bījam," and "praśastikā" are synonyms; furthermore, "mṛtsā" should be known as the supreme falsehood. (1)

*Hrīṃ* is the seed-syllable of clay (*mṛd-bīja*). The revealed mantra is: *Oṃ hrīṃ bhagavati bagalāmukhi devi sarvaduṣṭānāṃ vācaṃ mukhaṃ padaṃ stambhaya 2 jihvāṃ kīlaya 2 buddhiṃ vināśaya 2 hrīṃ oṃ svāhā* (52). Now follows the extraction of the mantra of Indrākṣī.
In the Rudrayāmala:
"O Goddess, [the mantra consists of] the three-eyed one (tryakṣa), two kuntīs, likewise a pair of kūrcas, the seed-syllable of prastha, Parā, Padmā, Carmāṇa, and then the name. (1)
Indra, the eye, the thunderbolt, the hand, at the end Lakṣmī, and Lajjā; Puṣkara, the pair of banks, two tongues, Trāsa, Candra, Hara, and Vana. (2)
The mantra of twenty-eight syllables belongs to Indrākṣī, the goddess of gods.
Regarding that, the names of the seed-syllables of the *prastha* are given in the *Śāradā-paṭala*:
"The *prastha*-seed, the *sānu*-seed, as well as the *śikhara* and the *puṣkara*."
This indeed is the extraction of the seed-syllable *mlauṃ*; one should speak nothing else that is false.
Aloud: Oṃ krīṃ krīṃ hūṃ hūṃ mlauṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aiṃ indrākṣi vajrahaste śrīṃ hrīṃ mlauṃ hūṃ hūṃ krīṃ krīṃ oṃ aiṃ phaṭ svāhā (28). Thus.
The venerable Īśvara said: "O Goddess, these three deities of the worlds have been declared by me;
they were revealed in this worldly existence through devotion by Dakṣiṇāmūrti. (1)
Then, O Goddess of the gods, I shall indeed declare the mantra of Khecarī;
by resorting to which the yogi attains the portion that bestows the perfection of Khecarī. (2)
The extraction of the Khecarī mantra from the Viśvayāmala:
One should extract the tenth letter from the [alphabet of] speech (the vowels) in reverse order;
then one should place the seed-syllable of darkness (Ta), and after that, the seed-syllable of Māyā (Hrīṃ). (1)
Then one should give the autumn seed; this is proclaimed as the *kūṭa*.
The fourth head of the mantra (the seed-syllable) is to be known, and then the yogi should give the name. (2)
Then one should offer to Khecarī, and at the end, indeed, to Auśmakī as well;
the formula for the manifest [offering] is: *mūlhrīṃ sauḥ phecarīyai namaḥ*.

Thus ends the sixth chapter, titled "The Narration of the Treasury of the Three Goddesses and Khecarī," in the *Uddhārakośa*, the essence of all Āgamas, composed by the venerable sage Dakṣiṇāmūrti. 6.
Now begins the seventh chapter:
Śrī-Īśvara.
Now, O Goddess, I shall explain to you the meditations determined by the scriptures;
listen, O Pārvatī, to these deities according to their true nature.
In that regard, O Goddess of the Suras, I shall first describe the meditation on the ten Vidyās of Tripurā as taught in the Vāmakeśvara Tantra; listen to it.
Her body adorned with divine garments, her eyes like the sun, fire, and moon, wearing a crown of the nectar-rayed moon,
and possessing a luster white as snow; seated upon a lion-throne, holding an axe and a sword in her two arms, she is saluted by Brahmā, Indra, and Viṣṇu.
I worship Tripurā. || 3 ||
Now I shall describe the meditation on Śrī as spoken in the Rudrayāmala, which is well-honored by sages, practitioners, gods, and hosts of obstacles (or brahmins).
Lakṣmī, whose hips rest upon a lotus seat, whose eyes are the sun and the moon, and whose hands hold a lotus, a conch, and a sword, possessing the radiance of rising gold and the sun;
I bow with devotion to her whose limbs are adorned with many well-fashioned pearls and gems, who has two arms, and who eternally bestows the fruits of the three worlds. || 5 ||
Now, O Śivā, I shall describe the meditation on Vāgdevī which bestows knowledge—
a meditation that is difficult to find even in heaven within the work known as the Tantramuktāvalī.
I worship Vāṇī, whose face is as radiant as the full moon, who possesses the luster of camphor and jasmine,

and whose head is marked by the crescent moon; she respectfully holds with her own hands a lute, a rosary, a jar brimming with nectar, and the goddess of learning, while her breasts are full and high.
I worship her whose body is adorned with divine ornaments and who is mounted upon a lion. || 7 ||
Now I shall describe the meditation on Tārā according to the Bhairava Tantra—on the Goddess who is devoid of differentiation and worshipped by sages and practitioners. (8)
The Goddess, adorned with serpents, possessing the luster of snow and the cool-rayed moon as well as the radiance of a conch,
her neck encircled by bracelets of pearls and gems, wearing crimson garments, bearing a trident, lotus, sword, and mace, and eternally praised by the hosts of gods led by Vaikuṇṭha— [I bow to her].
I worship Tārā, who has three eyes and is solely intent upon protecting the three worlds. || 9 ||
Now I shall describe the meditation on Bhuvaneśvarī; listen to that, which has emerged from the Rudrayāmala, a text that grants the desires of practitioners. (10)
Her face resembles a thousand rising suns; she has full breasts and dwells upon a lotus;
she respectfully holds in her arms a goad, a noose, a book, and a rosary;
she is constantly praised with salutations by Brahmā, Upendra, Maheśvara, Indra, and the sages.
With hymns and other offerings, I worship the three-eyed Bhuvaneśvarī within the lotus of my heart.
Now, O daughter of the mountain, I shall describe the meditation on Mātaṅgī, even from my own work, the *Kubjikāsarvasva*, which is extremely difficult to obtain. (12)
Her crest is marked by the crescent moon; she has three eyes and the radiance of ten million moons and suns;
her girdle is bound with thousands of various jewels; and she is seated upon a corpse throne.
I shall always meditate with joy in my heart upon the enchanting Goddess Mātaṅginī, who joyfully bears a conch, a tomara-spear, a paṭṭisa-club, and a pair of lotuses in her arms. 13.
Now, O Maheśānī, I shall describe the supreme meditation on Śārikā, which has emerged from the *Āgamāmṛtamañjarī* and is difficult for people to obtain. (14)

I meditate in my heart upon the illustrious Śārikā, who has three eyes; whose hands hold a conch, a discus, a mace, and a pair of lotuses; whose neck is adorned with a garland marked by bracelets and a necklace of lordly serpents; and who blazes with the radiance of a thousand rays of vermilion and saffron.
Now, O Goddess of gods, daughter of Parvateśvara, I shall describe the unsurpassed meditation upon the Queen (Rājñī), as taught in the Vāmakeśvara Tantra. 16.

I worship the Great Goddess, the Queen who has the form of the snowy mountain; she whose eyes are the moon, the morning sun, and fire, who possesses four arms, who sits upon a seat of deer-skin, and who holds a conch, a lotus, a trident, and a sword. 17.
Now I shall describe the meditation on Bhīḍā, which bestows the fruits of one's desires, as it has emerged from the *Āgamoddyota* composed by me myself. (18)
I worship Bhīḍā, who resembles the mass of light from the rays of the rising moon, seated upon a full-blown lotus, holding in her four adorable arms a lute, the king of serpents, a conch, and an axe;
whose heart is adorned with pearl necklaces and various jewels, and who carries a vessel of spirituous liquor.
Bhavānī, whose face is smiling, who bestows the desired objects upon her practitioners. || 19 ||
Now, O Goddess of the Gods, I shall describe the unsurpassed meditation on Jvālāmukhī, as composed by me in my work titled *Jvālāśiromaṇi*. (20)
I meditate in my heart upon Jvālāmukhī, whose face and hair are surrounded by flames, who holds a lotus, a conch, a sword, and a mace, and whose pair of feet is placed upon a lion throne. (21)
Now I shall declare the meditation on Bhadrakālī as it emerged from the Vāmakeśvara Tantra itself, which was composed by me.
I meditate upon her who holds the shaven head of the Creator of the universe in the palm of her lotus-hand, laughing and saying "I am not satiated," while she is always devouring all people;
dark-complexioned, she carries Viṣṇu and Śiva impaled on her trident by the strength of her multitude of arms.
Bhadrakālī, resembling a fresh rain-cloud, seated upon the midst of corpses. || 23 ||

I shall declare the meditation on the Fourth (turīya), which has emerged from the nectar of the scriptures, renowned throughout this world of moving and unmoving beings, and revealed by Brahmā himself. (24)
I bow to the auspicious Śivā, who is white as the moon, adorned with a crescent moon bound with various jewels upon her head encircled by matted locks; she holds a noose and a lotus,
possesses two arms, has three eyes of the sun, moon, and fire, a smiling face, and is seated upon a corpse.
I worship the Goddess Turi, who is bowed down to by Brahma, Upendra, and Maheśvara. 25.
Now, O Goddess, I shall describe the visualization of Chinnamastā as it emerged from my own work, the *Śiromaṇi*, a treatise on Tripurā. (26)
Her forehead-slate is encircled by the rays of the moon; she possesses the brilliance of ten million rising suns;
she bears a multitude of highly precious jewels bound with flames; she is radiant with the pride of Kandarpa;
and she holds a trident, a discus, a goad, a noose, a flute, a mace, a lotus, and the gesture of fearlessness—granting the desires of her devotees.
I worship Śrī Chinnamastā, whose pair of lotus feet are honored by devotees;
I meditate always upon the Goddess Chinnamastakā within the lotus of my heart. 27.
And I shall describe the meditation on Dakṣiṇākālikā as it has emerged from this text, the *Kālīrahasya*, O daughter of Parvateśvara. (28)
She has a girdle made of the bones and skulls of Brahmā, Upendra, and Śiva; her lower lip is red with betel; she resembles a rain cloud;
and she holds a trident, a mace, a lotus, a sword, a noose, and a goad.
I meditate upon that goddess Dakṣiṇakālikā, who is red-robed, mounted upon a corpse, and who holds a conch, a sword, and a trident in her ten excellent arms. (29)
Now, O daughter of the mountain, I shall describe the meditation on Śyāmā, as it was declared by me in the Śyāmātantra, which is an ocean of all the Āgamas. (30)
I worship her who is dark-complexioned, whose two lotus-feet are worshipped by the three worlds, who bears a form resembling a cloud charged with black rain, who possesses three eyes,
and who carries a trident, a sword, a conch, and a large discus in her arms.
Seated upon a corpse as her throne. || 31 ||
Now, O Goddess, I shall declare the meditation that has emerged from Kālarātri, as it was composed by me in the Vāmakeśvara Tantra. (32)

I meditate in my heart upon the Great Goddess Kālarātri, who has four arms holding a trident, a lotus, a noose, and a goad; she is smoke-colored, possesses three eyes, sits upon a lion-throne, and wears yellow garments.
O Goddess adorned with various ornaments, I shall speak; listen!
This meditation on Śrī Vajrayoginī emerged from the Ocean of Kulikās. (34)
I worship Vajrayoginī, who has the moon, fire, and sun as her eyes, who holds a noose and a goad, who is auspicious (Śivā),
two-armed, and seated upon a lion.
[The one who bestows fearlessness. || 35 ||
Now, O Goddess, I shall describe the meditation on Vārāhī as determined in the Tantra,
which bestows all desired objects, O beloved, in the Kulacūḍāmaṇi.

I meditate upon her in the lotus of my heart— she who has the crescent moon as her crest-jewel, who is two-armed and holds a trident and a goad in her two hands, whose face is dark blue, and whose lotus-eyes consist of the sun, fire, and moon.
Vimalā Varāhī. || 37 ||
Now, O Goddess of the Gods, I shall describe the supreme meditation on Śāradā,
even though it has already been composed by me myself in the chapter on Śāradā within this work. (38)

I meditate in my heart upon the blessed Goddess Śāradā, who has six arms and three eyes, whose face is graced with a smile, whose lotus feet are praised by the sage Śāṇḍilya, who stands upon a mountain, and who holds a trident. (39)
Now, O Goddess of the Gods, listen as I shall describe the supreme meditation upon Kāmeśvarī Tripurā, the very essence of this most excellent tantra. (40)

I meditate in my heart upon that Kāmeśvarī, who has three eyes and the splendor of a thousand suns; she is seated upon a lion-throne, possesses two arms, and holds a sword; she is clad in yellow garments and is served by Viṣṇu and Maheśa. 41.
Now, O daughter of Parvateśvara, I shall describe to you the meditation on Gaurī according to the Bhairava Tantra, as composed by me in this work.
I bow to Gaurī, who has a fair complexion, holds a lotus, possesses three eyes, is clad in white garments, and rides upon a lion;
her crest is illuminated by the moon, her face is smiling, and she carries a mace with her two arms;
her two feet are worshipped by Viṣṇu, Indra, Brahmā, Śiva, and the other gods.
I worship that Blessed Lady, the bestower of the desires of her devotees, within the lotus of my mind. || 43 ||
Now I shall describe the meditation on Annapūrṇā; listen, O Goddess, as it was revealed by me in the Bhairavītantra. (44)

I meditate in my heart upon that Annapūrṇā, who bears the crescent moon on her crest, who has two arms and three eyes, who holds a trident and a rosary in her two hands, who is seated upon a deer, and who has a serpent as her sacred thread.
O beloved, I shall describe the meditation on Kulavāgīśvarī; listen to me, for it is difficult to find even for me within this *Āgamāmṛtamañjarī*. (46) p. 568)
I worship Kulavāgīśvarī, who holds a trident and a sword with her two arms, whose face is red, who resembles fire, who has three eyes, and who is seated upon a lion-throne. 47.

Now, O Ambikā, I shall describe the meditation on Gaṇeśa, who is worshipped by the hosts of gods and sages, within this ocean of the nectar of the Āgamas, which is difficult to find in this world. (48)

I worship the son of Śiva, the elephant-faced one, whose limbs are adorned with two, four, and fourteen colors; who holds a mace and a lotus and wears a serpent as a sacred thread; who walks like a lord of deer and possesses three eyes. 49.
Now, O Pārvatī, listen as I describe the meditation of the Youth (Kumāra), which has emerged from the illumination of the Āgamas and was composed by me myself. (50)

I meditate in my heart upon the primordial Kumāra, who bestows all desired boons; who is white as the snowy mountain, two-armed, his body entwined by serpents, seated upon a peacock throne, and the beloved son of the Daughter of the Mountain King. (51)
O Haihaya, out of curiosity I shall thus describe to you this meditation, which grants the desires of men and is determined by Uḍḍāmara. (52)
I meditate within my heart upon the Lord of the World, who has a thousand-armed retinue and has conquered the lords of the hosts of demons; whose face resembles the moon,
who carries a thousand quivers,
who is ever clad in white garments, and who stands in the midst of the king of horses.
Kārtavīryārjuna. || 23 ||
Now, O Goddess of gods, I shall describe the meditation that has issued forth concerning that Lord Mṛtyuñjaya, as found in the *Kubjāśiromaṇi* treatise. (54)
The Lord of the Gods, whose hair is illuminated by the moon, holds a vessel of nectar in his large lotus-hand;
he is as stainless as ten million moons, with a lotus resting in his hand.
I meditate upon that Paśupati, the conqueror of death, who is imperishable, whose eyes are the sun, fire, and moon, and who holds in his palms a noose, a rosary, a goad, and a lotus.
Now, O daughter of the mountain, I shall describe the meditation upon Sugrīva in the *Mantrasāgara*, a work composed as the crest-jewel of its lineage. (56)

I worship the descendant of Kakutstha, who appears as a sixteen-year-old youth, who is the lord of monkeys and radiant with the brilliance of fire; who respectfully bears trees, clubs, bows, and multitudes of arrows in his arms; and who is being reverently honored by the monkey hosts intent on searching for Sītā.
[He saw] Sugrīva, the son of the Sun, worshipping [him] in his heart.
Now, O daughter of Parvateśvara, I shall describe to you the meditation on Hanumān as it has emerged in the Kulacūḍāmaṇi treatise. (58)

I meditate in my heart upon the praiseworthy Hanumān—the beloved friend of Rāma, the sole hero in the world, who received salutations from the king of the lordly monkeys; he who resembles a peak of Mount Sumeru, inconceivable, primordial, and worthy of worship. (59)
Now, O Pārvatī, I shall describe to you the meditation on Bhairava, as it has emerged from the Bhairava Tantra, bestowing the fruits one desires. (60)

With a skull in his hand, a serpent as his sacred thread, dark-complexioned, holding a staff, and possessing three eyes—meditate in your heart upon that inconceivable, primordial Bhairava, devoted to drinking wine, the granter of all desires. 61.
Now I shall describe the meditation on the Sun as determined in the Tantras,
according to the *Tripurāsarvasva* treatise composed by Dakṣiṇāmūrti. (62)

I worship the primordial god Mihira within the lotus of my heart— he who is directly perceptible, radiant, beautifying the region of the earth with a thousand rays, mounted upon seven horses, and holding a noble banner in his hand.
Now I shall describe the meditation on Saumya according to the Bhairava Tantra;
it truly bestows all desired objects, O you who are saluted by gods and asuras. (64)

I remember Budha, the son of Soma, seated upon a swan, with two arms, having the luster of a conch and the moon, holding a sword and a noose in his hands, a treasure-house of compassion, his limbs adorned with ornaments, within the lotus of my mind. (65)
Now I shall explain the visualization of Śukra as determined in the Tantras, as revealed by Brahmā himself in the *Kubjikāsarvasva* treatise. (66)
One should meditate upon Śukra in the heart— resembling molten gold, two-armed, compassionate, clad in yellow garments,
holding a pair of lotuses and a trident,
seated upon a Krauñca throne, his lotus feet served by the Asuras, and possessing two eyes.
I am in the lotus. || 67 ||

Now I shall speak of the meditation upon the individual soul (jīva) according to its true nature; listen, O Pārvatī, to this meditation as taught in the Bhairava-tantra, which bestows all goals upon men. 68.
I remember the Guru, who is composed of light, holding a trident and a spear in his hands, whose lotus feet are praised by the foremost of the lords of gods,
who is a treasury of wisdom, mounted upon an elephant, possessing two arms,
within the lotus of my mind. (69)
571) Now I shall describe the meditation on the Moon; listen, O dear Goddess, for it has emerged from the illumination of the scriptures, like a river of manifold meditations. (70)
I meditate upon the Moon, the lord of the night, who possesses the luster of a conch shell, who is dear to the deer, whose conduct is worthy of praise as he rests upon the crown of the Lord (Śiva),
and who holds a pair of lotuses in his hands— [I meditate on that Moon] within the lotus of my heart.
The lord of the planets. || 71 ||
Now I shall describe the meditation on Bhauma as determined in the Tantras;
listen with a one-pointed mind, O beloved, in this *Āgamāmṛtamañjarī*. (72)
