I meditate in my heart upon the compassionate Bhauma, who resembles molten gold from the Ganges, who sits upon a lion-throne with a lotus and a sword in his hands, and whose lotus-feet are worshipped by gods and asuras alike. (73)
Now I shall describe the meditation on Saturn, which bestows desired fruits;
it has emerged, O Great Goddess, from the nectar of the scriptures and grants auspiciousness. (74)

I meditate upon Śani within the lotus of my mind—he who has the luster of blue collyrium, the beloved son of Mihira (the Sun), the lord of the planets, holding a noose and a serpent in his hands, two-armed, and the bringer of fear to both gods and demons. 75.
Now I shall describe the meditation on Saiṃhikeya; listen to it, which has emerged from the Vāmakeśvara Tantra and yields fruit for men. (76)

I remember in my heart Rāhu, the lord of planets, who has the form of the friend of the cool-rayed moon and the end-maker, whose appearance is both formidable and like lapis lazuli, who possesses many arms, is supremely intent on protecting the three worlds, and bestows all that is desired.
Now I shall explain the visualization of Ketu as determined by the Āgamas,
which has emerged in the work titled *Āgamoddyota* within the *Tantrasāgara*. (78)

I worship in the lotus of my mind that solitary hero whose banner is endowed with a tail, who strikes fear into people, who resembles a dark rain-cloud, who wears black garments, and who holds a spear and a trident in his hands. 79.
Now, O Goddess of gods, O Bhavānī, I shall describe the supreme meditation upon you, which has emerged from the text *Kulacūḍāmaṇi*, O Mistress of the World. (80)
May Durgā—who holds a discus, conch, sword, shield, arrows, a great bow, a trident, and a threatening finger;
who stands upon the head of Mahiṣa; and who resembles fresh dūrvā grass—be for your prosperity.

I worship Bhavānī, who bestows fearlessness, seated upon the head of a buffalo, and resembling fresh dūrvā grass. Now, I shall describe the meditation on Bagalāmukhī as it has emerged from the *Āgamāmṛtamañjarī*, which is honored by gods and demons alike.

I bow to the auspicious Śivā, who is seated upon a lion-throne, adorned with a beautiful crown set with various jewels, clothed in yellow garments, the bestower of fortune, whose eyes possess the radiance of the sun, fire, and moon, and who is beloved by the Lord of Caṇḍī (Śiva).
She resembles the rising sun and the golden Aṅgada.
I worship in my heart the Goddess Śrī Bagalāmukhī, whose limbs are illuminated by highly precious jewels, who always grants the desires of her devotees and bestows liberation. 83.
Now I shall speak; listen, O Indrākṣī, to this supreme meditation which emerged from the *Rudrayāmala* treatise, O Mistress of the World. (84)
She holds a garland, a goad, and a pair of lotuses; she is marked with a thousand eyes, rides upon the back of the intoxicated Airāvaṇa, and has a face like the moon.

I worship in my heart Indrākṣī, the mother of all people, who is intent on protecting the three worlds, who delights in singing with her arms, who resembles a full-blown lotus, who is praised by Brahmā and the other gods, and who is the supreme embodiment of compassion. 85.

Now, O Maheśānī, I shall describe the supreme meditation on Khecarī, meditating upon which a yogi becomes liberated while living in the Kali age; this [teaching] emerged from the scripture known as the Bhairava Tantra, O you who are worshipped by the thirty gods. (86)

I meditate in my heart upon Khecarī, whose two feet are worshipped by sages with white lotuses and blue water-lilies; she is white in complexion, her moon-like lotus-hands are white, and her crest is radiant with white rays; her eyes are the sun, the moon, and fire, and she holds the gestures of fearlessness and a book.
The mother of the world, the bestower of spiritual accomplishments. || 87 ||

O Goddess of the gods, this collection of mantras and meditations for these [deities] is remembered; it must not be given to just anyone, for it is a treasury containing the extraction of the texts. 88.
The sages said:
"Blessed is he whose son you are, having reached the further shore of all the scriptures.
Victory to you! You ought to command us to go to our own homes. (89)
"Dakṣiṇāmūrti said:
'Go now, all you sages; forgive me out of compassion.
Having spoken thus, the sages, eager for the mantra, went to their own homes. (90)
The venerable Lord said:
Having seen those delightful tantras, Dakṣiṇāmūrti composed this work called the Uddhārakośa; keep it as the most secret of secrets.
The Goddess said:
"O Lord of the Gods, I have been purchased by you with this book."
Having spoken thus, both the goddess Ambikā and the moon-crested god went to the great grove on Mount Kailāsa.

Thus ends the seventh chapter, the exposition on the visualization of the sixteen goddesses, the seven goddesses, the seven maidens, the nine planets, the three goddesses, and the Khecarīs, in the *Uddhārakośa*, the essence of all Āgamas, composed by the venerable sage Dakṣiṇāmūrti. || 7 ||
And thus this Uddhārakośa is completed; may there be auspiciousness.
